question_text: Let P(z) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 in C[z] whose Hessian matrix Hes P is nilpotent, so P is Hessian nilpotent. If Delta := sum_{i=1}^n D_i^2 is the Laplace operator on C[z], must the iterated Laplacians of the powers of P eventually vanish in the sense that Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) = 0 for all sufficiently large m?
context_brief: vanishing conjecture for degree-4 Hessian nilpotent polynomials

question_text: Suppose P(z) is a formal power series in C[[z]] with order at least 2 and with (Hes P)(0) nilpotent, so that its inversion pair Q(z) is defined by the symmetric formal map F(z) = z - grad P(z) and its formal inverse G(z) = z + grad Q(z). If P is self-inverting, meaning that its inversion pair satisfies Q(z) = P(z), must every self-inverting polynomial or formal power series automatically be Hessian nilpotent?
context_brief: whether self-inverting series are automatically Hessian nilpotent

question_text: Classify all self-inverting polynomials and formal power series whose inversion pair equals the series itself, and in particular classify all such examples that are Hessian nilpotent.
context_brief: classification of Hessian nilpotent self-inverting series

question_text: Does there exist a Hessian nilpotent formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] that is not a polynomial and for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails? Equivalently, can one find a non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent formal power series over C such that the quantities Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) do not eventually vanish, or prove that no such example exists?
context_brief: possible failure of the vanishing conjecture for non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent series

question_text: Let P(z) be a formal power series in C[[z]] with order o(P(z)) >= 2. If the sequence Delta^m(P(z)^m) eventually vanishes, meaning Delta^m(P(z)^m) = 0 for all sufficiently large m, must P(z) be Hessian nilpotent?
context_brief: eventual vanishing of Delta^m P^m versus Hessian nilpotency

question_text: Let P(z) be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree d >= 2 written in the form P(z) = sum_{i=1}^k h alpha_i, z i^d with isotropic vectors alpha_i in C^n, and define the graph G(P) to have vertex set {1, 2, ..., k} with an edge between i and j exactly when <alpha_i, alpha_j> is nonzero. What necessary or sufficient conditions on this labeled graph G(P) ensure that P(z) is Hessian nilpotent?

In the same graph-theoretic setting for a homogeneous harmonic polynomial P(z) and its associated graph G(P), what necessary or sufficient conditions on the labeled graph G(P) guarantee that the Vanishing Conjecture holds for the homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomial P(z)?
context_brief: graph-theoretic criteria for the vanishing conjecture

question_text: Fix a real number epsilon > 0, let v(m) denote the number of distinct prime factors of the integer m, and call an integer n a barrier for the arithmetic function epsilon v(m) when m + epsilon v(m) <= n for every integer m < n. Are there infinitely many such barriers for at least one choice of epsilon > 0?
context_brief: barriers for epsilon times the number of distinct prime factors

question_text: Let d(m) denote the number of positive divisors of the integer m. Is the quantity max_{m<n}(m + d(m)) - n unbounded as n tends to infinity; equivalently, is it true that lim_{n->infinity} (max_{m<n}(m + d(m)) - n) = infinity?

Does the collection of known polynomial invariants of degree at most 9 cut out the algebraic variety of 4×4×4 contingency tables (pijk) over C that have tensor rank at most 4, equivalently tables admitting a decomposition pijk = ρAi·σAj·θAk + ρCi·σCj·θCk + ρGi·σGj·θGk + ρTi·σTj·θTk for i, j, k ∈ {A, C, G, T}?

How can one study the geometry and commutative algebra of graphical models with hidden random variables by constructing the associated varieties through gluing familiar secant varieties and by using representation theory to describe their defining equations?

Which projective varieties M in projective space P^n have maximum likelihood degree 1, meaning that for generic data vector (u0, u1, ..., un) the restriction of the likelihood function L(p0, p1, ..., pn) = p0^u0 · p1^u1 · ... · pn^un / (p0 + p1 + ··· + pn)^(u0 + u1 + ··· + un) to M has exactly one complex critical point after excluding singular points of M and points where L has poles or zeros?

How should the geometry of maximum likelihood estimation for algebraic statistical models be studied, and how do statistical features of a model relate to geometric properties of the corresponding projective variety?

What relationship, if any, does the maximum likelihood degree of an algebraic statistical model have to the convergence properties of numerical statistical algorithms such as iterative proportional scaling and the EM algorithm?

What is the formula, in terms of m, n, and r, for the maximum likelihood degree of the variety of m×n matrices of rank at most r? In particular, the paper identifies the first interesting unresolved case as m = n = 4 and r = 2.

For the DNA alignment example whose model M is the set of positive 4×4 matrices (pij) of rank at most 2 and whose likelihood function is L = (∏i pii)^4 · (∏i≠j pij)^2 · (∑i,j pij)^−40, is the matrix (1/40)·[[3,3,2,2],[3,3,2,2],[2,2,3,3],[2,2,3,3]] a global maximum of L?

Which sets of almost-principal minors can simultaneously vanish for a positive definite symmetric 5×5 matrix Σ, where an almost-principal minor [i ⊥⊥ j | K] is the determinant of the submatrix with row indices {i} ∪ K and column indices {j} ∪ K?

Which conditional independence models can actually be realized by multivariate Gaussian distributions on R^n? Equivalently, how can one study the geometry of Gaussian conditional independence models, that is, semi-algebraic subsets of the cone PD_n of positive definite symmetric n×n matrices defined by equations of the form [i ⊥⊥ j | K] = 0?

For n = 5, which collections of almost-principal minors are representable by some matrix in PD_5 if one requires the collection to satisfy the gaussoid axioms? In the paper’s terminology, a gaussoid is a collection of almost-principal minors satisfying the four axioms (a)-(d) after relabeling and applying Schur complements, and it is representable if it is the set of vanishing almost-principal minors of some matrix in PD_n.

What is the image of the entropy map H: PD_n → SubMod_n given by H(Σ)_I = -log det(Σ_I) for each principal minor Σ_I of a positive definite symmetric matrix, how does that image intersect the faces of the submodular cone SubMod_n, and what are the fibers of H?

Does every strict conditional independence model for discrete random variables have a Q-rational point? Here a strict conditional independence model is the intersection of the positive orthant with the constructible set of tables for which a specified collection of conditional independence statements Xi ⊥⊥ Xj | XK holds and all other such statements do not hold.
context_brief: Rational points on strict CI models

question_text: Let S be a semi-algebraic subset of R^k defined by s polynomial equalities and inequalities whose degrees are bounded by d. Is there an algorithm that computes all Betti numbers of S in time single exponential in k? More concretely, can the currently known single-exponential methods for computing only the first l Betti numbers for fixed l be extended to compute the full Betti sequence of S within a single-exponential running time in the ambient dimension?
context_brief: Single-exponential algorithms for all Betti numbers

question_text: For semi-algebraic sets, are the middle Betti numbers intrinsically harder to compute than the lowest and highest Betti numbers or the Euler-Poincare characteristic? In particular, is there a complexity-theoretic hardness result that explains the apparent algorithmic gap, or an analogue of the phenomenon from smooth projective complex varieties in which the middle Betti numbers contain essentially all the information?

Consider a semi-algebraic set in R^k defined by l quadratic inequalities. Can the number of connected components of such a set be computed by an algorithm with complexity k^O(l), or even k^O(l^2), rather than the currently best known k^(2^O(l)) type bound coming from the available all-Betti-number methods? Equivalently, is there a substantially more efficient algorithm for counting connected components in the quadratic case than the general-purpose approach currently provides?

For a general semi-algebraic set, can the exponent O(k^2) in the complexity of roadmap algorithms be improved to O(k), so that testing connectivity has asymptotically the same complexity as testing emptiness? More broadly, can one design roadmap or connecting-path algorithms whose complexity improvement would also yield sharper effective bounds on the lengths of semi-algebraic connecting paths?
context_brief: Improve roadmap complexity for general sets

question_text: Let Ω be an open connected subset of C^n, and let Γ: Ω -> C^n be a holomorphic mapping such that the maximal rank of its Jacobian DΓ is an integer k with 1 <= k <= n - 1. For each point ξ in the maximal-rank set Ω^(k) = {ξ in Ω : rank DΓ(ξ) = k}, assume the level set Γ^{-1}(Γ(ξ)) is an affine (n-k)-dimensional space through ξ, equivalently of the form ξ + κ(ξ) where κ(ξ) = ker DΓ(ξ). Under these hypotheses, when does the resulting affine fibration extend analytically from Ω^(k) to all of Ω?

Let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal. For finite-dimensional Banach space E, Banach space Y, finite-dimensional subspace F of Y', and operator T in L(E, Y''), say that the principle of A-local reflexivity (A-LRP) holds when for every epsilon > 0 there exists S in L(E, Y) such that A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T), <Sx, y'> = <y', Tx> for all (x, y') in E x F, and j_Y Sx = Tx for all x in T^{-1}(j_Y(Y)). Does every maximal Banach ideal satisfy this A-local reflexivity principle?
context_brief: A-local reflexivity for maximal Banach ideals

question_text: Let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal. Call (A, A) right-accessible when, for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, Banach space Y, operator T in L(E, Y), and epsilon > 0, there exist a finite-dimensional subspace N of Y and S in L(E, N) such that T factors through N and A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T). Is this right-accessibility property equivalent to the A-local reflexivity principle for maximal Banach ideals?

Pisier constructed an explicit maximal Banach ideal (AP, AP) that is not right-accessible. If AP-LRP denotes the A-local reflexivity principle specialized to this ideal, does Pisier's maximal Banach ideal (AP, AP) satisfy the AP-LRP?
context_brief: AP-LRP for Pisier's maximal Banach ideal

question_text: Is the product ideal (L1 o L_infinity)** o L2 normed? Equivalently, does this product of operator ideals admit an ideal norm?
context_brief: normedness of the product ideal (L1 o L_infinity)** o L2

question_text: Let (C2, C2) denote the maximal injective Banach ideal of all cotype 2 operators. Does the product ideal C2* o L_infinity have property (I), meaning that for every epsilon > 0 each finite-rank operator in C2* o L_infinity can be factorized almost isometrically with one factor having finite-dimensional range?

Corollary 2.6 states that if (B, B) is a maximal Banach ideal, X0' and Y0 are of cotype 2, B*(X0, Y0) is not a subset of L2(X0, Y0), and B o L_infinity is right-accessible and has property (I), then the B-LRP is not satisfied. Can the hypothesis that B o L_infinity is right-accessible be dropped while keeping the same conclusion?
context_brief: whether right-accessibility is needed in Corollary 2.6

question_text: Does every subgroup H of an infinite-dimensional Lie group G admit a smooth manifold structure making H an initial Lie subgroup of G? Here this means that, for every k in N union {infinity}, H is C^k-initial in G in the sense that the inclusion map lambda: H -> G is C^k and every map f: X -> H from a C^k-manifold X is C^k whenever lambda o f is C^k, and moreover the induced tangent map L(lambda): L(H) -> L(G) is injective.

If G = lim-> Gn is the direct limit of an ascending sequence G1 subseteq G2 subseteq ... of finite-dimensional real Lie groups with smooth inclusion homomorphisms, must every subgroup H of G be an initial Lie subgroup of G? Equivalently, can H be equipped with the direct-limit Lie group structure coming from Hn := Gn intersection H so that the inclusion H -> G is strongly C^k-initial for every k in N union {infinity}?
context_brief: Subgroups of direct limit Lie groups

question_text: If G = lim-> Gn is the direct limit of an ascending sequence of finite-dimensional Lie groups with smooth inclusion homomorphisms, is G a topological group with Lie algebra in the sense of Hofmann and Morris? That is, do the continuous one-parameter subgroups Hom_c(R, G) carry the vector-space and Lie-bracket operations specified by Definition 3.1, with addition given by the Trotter-type limit of (gamma(t/n) eta(t/n))^n and bracket given by the commutator limit, so that Hom_c(R, G) becomes a topological Lie algebra naturally identified with L(G)?
context_brief: Direct limits as topological groups with Lie algebra

question_text: Let M be a sigma-compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold of dimension n > 0, let p be a point of M, and let Diff_c(M)_{p,0} be the subgroup of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms fixing p whose tangent map at p has positive determinant. Is every formal diffeomorphism of R^n whose linear part has positive determinant realized as the Taylor series at p of some element of Diff_c(M)_{p,0}? Equivalently, is the Taylor-series homomorphism T_p^infinity: Diff_c(M)_{p,0} -> G^n_f(R)_0 surjective?

For the Lie superalgebra osp(1|2), can one complete the final identification over the two independent parameters c0 + d0^2 and d0^2 and thereby derive a genuine super-triangle sum rule, expressed with the supertriangle Delta_S and parity-independent 6-j^S symbols, that plays the same role for osp(1|2) that the ordinary triangle sum rule plays for su(2) and su_q(2)?

Let P_pi(lambda, kappa) denote the symmetric polynomials that appear in the closure relation for osp(1|2) iterated tensor operators, expanded in the binomial basis (c0 + d0^2)^([pi]-m) (d0^2)^m with coefficients x^pi_m(lambda, kappa). Is there a general closed formula, valid for arbitrary pseudo-degree pi, for these expansion coefficients x^pi_m(lambda, kappa) rather than only the low-order cases computed in the paper?

For the coefficients x^pi_m(lambda, kappa) defined by expanding the osp(1|2) polynomials P_pi(lambda, kappa) in powers of c0 + d0^2 and d0^2, is every coefficient x^pi_m(lambda, kappa) always an integer for all allowed lambda, kappa, pi, and m?

If Q_pi(lambda; kappa) denotes the polynomial family arising from the low-rank closure relations and P_pi(lambda, kappa) denotes the family from the high-rank closure relations, does the identity Q_pi(lambda; kappa) = P_pi(lambda, kappa - lambda + pi) hold for every admissible lambda, kappa, and pi?
context_brief: Relation between P and Q polynomials

question_text: In the attempted derivation of an osp(1|2) triangle sum rule, is it mathematically legitimate to identify coefficients over tensor operators S_c even though some of these operators are proved in the paper to be zero by construction?

Can one explicitly compute, program, and publish tables of parity-independent osp(1|2) 6-j^S symbols for low spins (for example up to spin 20) from the general formulas cited by the paper, so that low-spin calculations can test candidate triangle-sum-rule identities and reveal patterns among the expansion coefficients x?

The paper restricts the parameters c0 and d0 to be real numbers throughout the osp(1|2) analysis. If one allows c0 and/or d0 to take imaginary values instead, does the obstruction to completing the osp(1|2) triangle-sum-rule derivation change, and can such an extension lead to a valid final solution?

For a non-commutative group G, determine the invariant ν(G), the minimal number of colors required to color G so that G contains no infinite monochromatic subset A that is symmetric in the group-theoretic sense A = gA^{-1}g for some g in G. In particular, decide whether ν(F_2) is finite for the free group F_2 on two generators.
Given any infinite group G and any finite coloring of G, determine whether one must always be able to find a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G of arbitrarily large finite cardinality.
context_brief: Large finite symmetric subsets in infinite groups

question_text: For the free Abelian groups Z^n with n > 3, compute the numbers χ(Z^n) and determine the structure of their central sets, where a central set E in a group G is one such that every r-coloring of G with r < ν(G) contains an infinite monochromatic subset symmetric with respect to some point x in E.
context_brief: Central sets in free Abelian groups

question_text: For every finite group G of odd order and every integer r > 1, determine whether the invariant ms(G, r), the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset guaranteed in every r-coloring of G, is always strictly greater than 1/r^2.
context_brief: Odd-order groups and the ms invariant

question_text: Fix ε > 0 and an integer r > 1. Determine whether there exists a finite group G whose invariant ms(G, r), the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset guaranteed in every r-coloring of G, is smaller than ε.
context_brief: How small ms(G,r) can be for finite groups

question_text: Determine whether there exists a connected compact group G and an integer r such that ms(G, r), the largest guaranteed Haar measure of a monochromatic symmetric measurable subset in every measurable r-coloring of G, is strictly less than 1/r^2. In particular, compute the exact value of ms(SO(3), 2).

For integers n > 1 and r > 1, determine whether ms(S^n, I^+_2, r) = 1/r^2, where S^n is the n-dimensional sphere and I^+_2 denotes the orientation-preserving involutive isometries. Equivalently, decide whether every measurable r-coloring of S^n contains a monochromatic subset of measure at least 1/r^2 that is symmetric with respect to some line passing through the center of the sphere.

Classify the invariant ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in R^n when n > 2. In particular, compute ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in R^n with n > 2, and compute ms(T, 2) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3, equivalently ms(S_4 × I, 2).

Compute the blurred interval invariants bms([n], r), at least for small n when r = 2, where bms([n], r) is the blurred analogue of the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset in an r-coloring of the discrete interval [n].

Compute the invariant ms([0, 1], r), the largest guaranteed Lebesgue measure of a monochromatic symmetric measurable subset in every measurable r-coloring of the unit interval [0, 1], at least in the case r = 2.
context_brief: Symmetric subsets in colored unit intervals

question_text: Determine the constant c appearing in Theorem 8.1(7), namely the limit value characterized by lim_{r→∞} ms([0, 1], r) r^2 = inf_{r∈N} ms([0, 1], r) r^2 = c with 1/2 ≤ c < 5/6.
Determine how fast the sequences {ms([n], r)}_{n=1}^{∞} and {bms([n], r)}_{n=1}^{∞} converge to their common limit ms([0, 1], r).

For integers p, q, k with p >= q >= k + 1, Matousek's theorem states that there is a constant c(p,q,k) such that every k-uniform hypergraph satisfying the (p,q)-property has transversal number at most c(p,q,k). Is it possible to choose this bound with asymptotic growth c(p,q,k) = O(p^k)?

For integers p, q, k with p >= q >= k >= 2, a dense-hypergraph (p,q)-theorem gives a bounded transversal number under an explicit density assumption (for example, requiring at least x n^k edges, equivalently a fixed positive edge-density level). Can this density requirement be strictly weakened, or removed entirely, while still guaranteeing a bounded transversal number from the (p,q)-property?

For fixed integers k and p, does there exist a constant c = c(k,p) such that every k-uniform hypergraph in which every set of p edges has nonempty common intersection (that is, the (p,p)-property) has transversal number strictly less than c?

Given a p-compact group X, does there exist a sequence of finite groups G_0 -> G_1 -> G_2 -> ... and homomorphisms between them such that the homotopy colimit of the classifying spaces B G_i is homotopy equivalent to B X after p-completion? Equivalently, is every p-compact group a telescope of finite groups in the sense that hocolim_i B G_i recovers B X up to p-completion?
context_brief: p-compact groups and telescopes of finite groups

question_text: Let {B X_m}_{m in N} be a direct system of classifying spaces of p-local finite groups with maps f_m: B X_m -> B X_{m+1}, and suppose the homotopy colimit hocolim_m B X_m is homotopy equivalent to B X for a p-compact group X. Must there exist some stage m and a map g-hat: B G_p-complete -> B X_m, where B G_p-complete is the p-completed classifying space of a finite group or of a p-local finite group, such that the induced map from B G_p-complete to B X factors the given map to B X up to homotopy through that stage?
context_brief: factorization through a stage of a p-local finite group system

question_text: Fix a homological degree s and let Sq^0: Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) -> Ext_A^{s,2t}(F_2, F_2) be the squaring operation induced by the Frobenius map on the dual Steenrod algebra. If Im((Sq^0)^i) denotes the image of the i-fold iterate on Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2), does there exist a number r = r(s) such that for every i >= r the map (Sq^0)^{i-r}: Im((Sq^0)^r) -> Im((Sq^0)^i) is an isomorphism? Equivalently, for fixed s, is every finite Sq^0-family in Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2) bounded in length by some r(s)?
context_brief: eventual periodicity of Sq^0 on Ext over the Steenrod algebra

question_text: For the algebraic transfer tau_{s,t}: Hom_A^{t-s}(H_*((Z/2)^s; F_2), F_2)^{GL_s(Z/2)} -> Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2), prove or disprove the vanishing conjecture that Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) = 0 whenever alpha(t) > s, where alpha(t) is the number of 1s in the binary expansion of t.
context_brief: vanishing line for Ext over the Steenrod algebra

question_text: Can the bigraded algebraic transfer tau^{*,*} be realized as the edge homomorphism of a spectral sequence in a way that gives a sensible measure of how far tau^{*,*} is from being an isomorphism of bigraded algebras?
context_brief: spectral sequence interpretation of the algebraic transfer

question_text: Fix s. Is there a calculation of Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) that is uniform for all sufficiently large primes p? In other words, for fixed Adams filtration s, does the structure of Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) eventually become independent of p for large enough p, analogous to the stated behavior of Ext_A^{1,*}(F_p, F_p) for p > 2?
context_brief: large-prime uniformity of Ext over the Steenrod algebra

question_text: For each s, is the algebraic transfer Tr_s: F_2 tensor_{GL_s} P H_*(B V_s) -> Ext_A^{s,s+*}(F_2, F_2) injective? Equivalently, does Singer's open conjecture hold that Tr_s is a monomorphism for every s?
context_brief: Singer conjecture on injectivity of the algebraic transfer

question_text: Let p be a prime, let P_* be the polynomial part of the dual Steenrod algebra with P_* congruent to F_p[xi_1, xi_2, xi_3, ...], let P be its dual Hopf algebra, and consider Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p). The p-th power map on P_* induces an endomorphism P^0: Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p) -> Ext_P^{s,pt}(F_p, F_p). For fixed s > 0, is every element z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p) eventually sent to a nilpotent element by some iterate of P^0; equivalently, whenever z lies in the preimage (P^0)^-1 Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), must z be nilpotent?
context_brief: nilpotence under the P^0 endomorphism on Ext over P

question_text: In the setting of Conjecture 4.1, can one always choose the iterate n to be 1? That is, for every z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), is P^0 z already nilpotent after a single application of P^0?

Let p = 2 and G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2). Let A_{n,n} be the maximal elementary 2-subgroup consisting of block upper triangular matrices with identity blocks on the diagonal, so that H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2) = F_2[x_{i,j} | 1 <= i,j <= n], and let det_n = det(x_{i,j}) be the degree-n class in the invariants H^n(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}. If res: H^*(G_{2n}; F_2) -> H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n} is the restriction homomorphism, is det_n in the image of res?
context_brief: restriction image for determinant classes in group cohomology

question_text: Let p = 2 and G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2). Is the degree-n homology group H_n(G_{2n}; F_2) one-dimensional over F_2 and generated by the determinant class det_n arising from the maximal elementary 2-subgroup A_{n,n}?
context_brief: generation of H_n(GL_{2n}(F_2); F_2) by det_n

question_text: Let E be the extraspecial p-group p^(1+2)_+ of order p^3 and exponent p for an odd prime p. A graph in Theorem 6.2 of the cited companion paper describes the stable splitting of B G for all p-local finite groups G having Sylow p-subgroup E when p = 3. Determine the analogous stable-splitting graph for p = 7, using Theorem 9.4 from the same paper as a partial input.
context_brief: stable splitting graph for p-local finite groups over an extraspecial p-group

question_text: In a lattice-ordered group (an "l-group"), if the group is l-simple, must every convex normal subgroup be trivial?
context_brief: l-simple l-groups and convex normal subgroups

question_text: For a free lattice-ordered group, can its lattice order be extended to a total order that is weakly abelian?
context_brief: extensions of orders on free l-groups

question_text: Is every Engel lattice-ordered group residually ordered (also called o-approximable or representable)?
context_brief: Engel condition vs residual orderability in l-groups

question_text: Is the conjugacy problem solvable for nilpotent finitely presented lattice-ordered groups?
context_brief: algorithmic problems in finitely presented l-groups

question_text: Let F_n denote the free lattice-ordered group on n generators with n not equal to 1. Is F_n Hopfian, i.e., not l-isomorphic to any proper quotient of itself?
If two finitely presented abelian lattice-ordered groups satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences, must those two groups be isomorphic?
An R* group is a group in which a non-empty product of conjugates of a non-identity element is never the identity. Must every R* group be right orderable?
Does every right-orderable n-Engel group admit a Conrad right order?
context_brief: Engel right-orderable groups and Conrad orders

question_text: Is the group ring of every right-orderable group embeddable in a skew field?
Does there exist a finitely generated simple right-orderable group?
Does there exist a universal countable right-orderable group?
Does there exist a universal countable totally orderable group?
context_brief: universal objects in totally orderable groups

question_text: Is every right-orderable n-Engel group nilpotent?
Is every torsion-free n-Engel group orderable?
An O* group is one in which every partial order extends to a total order making the group a totally ordered group. Can every orderable group be embedded in an O* group?
Is there a simple O* group?
Is every orderable abelian-by-nilpotent group an O* group?
For each positive integer k, construct an orderable group G_k that has exactly 2k total orders; in particular, the existence of groups with exactly 10 and exactly 18 total orders is still open.
Is there a finitely presented orderable group with insoluble word problem?
context_brief: word problem in finitely presented orderable groups

question_text: Does there exist a totally ordered group in which all strictly positive elements are conjugate?
Let G be an abelian-by-nilpotent ordered group. (i) Is G order-embeddable in a divisible ordered group? (ii) If G is also nilpotent-by-abelian, is G order-embeddable in a divisible ordered group?
Solved problem record: if V is a variety of residually ordered l-groups and satisfies no group laws, must V contain a free linearly ordered group, and is V = R?
Solved problem record: is there a group with exactly a countable infinity of right orders?
Solved problem record: does there exist a soluble orderable group G with G/[G, G] periodic?
context_brief: solved problem from totally ordered section

question_text: Does there exist a maximal curve over the finite field F_{27^2} whose Frobenius dimension is 3 and whose Frobenius linear series has D-order sequence (0, 1, 3, 27)? Equivalently, can case (A) occur for a maximal curve with Frobenius dimension 3, namely the case in which the second generic D-order satisfies epsilon_2 = 3?

Does there exist a maximal curve X over a finite field F_{q^2} whose Frobenius dimension is 3, whose Frobenius linear series has second generic D-order epsilon_2 = 2, and which has an F_{q^2}-rational point P with second (D,P)-order j_2(P) = 3?

Does there exist a maximal curve X over a finite field F_{q^2} whose Frobenius dimension is 3, whose Frobenius linear series has second generic D-order epsilon_2 = 2, and which has an F_{q^2}-rational point P such that the second (D,P)-order satisfies j_2(P) = q + 1 - floor((2/3)(q + 1))?

Let q be odd with q congruent to 2 modulo 3. Let K = F_{q^2}, let F = K(x, y) be the function field defined by y^{(q+1)/3} + x^{(q+1)/3} + 1 = 0, choose w in F_{q^2} such that w^{(q+1)/3} = 3, let z satisfy z^3 = wxy, and set Fbar = F(z). The paper proves that Fbar is an F_{q^2}-maximal function field of genus (q^2 - q + 4)/6 and Frobenius dimension 3. Is Fbar isomorphic to the F_{q^2}-maximal function fields of genus (q^2 - q + 4)/6 and Frobenius dimension 3 constructed earlier in reference [14]?

Let K_0, K_1, K_2, K_3, S, M, and G be the classes of groups considered in the paper, and recall that Theorem 1.1 proves the following statement whenever A and B are members of this collection with B properly contained in A and A containing K_3: there is no algorithm that decides, given a finite presentation of a group known to lie in A, whether that group lies in B. Does the same undecidability statement remain true in the case A = K_2?

Is the isomorphism problem for 2-knot groups algorithmically unsolvable? In other words, is there no algorithm that takes finite presentations of two groups known to belong to K_2, the class of groups of 2-knots, and always decides whether the two groups are isomorphic?

Does there exist a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem? Here K_2 is the class of groups of 2-knots, so the question asks whether some group of a 2-knot has no algorithm deciding, for an arbitrary word in its generators, whether that word represents the identity element.

Does every finitely presented group embed in a 2-knot group? That is, for each finitely presented group G, must there exist a group in K_2, the class of groups of 2-knots, that contains an isomorphic copy of G as a subgroup?

In the setting of Theorem 5.1, let C be a class of infinite sequences of abelian groups, closed under isomorphism, such that there exist finitely presented groups G_1 and G_2 with the same first homology H_1(G_1) isomorphic to H_1(G_2), with H_*(G_1) in C and H_*(G_2) not in C. Theorem 5.1 proves that the set of finite presentations P for which the integral homology sequence H_*(P) belongs to C is not recursive. Under what additional hypotheses on C can this conclusion be strengthened by replacing 'not recursive' with 'not recursively enumerable'?
If g is a non-negative integer, is there an algorithm to decide whether or not a given locally flat PL-embedded surface of genus g in S^4 is unknotted?
context_brief: Unknot recognition for surfaces in S4

question_text: Consider the multi-server first-come-first-served queue G/G/m with interarrival times {(t_n)} and service times {(sigma_n)} such that the two-dimensional sequence {(sigma_n, t_n)} is stationary ergodic, the stability condition E sigma_1 < m E t_1 holds, and the Kiefer-Wolfowitz workload vector starts from the zero initial value. Is it true that, under these assumptions alone and without any further mixing or regenerative condition, the distribution of the workload vector converges in total variation to a stationary distribution as n tends to infinity?
context_brief: TV convergence in stationary ergodic G/G/m FCFS

question_text: Let D be the stationary waiting time in an i.i.d. G/G/m first-come-first-served queue where the service-time sequence {(sigma_n)} and interarrival-time sequence {(t_n)} are independent, identically distributed, and satisfy rho := E sigma_1 / E t_1 < m. When rho is an integer, what conditions are necessary and sufficient for the power moment E D^gamma to be finite?
context_brief: Moments of stationary delay at integer load

question_text: In the two-server queue case m = 2 with stationary waiting time D, when the load satisfies rho = 1 and the service-time distribution is subexponential (for example regularly varying), what is the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large?
context_brief: Tail asymptotics for two-server queue at rho=1

question_text: In the two-server queue case m = 2 with stationary waiting time D, when the load satisfies rho in (1, 2) and the service-time distribution is heavy-tailed but has all power moments finite, for example P(sigma_1 > x) = exp(-x^beta) for some beta in (0, 1), what is the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large?
context_brief: Tail asymptotics for two-server queue with finite moments

question_text: For the two-server queue regimes just described, namely the case rho = 1 with a subexponential service-time distribution and the case rho in (1, 2) with a heavy-tailed service-time distribution having all power moments finite, what are the typical sample paths that lead to large values of the stationary waiting time D?
context_brief: Typical paths producing large stationary delays

question_text: Consider a multi-server queue, for example a two-server queue, with stationary ergodic input {(t_n, sigma_n)} and the join-the-shortest-queue discipline, meaning each arriving customer immediately joins the shortest of the individual queues. Assuming only the obvious stability condition and no extra hypotheses, how many stationary regimes can this model have?
context_brief: Number of stationary regimes for join-the-shortest-queue

question_text: For the same join-the-shortest-queue model with stationary ergodic input, what are the minimal assumptions that guarantee uniqueness of the stationary regime?

For the join-the-shortest-queue model with stationary ergodic input and only the obvious stability condition, under what conditions, if any, do the queue-length or workload distributions converge weakly or in total variation to stationarity?

A single server moves on a circle. Particles arrive according to a Poisson process of rate lambda and are placed uniformly on the circle. Serving a particle takes one unit of time, and after each service the server moves at positive finite constant speed to the nearest waiting particle, ignoring new arrivals while moving. Is this greedy-server model stable for every lambda < 1?
context_brief: Stability of a greedy server on a circle

question_text: On a circle, black particles arrive according to a Poisson stream of rate lambda and remain there, while white particles arrive according to an independent Poisson stream of rate 1 and immediately disappear after, if possible, deleting the nearest black particle within distance epsilon of their arrival location. Is this model stable whenever lambda < 1, independently of the circle length and of epsilon?
context_brief: Stability of black-white particle circle model

question_text: Consider the following queueing system. There are three servers and a Poisson arrival process of rate lambda. Each arrival becomes class 1, 2, or 3 with probability 1/3. Class 1 customers may be served by servers 1 and 2, class 2 customers by servers 2 and 3, and class 3 customers by servers 3 and 1. Upon arrival, a customer chooses the accessible server with the shorter workload. If served by its left server, the service time has distribution F_l; if served by its right server, the service time has distribution F_r. In this model, can stability depend on both the initial state and the full service-time distributions F_l and F_r rather than only on coarse summary parameters?

Consider an open polling system with two stations and two heterogeneous servers. Each station has Poisson input of rate 1. For i, j in {1, 2}, service times of server j at station i are i.i.d. exponential with rate mu_i^(j). Both servers use the exhaustive service policy, switch-over times are zero, and a server becomes passive if neither station has a free customer. In the positive four-dimensional parameter cube for {(mu_i^(j))}, does the subset of parameter values for which the system is null recurrent have positive Lebesgue measure?
context_brief: Positive-measure null recurrence in polling system

question_text: Consider a slotted multi-access channel in which packets have unit service time, arrivals during each slot are Poisson with parameter lambda, W_n is the number of packets in the system at the beginning of slot n, and each packet attempts transmission in slot n with probability p_n. A transmission succeeds if exactly one packet transmits, collides if two or more transmit, and is empty if none transmits. Suppose p_{n+1} may depend only on p_n and on the binary information of whether slot n contained a successful transmission. Does there exist a protocol of this form for which the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) is positive recurrent for some lambda > 0?

Let F and G be Keller maps, meaning polynomial endomorphisms such that det(Jac(F)) = det(Jac(G)) = 1. If the restrictions of F and G agree on the subset defined by xy = 0, must F and G be equal everywhere?
context_brief: Keller maps determined by agreement on xy=0

question_text: Let k be a field of characteristic zero. Is the group GAn(k) generated by tame automorphisms together with finitely many one-parameter subgroups of automorphisms?

Find an intrinsic algebraic invariant of normal finitely generated k-algebras that captures the algebraic rigidity of the tubular neighborhood of infinity and can be viewed as adding a continuous dimension to the homotopy type at infinity. The invariant should, in a straightforward way, distinguish all isomorphism classes of the algebras k[x, y, z]/(x^n z - y^2 - f(x)y).
Classify normal affine equivariant embeddings of connected solvable linear algebraic groups for which all isotropy groups are semisimple.

Let R = C[a, b]. Let D : R[x, y, z] -> R[x, y, z] be a triangular locally nilpotent R-derivation, meaning that D(x) belongs to R, D(y) belongs to R[x], and D(z) belongs to R[x, y]. If D has a slice, does it follow that ker(D) = R[2]?
context_brief: Kernels of triangular locally nilpotent derivations

question_text: Let k be a field and let n > 2. Is the group Aff_n(k) a maximal subgroup of the tame transformation group TA_n(k)?
context_brief: Maximality of affine subgroup inside tame group

question_text: For each i, let Gi be the subgroup of GAn(k) that stabilizes k ⊕ kx1 ⊕ ... ⊕ kxi, so that Gn = Aff_n(k), G2 = Aff_2(k) when n = 2, and G1 is the set of triangular automorphisms. Is GAn(k) generated by G1, ..., Gn? If so, is the group described in the source as an amalgamated product of the Gi along pairwise intersections?
context_brief: Generation and amalgam structure from stabilizer subgroups

question_text: Using the same subgroups Gi from the previous problem, define Hi = Gi cap TAn(k). Is TAn(k) generated by H1, ..., Hn? If so, is TAn(k) the amalgamated product of the Hi along pairwise intersections?

Let x = (x1, x2, ..., xn) and let Cn = [0, 1]^n be the n-cube in R^n. Suppose f(x) belongs to C[x] and every moment integral over the cube vanishes, meaning that integral over Cn of f(x)^m dx equals 0 for every integer m >= 1. Does this force f to be the zero polynomial?
context_brief: Vanishing moments on the unit cube

question_text: Let R be a commutative ring, let A be a commutative R-algebra, and call an R-subspace M of A a Mathieu subspace if for any a, b in A, whenever a^m belongs to M for all sufficiently large m, one also has a^m b in M for all sufficiently large m. Let M = {f in C[x] | integral over Cn of f(x) dx = 0}. Is M a Mathieu subspace of the polynomial algebra C[x]?
Let A be a finitely generated k-algebra over a field k. If M1 and M2 are Mathieu subspaces of A, must their sum M1 + M2 also be a Mathieu subspace of A?
context_brief: Closure of Mathieu subspaces under addition

question_text: Let A and B be rings. Suppose that A tensor B is Fn, where Fn is a free associative algebra of rank n. Does it follow that A and B are both free associative algebras?
context_brief: Tensor factors of a free associative algebra

question_text: For the full matrix algebra M_n, does there exist an abelian group Γ and a Γ-grading under which M_n becomes Γ-commutative, meaning that for homogeneous elements a and b in the graded algebra, the multiplication satisfies the graded-commutativity rule described in Definition 2.1?

Develop and investigate the notion of the spectrum of a Γ-commutative algebra, where a Γ-commutative algebra is an algebra graded by an abelian group Γ such that, for homogeneous elements, multiplication satisfies the graded-commutativity condition from Definition 2.1.

For the incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid model on a bounded domain Ω with motion equation ∂v/∂t + Σ_i v_i ∂v/∂x_i − Div σ + ∇p = f, incompressibility condition div v = 0, no-slip boundary condition v|∂Ω = 0, and constitutive law σ + λ1 Dσ/Dt = 2η(E + λ2 DE/Dt) where E is the strain-rate tensor and D/Dt is an objective derivative, does the initial-boundary value problem admit global-in-time strong solutions for arbitrary coefficients, external force, and initial data in every spatial dimension n ≥ 2?
context_brief: Global strong solvability for the Jeffreys model.

question_text: For the same incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid model with div v = 0, v|∂Ω = 0, motion equation ∂v/∂t + Σ_i v_i ∂v/∂x_i − Div σ + ∇p = f, and constitutive law σ + λ1 Dσ/Dt = 2η(E + λ2 DE/Dt), are all weak solutions regular without placing restrictions on the coefficients, external force, or initial data, in dimensions n ≥ 2?

For the same incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid model with div v = 0, v|∂Ω = 0, motion equation ∂v/∂t + Σ_i v_i ∂v/∂x_i − Div σ + ∇p = f, and constitutive law σ + λ1 Dσ/Dt = 2η(E + λ2 DE/Dt), are weak solutions unique without restrictions on the coefficients, external force, or initial data, in dimensions n ≥ 2?

For the same incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid problem, can one estimate the Hausdorff dimension of the trajectory attractor and of the global attractor without imposing restrictions on the coefficients, external force, or initial data, in dimensions n ≥ 2?

For the incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid model with motion equation ∂v/∂t + Σ_i v_i ∂v/∂x_i − Div σ + ∇p = f, incompressibility div v = 0, no-slip boundary condition v|∂Ω = 0, and constitutive law σ + λ1 Dσ/Dt = 2η(E + λ2 DE/Dt), do there exist any generalized solutions of the stationary boundary-value problem without restrictions on the coefficients or external force?

For the same incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid model, do there exist any generalized global-in-time solutions of the evolutionary initial-boundary value problem without restrictions on the coefficients, external force, or initial data?
For the same incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid model, do there exist time-periodic solutions without restrictions on the coefficients, external force, or initial data?

In the incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid model with constitutive law σ + λ1 Dσ/Dt = 2η(E + λ2 DE/Dt), when the objective derivative is the Jaumann or corotational derivative D0T/Dt = dT/dt + TW − WT, is the claimed global weak-solvability result in reference [53] actually correct? In particular, can one rigorously justify the step that requires the identity η|_{t=0} = 0 in the limit passage for the non-Newtonian stress tensors?
context_brief: Validity of the corotational-case result in [53].

question_text: If global-in-time solutions of the evolutionary incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid problem can be constructed, can one then build generalized attractors and/or inertial manifolds for that problem?

Consider the normal linear regression prediction problem with unknown variance, under the special design assumption (AS1) used in the paper: m >= k >= 3, n = mN for a positive integer N, and the design matrix satisfies X = 1_N \otimes X~ = (X~', ..., X~')'. Under alpha-divergence loss D_alpha with -1 < alpha < 1, does the predictive density based on the same shrinkage prior pi_S,1(beta, sigma^2) = (beta' X~' X~ beta)^(1-k/2) (sigma^2)^(-2) improve on the best invariant predictive density, namely the generalized Bayes predictive density based on the right invariant prior pi_I,1(beta, sigma^2) = (sigma^2)^(-1)?
context_brief: Open dominance question under general alpha-divergence

question_text: Under D_1 loss for predictive density estimation in the normal linear regression model with unknown variance, and in the low-dimensional cases k = 1 or k = 2, can one construct Bayesian predictive densities that improve on the best invariant predictive density, even though improved non-Bayesian predictive densities are already known to exist in this setting?

For the normal linear regression prediction problem with unknown variance, when the number of regression coefficients is k = 1 or k = 2 and the loss is alpha-divergence D_alpha with -1 <= alpha < 1, does the best invariant predictive density remain inadmissible? If it does, which Bayesian predictive density or class of Bayesian predictive densities improves upon it?
Find new examples of hyperkahler manifolds.

Let X and X' be hyperkahler manifolds of the same dimension. If there is a Hodge isometry lambda: H^2(X, Z) -> H^2(X', Z), determine what geometric relationship between X and X' follows, and whether one can force X and X' to be isomorphic by requiring lambda to preserve additional structure beyond the Hodge structure itself.

For a hyperkahler manifold X, determine which integral quadratic forms can occur as the Beauville-Bogomolov form q on H^2(X, Z), whether q must always be even, and which values can occur for the Fujiki constant f_X defined by the relation integral_X alpha^(2r) = f_X q(alpha)^r in dimension 2r.
Determine whether there are only finitely many hyperkahler manifolds, up to deformation, in each dimension.

For a hyperkahler fourfold X, determine whether additional values of the second Betti number b2 can be excluded beyond the currently known cases, especially whether b2 = 3 can occur at all; and if b2 = 23, determine whether X must be deformation equivalent to the Hilbert square S^[2] of a K3 surface.

Let X be a hyperkahler manifold of dimension 2r. If L is a nontrivial nef line bundle on X with Beauville-Bogomolov square q(L) = 0, determine whether there must exist a Lagrangian fibration f: X -> P^r such that L = f^* O_{P^r}(k) for some integer k >= 1. More generally, determine whether X is birational to a hyperkahler manifold X' admitting a Lagrangian fibration X' -> P^r exactly when X carries a nontrivial line bundle L with q(L) = 0.
Does every hyperkahler manifold admit a deformation that carries a Lagrangian fibration?

Let X be a hyperkahler manifold and let T subset X be a Lagrangian submanifold that is a complex torus. Must T occur as a fibre of a Lagrangian fibration X -> P^r, or at least of a birational model of such a fibration?

For a polarized K3 surface S of genus g, describe the general projective deformation of S[2], for some choice of polarization on S[2], or at least find more examples of locally complete projective families. Ask the same question for S[r] with r >= 3.

Let X be a projective hyperkahler manifold. If z in CH(X) is a Chow class that is a polynomial in divisor classes D1, ..., Dk from Pic(X) and in the Chern classes c_i(X), and if the cohomology class of z vanishes in H^*(X, Z), must z already vanish in the Chow ring?

Let X be a Fano complex manifold with a holomorphic Poisson structure, and for even s let X_{<=s} be the union of the loci X_k where the Poisson structure has rank k for k <= s. Must X_{<=s} contain a component of dimension greater than s?

Let X be a compact complex manifold with a holomorphic Poisson structure. If X_s, the locus where the Poisson structure has rank s, is non-empty, must it contain a component of dimension greater than s?

Classify projective contact manifolds: is every projective contact manifold either the projectivized cotangent bundle P(T^*M) of a compact complex manifold M or the closed contact Fano orbit X_g associated with a simple complex Lie algebra g?
Is every contact Fano manifold homogeneous?
Are the only compact quaternion-Kahler manifolds with positive scalar curvature homogeneous?

Let a polygon with at least four sides be circumscribed to a circle, and let D consist of its diagonals together with the lines joining the points of contact of two non-adjacent sides. The paper proves that D contains at least three concurrent lines. Determine conditions under which more than three of these lines are concurrent.

For a polygon circumscribed to a circle, with D defined as the set of diagonals and the lines joining the points of contact of two non-adjacent sides, determine the maximum possible number of concurrent lines in D and characterize the configurations in which this maximum is attained.

Replace the circle in the circumscribed-polygon concurrency problem by an ellipse, and consider a polygon all of whose sides are tangent to that ellipse. How many concurrent lines can occur among the polygon's diagonals and the lines connecting the contact points of two non-adjacent sides?

Generalize the following triangle identity from cevians to polygons: if cevians AA1, BB1, and CC1 in triangle ABC intersect at P, then (|PA|/|PA1|) (|PB|/|PB1|) (|PC|/|PC1|) = (|AB| |BC| |CA|) / (|A1B| |B1C| |C1A|). Find the corresponding polygon statement and prove it.
context_brief: Polygon generalization of a cevian product identity

question_text: Let A1A2...Am be a polygon and let P be a point inside it. Drop perpendiculars from P to each side AiAi+1, and let Ai' be the foot of the perpendicular on AiAi+1. The polygon A1'A2'...Am' is the pedal polygon of P. Determine what properties this pedal polygon must satisfy.

Let A1A2...An be a polyhedron and let P be a point inside it. From P draw perpendiculars to each edge AiAj, and let Aij' be the foot of the perpendicular on the edge AiAj. Study the resulting edge pedal polyhedron and determine its geometric properties.

Let A1A2...An be a polyhedron and let P be a point inside it. From P draw perpendiculars to each face Fi, and let Ai' be the foot of the perpendicular on Fi. The resulting polyhedron A1'A2'...Ap', where p is the number of faces, is a face pedal polyhedron. Determine what properties this face pedal polyhedron has.

Generalize the circle-locus theorem of Problem 9 to 3D. Let two spheres intersect in a circle C, let a line through a point of C meet the two sphere surfaces again at M1 and M2, and let M divide M1M2 in the ratio k. Determine the full geometric locus of M, especially in the case where the line M1M2 and the line joining the sphere centers are not coplanar.

Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed subset of U. The Bregman distance induced by f is D(x, y) = f(x) - f(y) - <grad f(y), x - y> for y in U. The set C is called left D-Chebyshev when, for every y in U, the left nearest-points map P_left,C(y) = {x in C | D(x, y) = inf_{z in C} D(z, y)} is a singleton. It is known that if f is supercoercive and C is left D-Chebyshev, then C is convex. Is the supercoercivity assumption actually necessary for that convexity conclusion?
context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity for left D-Chebyshev convexity

question_text: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function with U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed subset of U. The set C is called right D-Chebyshev when, for every x in U, the right nearest-points map P_right,C(x) = {y in C | D(x, y) = inf_{z in C} D(x, z)} is a singleton. Fact 3.2 states that if dom f = X, C* = grad f(C) is contained in U* = int dom f*, and C is right D-Chebyshev, then C* is convex. Are the assumptions that f have full domain and that C* be contained in U* both genuinely necessary for that conclusion?
context_brief: Necessity of the assumptions in Fact 3.2

question_text: Does there exist a Legendre function f: R^n -> [-infinity, +infinity] with full domain X = R^n such that f is not quadratic, yet every nonempty closed convex subset of X is right D-Chebyshev with respect to the Bregman distance induced by f? Equivalently, can there be a nonquadratic full-domain Legendre function whose gradient map grad f is nonaffine but still preserves convexity in the strong sense needed for every nonempty closed convex subset of X to have a unique right Bregman nearest point from each x in U?
context_brief: Existence of nonquadratic full-domain right D-Chebyshev geometry

question_text: Let X = R^n_{++} be the strictly positive orthant, and let f be the negative entropy Legendre function from Example 1.1(ii). For this Bregman distance, closed convex sets are known to be right D-Chebyshev, but there are also nonconvex examples that are right D-Chebyshev. Is it possible to characterize exactly which subsets of the strictly positive orthant are right D-Chebyshev for the negative-entropy Bregman distance?
context_brief: Characterizing right D-Chebyshev sets for negative entropy

question_text: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed subset of U. Suppose f is twice continuously differentiable and the Hessian grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. Fact 3.5 says that if f is also supercoercive, then the left nearest-point map P_left,C is single-valued almost everywhere and generically on U. Is that extra supercoercivity assumption really essential for the almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness conclusion?
context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity in near-Chebyshev single-valuedness

question_text: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a bounded nonempty closed subset of U. Suppose f is twice continuously differentiable and the Hessian grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. Fact 4.4 says that if f is also supercoercive, then the left farthest-point map Q_left,C is single-valued almost everywhere and generically on U. Is supercoercivity actually necessary for that almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness result?
context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity for near-Klee single-valuedness

question_text: In the theory of Chebyshev functions and Klee functions for a proper lower semicontinuous function g: X -> [-infinity, +infinity], the paper uses the halved Euclidean distance q = (1/2)||.||^2 through the proximal map P_lambda g and the farthest map Q_mu g. What are the corresponding characterizations when the Euclidean discrepancy is replaced by a Bregman distance generated by a Legendre function f? In particular, how should one characterize the admissible generator f and the analogue of the Chebyshev point in that Bregman setting?
context_brief: Bregman analogues of Chebyshev and Klee functions

question_text: How do the results on Chebyshev functions and Klee functions extend beyond finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces to Hilbert spaces, and more generally to Banach spaces? This asks for analogues of the single-valuedness, characterization, and Chebyshev-point results developed for functions in X = R^n under the Euclidean framework.
context_brief: Extending Chebyshev and Klee function results to Hilbert and Banach spaces

question_text: Let X be a nonsingular projective variety over C, let M_g(X, beta) be the moduli space of stable maps to X in curve class beta, let M_g be the moduli space of genus-g stable curves, and let pi: M_g(X, beta) -> M_g be the forgetful morphism. The stable-map space has a virtual fundamental class [M_g(X, beta)]^vir from deformation theory. Is the pushforward class pi_*([M_g(X, beta)]^vir) always contained in the tautological subring of H_*(M_g)?

In the same setting where X is a nonsingular projective variety over C, M_g(X, beta) is the moduli space of stable maps, pi: M_g(X, beta) -> M_g is the forgetful morphism, and [M_g(X, beta)]^vir is the virtual class, for which targets X and curve classes beta does the Chow-theoretic pushforward pi_*([M_g(X, beta)]^vir) lie in the tautological subring of A_*(M_g)?
For the Gromov-Witten theory of a target variety X, prove that the full set of Virasoro constraints holds when X is an Enriques surface.

For a nonsingular projective 3-fold X, establish the conjectural equivalence between Gromov-Witten curve counting and Donaldson-Thomas curve counting, i.e., prove the GW/DT correspondence for 3-folds.
Define Donaldson-Thomas invariants for varieties of dimension greater than 3 by providing a mathematically sound framework that extends the 3-fold theory.
Let M_{2n}^{K3} denote the moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces (S, L) with L^2 = 2n. What should be the correct analogue of the tautological ring in the cycle theory of M_{2n}^{K3}?
For the moduli space M_{2n}^{K3} of polarized K3 surfaces of degree 2n, do the Noether-Lefschetz divisor classes generate the rational Picard group, i.e., do they span Pic(M_{2n}^{K3}) tensor Q?
For K3 surfaces, prove the Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture in every genus and for all curve classes.
Develop effective mathematical techniques for computing higher-genus Gromov-Witten invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds.

For each natural number n, let R_n^infty be the maximum Banach-Mazur distance between an n-dimensional Banach space X and l_infty^n. Determine the asymptotic behavior of R_n^infty as n tends to infinity.

Fix 0 < delta <= 1. A normalized basic sequence is delta-near unconditional with constant K when its basis constant is at most K and, whenever coefficients a_0,...,a_k lie in [-1,1], every projection onto indices i with delta <= |a_i| <= 1 has norm at most K times the norm of the full linear combination. Let K(delta) be the infimum of the constants K such that every normalized weakly null sequence has a delta-near unconditional subsequence with constant K. Does there exist M > 1 such that K(delta) <= M for every 0 < delta <= 1?

A normalized basic sequence (x_n) is called a Rosenthal basis when every normalized block sequence of (x_n) has a subsequence equivalent to (x_n). Must every Rosenthal basis be equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?

Let X be a reflexive Banach space such that every normalized weakly null sequence in X generates, up to equivalence, the same spreading model. Is that unique spreading model necessarily equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?

Let X be a reflexive Banach space for which the set of equivalence classes of spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences in X is countable. Must X contain a normalized weakly null sequence that generates a spreading model equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?

Suppose X has a normalized Schauder basis (x_n) such that every normalized block sequence of (x_n) spans a subspace isomorphic to X. Must X itself be isomorphic to c_0 or to l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?
If X is a separable non-Hilbertian Banach space, must there exist a sequence (X_n) of subspaces of X that are pairwise non-isomorphic?
Let X be a separable Banach space that fails to have type 2 - epsilon, or fails to have co-type 2 + epsilon, for some epsilon > 0. Must X contain continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces?
Is every complemented subspace of C[0,1] isomorphic to C(K) for some closed subset K of [0,1]?

Let T: C[0,1] -> C[0,1] be a bounded linear operator, and let X be a separable Banach space that does not contain a copy of c_0. Assume T fixes a copy of X, meaning that there is a subspace of C[0,1] isomorphic to X on which T acts as an isomorphic embedding. Must T then fix a copy of C[0,1]? Equivalently, must the dual operator T^* have non-separable range?
A distortable Banach space is called boundedly distortable when it is lambda-distortable for some lambda > 1 but not for every lambda > 1. Does there exist a boundedly distortable Banach space?
Is Tsirelson's space T, or its dual, boundedly distortable rather than arbitrarily distortable?

Give a purely combinatorial proof that every real-valued uniformly continuous map on the unit sphere of c_0 is oscillation stable, where oscillation stable means that for every epsilon > 0 there is an infinite-dimensional subspace Y such that the oscillation of the map on the unit sphere of Y is at most epsilon, and do so without using ultrafilters.
Let X be a separable Banach space with the property that every separable Banach space is Lipschitz isomorphic to a subset of X. Must X contain a copy of c_0?
Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have an infinite-dimensional quotient with a Schauder basis?
Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a non-trivial infinite-dimensional separable quotient?

Given an infinite-dimensional Banach space X, what is the greatest possible order type of a Schauder basis carried by a quotient of X? In particular, must every non-separable Banach space have an uncountable biorthogonal system?
context_brief: long Schauder bases and biorthogonal systems

question_text: Assume the P-ideal dichotomy, namely that for every P-ideal I of countable subsets of some index set S either there is an uncountable T subset of S whose countable subsets all belong to I, or S can be decomposed into countably many pieces with no infinite subset in I. Under that assumption, are the following equivalent: (1) every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system, and (2) b = aleph_2?

A support set in a Banach space X is a nonempty convex set C such that every point x of C is a support point, meaning there is a functional f on X with f(x) equal to the infimum of f over C and strictly less than the supremum of f over C. Which Banach spaces admit support sets, and do all non-separable Banach spaces have support sets?
Does every Banach space of density greater than aleph_1 have a support set?

Does every Banach space X of density greater than the continuum c have an infinite unconditional basic sequence? If not in full generality, does adding hypotheses such as reflexivity change the answer?

For a given prime p, does there exist a field F and an F-division algebra of degree p that is not cyclic? Equivalently, can one construct a prime-degree division algebra whose maximal Galois subfield is not cyclic over its center?

If an F-division algebra has prime period, must it be a crossed product? In other words, for each prime p, is every central division algebra whose Brauer class has order p necessarily obtained from a Galois crossed-product construction?
If F has characteristic p, must every p-algebra of degree p^2 be a crossed product? Here a p-algebra means a central simple algebra whose period is a power of p.
If a field F has cohomological dimension at most 2, is every central simple F-algebra a crossed product?

For an F-division algebra A of degree n, what is the smallest finite group that can occur as the Galois group of the Galois closure of a maximal subfield of A? In particular, does every degree-n division algebra have a separable maximal subfield whose Galois closure has Galois group the alternating group A_n?
context_brief: Minimal splitting groups from maximal subfields

question_text: Is every division algebra split by an abelian Galois extension of its center, and for specific ground fields can one bound the degree of such an abelian splitting field?

For semidirect products G = C_p semidirect C_m with m prime to p, when does every G-crossed product over F descend to a crossed product for a smaller or more abelian group G'? In particular, is every division algebra of prime degree p that is split by C_p semidirect C_m necessarily cyclic, and are all quasi-symbols cyclic?
For a field F and positive integer n, is the n-torsion subgroup nBr(F) generated by Brauer classes of cyclic algebras of degree dividing n?
When char F is not 7 and F does not contain a primitive seventh root of unity, is the 7-torsion subgroup 7Br(F) generated by cyclic algebras of degree 7?
More weakly than asking for cyclic generators, is every class in the n-torsion subgroup nBr(F) representable by a central simple algebra of degree n?

Fix a prime p and integers r <= s. Assuming p^r Br(F) is generated by cyclic algebras, what is the minimal number l_F(p^r, p^s) such that every central simple F-algebra of degree p^s and period dividing p^r is Brauer-equivalent to a tensor product of that many cyclic algebras of degree p^r?
For primes p >= 3, can one prove a finite upper bound for the symbol lengths l_F(p, p^2) and l_F(p^2, p^2)?
If a field F is finitely generated over a subfield F_0 whose Brauer dimension is finite, must the Brauer dimension of F also be finite?
Can one define a notion of dimension for a useful class of fields F such that Br.dim(F) <= dim F - 1 and dim(F(t)) = dim F + 1?
For the center Z(F,n) of generic n-by-n matrices, and similarly for Z_m(F,n) and Z_H(F,n), is the field extension over F rational, stably rational, or retract rational?
Let H = C_3 x C_3 be the transitive subgroup of S_9 described in the paper. Is the corresponding field Z_H(F,9) rational, stably rational, or retract rational over F?
context_brief: Transitive C3 x C3 center in degree 9

question_text: What are the essential dimension ed(PGL_n) and essential p-dimension ed_p(PGL_n) of the projective linear group? In particular, what are ed_F(PGL_4) in characteristic 2 and ed_F(PGL_5)?

What structural consequences for central simple algebras can be deduced from bounds on essential dimension or essential p-dimension? In particular, can one bound ed(CPAlg_n) and ed(Alg_G), compute ed(Alg_G) - ed(G), and determine whether equality ed(CPAlg_n) = ed(PGL_n) forces every degree-n algebra over every field extension of F to be a crossed product?
Compute the unresolved essential dimensions ed_F(GL_8 / mu_2) in characteristic 2, ed_F(GL_16 / mu_2) in characteristic not 2, and ed_F(GL_{p^2} / mu_p) for odd primes p over arbitrary fields F.
If sigma is an anisotropic orthogonal or symplectic involution on a central simple algebra A over F, must sigma remain anisotropic after scalar extension to every odd-degree field extension of F?

If sigma is an anisotropic orthogonal involution on a central simple algebra A over F, must sigma remain anisotropic after scalar extension to the function field F_A of the Severi-Brauer variety of A?
context_brief: Orthogonal involutions over Severi-Brauer function fields

question_text: Let G be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group that is anisotropic over F. Does G remain anisotropic over every finite extension K/F whose degree is not divisible by any prime in the set S(G) of homological torsion primes of G?
For a geometrically connected smooth projective surface X over a finite field, does the 2-primary torsion subgroup Br(X)(2) admit a non-degenerate alternating pairing with values in Q/Z?
context_brief: Pairings on Brauer groups of surfaces

question_text: Is there a structural criterion that decides when the tensor product A tensor_F B of two F-division algebras contains a zero divisor, equivalently when it fails to remain a division algebra?

Suppose (a,b)_n and (c,d)_n are symbol algebras of degree n over F and their tensor product has index less than n^2. Must there exist symbol algebras in the same Brauer classes that share a common maximal subfield and whose tensor product is isomorphic to the original one?
context_brief: Common maximal subfields for symbol algebras

question_text: If ind(A tensor_F B) is strictly smaller than ind(A) ind(B), what common splitting fields can the division algebras A and B have?
context_brief: Common splitting fields in tensor-product collapse

question_text: If central simple F-algebras A and B have the same degree and generate the same subgroup of Br(F), must their generic splitting fields F(A) and F(B) be isomorphic? Equivalently, are the Severi-Brauer varieties SB(A) and SB(B) necessarily F-birational under that hypothesis?

If two division algebras have the same splitting fields inside a specified class of field extensions, for example finite extensions or extensions of transcendence degree at most one, must they generate the same subgroup of the Brauer group?
If two degree-3 division algebras have the same splitting fields of transcendence degree at most one, must they generate the same subgroup of the Brauer group?

If F is finitely generated over a prime field or over an algebraically closed field, must any two quaternion division algebras over F that have the same finite splitting fields, or even just the same maximal subfields, already be isomorphic?

If F is finitely generated over a prime field or over an algebraically closed field and D is a division algebra over F, are there only finitely many other division algebras over F with exactly the same finite splitting fields as D?
For a given field F, which finite groups G are F-admissible, meaning that there exists a G-crossed-product F-division algebra?
Is every Sylow-metacyclic finite group Q-admissible, that is, realizable as the Galois group of a maximal subfield of some crossed-product division algebra over Q?
If SK_1(A tensor_F L) vanishes for every field extension L/F, must the index of the central simple algebra A be square-free?
For which natural numbers n does there exist a field F whose Brauer group has exactly n elements?

For each prime p and field F, must the p-primary component of the Brauer group satisfy one of the following: it is zero, it contains a nonzero divisible subgroup, or else p = 2 and the 2-primary component is an elementary abelian 2-group?
Does there exist a field whose Brauer group is isomorphic to Z/7Z?

For an open dynamical system with a hole H ⊂ Ω, survival probability P(t), escape rate γ = - lim_{t→∞} (1/t) ln P(t), and natural invariant measure ν on the repeller, for which classes of maps and flows does the escape-rate formula γ = ∑_{i:λ_i>0} λ_i - h_KS remain valid, where the sum runs over positive Lyapunov exponents and h_KS is the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy computed with respect to ν?
For which billiards, and under which joint limits of long time t and small hole size h, does the survival probability P(t) reduce to a function only of the combined variable h t?
Does every triangular billiard, or more generally every polygonal billiard, contain at least one periodic orbit?
In polygonal billiards, is the asymptotic long-time survival probability P(t) completely determined by neighborhoods of non-escaping periodic orbits?

For stadium-like billiards that contain marginally unstable periodic orbits, can one comprehensively characterize their dynamical and escape properties in terms of the reinjection dynamics of trajectories that leave and later return to the neighborhood of those periodic orbits?

Is there a universal asymptotic decay law for the long-time survival probability in generic open billiards with mixed phase space, where sticky motion near elliptic islands can produce algebraic decay?

In mushroom billiards and related systems with mixed phase space, how does the boundary between regular and chaotic regions affect escape, including the slowing of survival decay caused by stickiness from marginally unstable periodic orbits and by the regular-chaotic interface itself?

What are the minimal microscopic dynamical properties needed for a chaotic macroscopic limit in billiard-like transport models, for example recurrence, ergodicity, existence of a normal diffusion coefficient, or convergence to a limiting Wiener process?

For an open quantum billiard, let k_n denote the resonances of the Helmholtz equation (∇^2 + k^2)ψ = 0 with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Is it true that the number of resonant states satisfying Re(k_n) < k and Im(k_n) > -C grows on the order of k^(d_H+1) as k → ∞, where d_H is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the classical non-escaping set?
For a given open or generalized billiard system, can the survival probability P(t) be computed exactly, or at least expanded for large t beyond its leading asymptotic term?

How do recurrences in a dynamical system, including periodic orbits and more general recurrent structures either near the hole or elsewhere in phase space, affect escape for systems with little or no hyperbolicity?
What information about the dynamics or geometry of a billiard can be recovered from escape measurements alone, and to what extent can such measurements reveal the shape of the underlying domain?

For the disordered copolymer model whose critical curve satisfies h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ in the weak-coupling regime when α ∈ (0,1), determine the universal slope m_α as an explicit function of α. Equivalently, identify the weak-coupling asymptotic of the critical curve beyond the currently known bounds, using only the model data supported in the paper: α is the tail exponent in the renewal law K(n) ~ C_K / n^(1+α), h_c(λ) is the localization-delocalization critical curve, and m_α depends only on α and not on the detailed law of the disorder sequence or on the full renewal distribution.
In the same weak-coupling copolymer setting, prove the strict lower bound m_1/2 > 2/3 for the universal slope m_α of the critical curve h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ when α = 1/2.

Does there exist any α > 0 for which the universal weak-coupling slope m_α of the copolymer critical curve equals 1/(1+α)? Here m_α is defined by h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ for small λ when the limit exists, and the question asks whether the lower-bound expression 1/(1+α) is ever the exact value of the slope for the original copolymer model.

The paper proves that for every λ > 0 there exists c(λ) < ∞ such that F(λ, h_c(λ)+δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ^2 for every δ > 0, where F is the quenched free energy and h_c is the critical curve. Can this smoothing estimate be strengthened by replacing the power δ^2 with a strictly larger exponent, i.e. by proving that the free energy vanishes faster than quadratically as the critical point is approached from the localized side?

In the localized phase, let μ(λ,h) := -lim_{N→∞} (1/N) log E[(1 + exp(-2λ Σ_{n=1}^N (ω_n+h)))/Z_{N,ω}] and let F(λ,h) be the free energy. As h approaches the critical curve h_c(λ) from below, are the two quantities logarithmically equivalent in the sense that log μ(λ,h) ~ log F(λ,h)? This asks whether the decay scale controlling correlation length or longest-excursion asymptotics vanishes at the same logarithmic rate as the free energy near criticality.

Fix parameters (λ,h) in the interior of the delocalized region D, where D = {(λ,h) : F(λ,h)=0}. Is it true that for every ε > 0, the quenched polymer measure of the event that the polymer stays entirely in the favorable solvent during the whole terminal segment [εN, N] tends to 0 almost surely as N → ∞? In the paper's notation this is the question whether lim_{N→∞} P_{N,ω}(Δ_n = 0 for every n ∈ [εN, N] ∩ N) = 0 almost surely, where Δ_n is the indicator that monomer n is below the interface, so Δ_n = 0 means that monomer n is not below the interface.

Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a finite set P of points in the plane whose visibility graph is exactly G, where two points of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of P.

Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of finite point sets in the plane, where two points are adjacent when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of the set.
Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a finite point set P in the plane, construct coordinates for a point set whose visibility graph is G.
Prove that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) <= 4 has chromatic number chi(G) <= 5.
Prove that there is a constant c such that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) = 5 satisfies chi(G) <= c.

For integers k >= 2 and ell >= 2, every sufficiently large planar point set should contain either ell collinear points or k mutually visible points. Prove this in the remaining open cases k = 6 or ell = 4.

Let b(P) be the minimum size of a blocking set Q for a finite point set P in general position, and let b(n) be the minimum of b(P) over all n-point sets with no three points collinear. Prove that b(n)/n tends to infinity as n tends to infinity.

Is every n-vertex graph representable by an obstacle representation that uses only O(n) polygonal obstacles, where vertices are points in the plane and two vertices are adjacent exactly when the segment joining the corresponding points avoids every obstacle?
Improve the current lower bound O(n / log^2 n) for the maximum possible obstacle number of an n-vertex graph.
For each integer h > 1, determine the smallest number of vertices that a graph can have while having obstacle number exactly h.
Does every planar graph have obstacle number 1?

Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a set S of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is G, where vertices correspond to segment endpoints and two endpoints are adjacent when the segment joining them avoids all segments of S, with the two endpoints of each original segment also adjacent.
Characterize exactly which graphs arise as segment visibility graphs of finite collections of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane.
Given a graph G known to be a segment visibility graph, construct a set of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is G.
Given the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, find a Hamiltonian cycle of G in polynomial time.
context_brief: Hamiltonian cycles in segment visibility graphs

question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, identify which edges of G correspond to the original segments of the underlying segment set S.
Characterize exactly which graphs admit a unit bar visibility representation, meaning a bar visibility representation in which all horizontal bars have the same length.
Is recognizing unit bar visibility graphs an NP-complete problem?

Characterize exactly which graphs are bar k-visibility graphs, where vertices are horizontal bars and two bars are adjacent exactly when some vertical segment between them intersects at most k other bars.
Triangle-free non-planar graphs are already known to be forbidden subgraphs of bar k-visibility graphs. Determine whether there are other classes of forbidden subgraphs for bar k-visibility graphs.
For k >= 5, determine whether there exist (2k + 2)-regular bar k-visibility graphs.
Determine whether there exist d-regular bar k-visibility graphs with degree d >= 2k + 3.
