Improve the current upper bound 6k + 6 on the chromatic number of a bar k-visibility graph.
context_brief: Chromatic number of bar k-visibility graphs

question_text: The thickness of a bar k-visibility graph is known to be at most 2k(9k - 1). Improve this upper bound.
What is the largest possible crossing number of a bar k-visibility graph?
context_brief: Crossing numbers of bar k-visibility graphs

question_text: What is the largest possible genus of a bar k-visibility graph?

Characterize exactly which graphs are rectangle visibility graphs, where vertices are isothetic rectangles with pairwise disjoint interiors and two vertices are adjacent exactly when their rectangles are horizontally or vertically visible by an unobstructed beam of finite width.

Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a simple polygon P whose vertex visibility graph is G, where two vertices of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them lies entirely inside P.
Is the problem of recognizing whether a graph is the visibility graph of a simple polygon in NP?
Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G together with a Hamiltonian cycle C of G, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a simple polygon P whose boundary order is exactly the cycle C.
Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of simple polygons.
Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a simple polygon, construct a simple polygon whose visibility graph is G.
Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P, determine which Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponds to the boundary of P.
Design a constant-factor approximation algorithm for the minimum dominating set problem on visibility graphs of simple polygons.

Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P together with the Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponding to the boundary of P, determine a maximum hidden set of G, meaning a largest set of vertices no two of which are adjacent.
context_brief: Maximum hidden sets with boundary order

question_text: Design an approximation algorithm for computing a maximum hidden set in a visibility graph.
Given the adjacency matrix of a visibility graph G, compute a maximum clique of G.
Improve the current lower and upper bounds on the number of non-isomorphic visibility graphs of simple polygons with n vertices.
Can every visibility graph be realized so that all endpoint coordinates are integers using only polynomially many bits per coordinate?

Determine the correct asymptotic order of the minimum number of bits needed by an optimal covering-set representation of a visibility graph, where a covering set is a family of cliques and complete bipartite graphs whose members are subgraphs of the visibility graph and whose union covers every edge.
Find a polynomial-time algorithm that constructs a covering set for a visibility graph matching the optimal asymptotic bit bound.

For each integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every k-blocked point set has at most n points? Here a k-blocked point set is a set of planar points colored with k colors so that mutually visible points receive different colors and points that are not visible because of collinear blockers receive the same color.
context_brief: Bounded size of k-blocked point sets

question_text: Does every k-blocked point set have O(k^2) points?
context_brief: Quadratic bound for k-blocked point sets

question_text: In every k-blocked point set, must each color class contain at most k points?
context_brief: Color-class size in k-blocked point sets

question_text: Does every visibility graph G with minimum degree delta(G) have vertex-connectivity at least (2 delta(G) + 1) / 3?

Let S = {p_1, ..., p_r} be distinct points in projective space P^N over an algebraically closed field. If a(S,m) denotes the least degree d such that h^0(X, L(d,m)) > 0 for the divisor L(d,m) = dH - m(E_1 + ... + E_r) on the blow-up X of P^N at S, and if e(S) = lim_{m->infinity} a(S,m)/m is the Waldschmidt constant of S, develop computational or conceptual methods for evaluating, estimating, or bounding e(S).

Let S be a finite subset of P^N, let a(S,1) be the least degree of a hypersurface containing S, and let e(S) be the Waldschmidt constant lim_{m->infinity} a(S,m)/m. Is it always true that (a(S,1) + N - 1)/N <= e(S)?

Suppose S is a finite subset of P^N and a(S,m) is the least degree d such that h^0(X, L(d,m)) > 0 on the blow-up of P^N at S. If for some m one has a(S,m)/m = (a(S,1) + N - 1)/N, must S either lie in a hyperplane or be a star configuration? Likewise, if e(S) = (a(S,1) + N - 1)/N, must S either lie in a hyperplane or be a star configuration?

Let f : X -> P^N be the blow-up of distinct points p_1, ..., p_r with exceptional divisors E_1, ..., E_r, and let D = dH - m_1 E_1 - ... - m_r E_r where H is the pullback of a hyperplane. Is there a general way to determine whether the divisor D is semi-effective, meaning that h^0(X, nD) > 0 for some integer n > 0?

For a finite-length monomial subscheme type Z = Spec k[x,y]/I on a smooth projective surface S, let Hilb_I S denote the constructible locus in the Hilbert scheme whose closed points are subschemes Y subset S isomorphic to Z. Describe Hilb_I S: is this locus locally closed, and what adjacency relations occur between such loci inside the Hilbert scheme?

Let Y be a general subscheme of a smooth projective surface S lying in the monomial Hilbert-scheme locus Hilb_I S associated to a finite-length monomial ideal I, and let D be a divisor on S. What can be said about the cohomology of I_Y tensor O_S(D)? In particular, what conditions on S, I, and D force h^0(I_Y tensor O_S(D)) = max{0, h^0(O_S(D)) - n}, where n is the length of the monomial scheme?

Let S = P^2 and let I = (y, x^r)^m with integers r > 9 and m >= 1. If Y is a general element of the Hilbert-scheme locus Hilb_I S associated to this monomial ideal, is it true that for every degree d > 0 one has dim H^0(I_Y tensor O_{P^2}(d)) = max{0, binom(d+2,2) - r binom(m+1,2)}?

Let S = P^2 and let I = (y, x^r)^m with integers r > 9 and m >= 1. If Y is a general element of the Hilbert-scheme locus Hilb_I S associated to this monomial ideal, is it true that H^0(I_Y tensor O_{P^2}(d)) = 0 for every degree d satisfying d <= m sqrt(r)?
Let X -> P^2 be the blow-up of generic points p_1, ..., p_s. If C subset X is a prime divisor, must h^1(X, O_X(C)) vanish?

Can the SHGH vanishing statement for blow-ups of P^2 be extended beyond the case of generic blown-up points? More concretely, how can one remove the assumption that the points are generic in the SHGH conjecture?
Let X be a smooth projective surface, either rational or in characteristic 0. Does there exist a constant c_X such that for every prime divisor C on X one has h^1(X, C) <= c_X h^0(X, C)?

Let X be a projective manifold with large algebraic fundamental group, and let L be an ample line bundle on X. Given a positive number N, does there exist a finite etale cover p : X' -> X such that either (1) the Seshadri number of p^*L at every point of X' is greater than N, or (2) the Seshadri number along the diagonal D' subset X' x X' of p_e^*(p_1^*L tensor p_2^*L) is greater than N? If neither statement is always true, what condition on the fundamental group of X guarantees a positive answer?

Do the known results for line arrangements in P^2 extend to arrangements in higher-dimensional projective space? In particular, if A is a hyperplane arrangement in P^n, can one give an explicit description of the graded Betti numbers of the Orlik-Terao algebra C(A) in terms of the geometry of A?
Let I be a radical ideal of big height e. Must the symbolic power containment I^(m) subset I^r hold whenever m >= re - (e - 1)?

Suppose (R, m) is a regular local ring of dimension n and I subset R is an ideal with big height e. Do the following containments hold: (1) I^(m) subset m^(rn-r) I^r for m >= rn; (2) I^(m) subset m^(rn-r-(n-1)) I^r for m >= rn - (n - 1); (3) I^(m) subset m^(re-r) I^r for m >= re; and (4) I^(m) subset m^(re-r-(e-1)) I^r for m >= re - (e - 1)?

Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at r distinct points in arbitrary position, and let L be an effective nef divisor on X. Must one of the following hold: (a) there exists m >= 1 such that h^1(mL) = 0, with m = 1 expected when the points are in general position; or (b) there exists a curve C on X, not necessarily irreducible, such that |L - C| is nonempty, the arithmetic genus p_a(C) is positive, and L.C = 0?
Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero. Does there exist a positive constant b(X) such that every reduced irreducible curve C subset X satisfies C^2 >= -b(X)?

Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero and fix an integer g >= 0. Does there exist a positive constant b(X,g) such that every reduced irreducible curve C subset X whose normalization has genus g satisfies C^2 >= -b(X,g)?

Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero and fix an integer g >= 0. Does there exist a positive constant b_s(X,g) such that every smooth irreducible curve C subset X of geometric genus g satisfies C^2 >= -b_s(X,g)?

Let f : Y -> B be a morphism from a smooth projective threefold to a smooth curve whose general fiber is a smooth surface. For a fixed geometric genus g, does there exist a constant b(Y,g) such that every vertical curve C subset Y of geometric genus g satisfies C^2 >= -b(Y,g), where the self-intersection is computed inside the fiber containing C?
Is the global Seshadri constant epsilon(X) = inf{epsilon(L) : L in Pic(X) is ample} positive for every smooth projective surface X?

Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero. Does there exist a positive constant b_w(X) such that for every irreducible curve C subset X and every big and nef line bundle H with H.C > 0, one has C^2 >= -b_w(X) (H.C)^2?

Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero. Does there exist a positive constant b'(X) such that every reduced curve C subset X, without assuming irreducibility, satisfies C^2 >= -b'(X)?

Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at r general points, let D be an effective divisor on X, and let E be a (-1)-curve. For the restriction map rho : |D| -> |D|_E, is it true that (1) every base point in the image of rho comes from a base curve in |D|, and (2) if |D| has no fixed component, then rho has maximal rank?

Let L(d; m_1, ..., m_n) denote the linear system of plane curves of degree d passing through n points with multiplicities at least m_1, ..., m_n, and let L(d; m_1, ..., m_r, m_{r+1}, ..., m_n) denote the analogous system where the first r points are constrained to be collinear but are otherwise general. If d >= m_1 + ... + m_r, is it true that L(d; m_1, ..., m_n) is nonempty if and only if the corresponding system with the first r points collinear is nonempty?

Give a mathematical proof for the page-5 observation that, in the three displayed examples of bimagic squares of orders 256x256, 625x625, and 2401x2401, the first listed subgroup orders 64x64, 125x125, and 343x343 respectively have a common bimagic sum S2 within each case. Here S2 denotes the common sum of the squares of the entries in each row, each column, and the two principal diagonals of a bimagic square.

Suppose f and g are distinct non-constant meromorphic functions that share four distinct values a1, a2, a3, and a4 in the sense that, for each shared value a_nu, the set of points where f = a_nu is the same as the set of points where g = a_nu, but no agreement of multiplicities is assumed. Must Nevanlinna's Four-Value conclusion still hold: after relabelling the shared values, must the cross-ratio (a1, a2, a3, a4) equal -1, so that a1 and a2 are Picard values of both functions and g is a Mobius transformation of f that fixes a3 and a4 and permutes a1 and a2?
context_brief: Nevanlinna four shared values without multiplicity agreement

question_text: Suppose f and g are non-constant meromorphic functions that share four distinct values, and one of those four shared values is shared by counting multiplicities, meaning that for that one value the two functions take the value at exactly the same points with the same multiplicities, while for the other three values only the sets of shared points are assumed to coincide. Must the conclusion of Nevanlinna's Four-Value Theorem still follow, namely that after relabelling the values the cross-ratio (a1, a2, a3, a4) equals -1, a1 and a2 are Picard values of both functions, and g is a Mobius transformation of f that fixes a3 and a4 and permutes a1 and a2?

Can the general problem of two meromorphic functions sharing four values be reduced by Zalcman rescaling to a limit pair with bounded spherical derivative without losing the essential shared-value data? More precisely, after passing to rescaled limits, can one rule out the possibilities that a value shared by the original pair becomes only a Picard value of the limit pair, that a value not originally shared by counting multiplicities becomes shared by counting multiplicities in the limit, or that the two limit functions collapse to the identical function, so that a proof of the (1+3) conjecture in the bounded-spherical-derivative setting would imply the general case?
context_brief: Open rescaling reduction for the (1+3) problem

question_text: For each positive integer n, determine C(n), the number of Costas arrays of order n. In particular, do Costas arrays exist for every order n > 0, and if not, which positive integers n satisfy C(n) = 0?

Let E(n) be the decision problem that asks whether at least one Costas array of order n exists, equivalently whether C(n) > 0. What is the computational complexity of E(n) as a function of n, and in particular is this decision problem NP-complete?

Define the degrees of freedom of a Costas array of order n as the smallest k <= n for which there exist indices i1 < i2 < ... < ik in [n] such that, for any prescribed values f1, ..., fk in [n], there is at most one Costas permutation f:[n]->[n] with f(ij)=fj for all j. Determine this quantity for Costas arrays of order n, and if possible improve the definition so it captures the phenomenon more effectively.

Find an upper or asymptotic bound for C(n), the number of Costas arrays of order n, that matches the empirically observed decay of C(n)/n! more closely than the currently known O((n-1)!) bound. Also prove or disprove whether the ratio C(n)/n! decreases monotonically to 0.
Determine whether sporadic Costas arrays form only a finite set, or whether they instead arise from one or more still-unknown generally applicable construction techniques.

A pair of Costas permutations g1,g2:[n]->[n] is called twin when both are obtained from a Costas permutation f:[n]->[n] by shifting the graph of f one step and adding opposite corner points exactly as specified in Definition 7. Is the unique known example of a twin pair the only one, or do finitely or infinitely many twin Costas pairs exist? If more exist, can they be constructed systematically?

Do there exist finite-order sporadic Costas arrays of order n > 1 whose dots also form a configuration of non-attacking queens on an n x n chessboard? If such arrays exist, how many are there, and can they be constructed systematically?

Let g:[l]->[l] be a Costas permutation. Does there always exist a larger Costas permutation f having an arithmetic-progression substructure S1,S2 as in Definition 8 such that g(i) = (f(a1 + b1 i) - a2)/b2 on those progressions, so that g is a sub-permutation of f? Is this always true at least for particular families such as sporadic Costas permutations?

Describe the cycle structure of Costas permutations under iteration. In particular, for a specific Costas permutation or a specific family, determine the full cycle decomposition, whether cycles of a given length can occur, the longest cycle length, and the smallest positive integer k for which the k-fold iterate equals the identity permutation.

Consider the algebraic Costas-array construction families listed in Section 3.2, including the Welch- and Golomb-type families W1, W2, G2, G3, G4, W3, G4*, G4**, and G5*. Is it true that for every order n > 5 these construction methods are pairwise disjoint, so that no Costas array of that order can be produced by two different methods?

For each unpredictably emergent Costas-array construction method obtained by adding one or more dots to an existing Costas array, determine whether there is a finite threshold N beyond which that method never produces a Costas array of order n > N.

Do any two sufficiently large Costas arrays necessarily share a common distance vector? More specifically, is it enough for the smaller array to have size at least 3 x 3 and the larger to have size at least 5 x 5 for a common distance vector to be forced?
Develop a stochastic search algorithm for Costas arrays that continues to work at larger orders of practical interest, especially orders 30, 31, 32, and 33.

A Costas array is called singly periodic when cyclic shifts of the columns of a W1 array again produce W1 arrays, and more generally the paper asks whether any singly periodic Costas array must belong to the W1 family. Is every singly periodic Costas array necessarily a W1 array?

Suppose a Costas array has the property that after adding one blank row at the top, every cyclic shift of the rows still yields a non-square array with the Costas property. Must the original Costas array be an exponential Welch W1 array?

Suppose a Costas array has the property that after adding one blank row at the top and one blank column at the side, every cyclic shift of rows and columns still yields a square non-permutation array with the Costas property. Must the original Costas array be a G2 array?

For G2 Costas arrays constructed over finite fields of characteristic 2, determine the four parity populations ee, eo, oe, and oo, namely the numbers of dots whose coordinates are respectively even-even, even-odd, odd-even, and odd-odd.
Fix a prime power q and an integer r relatively prime to q-1. Determine how many elements x of the finite field F(q) satisfy the equation x^r + x = 1.

Let p be a prime, let C be a nonzero element of the finite field F(p), and let alpha be a primitive root modulo p. Determine the number of integers i in [p-1] that satisfy the congruence i ≡ C alpha^i (mod p).

For a fixed order n, determine the forbidden positions of Costas arrays: grid locations in the n x n board that are not occupied by a dot in any Costas array of that order. Solve this without relying on exhaustive enumeration.

For the families of Welch W1 and Golomb G2 Costas arrays, determine the maximal pairwise cross-correlation quantities defined by the paper as Ψ_W1(p) and Ψ_G2(q), classify primes and prime powers into the cases stated in Problem 21, prove the listed formulas and exceptional cases, derive formulas for the local minima, and show where the maxima are attained in the non-safe cases described there.

For G2 arrays generated over finite fields of characteristic 2, find an intrinsic necessary structural property analogous to the anti-reflective symmetry known for W1 arrays and analogous to the congruence f(mu + i) - f(mu - i) ≡ i [f(mu + 1) - f(mu - 1)] mod (q - 1), where mu = (q - 1)/2, which is known for G2 arrays over odd characteristic.

Let C(m,n,N) denote the number of m x n Golomb rectangles containing N dots, where a Golomb rectangle is a rectangular dot pattern whose autocorrelation takes exactly the three values {N, 1, 0}. Determine C(m,n,N). In particular, for fixed m and n find the largest N with C(m,n,N) > 0, and for fixed N find the smallest m and n with C(m,n,N) > 0.
Enumerate all honeycomb arrays, where a honeycomb array is equivalently a Costas array with exactly one dot on every bottom-left to top-right diagonal.

Find exact formulas for the two fundamental extremal functions for Golomb rulers: the minimum possible length n of a Golomb ruler with a given number m of points, and the maximum possible number of points m in a Golomb ruler of a given length n.

Give an efficient conversion in both directions between Costas arrays (or more generally Golomb rectangles) and Golomb rulers. In particular, for a given Costas array or family of Costas arrays, determine the minimum number of blank rows that must be added at the bottom so that stacking the columns in order produces a Golomb ruler.

Let (X, X, µ, T1, ..., Tℓ) be a measure preserving system and define the multiple correlation sequence by C(n1, ..., nℓ) := ∫ f0 · T1^n1 f1 · ... · Tℓ^nℓ fℓ dµ. Is every such sequence an approximate integral combination of generalized ℓ-step nilsequences in ℓ variables?
Let (X, X, µ, T) be a system and f, g, h ∈ L∞(µ). If C(n) := ∫ f · T^n g · T^(2n) h dµ, is the sequence (C(n)) an approximate integral combination of generalized 2-step nilsequences?

Let CT,S be the set of sequences of the form (∫ f · T^n g · S^n h dµ) as (X, X, µ, T, S) ranges over systems and f, g, h range over L∞(µ), and let CT be the subclass where T and S are powers of a single transformation. Must CT,S and CT actually coincide?

For integer sequences a1(n), ..., aℓ(n), are the following conditions equivalent: (i) the sequences are good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations; (ii) they are good for ℓ-convergence on ℓ-step nilsystems; and (iii) for every basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence ψ in ℓ variables, the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a1(n), ..., aℓ(n)) converge?

Let a(n) be an integer sequence such that the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a(n)) converge for every basic generalized 2-step nilsequence ψ. Must it follow that for every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and f, g ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{a(n)} f · S^{a(n)} g converge weakly in L2(µ)?

Let (wn) be a complex sequence such that the weighted averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N wn ψ(n) converge for every generalized 2-step nilsequence ψ. Must it follow that for every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and f, g ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N wn T^n f · S^n g converge weakly in L2(µ)?

Suppose an integer sequence a(n) has the property that for every connected ℓ-step nilmanifold X and every irrational nilrotation b on X, the sequence (b^{a(n)} Γ) is equidistributed in X, and for every r ∈ N the set {n ∈ N : r divides a(n)} has positive upper density. Must a(n) then be good for ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations?
If an integer sequence a(n) is good for ℓ-recurrence of powers, must each power sequence a(n)^k be good for 1-recurrence for k = 1, ..., ℓ?
If an integer sequence is good for 2-convergence of powers of a single transformation, must it also be good for 2-convergence of commuting transformations?
Does there exist an integer sequence that is good for 2-recurrence of powers of a single transformation but is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations?

Can one give an explicit fast growing sequence of positive integers, meaning a(n) grows faster than every power of n, that is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence both for powers of a single transformation and for commuting transformations?

Let P be a family of at least two essentially distinct integer polynomials, and let dmin(P) be the least d such that the Host–Kra factor Zd,T is characteristic for mean convergence of the averages (1/N) Σ T^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · T^{pℓ(n)} fℓ. Must one always have dmin(P) ≤ |P| - 1?

For the same polynomial family P, let dW_min(P) be the least d for which Zd,T is characteristic for the corresponding averages on every Weyl system, that is, every system (T^d, X_{T^d}, m_{T^d}, T) with T a unipotent affine transformation. Must one always have dW_min(P) ≤ |P| - 1?
context_brief: optimal characteristic factor on Weyl systems

question_text: Suppose (p1,N, ..., pℓ,N) is a good sequence of ℓ-tuples of real polynomials, meaning every nontrivial linear combination of the sequences p1,N, ..., pℓ,N is good in the sense that its exponential sums against every nonzero frequency tend to zero. Must it follow that for every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and f1, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) Σ T^[p1,N(n)] f1 · ... · T^[pℓ,N(n)] fℓ converge in L2(µ) to ∫f1 dµ · ... · ∫fℓ dµ?

For every system (X, X, µ, T) and bounded functions f, g, h, do the polynomial multiple ergodic averages (1/N) Σ f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) h(T^{3n} x) and (1/N) Σ f(T^n x) g(T^{n^2} x) converge pointwise almost everywhere?

Let (X, X, µ, T) be a system and f, g ∈ L∞(µ). If Λ is the von Mangoldt function and φ is a multiplicative function with values in the closed unit disk that has convergent means, do the weighted averages (1/N) Σ Λ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) and (1/N) Σ φ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) converge pointwise almost everywhere?

Let a(n) be one of the sequences p_n (the nth prime), [n^c] with c > 0, or 2^n. For every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and f0, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(µ), does the correlation sequence ∫ f0 · T^{a(n)} f1 · ... · T^{ℓ a(n)} fℓ dµ always admit a decomposition ψ(a(n)) + e(n), where ψ is an ℓ-step nilsequence and the Cesàro average of |e(n)| tends to 0?

If p1, ..., pℓ are integer-valued generalized polynomials and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure preserving transformations on a common system, must the averages (1/N) Σ T1^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)} fℓ always converge in L2?

Suppose p1, ..., pℓ ∈ Z[t] are pairwise independent polynomials. Do there exist an integer d and Host–Kra factors Zd,T1, ..., Zd,Tℓ such that these factors are characteristic for the commuting-transformation averages (1/N) Σ T1^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)} fℓ?
context_brief: characteristic factors for commuting polynomial averages

question_text: In the special case where T1, ..., Tℓ are weak mixing and p1, ..., pℓ are pairwise independent integer polynomials, must the averages (1/N) Σ T1^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)} fℓ converge in L2(µ) to the product of the integrals ∫f1 dµ · ... · ∫fℓ dµ?

If p1, ..., pℓ ∈ Z[t] are rationally independent, are the rational Kronecker factors K_rat(T1), ..., K_rat(Tℓ) characteristic for the commuting-transformation averages (1/N) Σ T1^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)} fℓ?

Suppose p1, ..., pℓ ∈ Z[t] are rationally independent and have zero constant term. For every measurable set A and every ε > 0, must there exist n ∈ N such that µ(A ∩ T1^{p1(n)} A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{pℓ(n)} A) ≥ µ(A)^{ℓ+1} - ε?
context_brief: optimal lower bounds for polynomial recurrence

question_text: If {p1, ..., pℓ} is an intersective family of integer-valued polynomials, meaning that for every r ∈ N there exists n with each pi(n) divisible by r, then for every system (X, X, µ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and every A ∈ X with µ(A) > 0, must there exist n ∈ N such that µ(A ∩ T1^{p1(n)} A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{pℓ(n)} A) > 0?
For every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and bounded functions f, g, do the commuting-transformation averages (1/N) Σ f(T^n x) g(S^n x) converge pointwise almost everywhere?

For commuting transformations T1, ..., Tℓ and bounded functions f0, ..., fℓ, does every correlation sequence ∫ f0 · T1^n f1 · ... · Tℓ^n fℓ dµ admit a decomposition ψ(n) + e(n) where ψ is an ℓ-step nilsequence and the Cesàro average of |e(n)| tends to 0?
context_brief: optimal error term in nilsequence decomposition

question_text: Let T1, ..., Tℓ be arbitrary invertible measure preserving transformations, and let p1, ..., pℓ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Must every measurable set A of positive measure contain a pattern of the form A ∩ T1^{m+p1(n)} A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{m+pℓ(n)} A with positive measure for some m, n ∈ N?
context_brief: noncommuting polynomial recurrence with extra variable

question_text: In particular, given invertible measure preserving transformations T, S, R on a common probability space and a set A of positive measure, must there exist m, n ∈ N such that µ(A ∩ T^m A ∩ S^{m+n} A ∩ R^{m+2n} A) > 0?

Let F = {a1(t), ..., aℓ(t)} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth. Is the family of integer sequences {[a1(n)], ..., [aℓ(n)]} good for ℓ-convergence of a single transformation exactly when every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) either stays farther than logarithmic scale from every real multiple of an integer polynomial, or differs from some real multiple of an integer polynomial by a finite limit, or stays within O(log t) of t/m for some nonzero integer m?

Let F = {a1(t), ..., aℓ(t)} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth such that every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) stays farther than logarithmic scale from every real multiple of every integer polynomial. Must it follow that for every ergodic system (X, B, µ, T) and bounded functions f1, ..., fℓ, the averages (1/N) Σ T^[a1(n)] f1 · ... · T^[aℓ(n)] fℓ converge in L2 to the product of the integrals?

If a and b are distinct positive nonintegers, then for every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and bounded functions f, g, must the averages (1/N) Σ f(T^[n^a] x) g(T^[n^b] x) converge almost everywhere to ∫f dµ · ∫g dµ?

Let F = {a1(t), ..., aℓ(t)} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth such that every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) stays unbounded away from every real multiple of every integer polynomial. Must the family {[a1(n)], ..., [aℓ(n)]} then be good for ℓ-recurrence of a single transformation?

Can one find a Hardy-field function a(t) with super-polynomial growth, meaning a(t)/t^k → ∞ for every k, such that the integer sequence [a(n)] is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers?
If c is a positive noninteger and p_n denotes the nth prime, is the sequence [p_n^c] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers?
Is the oscillatory sequence [n sin n] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers?

If c > 1 is not an integer, is the sequence [n^c] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of commuting transformations? More strongly, for every system (X, X, µ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and bounded functions f1, ..., fℓ, is the L2-limit of (1/N) Σ T1^[n^c] f1 · ... · Tℓ^[n^c] fℓ equal to the L2-limit of the linear averages (1/N) Σ T1^n f1 · ... · Tℓ^n fℓ?
Do the prime numbers contain infinitely many patterns of the forms {m, m + [n^c], m + 2[n^c], ..., m + ℓ[n^c]} and {m, m + [n^c1], ..., m + [n^cℓ]} for given positive real exponents c, c1, ..., cℓ?

Let (a_n(ω)) be a random non-lacunary sequence built by independently selecting n with probability σ_n, where σ_n decreases and nσ_n → ∞. Almost surely, is (a_n(ω)) good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of commuting transformations, and do the averages (1/N) Σ T1^{a_n(ω)} f1 · ... · Tℓ^{a_n(ω)} fℓ always converge in L2 to the same limit as the linear averages (1/N) Σ T1^n f1 · ... · Tℓ^n fℓ?

For a random sequence (a_n(ω)) selected with nσ_n → ∞, is it almost surely true that for every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and bounded functions f, g, the averages (1/N) Σ T^n f · S^{a_n(ω)} g converge in L2 to E(f | I_T) · E(g | I_S)? If σ_n = n^{-a} with a ∈ (0,1), does the convergence also hold almost everywhere?

Let (a_n(ω)) and (b_n(ω)) be two independent random sequences built from selection probabilities n^{-a} and n^{-b} with a, b ∈ (0,1) and a ≠ b. Is it almost surely true that for every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and bounded functions f, g, the averages (1/N) Σ T^{a_n(ω)} f · S^{b_n(ω)} g converge, in L2 or pointwise, to E(f | I_T) · E(g | I_S)?

A system with multiplicative structure is a quadruple (X, X, µ, T_n) where T_0 = T_1 = id and T_m ◦ T_n = T_{mn}. In every such system and for every measurable set A of positive measure, do there exist integers m > n ≥ 1 such that µ(T_{2mn} A ∩ T_{(m-n)(m+n)} A) > 0?

In every measure preserving system with multiplicative structure and every measurable set A of positive measure, do there exist m, n ∈ N such that µ(T_{m(m+n)} A ∩ T_{(m+2n)(m+3n)} A ∩ T_{(m+4n)(m+5n)} A) > 0?
In noncommutative group-based cryptography, what is the most appropriate choice of platform group?
In noncommutative group-based cryptography, should the underlying group platform be finite or infinite?
For new noncommutative cryptographic schemes such as public-key exchange, digital signatures, and authentication, how can one prove that a chosen group platform is secure?
Can additional public-key constructions for noncommutative cryptography be built from other search problems and decision problems in combinatorial group theory?
How can the security of these noncommutative group-based cryptographic protocols be analyzed rigorously?
What notion of security should be used for noncommutative group-based cryptography: practicality, worst-case complexity, average-case complexity, generic complexity, or some other measure?
Only three noncommutative digital signature schemes were known at the time of writing; can additional noncommutative digital signature schemes be designed?
What authentication schemes should be developed for noncommutative group-based cryptography?
For polycyclic-group-based cryptography, which commuting subgroups should be chosen so that the described schemes remain secure?
What is the computational complexity of the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?
What is the computational complexity of the decision conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups, for example for the Eick-Ostheimer algorithm?
What is the computational complexity of the collection algorithm used to compute normal forms of elements in polycyclic groups?
What is the computational complexity of the twisted search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?
What is the computational complexity of the Reidemeister-Schreier rewriting algorithm in free groups?
What is the generic-case complexity of the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?
For polycyclic groups, both finite and infinite, can quantum algorithms be designed for the decision problems used in cryptography?
Is there a quantum algorithm for the search conjugacy problem in a polycyclic group that lowers the complexity of solving that problem?
How can the proposed noncommutative group-based cryptosystems be implemented in practice?
Can the computer algebra system GAP be used to build cryptographic implementations that are both practical and secure?

For an open chaotic quantum scattering system with hyperbolic trapped set of Minkowski dimension 1 + 2 nu, what is the sharp asymptotic counting law for long-living resonances? Equivalently, in a fixed high-frequency window [k, k + W] - i[0, gamma] or in the semiclassical strip [E - C hbar, E + C hbar] - i[0, gamma hbar], is the number of resonances of order hbar^(-nu), and does there exist a nontrivial profile F(gamma) such that the count equals C F(gamma) hbar^(-nu) + o(hbar^(-nu))?
context_brief: Fractal Weyl law for resonance counting

question_text: For open chaotic scattering systems with hyperbolic trapped sets, does there exist a resonance-free strip of depth gamma > 0 below the real axis at high frequency, and what is the optimal value of that gap? In particular, for obstacle scattering, can the asymptotic resonance gap be as large as gamma_cl / 2, or must it be strictly smaller?

Can one rigorously prove enough cancellation among the phases accumulated along different classical paths in the quantum monodromy expansion so that the off-diagonal terms behave as if the phases were random, yielding the sharper spectral-radius bound rsp(M(alpha, hbar)) <= exp(P(-phi^+ + 2 log |alpha|)/2 + eps)?
context_brief: Phase cancellations for sharper spectral bounds

question_text: For obstacle scattering in the high-frequency limit, given an infinite sequence of long-living resonances k_j with Re k_j -> infinity, what spatial or phase-space structure do the associated metastable states have? More specifically, can one prove in the obstacle setting that these metastable states microlocalize near the outgoing tail K^+ and are described by semiclassical measures that are invariant under the flow up to global decay?

Fix Lambda >= 0 and a sequence of resonances z(hbar) whose imaginary parts satisfy Im z(hbar) / hbar -> -Lambda / 2. Which Lambda-eigenmeasures can occur as semiclassical measures of the corresponding metastable states, and is there a favored or even unique limiting measure?

Given an incoming scattering state u_E,in at energy E > 0 for a semiclassical scattering Hamiltonian, what is the spatial or phase-space structure of the full solution u_E inside the interaction region? In particular, how are that structure and its visible patterns influenced by trajectories that spend a long time near the trapped set K_E or remain forever on the incoming tail K_E^-?

Is the maximal abelian extension Qab of the rational numbers Q an ample field, where a field K is called ample when every smooth K-curve with a K-rational point has infinitely many K-rational points, equivalently when K satisfies the other equivalent conditions listed in Proposition 2.1?
context_brief: Ampleness of the maximal abelian extension of Q

question_text: Is the maximal solvable Galois extension Qsolv of Q an ample field?
context_brief: Ampleness of the maximal solvable extension of Q

question_text: Is the maximal solvable Galois extension Qsolv of Q pseudo algebraically closed, meaning that every absolutely irreducible Q-variety has a Qsolv-rational point? Equivalently, does every absolutely irreducible Q-variety admit a solvable rational point?

Fix a finite set S of places of Q, and let Qtot,S be the maximal extension of Q in which every place in S is totally split. Is the field Qtot,S intersected with Qsolv pseudo S-closed (PSC), where a subfield K of Qtot,S is PSC if every smooth Q-variety that has a point over Qp for each p in S (with Q_infinity = R) has a K-rational point?
context_brief: Whether Qtot,S intersect Qsolv is PSC

question_text: For every non-zero abelian variety A defined over Q, is the Mordell-Weil rank of A over Qab infinite; that is, does rank(A(Qab)) = infinity hold for every such A?
context_brief: Ranks of abelian varieties over Qab

question_text: If K is an infinite field whose absolute Galois group GK is prosolvable, must K be ample?
If K is an infinite field whose absolute Galois group GK is finitely generated as a topological group, must K be ample?
Let K/Q be an algebraic extension whose absolute Galois group GK is finitely generated, and let A be a non-zero abelian variety over K. Must the Mordell-Weil rank rank(A(K)) be infinite?

What is the precise relationship among ample fields, virtually ample fields, and weakly ample fields? In particular, if a field K is called virtually ample when some finite extension of K is ample, and weakly ample when every K-curve C becomes infinite over some finite extension L/K, must every weakly ample field be virtually ample, and must every virtually ample field already be ample?
context_brief: Ample versus virtually ample versus weakly ample

question_text: Is every radically closed field ample, where radically closed means that the multiplicative group K^times of the field is divisible?
Is every infinite almost radically closed field ample, where almost radically closed means that for every positive integer n the subgroup of n-th powers has finite index in K^times?
Is every minimal field algebraically closed, where an infinite field K is called minimal when every subset A of K definable by a first-order formula in the language of rings is finite or cofinite?

Does there exist a non-ample field K such that every finite split embedding problem over K has a regular solution? Equivalently, does there exist a non-ample field K for which the Debes-Deschamps conjecture holds?
context_brief: Non-ample fields satisfying the Debes-Deschamps conjecture

question_text: Consider the family of elliptic one-variable germs f_{lambda,a}(z)=lambda z+z^2 g_a(z), where |lambda|=1 and lambda is not a root of unity. Find concrete families for which holomorphic linearizability is equivalent to lambda satisfying the Brjuno condition, and in particular determine whether every elliptic polynomial (or at least every elliptic cubic polynomial) is holomorphically linearizable exactly when its multiplier is a Brjuno number.

Let B(theta) be the Brjuno function and r(theta) the infimum of radii of convergence of linearizations for injective germs on the unit disk with multiplier e^{2 pi i theta}. Does the function log r(theta)+B(theta) extend from irrational theta to all theta in [0,1) as a 1/2-Holder continuous function?
context_brief: Regularity of log r plus Brjuno

question_text: For elliptic non-linearizable one-variable germs (Cremer points), are the pair of invariants consisting of (i) the multiplier and (ii) the homeomorphism class of the germ of the stable set at the origin a complete set of topological invariants for topological local conjugacy?
Given two one-variable germs tangent to the identity (multiplier 1), provide an effective and implementable decision procedure that determines whether they are holomorphically locally conjugated.
Given two one-variable parabolic germs (multiplier a root of unity), provide an effective and implementable decision procedure that determines whether they are holomorphically locally conjugated.

Let f in End(C^n,O) be non-invertible and dominant, let c(f^k) be the order of the k-th iterate, and let c_infinity(f)=lim_{k->+infinity} c(f^k)^{1/k}. Must c_infinity(f) always be an algebraic integer of degree at most n? Equivalently, do there always exist integers a_0,...,a_{n-1} such that c_infinity^n + a_{n-1} c_infinity^{n-1} + ... + a_0 = 0, and does there always exist delta in (0,1] with delta c_infinity^k <= c(f^k) <= c_infinity^k for all k >= 1?
context_brief: Asymptotic attraction rate in higher dimensions

question_text: For a non-invertible dominant germ f in End(C^n,O), does the integer sequence {c(f^k)}_{k in N} satisfy, at least for all sufficiently large k, a linear recurrence relation with integer coefficients?

Let f be a superattracting germ in End(C^n,O), and let H be the first nonzero homogeneous term in its expansion. Assume H is degenerate, meaning H(v)=0 for some nonzero v. If the postcritical set PCrit(f)=union_{k>=0} f^k(Crit(f)) is an analytic cone near the origin, must f be holomorphically locally conjugated to H?
context_brief: Degenerate leading term and analytic cone

question_text: Let f be a superattracting germ in End(C^n,O) with first nonzero homogeneous term H. If the postcritical set of f is a topological cone near the origin, under what conditions is f topologically locally conjugated to H, and specifically does this always hold when H is non-degenerate?

Let f and g be superattracting germs in End(C^n,O) with c(f)=c(g). Is local conjugacy equivalent to conjugacy of postcritical sets: topological conjugacy iff a local homeomorphism sends PCrit(f) onto PCrit(g), and holomorphic conjugacy iff a local biholomorphism sends PCrit(f) onto PCrit(g)?
Classify, up to formal conjugacy, superattracting germs of order 2 in End(C^n,O) for n >= 3, and superattracting germs of order 3 in End(C^2,O).
Classify rigid non-invertible dominant holomorphic germs in complex dimension 3.

Determine conditions on a germ f in End(C^3,O) guaranteeing existence of a modification pi: M~ -> C^3 based at O, a point p in E=pi^{-1}(O), and a (possibly weakly) rigid germ f~ in End(M,p) such that pi o f~ = f o pi.

Let f in End(C^n,O) be tangent to the identity, with the origin an isolated fixed point. Must there always exist at least one Fatou flower (a collection of nu-1 parabolic curves with the standard petal geometry) tangent to some direction?
context_brief: Existence of Fatou flowers in C^n

question_text: For a germ tangent to the identity in C^n, describe the stable set using invariants attached to characteristic directions (including directors and indices), and determine what additional invariants are needed to capture the full structure of the stable set.

Suppose f in End(C^n,O) has expansion f(z)=z+P_nu(z)+O(||z||^{nu+1}) and all characteristic directions are non-degenerate. Is f topologically locally conjugated to the time-1 map of the homogeneous vector field P_nu?
context_brief: Topological normal form via time-1 map

question_text: Find formal normal forms and formal invariants for germs tangent to the identity whose characteristic directions are all degenerate.
context_brief: Formal classification with only degenerate directions

question_text: Consider a geodesic-type vector field G=g1(z)v d/dz + (nu-1)g2(z)v^2 d/dv associated to a homogeneous vector field in dimension two. Describe the local dynamics of G near an irregular singularity (zeta_0,0), i.e., where the vanishing orders satisfy mu1(zeta_0) > mu2(zeta_0)+1.

Let lambda=(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) be eigenvalues with divergent Brjuno-type sum sum_{k>=0} 2^{-k} log(1/Omega_lambda(2^{k+1}))=+infinity, where Omega_lambda(m)=min{|lambda_1^{k_1}...lambda_n^{k_n}-lambda_j|: 2<=k_1+...+k_n<=m, no resonance equality}. Does there exist a germ f in End(C^n,O) with diagonalizable differential having these eigenvalues that is formally linearizable but not holomorphically linearizable?

Given lambda=(lambda_1,...,lambda_n), construct families {f_{lambda,a}} of formally linearizable germs with diagonal linear part diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) such that holomorphic linearizability is equivalent to the multivariable Brjuno condition sum_{k>=0} 2^{-k} log(1/Omega_lambda(2^{k+1}))<+infinity; in particular, decide this equivalence for two-dimensional quadratic perturbations f(z)=(lambda_1 z_1, lambda_2 z_2)+Q(z) in the non-resonant case.

Let f(n) be the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Is it true that the asymptotic normalized gap between f(n) and n satisfies lim_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n = √2.4?
context_brief: Asymptotic growth of graphs with distinct cycle lengths.

question_text: Let f(n) be the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Does the lower asymptotic normalized gap satisfy lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n ≤ √3?
context_brief: Weaker asymptotic bound for distinct-cycle-length graphs.

question_text: Let f(n) be the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Does the lower asymptotic normalized gap satisfy lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n ≤ √2.4?
context_brief: Sharper weaker asymptotic bound for distinct-cycle-length graphs.

question_text: Let f2(n) be the maximum number of edges in a 2-connected graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Is it true that lim_{n→∞} (f2(n) − n)/√n = 1?
context_brief: Asymptotic 2-connected version of the distinct cycle-length problem.

question_text: Among hamiltonian graphs on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length, what is the maximum possible number of edges?
context_brief: Hamiltonian graphs with all cycle lengths distinct.

question_text: Let g(n) denote the least number of edges of a graph that contains a cycle of length k for every integer 1 ≤ k ≤ n. Is it true that g(n) = n + log2 n + O(1) as n → ∞?
context_brief: Edge-minimal graphs containing every cycle length up to n.

question_text: Fix nonnegative integers a1, a2, …, an. For a graph G of order n, let ci denote the number of cycles of length i in G, and let f(a1, a2, …, an) be the maximum possible number of edges in a graph satisfying ci ≤ ai for every i. Determine f(a1, a2, …, an) for the general cycle-length distribution constraint problem.
context_brief: Generalized extremal problem with prescribed upper bounds on cycle counts.

question_text: For a fixed integer k ≥ 2, let ex(n, C2k) denote the Turán number of the even cycle C2k, meaning the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph containing no copy of C2k. Does there exist a positive constant c such that ex(n, C2k) ≥ c n^(1+1/k)?
context_brief: Lower bounds for even-cycle Turán numbers.

question_text: Let G be a simple eulerian graph on n vertices, and let cd(G) denote the smallest number of edge-disjoint circuits in a circuit decomposition of G. Must cd(G) ≤ |V(G)|/2 hold for every simple eulerian graph G?

Let X be a compact subset of R^n with positive Lebesgue measure, where n > 2, and let ms_r(X) denote the largest measure that is guaranteed for a monochromatic symmetric subset in every measurable r-coloring of X. Classify the numbers ms_r(X) for such sets X. In particular, determine ms_r(X) for every regular convex polyhedron in R^n with n > 2, and determine ms_2(T) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3.
context_brief: Maximal symmetry numbers in higher-dimensional Euclidean space

question_text: For the sphere S^n, let S^+_2 be the family of non-identity involutive orientation-preserving isometries, that is, 180-degree rotations about lines through the center. Is ms_r(S^n, S^+_2) = 1/r^2 for all n, r > 1? Equivalently, does every measurable r-coloring of S^n contain a monochromatic subset of measure at least 1/r^2 that is symmetric with respect to some line through the center of the sphere?

For the finite interval n = {0, 1, ..., n-1} with counting measure and integer central symmetries, let bms_r(n) be the blurred maximal symmetry number obtained by taking the infimum over measurable blurred r-colorings. Calculate the values of bms_r(n), at least for small n and for r = 2.
context_brief: Blurred maximal symmetry numbers on finite intervals

question_text: Let I = [0,1] be the unit interval with Lebesgue measure and the family of central symmetries s_c(x) = 2c - x. Calculate the maximal symmetry numbers ms_r(I), at least in the first nontrivial case r = 2.
context_brief: Maximal symmetry numbers of the unit interval

question_text: In the asymptotic formula lim_{r→∞} r^2 · ms_r(I) = inf_{r∈N} r^2 · ms_r(I) = S', determine or estimate the constant S'. Is S' strictly larger than the constant S defined from the autoconvolution infimum appearing in the lower bound for ms_r(I)?
context_brief: Asymptotic constant for interval symmetry numbers

question_text: How quickly do the sequences {ms_r(n)/n}_{n=1}^∞ and {bms_r(n)/n}_{n=1}^∞ converge to their common limit ms_r(I) = bms_r(I)?
context_brief: Convergence rate from discrete to continuous interval symmetry numbers

question_text: Fix an integer r ≥ 1. For a compact Abelian group G with Haar measure and central symmetries s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c, determine exactly which groups satisfy ms_r(G) = 1/r^2.
context_brief: Compact Abelian groups with extremal symmetry number

question_text: For a finite group G of odd order, is the maximal symmetry number always strictly larger than 1/r^2 for every r > 1?
Given ε > 0 and an integer r > 1, does there exist a finite group G whose maximal symmetry number ms_r(G) is smaller than ε?
context_brief: How small finite-group symmetry numbers can be

question_text: Does there exist a connected compact group G for which ms_r(G) < 1/r^2 for some integer r? In particular, what are the exact values of ms_2(SO(3)) and of ms_2(S^3), where S^3 is the multiplicative group of unit quaternions?

Let G be an infinite group, and let MS_r(G) and MS_r^+(G) be the cardinal symmetry numbers defined using central symmetries and the cardinal-valued measures card and card^+. Must both MS_r(G) and MS_r^+(G) be infinite for every finite number of colors r? Equivalently, does every finite coloring of an infinite group contain monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite size?
context_brief: Cardinal symmetry numbers of infinite groups

question_text: Let G = SL(K), where K is an infinite field. Is the cardinal symmetry number MS_r^+(G) equal to |G|^+ for every finite number of colors r?
context_brief: Cardinal symmetry numbers of special linear groups

question_text: For the free group F_2 on two generators, is the cardinal symmetry number MS_r^+(F_2) uncountable for every finite number of colors r?
context_brief: Cardinal symmetry numbers of the free group F2

question_text: Let H^2 be the hyperbolic plane with the family of central symmetries s_c that reflect points through a midpoint c, and let mds_r(H^2) be the corresponding dimension symmetry number based on asymptotic dimension. Is mds_r(H^2) ≥ 0 for every r ≥ 2? Equivalently, does every r-coloring of H^2 contain an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset?
context_brief: Dimension symmetry in the hyperbolic plane

question_text: Given a symmetry measure space X = (X, µ, S), a number of colors r, and a threshold λ in the measure range, calculate the (r, λ)-centerpole number c_r^λ(X), meaning the smallest size of a subfamily S' ⊂ S such that every measurable r-coloring of X contains a monochromatic S'-symmetric measurable set of measure at least λ.

For Euclidean space R^n and the integer lattice Z^n, both equipped with central symmetries and asymptotic dimension, is it always true that c_r^0(R^n) = c_r^0(Z^n) for every r ≤ n? Here c_r^0 is the minimum number of centers needed to force an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset in every r-coloring.
context_brief: Comparing Euclidean and lattice centerpole numbers

question_text: Call a subset C ⊂ R^4 4-centerpole when the central symmetries with centers in C force an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset under every 4-coloring. Is every 12-element 4-centerpole subset of R^4 affinely equivalent to the sandwich Ξ^3_1, the 12-point subset of Z^4 whose slices {-1} × 2^3_{<1}, {0} × 2^3_{<3}, and {1} × 2^3_{>1} have 1, 7, and 4 points, respectively?
context_brief: Structure of minimal 4-centerpole sets in R4

question_text: Determine the (5,0)-centerpole number c_5^0(R^5) for Euclidean 5-space, that is, the smallest number of centers needed to force an unbounded monochromatic symmetric subset in every 5-coloring of R^5. The known bounds are 18 ≤ c_5^0(R^5) ≤ c_5^0(Z^5) ≤ 25.
What is the growth rate of the sequence {c_r^0(R^r)}_{r=1}^∞? Is it exponential or polynomial in r?
context_brief: Asymptotic growth of diagonal centerpole numbers

question_text: For Euclidean spaces R^n equipped with central symmetries, calculate or estimate the centerpole numbers c_r^λ(R^n) for various choices of the number of colors r, the threshold λ, and the dimension n.
Given an (Abelian) group G viewed as the symmetry measure space (G, asdim, S) with central symmetries, calculate or estimate its dimension symmetry numbers mds_r(G).
Given a group G viewed as the symmetry measure space (G, asdim, S) with central symmetries, calculate or estimate its centerpole numbers c_r^λ(G).
Does the free group F_2 have finite centerpole numbers c_r^0(F_2) for every integer r?
context_brief: Centerpole finiteness for the free group F2

question_text: For the free group F_2 on two generators, is the 2-color centerpole number c_2^0(F_2) equal to 4, 3, or 2?
context_brief: Exact two-color centerpole number for F2

question_text: Let phi(k, G) denote the number of k-matchings in a graph G. For integers q >= 1, r >= 1, and 1 <= k <= qr, is the maximum number of k-matchings among all simple r-regular graphs on 2qr vertices attained by the disjoint union of q copies of the complete bipartite graph K_{r,r}? Equivalently, does Theta(k, qr, r) = phi(k, qK_{r,r}) hold for every k = 1, ..., qr, where Theta(k, n, r) is the maximum of phi(k, G) over simple r-regular graphs G on 2n vertices?

Let phi(k, G) denote the number of k-matchings in G, and let lambda(k, n, r) be the minimum of phi(k, G) over all r-regular bipartite multigraphs G on 2n vertices. Is it always true that for every 1 <= k <= n, lambda(k, n, r) is at least ((n choose k)^2) * ((nr - k) / nr)^(rn-k) * ((kr) / n)^k?

Let omega(k, n, r) be the minimum number of k-matchings among r-regular r-colorable multigraphs on 2n vertices. For each fixed r >= 3, does the perfect-matching minimum omega(n, n, r) grow exponentially in n?

Let G be an infinite r-regular graph, and let h_G(p) denote its p-matching entropy, defined from finite graph approximations G_k by h_G(p) = limsup_{k->infty} log(phi(m_k, G_k)) / |V_k| when 2m_k / |V_k| -> p. If h_{inf K_{r,r}}(p) is the corresponding entropy for a countable disjoint union of copies of K_{r,r}, is it always true that h_G(p) <= h_{inf K_{r,r}}(p) for every p in [0, 1]?

Let omega(k, n, r) be the minimum number of k-matchings among r-regular r-colorable multigraphs on 2n vertices. For fixed r >= 2, fixed density p in (0, 2/3), and integers k in the range pn <= k <= 2n/3, does omega(k, n, r) grow exponentially in n, and can one prove a quantitatively good lower bound for that exponential growth?

Let Psi_{2n} be the convex set of 2n x 2n symmetric doubly stochastic matrices with zero diagonal whose extreme points are the adjacency matrices of perfect matchings in K_{2n}. For each 2 <= k <= n, determine or give a good general lower bound for mu_{k,n} := min_{B in Psi_{2n}} haf_k(B), where haf_k(B) is the k-haffnian of B.

Let mu_{n,n} be the minimum of the haffnian over Psi_{2n}, and let mu := lim_{n->infty} log(mu_{n,n}) / n, whose existence follows from subadditivity. Is mu finite from below; equivalently, does one have mu > -infinity?
context_brief: Weak van der Waerden analog for haffnians

question_text: Find an analog of the asymptotic lower matching conjecture for arbitrary infinite r-regular graphs, at least for matching densities p in [0, 2/3]. In other words, determine a lower-bound principle for p-matching entropy in the non-bipartite infinite regular setting that plays the role that ALMC plays for bipartite infinite regular graphs.

What is the correct analog of the asymptotic lower matching conjecture for infinite cubic connected graphs with no bridges? Equivalently, what lower-entropy statement should replace the bipartite ALMC in the bridgeless infinite 3-regular setting?

Determine what criteria decide whether a positive series sum a_n converges or diverges. Equivalently, is there a universal algorithmic convergence test, or any general structural pattern, that characterizes convergence versus divergence for arbitrary positive series?

Let A be a subset of the positive integers, and for an increasing function ϕ: N -> (0, ∞) with ϕ(n) -> ∞, define the weighted upper density by d̄_ϕ(A) = lim sup |A ∩ [1, n]| / ϕ(n). If d̄_{n/ln n}(A) > 0, must the harmonic subseries sum_{n in A} 1/n diverge? More generally, does the same conclusion hold for weights of the form n/[(ln n)(ln ln n)...(ln^(k) n)]?
context_brief: Weighted-density criteria for divergent harmonic subseries

question_text: If A is a set of positive integers such that the reciprocal series sum_{n in A} 1/n diverges, must A contain arithmetic progressions of arbitrarily large finite length?
context_brief: Erdos conjecture on divergent reciprocal sets

question_text: Is every topological group a quotient group of a zero-dimensional topological group of the same weight? More specifically, when a topological group is almost metrizable, meaning that it contains a compact subset of countable character, under what additional conditions is it a quotient of a zero-dimensional topological group of the same weight?

For a metrizable space X, under which conditions is the free universal algebra of an uncountable signature over X paracompact? In particular, if L(X) denotes the free topological linear space over X over the discrete field of real numbers, is L(X) paracompact?

Let X be a zero-dimensional compact homogeneous topological space. Let S(X) be the semigroup of all continuous self-maps of X, viewed as a subsemigroup of X^X with the topology of pointwise convergence. A semigroup with identity e is called left bounded if for every neighborhood U of e there is a finite subset F such that the whole semigroup equals F U. Must S(X) be left bounded for every zero-dimensional compact homogeneous space X?

Let X be a zero-dimensional homogeneous topological space, and let S(X) be the semigroup of all continuous self-maps of X with the topology of pointwise convergence. A semigroup with identity e is called right bounded if for every neighborhood U of e there is a finite subset F such that the whole semigroup equals U F. Must S(X) be right bounded for every zero-dimensional homogeneous space X?

Let X be a compact topological space, and let H be a subgroup of S(X), the semigroup of continuous self-maps of X. Suppose H acts transitively on X and is distal, meaning that for any distinct points x1 and x2 in X and any point x in X there exists a neighborhood U of x such that {h(x1), h(x2)} is not contained in U for all h in H. Must H be left bounded?

Let G be a bounded semitopological group or a bounded quasitopological group. Here bounded means that for every neighborhood U of the identity there is a finite subset F with G = F U and also G = U F. A semitopological group is a group whose topology is invariant under both left and right shifts, and a quasitopological group is a semitopological group with continuous inversion. Must every such bounded semitopological group, and every such bounded quasitopological group, have countable cellularity?

Does every zero-dimensional compact homogeneous space admit a left-topological group structure? Equivalently, if a compact space is zero-dimensional and homogeneous, must there exist a group operation on its underlying set together with a topology invariant under all left shifts x ↦ g x? In particular, if K is a first-countable zero-dimensional compact space, does its countable power K^ω admit the structure of a left-topological group?
context_brief: Left-topological group structures on homogeneous compacta

question_text: Let G be a compact left-topological group, meaning a group endowed with a topology invariant under all left shifts. Must G support a strictly positive probability Borel measure, that is, a Borel probability measure μ such that μ(U) > 0 for every nonempty open subset U of G?

Let G be a paratopological group. Suppose G is right ω-bounded, meaning that for every neighborhood U of the identity there exists a countable subset F of G such that G = U F. Must G also be left ω-bounded, meaning that for every neighborhood U of the identity there exists a countable subset F of G such that G = F U?

Does there exist a metrizable topological group G that is o-bounded, meaning that for every sequence (U_n) of neighborhoods of the identity there is a sequence (F_n) of finite subsets of G such that G is contained in the union of the sets F_n U_n, and for which Player I nevertheless has a winning strategy in the game OF(G)? In this game, at each stage n, Player I chooses a neighborhood U_n of the identity and Player II chooses a finite subset F_n of G; Player II wins exactly when G is contained in the union of the sets F_n U_n.
context_brief: O-bounded groups and the OF game

question_text: Let A be a compact subset of the real line R such that the difference set A − A = {a − a′ : a, a′ ∈ A} is a neighborhood of 0 in R. Must the fourfold sumset A + A + A + A have nonempty interior in R?

For each integer n >= 2 and each n-tuple of real numbers theta_1, ..., theta_n, must one always have lim inf_{q -> +infty} q * ||q theta_1|| * ... * ||q theta_n|| = 0? In other words, does the multidimensional Littlewood-type statement hold for every set of n real numbers once n is at least 2?

Suppose n >= 2 and Lambda is a lattice in R^(n+1) with positive homogeneous minimum N(Lambda) > 0, where N(Lambda) is the infimum of |z_0 z_1 ... z_n| over nonzero lattice points z = (z_0, ..., z_n). Must every such lattice be algebraic?

Let BAD(alpha, beta, gamma; delta) be the set of xi = (theta_1, theta_2, theta_3) in [0,1]^3 such that inf_p max{p^alpha ||p theta_1||, p^beta ||p theta_2||, p^gamma ||p theta_3||} >= delta, and let BAD(alpha, beta, gamma) be the union of these sets over delta > 0, where alpha + beta + gamma = 1. For two distinct triples (alpha_1, beta_1, gamma_1) and (alpha_2, beta_2, gamma_2), is the intersection BAD(alpha_1, beta_1, gamma_1) ∩ BAD(alpha_2, beta_2, gamma_2) nonempty?

For a fixed prime p and any real number theta, must one always have lim inf_{q -> +infty} q |q|_p ||q theta|| = 0? Equivalently, for irrational theta, is it true or false that inf_{n,q in Z_+} q ||p^n q theta|| = 0?

In the homogeneous Peres-Schlag setting, where a sequence (t_j) satisfies t_{j+1}/t_j >= 1 + 1/M and one seeks a real alpha with all ||alpha t_j|| bounded away from zero, what is the correct order of approximation? More specifically, can Theorem 9 be improved beyond the lower bound gamma/(M log M), and what is the optimal dependence on M in the homogeneous case?

In Theorem 8, one assumes a function psi(t) that increases to infinity and then constructs real numbers theta_1, theta_2, eta_1, eta_2 with inf_{x in Z_+} x psi(x) ||x theta_1 - eta_1|| ||x theta_2 - eta_2|| > 0. Can the same conclusion still hold when psi(t) is the positive constant psi_0 for all t, rather than a function tending to infinity? If not, the paper notes that this would imply a stronger inhomogeneous version of Littlewood's conjecture.

Fix alpha, beta in (0,1) with alpha + beta = 1. Harrap proved that for a fixed vector (theta_1, theta_2) in BAD(alpha, beta), the set of shifts (eta_1, eta_2) such that inf_q max(q^alpha ||q theta_1 - eta_1||, q^beta ||q theta_2 - eta_2||) > 0 has full Hausdorff dimension. Does the same full-dimension statement, and even the winning-set statement, remain true without assuming that (theta_1, theta_2) belongs to BAD(alpha, beta)?

For fixed dimensions m and n and fixed norms on R^m and R^n, let z_nu = (x_nu, y_nu) be the sequence of best-approximation vectors, let M_nu = |x_nu|, and define G(Theta) = lim inf_{nu -> infinity} M_nu^(1/nu). What is the optimal lower bound for inf_Theta G(Theta), where Theta ranges over matrices satisfying the paper's nondegeneracy condition?

For a pair Theta = (theta_1, theta_2) of real numbers linearly independent together with 1, define psi_+(t) as the minimum of ||theta_1 x_1 + theta_2 x_2|| over positive integers x_1, x_2 with max(x_1, x_2) <= t, and define omega_+(Theta) by the decay rate of t^gamma psi_+(t). What is the optimal value of inf omega_+(Theta) in this two-variable positive-integer problem? In particular, is the optimal exponent equal to phi, equal to sigma, or something strictly between them?

For m >= 3 and numbers 1, theta_1, ..., theta_m linearly independent over Z, define omega_+(Theta) from approximation of the linear form theta_1 x_1 + ... + theta_m x_m by positive integers x_i. Does there exist such a collection with omega_+(Theta) < 2? The paper explicitly asks this first for m = 3 and then suggests the same possibility for arbitrary m.
context_brief: Existence of omega plus below two

question_text: Does there exist an absolute constant k such that for every positive integer q one can choose an integer a coprime to q whose continued fraction expansion a/q = [b_0; b_1, ..., b_s] has all partial quotients bounded by k? The paper also records Zaremba's stronger original guess that k = 5.

Fix integers s and q with gcd(s,q) = 1, and a digit set D = {d_0, ..., d_k} with 0 = d_0 < d_1 < ... < d_k < s, 1 <= k <= s - 2, and gcd(d_0, ..., d_k) = 1. Let K_s^D(N) be the set of positive integers x < N whose base-s digits all lie in D. Is it true that for some sufficiently large sigma > 0, whenever N >= q^sigma, every residue class lambda modulo q is represented by some x in K_s^D(N)?

In Theorem 29, a multiplicative subgroup R = v·U modulo a prime p is required to have size at least 10^8 p^(7/8) log^(5/2) p in order to guarantee an element a in R with bounded continued-fraction sum and hence discrepancy D(a,p) << log p log log p. Can the exponent 7/8 in that size condition be replaced by a smaller exponent?

For each dimension s >= 2 and positive integer q, let D(a_1, ..., a_s; q) be the discrepancy of the multidimensional Korobov-Hlawka sequence defined in the paper. Is the true order of min_{(a_1,...,a_s) in Z^s} D(a_1, ..., a_s; q) bounded by O_s((log q)^(s-1))? Equivalently, can the extra factor log log q in Bykovskii's bound O_s((log q)^(s-1) log log q) be removed?
context_brief: Remove log log from discrepancy bound

question_text: If d_n denotes the Fourier-Stieltjes coefficient integral_0^1 cos(2 pi n x) d?(x) of the Minkowski question mark function, does d_n tend to 0 as n goes to infinity?
context_brief: Salem problem for question mark function

question_text: The paper notes that the equation ?(x) = x on [0,1] has at least five solutions. Does it in fact have exactly five solutions?
context_brief: Fixed points of question mark function

question_text: Let R_n be the remainder term in formula (67), where the main term is 2^n integral_0^1 (?(x) - x)^2 dx for the Stern-Brocot points xi_{j,n}. Is it true that R_n tends to 0 as n tends to infinity?

For the Denjoy-Tichy-Uitz family g_lambda with lambda in (0,1), determine the threshold functions kappa_1(lambda) and kappa_2(lambda) defined by the growth rate of the partial-quotient sums S_t(x): kappa_1(lambda) is the supremum of kappa for which lim sup S_t(x)/t < kappa forces g_lambda'(x) = +infinity, and kappa_2(lambda) is the infimum of kappa for which lim inf S_t(x)/t > kappa forces g_lambda'(x) = 0.

Let f(n) denote the number of partitions of the integer n for which every nonzero multiplicity of a part is distinct. The paper proves the first-order asymptotic behavior of ln f(n). What are the lower-order terms in the asymptotic expansion of ln f(n)?
context_brief: Lower-order asymptotics of log-count of Wilf partitions

question_text: Let f(n) denote the number of partitions of the integer n for which every nonzero multiplicity of a part is distinct. Determine the first-order asymptotic behavior of f(n) itself, not just of ln f(n).
context_brief: First-order asymptotics of Wilf partition counts

question_text: Let f(n) denote the number of partitions of the integer n for which every nonzero multiplicity of a part is distinct. Is f(n) a nondecreasing function of n; that is, does f(n + 1) >= f(n) for all positive integers n?

Let T(n) be the set of partitions of n in which all nonzero multiplicities are distinct, and let sigma_n be the involution on T(n) obtained by interchanging the list of parts with the list of multiplicities and then reordering so that the multiplicities are increasing. Determine the asymptotic number of fixed points of sigma_n.
context_brief: Fixed points of the parts-multiplicities involution

question_text: For a one-dimensional excited random walk X = (X_n)_{n >= 0}, find conditions that force a zero-one law for the directional escape events. In other words, determine hypotheses under which each of P_0[sup_n X_n = infinity], P_0[inf_n X_n = -infinity], P_0[X_n -> infinity], and P_0[X_n -> -infinity] belongs to {0,1}.
context_brief: One-dimensional zero-one laws for directional escape

question_text: Consider the one-dimensional recurrence/transience criterion for excited random walks under the assumptions that the family of cookie stacks is i.i.d., that there is a deterministic bound M with M(z) <= M almost surely for every site z (so each site has only boundedly many non-placebo cookies), and that every direction remains possible at every site and visit in the weak-ellipticity sense. Can the i.i.d. assumption on the cookie stacks be weakened to the stationary-and-ergodic assumption while keeping the same recurrence/transience conclusion?
context_brief: Replace IID by stationary ergodic in one-dimensional criterion

question_text: In the transient one-dimensional case, compute the probability that an excited random walk started at 0 never returns to its starting point, namely P_0[for all n >= 1, X_n != 0].
context_brief: One-dimensional non-return probability in transient regime

question_text: For dimension d >= 2 and a nonzero direction l in R^d, find conditions that imply a zero-one law for directional transience, namely that P_0[A_l] is always either 0 or 1, where A_l is the event that X_n · l tends to infinity. In particular, are the assumptions of i.i.d. cookie stacks, a deterministic bound on the number of non-placebo cookies per site, and uniform ellipticity sufficient?
context_brief: Multidimensional zero-one law for directional transience

question_text: For dimension d >= 2, suppose the family of cookie stacks is i.i.d. and uniformly elliptic, meaning there exists kappa > 0 such that every transition probability ω(z,e,i) is at least kappa almost surely. Must the excited random walk always fall into one of the two global behaviors: recurrence, meaning every site is visited infinitely often almost surely, or transience, meaning no site is visited infinitely often almost surely?

Consider a balanced excited random walk, meaning that for every site z, direction e, and visit number i one has ω(z,e,i) = ω(z,-e,i), so the local cookies do not create directional bias. Under uniform ellipticity and either i.i.d. or stationary-and-ergodic cookie environments, is every such walk recurrent in dimension 2 and transient in dimensions d >= 3?
context_brief: Balanced excited random walks in dimensions two and higher

question_text: Assume the family of cookie stacks is i.i.d. and elliptic, so every transition probability ω(z,e,i) is strictly positive almost surely, and fix a nonzero direction l in R^d. On the event that the walk does not escape to infinity in norm, does the directional speed X_n · l / n converge almost surely to 0 as n tends to infinity?
context_brief: Directional speed on the non-escape event

question_text: In the one-dimensional speed theorem that assumes i.i.d. cookie stacks, weak ellipticity, and a deterministic bound on the number of non-placebo cookies per site, can the boundedness assumption be replaced by the weaker positivity condition that every cookie has nonnegative drift in the +1 direction?
context_brief: Replacing bounded cookies by positive-drift cookies in ballisticity

question_text: At the critical one-dimensional scaling regime δ = 1, Theorem 6.3 proves convergence to the running maximum of Brownian motion under the assumptions of i.i.d. cookie stacks, boundedly many non-placebo cookies per site, and weak ellipticity. If one instead assumes the broader condition (6.2) from Theorem 6.1 - namely stationary ergodic cookie stacks, nonnegative drift in the +1 direction, uniform ellipticity, and the additional integrability requirement stated there - does the same limit theorem remain true? If it does, can the positive-drift assumption also be removed?
context_brief: Critical scaling limit under weaker assumptions

question_text: Find probability measures P on cookie environments - excluding measures that merely encode ordinary random walk in random environment - such that for P-almost every environment ω, the quenched law of either the hitting time T_n or the position X_n, after whatever centering and normalization are needed, converges weakly to a nondegenerate limit distribution as n tends to infinity.
context_brief: Quenched central limit behavior beyond RWRE-type models

question_text: A pure O-sequence is the h-vector of a pure monomial order ideal, where all maximal monomials have the same degree; its type is the number of maximal monomials. What is the largest type t for which every pure O-sequence is unimodal, without imposing any restriction on codimension or socle degree? In particular, does unimodality always hold for pure O-sequences of type 2?

A pure O-sequence is the h-vector of a pure monomial order ideal, and codimension is the number of variables in the ambient polynomial ring. For a fixed codimension r, what is the largest type t for which every pure O-sequence of codimension r is unimodal?
context_brief: Unimodality threshold by codimension and type

question_text: A pure O-sequence is the h-vector of a pure monomial order ideal; its socle degree is the common degree of the maximal monomials, and codimension is the number of variables. For a fixed codimension r, what is the largest socle degree e for which every pure O-sequence of codimension r and socle degree e is unimodal?
context_brief: Unimodality threshold by codimension and socle degree

question_text: What is the smallest codimension r for which there exists a nonunimodal pure O-sequence of socle degree 4?

Let #P(*, e, t) denote the number of pure O-sequences of socle degree e and type t. For fixed e, determine the asymptotic behavior of #P(*, e, t) as t becomes large; in particular, what is the correct order of magnitude of #P(*, e, t)?

A pure f-vector is the rank vector of a pure simplicial complex, equivalently a pure O-sequence generated by squarefree monomials. What is the smallest number of variables n, equivalently the smallest number of vertices of the underlying simplicial complex, for which a nonunimodal pure f-vector can exist?
context_brief: Minimum variables for nonunimodal pure f-vectors

question_text: A matroid can be identified with a pure simplicial complex whose restriction to any subset of the vertex set is also pure. For such matroid complexes, are the face vectors (f-vectors) always unimodal, or even log-concave? What about the corresponding h-vectors?
If Delta is a matroid complex and S/I_Delta is its Stanley-Reisner ring, is the h-vector of S/I_Delta always a pure O-sequence?
Does every complete intersection have the Weak Lefschetz Property, meaning that multiplication by a general linear form has maximal rank in the case d = 1?
context_brief: Weak Lefschetz property for complete intersections

question_text: For the class of pure O-sequences, if two sequences agree in every entry except one and the differing entries differ by a positive integer alpha, must every intermediate value also occur in a pure O-sequence? In particular, does this Interval Conjecture for Pure O-sequences remain true in three variables?

Classify all finite projective planes, or at least determine exactly which integers q can occur as their orders. Here a projective plane is a collection of points and lines in which any two lines intersect in exactly one point and any two points lie on exactly one line; when the plane is finite, the number of points is q^2 + q + 1 and each line contains q + 1 points.

Does there exist a Steiner system S(4, 5, 21), that is, a 21-element set together with a collection of 5-element blocks such that every 4-element subset is contained in exactly one block? Equivalently, is the sequence (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197) a pure O-sequence?

Does there exist an explicit function f : F2^n -> F2, computable in NP, such that for every F2-polynomial p : F2^n -> F2 of degree at most log_2 n, the correlation satisfies |E[(-1)^<f(x), p(x)>]| <= 1/n?
context_brief: Correlation bounds for low-degree F2 polynomials

question_text: If a in R^n has Euclidean norm ||a||_2 = 1, must the probability over a uniform random x in {-1,1}^n satisfy Pr[|<a,x>| <= 1] >= 1/2?
Let f : {-1,1}^n -> R_{>=0} satisfy E[f] = 1, and fix 0 < rho < 1. Must the upper tail of the noise operator obey Pr[T_rho f >= t] < o(1/t)?
For every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, is the degree deg(f) bounded above by a polynomial in the sensitivity sens[f], where sens[f] = max_x |{i in [n] : f(x) != f(x^i)}|?

Among degree-k polynomial threshold functions f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, is the one with maximal total influence always the symmetric threshold f(x) = sgn(p(x_1 + ... + x_n)), where p is a degree-k univariate polynomial alternating sign on the k+1 values of x_1 + ... + x_n closest to 0?
If a nonempty set A subseteq F2^n satisfies |A + A| <= C|A|, must A be coverable by poly(C) affine subspaces, each having cardinality at most |A|?

Let f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} be computable by a DNF of size s > 1, and let epsilon in (0,1/2]. Is the Fourier spectrum of f always epsilon-concentrated on some collection F with |F| <= s^{O(log(1/epsilon))}?

Let T be a finite collection of vectors in R^n. Define b(T) = E_{x ~ {-1,1}^n}[max_{t in T} <t,x>] and define g(T) analogously with x replaced by a standard Gaussian vector.
