Does there always exist a finite collection T' such that g(T') <= O(b(T)) and for every t in T there exists t' in T' with ||t - t'||_1 <= O(b(T))?
Is there a universal constant C such that every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} satisfies H[\hat{f}^2] <= C * I[f], where H[\hat{f}^2] is the spectral entropy and I[f] is the total influence?
If f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is a linear threshold function on an odd number n of variables, must it satisfy Stab_rho[f] >= Stab_rho[Maj_n] for every rho in [0,1]?
context_brief: Noise stability of majority among LTFs

question_text: Fix r in N, odd n, and 0 < epsilon < 1/2. For f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, let P(f) be the probability that r independent epsilon-noisy copies of a uniform x all give the same output under f. Among odd functions f, is P(f) always maximized by a majority function Maj_k on some odd number k of inputs?
context_brief: Optimality of majority for correlation distillation

question_text: If f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is the intersection of k linear threshold functions, must its noise sensitivity satisfy NS_delta[f] <= O(sqrt(log k)) * sqrt(delta)?

Let f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} be unbiased. For a random restriction z in {-1,0,1}^n where each coordinate is independently +1 or -1 with probability p/2 each and 0 with probability 1-p, with p < 1/2 and n odd, is E_z[|f(z)|] maximized when f is the majority function, identifying f with its multilinear expansion?

Let A subseteq F2^n. If one must remove epsilon * 2^n elements from A to make it triangle-free, meaning there do not exist x, y, x+y in A, must the probability over uniform independent x,y in F2^n satisfy Pr[x,y,x+y in A] >= poly(epsilon)?
Fix a constant alpha > 0. If A subseteq F2^n has density at least alpha, must A + A contain a subspace of codimension O(sqrt(n))?
If f : {-1,1}^n -> [-1,1] has degree at most k, must there exist a coordinate i in [n] with influence Inf_i[f] >= (Var[f]/k)^{O(1)}?
context_brief: Influence lower bounds for bounded low-degree functions

question_text: Fix a possibly infinite collection of affine constraints {(M_1,sigma_1),(M_2,sigma_2),...} over F2. For each n, let P_n be the property that a function f : F2^n -> {0,1} is (M_i,sigma_i)-free for every i. Must there exist a one-sided-error constant-query property-testing algorithm for P_n?

Fix 0 <= rho, mu, nu <= 1. If A,B subseteq R^n have Gaussian measures mu and nu respectively and A is centrally symmetric, A = -A, what is the minimum possible value of Pr[x in A, y in B] when (x,y) are rho-correlated n-dimensional Gaussian vectors?

Fix 0 <= rho <= 1. Among all partitions of R^n into q parts of equal Gaussian measure, where 3 <= q <= n+1, is the maximum noise stability at rho achieved by a standard simplex partition, and for -1 <= rho <= 0 does the standard simplex partition minimize the noise stability?
context_brief: Gaussian simplex partitions and noise stability

question_text: For every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, is the sum of the absolute values of the linear Fourier coefficients bounded by sqrt(deg(f))?

Fix d in N and epsilon in (0,1). What is the least k = k(d,epsilon) such that every degree-d polynomial threshold event over a k-wise independent Gaussian-marginal random vector X approximates the corresponding event under a standard Gaussian vector Z within additive error epsilon; that is, |Pr[p(X) >= 0] - Pr[p(Z) >= 0]| <= epsilon for every degree-d polynomial p : R^n -> R?

For each constant delta > 0, do s^{-O(1)}-biased densities delta-fool all size-s DNF formulas; equivalently, if f : {0,1}^n -> {-1,1} is computable by a size-s DNF and phi is an s^{-O(1)}-biased density on {0,1}^n, must |E_{x~{0,1}^n}[f(x)] - E_{y~phi}[f(y)]| <= delta?
Does every polynomial threshold function representation of the inner product mod 2 function IP_{2n} : F2^{2n} -> {-1,1} require at least 3^n monomials?
context_brief: PTF sparsity for inner product mod 2

question_text: Fix any epsilon > 0. Is every monotone Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} epsilon-close to a junta whose size is polynomial in deg(f)?
context_brief: Monotone functions close to low-degree juntas

question_text: If f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is monotone, must its total influence satisfy I[f] < o(sens[f])?
What is the least possible degree of a function f : {-1,1}^n -> [-1,-2/3] union [2/3,1] such that f(x) lies in [2/3,1] whenever sum_i x_i >= n/2 and lies in [-1,-2/3] whenever sum_i x_i <= -n/2?

Suppose q_1, ..., q_m : F2^n -> F2 are degree-at-most-2 polynomials and the indicator of the all-ones vector, namely AND : F2^n -> {-1,1}, can be written as AND(x) = sum_{i=1}^m c_i (-1)^{q_i(x)} for real coefficients c_i. What lower bound on m is necessary?

Let A be a self-adjoint cyclic operator on a Hilbert space, let φ be a cyclic vector for A, and let A_alpha = A + alpha(·, φ)φ be a rank-one perturbation with spectral measure mu_alpha taken with respect to φ. Characterize the singular continuous part of mu_alpha in terms of the unperturbed spectral measure mu.
context_brief: Singular continuous spectrum under rank-one perturbation

question_text: Fix an interval I contained in R and a subset B contained in R. Can one construct a family of measures {mu_beta} such that for every subset J of I the singular part of mu_beta gives J positive mass exactly for parameters beta in B, while the absolutely continuous part of mu_beta gives J positive mass for every beta in R?

For the discrete random Schrodinger operator in dimension d >= 2 with independent identically distributed site variables having the uniform law on [-c, c], does the operator have purely singular spectrum for every c > 0? The paper notes that this is already known when c is above a dimension-dependent threshold.
context_brief: Higher-dimensional Anderson model with uniform disorder

question_text: For the discrete random Schrodinger operator in dimension d >= 2 with Bernoulli site variables omega_j taking the values +1 and -1 with equal probability, does the operator have purely singular spectrum?
context_brief: Higher-dimensional Anderson model with Bernoulli disorder

question_text: For finite-rank unitary perturbations of rank n > 1, extend the classical proof of the equivalence between an inner characteristic operator function and purely singular spectrum to the higher-rank setting, and use that extension to derive explicit density formulas for the absolutely continuous part of the spectral measure.

For higher-rank unitary perturbations, determine which parts of Aronszajn-Donoghue theory survive after the necessary modifications from the rank-one setting, especially when scalar spectral measures are replaced by vector-valued measures.

In the Aleksandrov-Clark setting for a non-inner characteristic function theta, interpret formula (6.3) for the adjoint Clark operator and find a useful expression for Phi*_1 f that does not involve the projection P_theta.
context_brief: Interpretation of the non-inner Clark-operator formula

question_text: For f in L^2(mu_gamma), can one control the jump across the unit circle of the normalized Cauchy transform of f mu_gamma, and can that control be used to generalize the connection with pseudocontinuation?
context_brief: Jump behavior of normalized Cauchy transforms

question_text: Determine how the boundary values of the characteristic function theta are related to the spectral behavior of the rank-one unitary perturbations U_gamma.
Kapustin's restriction is equivalent to the condition integral log |theta| > -infinity. Does that analytic condition admit an interpretation purely in spectral terms?
context_brief: Spectral meaning of an integrability condition

question_text: Does there exist a Banach algebra A that is approximately amenable, meaning that every continuous derivation D: A -> X* into the dual of any Banach A-bimodule X is approximately inner, but is not boundedly approximately amenable, meaning that one cannot choose the approximating inner derivations so that they form a bounded net of operators from A into X*?

Does there exist a Banach algebra A that is boundedly approximately amenable, meaning that every continuous derivation D: A -> X* into the dual of any Banach A-bimodule X is boundedly approximately inner, but is not boundedly approximately contractible, meaning that there is some Banach A-bimodule X for which a continuous derivation D: A -> X is not boundedly approximately inner?

If a Banach algebra A is approximately amenable, meaning that every continuous derivation from A into the dual of any Banach A-bimodule is approximately inner, must A also be pseudo-amenable, meaning that A has an approximate diagonal (u_i) in the projective tensor product A \hat{\otimes} A such that a u_i - u_i a -> 0 and \u03c0(u_i)a -> a for all a in A?

If a Banach algebra A is approximately amenable, meaning that every continuous derivation from A into the dual of any Banach A-bimodule is approximately inner, must A have a two-sided approximate identity, and must it even have a bounded approximate identity?

If A and B are approximately amenable Banach algebras, meaning that every continuous derivation from each algebra into the dual of any bimodule is approximately inner, must their direct-sum Banach algebra A \u2295 B also be approximately amenable?
context_brief: Direct sums of approximately amenable algebras

question_text: If A and B are approximately amenable Banach algebras, must their projective tensor product A \hat{\otimes} B be approximately amenable? Likewise, if A and B are pseudo-amenable Banach algebras, must A \hat{\otimes} B be pseudo-amenable?

Suppose T: A -> B is a Banach algebra homomorphism with dense range. If A has one of the generalized amenability properties discussed here, such as approximate amenability or pseudo-amenability, must B inherit the same property?

Let A be a boundedly approximately contractible Banach algebra, and let J be a closed ideal of finite codimension in A. Must J have a bounded approximate identity, extending the known codimension-1 case?

Let A be a pseudo-amenable Banach algebra, or an approximately amenable Banach algebra that already has an approximate identity. Under what additional conditions must a closed ideal of A have a two-sided approximate identity?
For a locally compact group G, how can one characterize when the Fourier algebra A(G) is pseudo-amenable and when it is approximately amenable?
Is every nontrivial Segal algebra non-approximately amenable?

Let G be a locally compact group and omega a continuous weight function on G. Is the Beurling algebra L^1(G, omega) approximately amenable, equivalently pseudo-amenable in this bounded-approximate-identity setting, exactly when it is amenable?
How can one characterize approximate amenability and pseudo-amenability of the semigroup algebra l^1(S) of a semigroup S?
Does there exist a uniform algebra that is not amenable but is approximately amenable or pseudo-amenable?

Let X be a Banach space and let K(X) denote the Banach algebra of compact operators on X with composition multiplication and the operator norm topology. Under what conditions is K(X) approximately amenable, and under what conditions is it pseudo-amenable?
Does there exist a C*-algebra that is approximately amenable but not amenable? If such C*-algebras exist, how can approximate amenability be characterized within the class of C*-algebras?
If S^1(G) is a Segal algebra on a locally compact amenable group G, must S^1(G) be pseudo-amenable?

Suppose x is a nicely defined cardinal invariant such that x = ℵ1 already forces the failure of the strong polarized relation \( inom{x}{\omega} 	o  inom{x}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\), meaning there is a 2-coloring of x×ω with no monochromatic rectangle A×B satisfying |A| = x and |B| = ω. Must it follow that x is the continuum c?

Is it consistent that the splitting number s equals ℵ1 and nevertheless the strong polarized relation \( inom{s}{\omega} 	o  inom{s}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds, meaning every 2-coloring of s×ω has a monochromatic rectangle A×B with |A| = s and |B| = ω?
Is it consistent that the splitting number s is strictly larger than ℵ2 and that the strong polarized relation \( inom{s}{\omega} 	o  inom{s}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) still holds?
context_brief: Large splitting number with positive relation

question_text: Is it consistent that the splitting number s equals the ultrafilter number u and still every 2-coloring of s×ω admits a monochromatic rectangle of sizes s and ω, i.e. \( inom{s}{\omega} 	o  inom{s}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?
Is it consistent that the splitting number s is strictly smaller than the continuum c while the positive strong polarized relation \( inom{s}{\omega} 	o  inom{s}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?

Is it consistent that the dominating number d equals ℵ1 and that every 2-coloring of d×ω has a monochromatic rectangle A×B with |A| = d and |B| = ω, that is, \( inom{d}{\omega} 	o  inom{d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?
Is it consistent that the dominating number d is singular and nevertheless the strong polarized relation \( inom{d}{\omega} 	o  inom{d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
Is it consistent that the dominating number d is at most the ultrafilter number u and still the positive relation \( inom{d}{\omega} 	o  inom{d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
Assume the positive relation \( inom{d}{\omega} 	o  inom{d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds. After adding λ many random reals for some λ > d, must that same positive relation for d and ω still hold?
Is it consistent that the independence number i equals ℵ1 and that the strong polarized relation \( inom{i}{\omega} 	o  inom{i}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
Is it consistent that the independence number i is at most the ultrafilter number u and still \( inom{i}{\omega} 	o  inom{i}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?

Can a real-valued measurable cardinal κ satisfy the positive strong polarized relation \( inom{\kappa}{\omega} 	o  inom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\), meaning every 2-coloring of κ×ω has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes κ and ω?

Is it consistent that the continuum c is strictly larger than ℵ2 and that for every cardinal κ in the interval [ℵ1, c], every 2-coloring of κ×ω has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes κ and ω, i.e. \( inom{\kappa}{\omega} 	o  inom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?

Is it consistent that the splitting number equals the continuum and both are larger than ℵ2, while for every κ in [ℵ1, c]—including κ = s itself—the strong polarized relation \( inom{\kappa}{\omega} 	o  inom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?

Is it consistent that ℵω is the only breaking point in the positive spectrum of strong polarized relations? More generally, can the continuum c be arbitrarily large while the only breaking points in that spectrum are exactly the cardinals of countable cofinality?
context_brief: Breaking points of the positive spectrum

question_text: Is it consistent that the positive polarized spectrum has two distinct breaking points below ℵω?

Is it consistent that the almost-disjointness number a equals the splitting number s and yet every 2-coloring of a×ω has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes a and ω, that is, \( inom{a}{\omega} 	o  inom{a}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?

Is the positive strong polarized relation for the pseudointersection number p exactly equivalent to p < s? In other words, does \( inom{p}{\omega} 	o  inom{p}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) hold if and only if p is strictly less than the splitting number s?

Suppose ℵ1 < κ < λ = c and the positive relation \( inom{\kappa}{\omega} 	o  inom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds. After forcing with the Lévy collapse P = Levy(κ, λ), is it possible that in the extension the full positive relation for κ and ω fails?
context_brief: Lévy collapse destroys the full relation

question_text: Is it consistent that the club principle ♣_{ℵ1} holds and at the same time the strong polarized relation \( inom{\omega_1}{\omega} 	o  inom{\omega_1}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?

For every successor cardinal κ, must the negative relation \((2^κ over κ) ↛ (2^κ over κ)^(1,1)_2\) hold? Equivalently, is there always a 2-coloring of 2^κ × κ with no monochromatic rectangle of sizes 2^κ and κ?
For every inaccessible cardinal κ that is not weakly compact, must the negative relation \((2^κ over κ) ↛ (2^κ over κ)^(1,1)_2\) hold?

If κ is measurable, is there a forcing extension that preserves the measurability of κ and makes the positive relation \( inom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} 	o  inom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2\) hold? Likewise, can the same be done when κ is only strongly compact?

Is it consistent that for some weakly compact cardinal κ that is not measurable, every 2-coloring of κ^+ × κ has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes κ^+ and κ, i.e. \( inom{\kappa^+}{\kappa} 	o  inom{\kappa^+}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2\)?
Suppose κ is regular and not weakly compact. Does ZFC prove the negative relation \((κ^+ over κ) ↛ (κ^+ over κ)^(1,1)_2\)?
context_brief: ZFC negative result below weak compactness

question_text: Let λ be a strong limit singular cardinal. Is it consistent that either every 2-coloring of λ^+ × λ has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes λ^+ and λ, or every 2-coloring of 2^λ × λ has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes 2^λ and λ; equivalently, can \( inom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} 	o  inom{\lambda^+}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2\) and \( inom{2^\lambda}{\lambda} 	o  inom{2^\lambda}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2\) consistently hold for such λ?

Suppose λ is singular of countable cofinality and GCH holds below λ in the sense that every θ < λ satisfies 2^θ = θ^+. Is it consistent that either \( inom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} 	o  inom{\lambda^+}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2\) or \( inom{2^\lambda}{\lambda} 	o  inom{2^\lambda}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2\) holds?

Suppose λ is singular and 2^λ > λ^+. Does ZFC prove that for every α < λ^+, every 2-coloring of λ^+ × λ has a monochromatic rectangle A×B with |A| = α and |B| = λ, i.e. \((λ^+ over λ) → (α over λ)^(1,1)_2\) for all α < λ^+?
If λ is singular and not a strong limit cardinal, does ZFC prove the negative relation \((λ^+ over λ) ↛ (λ^+ over λ)^(1,1)_2\)?
context_brief: Failure when λ is not strong limit

question_text: Let λ be a strong limit singular cardinal that is not a limit of measurable cardinals. Is it consistent that for every cardinal µ with λ < µ ≤ 2^λ, every 2-coloring of µ×λ has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes µ and λ; equivalently, does \( inom{\mu}{\lambda} 	o  inom{\mu}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2\) hold throughout the whole interval (λ, 2^λ]?
context_brief: Positive interval above a singular λ

question_text: For the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB, which gradings by small finite abelian groups preserve the algebraic or coalgebraic structure? More concretely, for groups such as Z2, Z3, Z4, and Z2 × Z2, classify the group actions or coactions that turn these paraparticle algebras into graded module algebras or graded module coalgebras.

For each grading of the paraparticle algebras under consideration, what braided group structures are possible? Equivalently, determine the compatible bicharacters, universal R-matrices of the corresponding group Hopf algebras, and braidings on the associated module or comodule categories, and decide which of these choices support compatible graded algebra and coalgebra structures that actually produce a braided group.

Can one apply or develop bosonization, or bosonization-like constructions, that convert the graded and braided paraparticle Hopf structures into ordinary Hopf structures with trivial braiding while preserving equivalent representation theory?

Can the braided-tensor-product method be completed to give explicit Fock-like representations of the infinite-degree-of-freedom parabosonic algebra PB? In particular, can one develop the needed multinomial theorem for the anticommuting creation operators that arise in the graded tensor-product realization, so that the action of PB generators and the corresponding matrix elements can be computed explicitly?

When one decomposes the graded tensor-product representations built for PB and PF, do irreducible components appear beyond the known p-Fock-like modules? In other words, can these decompositions produce direct summands or more general submodules that are not equivalent to the standard p-Fock-like representations?

Can the same braided-representation strategy be extended from PB and PF to the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB by viewing Ws and Was as suitable graded quotient algebras? To make that extension work, can one develop the required multinomial theorem that handles expressions mixing commuting and anticommuting variables?

Do the proposed paraparticle Hamiltonians built from a monochromatic parabosonic field and a (p + 1)-level system yield exactly solvable generalizations of the Jaynes-Cummings model? If so, can one compute their energy levels, eigenfunctions, and transition rates and compare those predictions directly with theoretical and experimental results?

Determine the exact enumeration and asymptotic growth of permutations that avoid the classical pattern 1324. In particular, determine the Stanley-Wilf limit for 1324-avoiding permutations and, if possible, an exact formula or asymptotic description for the number of 1324-avoiders of length n.
Prove or refute the conjectured upper bound SW(1324) < e*pi*sqrt(2/3) for the Stanley-Wilf limit of the classical pattern 1324.
Prove or refute that for every fixed inversion count k, the number of 1324-avoiding permutations of length n having exactly k inversions is an increasing function of n.
For each pattern length k, determine whether the largest Stanley-Wilf limit among all classical patterns of length k is always attained by a layered pattern.

For each positive integer k, determine the form of the layered permutation pattern of length k that is avoided by the largest number of permutations, equivalently the layered pattern of length k that is most easily avoided.
For every even integer k, prove or refute that the layered pattern of length k with layers (1, 2, 2, ..., 2, 2, 1) is the most avoided pattern among all patterns of length k.
For every integer k congruent to 1 modulo 4, prove or refute that the most avoided pattern of length k is the layered pattern with symmetric layer sizes (1, 2, ..., 2, 3, 2, ..., 2, 1).

Determine whether there exist two permutation patterns whose avoidance counts switch relative order more than once, and in particular whether two patterns can switch places infinitely often as n grows.
Determine whether the bound 2.25*k^2 is the best possible general upper bound for the Stanley-Wilf limit of a classical permutation pattern of length k.
Characterize completely the intervals [σ, τ] in the permutation pattern poset whose Möbius function satisfies μ(σ, τ) = 0.
Characterize the intervals [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset for which the absolute value |μ(σ, π)| of the Möbius function equals the number of occurrences of σ in π.
Find a bound for |μ(σ, τ)| in the permutation pattern poset that depends only on the number of occurrences of σ in τ, without requiring additional structure such as separability.
Determine for which permutations σ and π the order complex Δ(σ, π) of the interior of the interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset has the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres.

Let Γ be the subcomplex of Δ(σ, π) induced by those permutations τ in the interval [σ, π] with μ(σ, τ) not equal to 0. Determine whether Γ must always be pure, meaning that all of its maximal simplices have the same dimension.

If a permutation σ occurs precisely once in a permutation π and the Möbius function of the interval [σ, π] is μ(σ, π) = ±1, determine whether the order complex Δ(σ, π) must be homotopy equivalent to a sphere.
Determine for which permutations σ and π the order complex Δ(σ, π) associated with the interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset is shellable.

Prove a general finite-check theorem for linear combinations of vincular patterns: if two such combinations have the same distribution on permutations of all lengths up to some bound depending only on the pattern lengths involved, then they have the same distribution for all lengths.
Determine whether the ring of functions generated by vincular patterns has algebraic relations beyond the known upgrading relation, and if so describe those additional relations.
For an arbitrary permutation class C, determine whether the growth-rate definition gr(C) = lim sup_{n->infinity} |C_n|^(1/n) can always be strengthened by replacing the lim sup with an actual limit.
Determine whether the conjectures of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris become true when restricted to finitely based permutation classes, despite being false in full generality.

Characterize the possible growth rates of permutation classes in the interval between κ ≈ 2.21 and λ ≈ 2.48, where κ is the least accumulation point of accumulation points of growth rates and λ is the threshold above which every real number occurs as a growth rate of some permutation class.

Let X be an affine scheme, let a be a finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field, and let an algebraic group Gamma act completely reducibly on both X and a. Classify the irreducible finite-dimensional representations of the equivariant map algebra M(X, a)^Gamma in this more general setting, where Gamma is no longer required to be finite.

For equivariant map algebras whose target algebra is not the finite-dimensional Lie or associative algebra considered in the standard theory, develop the representation theory of the resulting EMA. In particular, determine finite-dimensional representations when the target is a Kac-Moody algebra, the Heisenberg algebra, an alternative algebra, a Jordan algebra, or another algebra with a well-defined notion of representation.

Extend the theory of equivariant map superalgebras by allowing more general target Lie superalgebras, replacing the coordinate algebra A by a supercommutative algebra so that X becomes a superscheme, and replacing Gamma by a Z2-graded group. Determine the resulting representation theory in this broader super setting.

Replace the algebraic setup of equivariant map algebras by an analytic one in which X is a Banach manifold, a is a Banach algebra, and one studies equivariant differentiable maps X to a. Build and analyze the corresponding analytic theory of equivariant map algebras and their representations.

Characterize equivariant map algebras up to isomorphism in substantially greater generality. In particular, generalize known isomorphism results for loop and multiloop algebras to broader multiloop situations and then to more general equivariant map algebras M(X, a)^Gamma.

Determine the automorphism groups of equivariant map algebras M(X, a)^Gamma in broad generality, including twisted and multiloop cases, as part of understanding how these algebras are characterized and related to one another.

Let M = M(X, a)^Gamma with a a finite-dimensional associative algebra. Go beyond the classification of irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules and describe all indecomposable finite-dimensional modules, together with the block decomposition of the finite-dimensional module category.

When the target algebra a is an associative bialgebra, use the comultiplication on a to define and analyze multi-orbit evaluation representations of the equivariant map algebra M(X, a)^Gamma, and determine their structure and role in the representation theory.

For an equivariant map Lie algebra M = M(X, g)^Gamma, compute higher extension groups between finite-dimensional modules, not just Ext^1, and explain how those higher Ext groups and the global dimension of the finite-dimensional module category depend on the geometry of the scheme X.

Extend the theory of global and local Weyl modules from current and loop algebras to more arbitrary equivariant map Lie algebras. In particular, determine lengths, dimensions, and characters of local Weyl modules in that general setting, and decide whether a suitable form of BGG reciprocity also holds for general EMAs.

Develop the theory of possibly infinite-dimensional representations of equivariant map Lie algebras beyond the finite-dimensional case. In particular, define and study analogues of category O, the category of integrable highest weight representations, the category of quasifinite representations with finite-dimensional weight spaces, and related representation-theoretic frameworks for general EMAs.

For a semisimple-target equivariant map Lie algebra M and a general M-module V, describe the cohomology and homology of M in greater generality: determine H^1(M, V), understand the special case H^1(M, M_ad) related to derivations, and determine the groups H_*(M, V), including how perfectness and representation-theoretic structure are reflected in these invariants.

For a perfect equivariant map Lie algebra (g tensor A)^Gamma, determine its central extensions, preferably the universal central extension, and decide in broad generality whether the natural comparison formula uce((g tensor A)^Gamma) is isomorphic to the Gamma-fixed subalgebra of uce(g tensor A).

For population-based metaheuristic algorithms in which multiple search agents form multiple interacting Markov chains, can one develop a mathematical theory that proves convergence and characterizes the rate of convergence for these algorithms, rather than only for the limited few metaheuristics that have already been analyzed mathematically?

For metaheuristic algorithms, is there an optimal way to balance local intensification, which focuses the search in promising local regions, and global diversification, which explores the search space more broadly? If such an optimal balance exists, how can it be achieved, and if it does not exist, what is the best achievable trade-off?

Why does a balanced combination of randomization and a deterministic component lead to a much more efficient metaheuristic algorithm than a purely deterministic algorithm or a purely random algorithm?
How can one measure or test whether a metaheuristic algorithm has achieved a proper balance among its interacting search components?
How can one prove that the use of memory can significantly increase the search efficiency of a metaheuristic algorithm, and under what conditions does such an efficiency gain hold?

Do No-Free-Lunch theorems hold for multiobjective optimization, given that they have been proved for single-objective optimization on finite search domains and do not hold for continuous infinite domains, and if they do hold or do not hold for multiobjective optimization, what implications would that have for algorithm development?

Can one develop a formal theoretical analysis and an agreed set of measures for comparing the performance of different metaheuristic algorithms, beyond commonly used empirical measures such as absolute objective value and number of function evaluations?

For the infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian with short-range or finite-range interaction considered in the paper, namely a system of the form H = sum_{j in Z^d} omega_j I_j + epsilon sum_{<i,j>} f_{i,j}(I_i, I_j; phi_i, phi_j), where the perturbation is short range or finite range and the frequencies are weakly correlated, KAM tori are constructed when the initial actions are strongly localized or even decay weaker than exponentially. Does there also exist an infinite-dimensional KAM torus when the initial actions decay only polynomially, in the sense that the action profile satisfies epsilon_j = I_j^0 approximately |j|^{-M} for some sufficiently large M > 0?

Consider a Hamiltonian system whose linearized operator, for example -Delta_f + v, has pure point spectrum, with part of that pure point spectrum dense in some finite interval. If the nonlinear part of the Hamiltonian is not short range, as in Hamiltonian partial differential equations posed on the whole space, do KAM tori still exist for that system?
context_brief: Pure point spectrum with non-short-range nonlinearity

question_text: Consider a Hamiltonian system whose linearized operator, for example -Delta_f + v, has continuous spectrum containing an interval. Can such a system admit any KAM tori, even in the case where the Hamiltonian itself may still have short-range interactions?
A planar billiard table Y is called integrable when the set of invariant circles of its billiard map has nonempty interior. Must every such integrable billiard table be an ellipse?
If Y is a smooth convex billiard table and the billiard flow on Y is an integrable Hamiltonian system with two degrees of freedom, must Y be an ellipse?

Given a closed convex curve gamma, let G(gamma, l) denote the outer curve produced by the string or gardener construction with string length l > |gamma|. If this construction is transitive in the sense that for ellipses one has G(G(gamma_1, l_1), l_2) = G(gamma_1, l_3) for a unique l_3, are ellipses the only closed convex curves that satisfy this transitivity property?
Construct a strictly convex C^1-smooth billiard table with positive entropy, and also construct a convex C^2-smooth billiard table with positive entropy.

Let Phi be the phase space of a piecewise smooth billiard table Y, let P be the set of periodic points in Phi, and let P_n be the set of periodic points of period n. Is it always true that mu(P) = 0, equivalently that mu(P_n) = 0 for every n >= 2?

A semi-dispersive billiard table is one whose boundary has dispersive inward-convex components together with neutral components such as line segments. Is every semi-dispersive billiard table hyperbolic?
For a hyperbolic billiard table Y, let f_Y(n) be the number of periodic points whose period is at most n. Does the exponential growth rate h = lim_{n -> infinity} log f_Y(n) / n exist?
If the limit h = lim_{n -> infinity} log f_Y(n) / n exists for a hyperbolic billiard table Y, must this finite positive number coincide with the topological entropy of the billiard map?

Let T(n) denote the moduli space of n-gons of a fixed combinatorial type, let E(n) be the subset consisting of ergodic n-gons, and let lambda be the corresponding Lebesgue measure. Does lambda(E(n)) > 0 hold?
Does there exist an irrational polygon whose billiard flow is not ergodic?

Let P be an irrational n-gon with phase space Phi, and for each side a_i let Phi_i be the set of phase points whose base points lie on a_i. If M is an invariant subset of Phi with positive measure and Phi_i is contained in M for some side index i, must M equal the whole phase space Phi?
Does every polygon admit at least one periodic billiard orbit?
For an irrational polygon P, let f_P(l) be the number of periodic bands of length at most l. Find efficient upper and lower bounds for the growth of f_P(l).

For a rational polygon P, the quadratic constants c_*(P) and c^*(P) are defined by inequalities c_*(P) l^2 <= f_P(l) <= c^*(P) l^2 for all sufficiently large l. Find efficient estimates for these quadratic constants.
For a rational polygon P, if f_P(l) / l^2 converges then P is said to have quadratic asymptotics. Does every rational polygon have quadratic asymptotics?

Let F_*(n) denote a partial billiard complexity obtained by coding only orbit families satisfying additional restrictions; for example, periodic complexity counts periodic-orbit codes. Find nontrivial explicit bounds on such partial billiard complexities for a general polygon.

A billiard table Omega is called secure if every pair of points x, y in Omega can be blocked by finitely many points z_1, ..., z_n in Omega \ {x, y}, meaning every billiard orbit from x to y passes through one of those blocking points. Characterize the secure polygons, and in particular find a criterion that decides security for rational polygons.
Does there exist an integer d >= 3 such that for every polygon the full billiard complexity has a cubic lower bound and also an upper bound by a polynomial of degree d?
An almost integrable polygon is one that is tiled under reflections by one of the integrable polygons. Is a polygon secure exactly when it is almost integrable?
For a compact smooth Riemannian manifold, is security equivalent to flatness? In other words, is every secure compact smooth Riemannian manifold flat, and every flat one secure?

Does the nonlinear Schrodinger equation posed on a tree graph admit a rigorous well-posedness theory comparable to the star-graph case, beyond the currently available partial results based on dispersive estimates?

When a nonlinear Schrodinger equation is posed on a system of thin tubes or guides connected at junctions and the transversal tube size shrinks to zero, does the limiting dynamics converge to an NLS on a metric graph, and if so which vertex boundary conditions appear in the limit? How do those limiting boundary conditions depend on the specific shrinking procedure for the tubes, guides, and junction size, and on whether the thin-tube boundary condition is Neumann or Dirichlet?

Can one rigorously derive a quasi-one-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii or nonlinear Schrodinger equation on a graph-like structure such as a Y-junction from a many-body Bose-Einstein-condensate model, for example by starting from an N-body theory on the graph and taking the N to infinity limit with suitable scalings, while correctly determining the vertex boundary condition in the limit? The boundary-condition issue is already open even for the simplest graph with two edges, namely a line with a defect.

For focusing NLS on a star graph with a delta interaction at the vertex, if the threshold condition that guarantees an absolute constrained minimum of the reduced action fails, does the action still have a local minimum on the Nehari manifold that lies above the infimum? Is there an analogous local constrained minimum for the energy functional when the mass falls outside the regime where a ground state exists?

On graphs more complicated than a star graph, such as trees or graphs with loops, can one build an orbital-stability or orbital-instability theory for nonlinear standing waves of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation when explicit formulas for the standing waves are unavailable? In particular, can one effectively count negative eigenvalues of the linearized operator and verify the Vakhitov-Kolokolov condition in these less explicit graph geometries?

For nonlinear Schrodinger equations on nontrivial graphs, how can one construct and identify branches of nonlinear stationary or bound states that do not bifurcate from any linear eigenstate? The paper notes that standard bifurcation theory can produce branches with a linear counterpart near the linear ground state, but it leaves open how to obtain excited states or other bound states without a linear counterpart.

Are standing waves of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on graphs asymptotically stable in the following sense: every solution that starts near a standing wave in the energy norm eventually decomposes into a possibly different nearby standing wave, a dispersive term evolving under the linear graph Hamiltonian, and a remainder that decays to zero in L2 as time goes to infinity? More concretely, can one control the spectrum and time evolution of the non-selfadjoint linearized Hamiltonian J L on graphs, together with the decay of nonlinear remainders, well enough to prove such relaxation?
context_brief: Asymptotic stability of graph standing waves

question_text: For the scattering of fast solitons in the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on star graphs, do multisoliton solutions exist, and what is the dynamical outcome when several solitons collide at the same vertex?

Can one develop a rigorous theory of soliton scattering for the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on graphs with nontrivial topology, especially trees, beyond the already treated star-graph and similar simple cases? In particular, how do network topology and the availability of Strichartz estimates affect the propagation and scattering of solitons on such graphs?

After a soliton scatters at a graph vertex, can the time interval on which the outgoing waves are accurately approximated by solitary waves be extended beyond the logarithmic-in-velocity scale proved in the paper? How does that longer-timescale question depend on the initial data and on the external potential?
context_brief: Longer validity timescale for outgoing solitons

question_text: For nonlinear Schrodinger equations on graphs whose nonlinearity is close to the integrable cubic case but not exactly cubic, are the outgoing waves produced by vertex scattering still close to solitons over timescales comparable to those proved in the integrable cubic setting?

What rigorous mechanisms describe the capture of solitons by graph defects or junctions and the generation of new solitons in the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on graphs, particularly in dynamical regimes that are neither close to a standing wave nor in the fast-soliton scattering regime?

Consider the single-input time-optimal control system q˙ = f(q) + u g(q) on a 3-dimensional smooth manifold M, where f and g are a generic pair of C-infinity vector fields, the control u is any measurable function with |u| <= 1, and trajectories are required to connect fixed endpoints in minimum time. Must every time-optimal trajectory for such a generic 3-dimensional system be piecewise smooth, meaning smooth except at finitely many switching points where the optimal control changes its regime?

For the same generic 3-dimensional single-input time-optimal problem q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, define sw(q) to be the least integer k such that every time-optimal trajectory contained in a sufficiently small neighborhood of q has at most k switching points, and set sw(q) = infinity if arbitrarily small neighborhoods of q contain time-optimal trajectories with infinitely many switching points. Is sw(q) finite for every point q in M?

In the generic 3-dimensional time-optimal control problem q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, is every individual time-optimal trajectory forced to have only finitely many switching points, even if one does not assume a uniform neighborhood-wise bound on the number of switchings?

In higher-dimensional single-input time-optimal control systems q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, there are examples of extremals with accumulating switching points whose qualitative structure survives small perturbations of the system. Are such extremals actually time-optimal?

Let M be a real analytic manifold and let f and g be real analytic vector fields, not necessarily generic, in the single-input time-optimal system q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1. If two points are connected by some time-optimal trajectory, must there exist a time-optimal trajectory connecting the same endpoints whose set of switching points is at most countable?

For the same real analytic single-input time-optimal control setting, can one always choose a time-optimal trajectory between two time-optimally connected points whose set of switching points avoids having positive measure?

Let gamma_0 and gamma_1 be smooth admissible paths of a sub-Riemannian structure on a manifold M with gamma_0(0) = gamma_1(0) = q_0 and with initial tangent vectors at q_0 that are not collinear. Does there always exist an admissible path connecting gamma_0(1) to gamma_1(1) whose length is strictly smaller than the length of the broken path obtained by concatenating gamma_0 and gamma_1?

Fix a point q_0 in a sub-Riemannian manifold and consider the endpoint map from the Hilbert manifold of H^1 admissible paths starting at q_0 to M, sending each path to its endpoint at time 1. Must this endpoint map always have at least one regular value, or equivalently, is it impossible for singular curves issuing from q_0 to fill the whole manifold M?

In a sub-Riemannian manifold, optimal singular curves starting from a fixed point q_0 are known to fill a nowhere dense subset of the manifold. Can the set filled by such optimal singular curves nevertheless have positive measure?

For a generic sub-Riemannian metric on a 3-dimensional Martinet distribution, consider a sub-Riemannian sphere centered at q_0 and a point where the sphere meets an optimal singular curve. What is the C^1-classification, up to germs of C^1-diffeomorphisms of R^3, of the germ of the sphere at such a point?

For the Engel distribution, namely a rank-2 distribution on R^4 with n_3(q) = 3 and n_4(q) = 4, sub-Riemannian spheres are 3-dimensional hypersurfaces and every point lies on a unique singular curve whose small segments are optimal. What is the corresponding local classification of sphere singularities at points where such optimal singular curves meet the sphere?

Consider a generic pair of smooth vector fields f_0 and f_1 near a point q_0 in R^2 such that f_0(q_0) and f_1(q_0) are collinear, n_2(q_0) = 1, and n_3(q_0) = 2, and define the almost-Riemannian distance S_{q_0}(q) as the minimum time needed to reach q from q_0 along trajectories of q˙ = u_0 f_0(q) + u_1 f_1(q) under the unit-norm constraint on the two control components stated in the paper. What is the C^1-classification of the germ of the distance function S_{q_0} for such generic pairs?

Let Delta be a vector distribution on a manifold M, and call it singular transitive when any two points of M can be connected by a concatenation of singular curves of Delta. Does singular transitivity force the symmetry group of Delta, meaning the diffeomorphisms Phi of M with Phi_* Delta = Delta, to be a finite-dimensional Lie group?

For each n, let mu(n) be the smallest integer m such that an m-times traversed plane convex curve admits arbitrarily small perturbations that become nondegenerate closed curves in R^n, where nondegeneracy means that the velocity, curvature, torsion, and higher Frenet data never degenerate. What is mu(n) for dimensions n > 3?

For regular closed curves in R^n equipped with their orthonormal Frenet frames in O(n), is the length of the Frenet frame always strictly greater than mu(n) times the length of the standard closed geodesic SO(2) embedded in O(n), where mu(n) is the minimum multiplicity needed for a plane convex curve to admit a regular perturbation in R^n?

Consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes equation on the torus with periodic boundary conditions, viewed as a control system on the space V of divergence-free H^1 vector fields, where the forcing eta(t, .) is constrained to lie in a finite-dimensional subspace E of the space of divergence-free fields supported in a fixed open subset D of the torus, and E is required not to depend on the viscosity nu. Is the system approximately controllable in any time under such a localized degenerate forcing?

In the same Navier-Stokes control setting on the torus, with forcing constrained to a finite-dimensional subspace E of divergence-free vector fields supported in a fixed open set D and chosen independently of the viscosity nu, is the system controllable in finite-dimensional projections in any time?

Let S be a numerical semigroup, meaning a cofinite submonoid of the nonnegative integers N, and let F(S) denote its Frobenius number, the greatest integer not belonging to S. Find a formula for F(S) in terms of a minimal system of generators of S when the embedding dimension e(S) is at least 3.
Let S be a numerical semigroup and let H(S) = N \ S be its set of gaps. Determine the genus g(S) = |H(S)| from a minimal system of generators of S when the embedding dimension e(S) is at least 3.
Determine the type t(S) of a numerical semigroup S from other standard invariants, especially the multiplicity m(S), embedding dimension e(S), genus g(S), or Frobenius number F(S).

Decide whether every numerical semigroup S satisfies Wilf's conjectured inequality e(S)g(S) <= (e(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1), where e(S) is the embedding dimension, g(S) is the genus, and F(S) is the Frobenius number.

For each genus g, let n_g be the number of numerical semigroups of genus g. Determine whether n_g > n_{g+1} fails never, equivalently whether there are always more numerical semigroups of genus g + 1 than of genus g, in the Fibonacci-like growth problem discussed by Bras-Amoros.

For a modular numerical semigroup S(a, b, 1), find formulas for the Frobenius number F(S(a, b, 1)), multiplicity m(S(a, b, 1)), type t(S(a, b, 1)), and embedding dimension e(S(a, b, 1)) in terms of the parameters a and b.
Determine whether Wilf's conjecture e(S)g(S) <= (e(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1) holds for every modular numerical semigroup.
Given a proportionally modular numerical semigroup by its minimal generators, find formulas for its Frobenius number, genus, and type directly from that minimal generating system.

Find an algorithm that decides whether a given numerical semigroup is of the form P(a, b, c, d) union {0}, where P(a, b, c, d) is the set of solutions of a contracted proportionally modular Diophantine inequality ax mod b <= cx - d with nonnegative integers a, b, c, d and b != 0 != c.

Characterize the numerical semigroups that can be written as quotients S / p = {x in N | px in S} of numerical semigroups of embedding dimension 3 by a positive integer, and determine whether every numerical semigroup arises in this way.
If a numerical semigroup S satisfies Wilf's conjecture, determine whether its half S/2 = {x in N | 2x in S} must also satisfy Wilf's conjecture.

For a numerical semigroup S, determine the smallest possible number of irreducible numerical semigroups whose intersection equals S, and decide whether there is a universal constant N such that every numerical semigroup is an intersection of at most N irreducible numerical semigroups.
Determine whether every contracted modular numerical semigroup admits a Toms decomposition.

Decide whether every system of proportionally modular Diophantine inequalities is equivalent to a system in which all proportions are equal to 1; equivalently, determine whether every numerical semigroup that admits a Toms decomposition can be expressed as an intersection of modular numerical semigroups.
Find simple sufficient conditions on a subset X of the positive integers N that guarantee that X is the set of fundamental gaps FG(S) of some numerical semigroup S.
For a given numerical semigroup S, let T range over all numerical semigroups with S = T/2. Find a formula, depending only on S, for the minimum Frobenius number among those doubles T.
Determine the Frobenius variety generated by the family of numerical semigroups of maximal embedding dimension.

Let V_T be the Frobenius variety of numerical semigroups admitting a Toms decomposition. Determine whether V_T is the least Frobenius variety containing all numerical semigroups of embedding dimension 2.

For an infinite Frobenius variety V, let G(V) be the directed tree whose vertices are semigroups in V and whose levels are measured by distance from the root N. Determine whether, for every n, the (n + 1)-st level of G(V) contains more vertices than the n-th level.
context_brief: Level growth in infinite Frobenius varieties

question_text: Characterize those Frobenius varieties whose associated trees satisfy the Bras-Amoros-type growth property that each level has more vertices than the preceding level.

Characterize those Frobenius varieties V for which every S in V satisfies the generalized Wilf inequality e_V(S)g(S) <= (e_V(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1), where e_V(S) denotes the cardinality of the unique minimal V-system of generators of S.
Determine the Frobenius variety generated by the symmetric numerical semigroups.
Determine the Frobenius variety generated by the pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups.
Characterize the numerical semigroups that can be expressed as quotients of complete intersection numerical semigroups by a positive integer.
Determine the least Frobenius variety that contains all complete intersection numerical semigroups.
Among families of numerical semigroups closed under gluing, determine the least family that contains all numerical semigroups of maximal embedding dimension.
Determine whether the cardinality of a minimal presentation of a symmetric numerical semigroup can be bounded solely as a function of the embedding dimension.

For a finite subset sigma of N^n x N^n of the displayed form with parameters c_i and a_jk, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on those integers ensuring that the quotient monoid N^n / <sigma> is isomorphic to a numerical semigroup.
context_brief: Quotient monoids that are numerical semigroups

question_text: Given positive integers r_ij for i, j in {1,2,3}, determine when the three integers r12 r13 + r12 r23 + r13 r32, r13 r21 + r21 r23 + r23 r31, and r12 r31 + r21 r32 + r31 r32 are pairwise relatively prime.

Let n1, n2, n3 be pairwise relatively prime positive integers, and let u be a positive integer with u n2 == 1 mod n1. Find a formula, in terms of n1, n2, n3, for the multiplicity of the proportionally modular numerical semigroup S(u n2 n3, n1 n2, n3), equivalently for the invariant c3 needed to recover the Frobenius problem in embedding dimension 3.

Give a proof, not using Fermat's Last Theorem itself, that for pairwise relatively prime integers a, b, c >= 2 and n >= 3, the proportionally modular numerical semigroup <a^n, c^{n-1}, b^n> is not minimally generated by {a^n, c^{n-1}, b^n}; equivalently, prove the semigroup-theoretic reformulation discussed in the paper without appealing to Wiles' theorem.
Characterize the numerical semigroups S for which the omega-primality omega(S) is different from the type t(S).
Determine which finite sets can occur as the set of factorization lengths L(s) of some element s in some numerical semigroup.
Determine whether the catenary degree function c(s) of a numerical semigroup is eventually periodic, meaning that there exist n in S and a threshold beyond which c(s + n) = c(s) for all s.
Determine whether the tame degree function t(s) of a numerical semigroup is eventually periodic.

Chaos and turbulence are deterministic dynamical behaviors rather than small stochastic perturbations around a mean signal. What mathematically and computationally effective description of chaotic dynamics, especially turbulence generated by Navier-Stokes flow, can replace Reynolds averaging, avoid the resulting closure problem, and still be useful in engineering practice? More specifically, can one find a description that works better than fractal dimension or SRB measures, and can shadowing or a related method be made practical at the scale of an entire turbulent attractor?

For incompressible fluid dynamics, especially at very large Reynolds number where viscosity is very small, is violent turbulence fundamentally caused by rough dependence on initial data rather than ordinary sensitive dependence on initial data? In this setting, rough dependence means that arbitrarily small perturbations of the initial condition can become substantial essentially instantly; for the Euler equations, at any nonzero time the solution map from initial data to the solution is continuous but nowhere locally uniformly continuous and nowhere differentiable. Does this mechanism, or the very large derivative of the Navier-Stokes solution map in the high-Reynolds-number regime, explain why sufficiently large-Reynolds-number turbulence develops violently in short time?

How does chaos theory explain the arrow of time, namely the emergence of macroscopic irreversibility from microscopically time-reversible dynamics? In particular, if a many-body system evolves chaotically so that unavoidable perturbations are amplified and trajectories lose memory of the initial macrostate, can that mechanism account for thermodynamic irreversibility, and in the cosmological setting would the universe still be expanding if the velocity of every object or molecule were simultaneously reversed?

In predator-prey dynamics, does increasing the prey's nutrient supply or carrying capacity genuinely make extinction of both prey and predator more likely, or is that prediction only an artifact of a particular mathematical model? After rewriting a Rosenzweig-type predator-prey system in dimensionless form with the capacity-predation number H = h/b, where h is the half-saturation prey density for predation and b is the prey carrying capacity, does the apparent paradox disappear because increasing carrying capacity b and decreasing half-saturation h both lower the same governing dimensionless quantity and therefore represent the same effect?

When a pest has a natural predator, how should pesticide application be timed and scaled so that it suppresses the pest instead of causing a later resurgence above the crop's economic threshold? More generally, what mathematical model captures the fact that pesticide application reduces both pest and predator populations, changes their ratio, and can make a later outbreak worse even when the immediate effect is a drop in pest abundance?

How can hundreds of phytoplankton species coexist while competing for only one or a few limiting nutrients, even though the principle of competitive exclusion predicts that at equilibrium only one or a few species should remain? Can a nonequilibrium model that combines turbulent water advection, species-specific drift relative to the water, regeneration of the limiting nutrient, and species-dependent nutrient uptake and growth explain sustained coexistence of many plankton species?

Can one give an elementary proof of the Hirzebruch signature theorem for closed smooth oriented manifolds, namely the theorem identifying the signature tau(M) with the L-polynomial in the Pontryagin classes evaluated on the fundamental class, and can one explain geometrically the functional equation for the associated virtual signature?
context_brief: Elementary proof of the signature theorem

question_text: For a given closed subgroup H of GL(n, R), is there a general criterion that decides whether an n-manifold admits an integrable H-structure, rather than only case-by-case criteria for special geometric structures such as almost complex, symplectic, or foliation-type structures?

Given an integer r with 0 <= r <= k, what criterion determines whether a manifold of dimension 2k+1 admits a globally defined Pfaffian equation whose class is everywhere exactly 2r+1, equivalently a 1-form alpha such that alpha wedge (d alpha)^r is nowhere zero while alpha wedge (d alpha)^(r+1) vanishes identically?

For each n, what is the minimal Euclidean dimension into which real projective n-space RP^n can be smoothly embedded? In particular, for RP^6, is the minimal embedding dimension 10 rather than the currently known upper bound 11 and the ruled-out value 8?
context_brief: Optimal embeddings of real projective spaces

question_text: Does four-dimensional Euclidean space E^4 contain a closed surface of genus 2 whose induced metric has Gaussian curvature negative at every point, and can such an example even be chosen to have constant negative Gaussian curvature?
context_brief: Negatively curved genus-2 surfaces in E^4

question_text: For an almost-complex manifold M, are the dimensions h^{p,q} defined as the kernel dimensions of the d-bar Laplacian independent of the choice of Hermitian metric, and if not, is there a replacement notion of h^{p,q} depending only on the almost-complex structure that extends Dolbeault cohomology from the integrable case?
context_brief: Dolbeault-type invariants for almost complex manifolds

question_text: Does complex projective 3-space CP^3 admit a complex structure whose second Chern class vanishes, equivalently a non-Kahler complex structure whose existence would in particular have consequences for the long-standing question of whether S^6 admits a complex structure?
context_brief: Complex structures on CP^3 with c2 = 0

question_text: For each n >= 3, determine all complex structures on the smooth manifold underlying complex projective space CP^n, including the possible existence and classification of non-Kahler complex structures beyond the standard algebraic one.

If one ranges over all smooth 4-manifolds homeomorphic to S^2 x S^2, rather than fixing the standard smooth manifold itself, must every complex structure on such a manifold come from an even Hirzebruch surface, or can there exist other complex surfaces homeomorphic to S^2 x S^2?
context_brief: Complex structures on manifolds homeomorphic to S^2 x S^2

question_text: Which rational linear combinations of Hodge numbers and Chern characteristic numbers of a smooth complex projective variety are topological invariants, under oriented or unoriented homeomorphism or diffeomorphism, and which are not?
context_brief: Topological invariance of Hodge and Chern data

question_text: Let x: M -> E^m be an immersion whose position vector admits a finite spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k with each non-constant term satisfying Δx_i = λ_i x_i for some Laplacian eigenvalue λ_i; such an immersion is called of finite type. Classify all finite-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space E^{n+1}. In particular, classify all finite-type surfaces in E^3.
If a compact surface in Euclidean 3-space E^3 is of finite type, meaning that its position vector is a finite sum of Laplacian eigenmaps, must that surface be a sphere?
If a compact hypersurface in Euclidean space is of finite type, meaning that its position vector has a finite Laplacian spectral decomposition, must it be a hypersphere?
context_brief: Compact finite-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space

question_text: Classify all finite-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere in E^{n+2}.
Does there exist any surface in the standard 3-sphere S^3 whose position vector is of finite k-type for some finite integer k greater than 2?
Are the only finite-type surfaces in the standard 3-sphere S^3 the minimal surfaces, the standard 2-spheres, and the products of two plane circles?
Classify all 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere of E^{n+2}. In particular, classify the 3-dimensional 2-type hypersurfaces of S^4 contained in E^5.
For a Dupin hypersurface M contained in a hypersphere, when is M of finite type, and when does finite type force M to be isoparametric?

Do there exist 2-type surfaces in S^4 that are not mass-symmetric, where mass-symmetric means that the constant vector c in the finite-type spectral decomposition is the center of the ambient hypersphere?
If an n-dimensional submanifold of E^{n+2} is of 2-type, has constant mean curvature, and is not of null 2-type, must it lie in a hypersphere?

Do there exist 2-type surfaces that lie fully in an even-dimensional hypersphere of a Euclidean space? In particular, do there exist mass-symmetric 2-type surfaces that lie fully in an even-dimensional hypersphere?

Suppose x: M -> E^m is a k-type immersion with spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, and let E_i be the subspace of E^m spanned by {x_i(p) : p in M}. Classify the 2-type immersions for which the subspaces E_1 and E_2 are linearly independent.
Classify the linearly independent submanifolds of codimension 2 in Euclidean space.

An isometric immersion x: M -> E^m is called biharmonic when Δ^2 x = 0, equivalently ΔH = 0 for the mean curvature vector H. Other than minimal submanifolds of E^m, which submanifolds of E^m are biharmonic?
Must every biharmonic submanifold of a Euclidean space be minimal?
Must every biharmonic hypersurface of a Euclidean space be minimal?
Must every complete biharmonic submanifold of a Euclidean space be minimal?
A null 2-type submanifold is one whose mean curvature vector satisfies ΔH = cH for some nonzero constant c. Does every null 2-type surface in Euclidean 4-space E^4 have constant mean curvature?
Classify all null 2-type submanifolds. In particular, classify all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces.

Let N be an irreducible compact homogeneous manifold, immersed into a Euclidean space by its first standard immersion φ, and let M be a submanifold of N. When is M of finite type in the ambient Euclidean space via φ? In particular, when is M of 1-type or 2-type via φ?

For a general Riemannian metric on a sphere of dimension at least 3, and in particular on S^3, does there exist a higher-dimensional extension of Lyusternik and Schnirelmann's theorem guaranteeing multiple closed geodesics?
Does every closed manifold of dimension at least 2 admit either a Riemannian metric or a Finsler metric whose geodesic flow is ergodic?
Every irreversible Finsler metric on S^2 has either exactly 2 or infinitely many distinct prime closed geodesics.
The existence of one hyperbolic prime closed geodesic on a Finsler S^2 implies the existence of infinitely many distinct prime closed geodesics.
Every Finsler S^2 has at least one elliptic prime closed geodesic.
Does every complete Riemannian manifold with finite volume have at least one closed geodesic?
Does there exist an irreversible Finsler metric of finite volume on R x S^1 with no closed geodesics?
Is there at least one closed magnetic geodesic in every positive energy level?
Does every Kropina metric on a closed manifold have a closed geodesic?
How do the sums of the Betti numbers for ΛTM and Ω(T (p, q) grow as T → ∞?
Does the number of closed geodesics with length ≤ T grow exponentially as T → ∞ if the Betti numbers of the loop space grow exponentially?
Do there exist a metric on S n and a homology class X ∈ H∗ (ΛM ; Z) with 0 < cr(mX) < cr(X) for some m ∈ N?
If a closed manifold admits a metric with Anosov geodesic flow, then it admits a metric with negative sectional curvature.
If (M, g) has no conjugate points, does M carry a metric with non-positive sectional curvature?
Is the fundamental group of a closed manifold without conjugate points semihyperbolic?
Two metrics with negative curvature on a compact manifold must be isometric if they have the same marked length spectrum.

Does the marked length spectrum determine such a metric (in the class of all locally CAT (−1) metrics on this space, or in the class of all 2-dimensional (metrical) simplicial complexes with the above properties homeomorphic to the given complex)?
What conditions on M , N and g imply boundary rigidity?
Compact Riemannian manifolds with negative curvature must be isometric if they have C^0 -conjugate geodesic flows.
htop = hLiou for a metric of negative curvature on a compact manifold if and only if it is locally symmetric.
Does there exist a closed Riemannian manifold of negative curvature such that E s and E u are C^1 smooth, but the dimension is > 2 and the metric is not 1/4-pinched?

Is there a metric of negative curvature for which the ratio of largest positive Lyapunov exponent to smallest positive Lyapunov exponent is greater than 2 for typical geodesics (not just exceptional closed geodesics)?
Are there infinitely many simple closed geodesics in every hyperbolic complete three-manifold of finite volume?
Is the geodesic flow of a metric of non-positive curvature on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure?
[Burns] Is there a C ∞ (or at least C k , k ≥ 3) metric for which there exists a non-closed geodesic along which the Gaussian curvature is everywhere zero?
Consider a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 with a metric of non-positive curvature.
Is the geodesic flow of a Finsler metric on the torus conjugate to that of the (locally) Minkowski metric on the torus?
Suppose α(0) = β(0).
Suppose dist(α(t), β(t)) → 0 as t → −∞.
Must homotopic closed geodesics in a manifold of dimension ≥ 3 with no conjugate points be homotopic through closed geodesics?
Must a metric satisfying this version of the parallel postulate be flat?
Let (M, g) be a closed symmetric space of noncompact type and of higher rank.
The metric on the Z-cover corresponding to S^1 factor is a direct product: (M × R, g) = (M, g1 ) × (R, dt2 ).
Consider a magnetic flow on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 and an energy level such that the topological entropy vanishes.
Is there a Riemannian metric on a closed manifold with everywhere positive sectional curvatures and ergodic geodesic flow?
Assume M is closed.
Assume M is closed.
Assume M is closed.
Is the union of the closed geodesics always dense in the manifold?
Does every metric on a compact surface of positive genus have a geodesic that is dense in the surface?
Describe Finsler metrics on S^2 of flag curvature 1.
Construct examples of Finsler metrics of constant curvature on S^2 that are not Zoll and such that they admit no Killing vector field.
Does Frankel’s Theorem remain true for Finsler manifolds?
Let (M 3 , F ) be a closed 3-dimensional reversible Finsler manifold of positive flag curvature and N be a closed totally geodesic 2-dimensional submanifold.
Generalize this statement to higher dimensions.

Does there exist, in the space of metrics with conical singularities, a (continuous or smooth) family of metrics gt such that g0 is the round metric of the sphere, g1 is the metric from the example above, and σ(gt ) is a decreasing function of t.
Does every Riemannian metric on S^2 with area 4π that is close enough to the round metric have a closed geodesic with length ≤ 2π?
Does a Riemannian metric on a real projective space with the same volume as the canonical metric have a closed geodesic with length ≤ π?
Can there be Riemannian metrics on S^3 or S^2 × S^1 with unit volume all of whose closed geodesics are long?
Let M be a closed manifold not covered by a sphere.
Let (M, g) be a closed simply connected manifold such that all geodesics are closed.
Does every closed Lorentzian manifold have at least one closed geodesic?

Can there exist a complete semi-Riemannian metric g and a nontrivial 1-form η on a closed manifold such that for every light-like geodesic γ(t) the function η(γ̇(t)) grows linearly in both directions: i.e.
What geometric assumptions imply that a metric (possibly, of a fixed signature) on a closed manifold is geodesically complete?
Assume that a compact Lorentzian manifold is globally conformal to a manifold of constant curvature.
Does there exist a Riemannian metric on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 whose geodesic flow is completely integrable?
Is there a Riemannian metric on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 whose geodesic flow has zero Liouville entropy?
Let F1 , F2 be Finsler metrics on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2.
Does there exist a non-Riemannian Finsler metric satisfying the Landsberg condition on a surface of genus ≥ 2?
If the geodesic flow of a Riemannian metric on the torus T^2 admits an integral that is polynomial of degree 3 in the velocities, then the metric admits a Killing vector field.
If the billiard in Ω is integrable, then the boundary of Ω is an ellipse.
Does every metric on S^2 admit a stationary Θ-graph?
Are non-trivial stationary nets dense on any closed Riemannian surface?
Suppose a closed manifold (M, g) admits a non-zero (1, 1)-tensor field that is self-adjoint with respect to g, parallel and nilpotent.
Describe all affinely equivalent Finsler metrics.

Construct a system of scalar invariants of a projective structure that vanish if and only if there exists (locally, in a neighborhood of almost every point) a metric compatible with a given projective structure.
In dimension 2, is each irreversible path structure metrizable?
Can a 3-dimensional sphere admit two non-proportional projectively equivalent metrics of Lorentzian signature?

Is there an algorithm C that takes as input a Diophantine equation D, returns an integer, and guarantees that this returned integer is greater than the number of non-negative integer solutions whenever that solution set is finite? The algorithm may fail to terminate, return nothing, or return something irrelevant when D has infinitely many non-negative integer solutions.

Let n be a positive integer. For a finite group K and an automorphism n−1 ϕ of K of order dividing n, let Xn,ϕ (K):= {x ∈ K | xxϕ · · · xϕ = 1}. Let cn be the supremum of the ratios |Xn,ϕ (H)|/|H| over all finite groups H and their automorphisms ϕ ∈ Aut(H) such that ϕn = id and Xn,ϕ (H) ̸= H. (a) Let n > 1 be a positive integer such that cd < 1 for all prime power divisors d of n. Is it true that cn < 1? (b) For a finite group G and a positive integer n, the generalized Hughes–Thompson subgroup is defined as Hn(G) = ⟨x ∈ G | xn ̸= 1⟩. Suppose that n is a positive integer for which there is a positive integer kn depending only on n such that |G: Hn(G)| ⩽ kn for all finite groups G with Hn(G) ̸= 1. Is it true that then cn < 1? This question is open even when n ⩾ 5 is prime.
Let S be a finite simple group, and let G be a finite group for which there exists a bijection f: G → S such that |x| divides |f(x)| for all x ∈ G. Must G necessarily be simple?

Let G = An or Sn and let H, K be soluble subgroups of G. For all sufficiently large n, can we always find an element x ∈ G such that H ∩ K x = 1? Does this hold for all n ⩾ 21? Note that the conclusion is false when G = S20 and H = K = (S4 ≀ S4) × S4.
Let G be a finite group with trivial solvable radical and let H1,..., H5 be solvable subgroups of G. Then do there always exist elements x_i ∈ G such that ⋂_i H_i^{x_i} = 1? Cf. 17.41(b).

Let p be a prime. Let G be a transitive subgroup of the group of finitary permutations F Sym(Ω) of a set Ω, let N be a normal subgroup of G, and let S be a transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G. (a) Is it true that S ∩ N is a Sylow p-subgroup of N? (b) Is it true that SN/N is a Sylow p-subgroup of G/N? (c) Are any two transitive Sylow p-subgroups of G locally conjugate in G? Two subgroups X, Y of a group G are said to be locally conjugate if there is a locally inner automorphism φ of G such that X φ = Y. An automorphism φ of G is said to be locally inner if for every finite subset A ⊆ G there is an element g = g(A) ∈ G such that aφ = g −1 ag for all a ∈ A.

Let p be a prime. A totally imprimitive p-group H of finitary permutations is said to have the cyclic-block property if in the cycle decomposition of every element the support of every cycle is a block for H. Let G be a transitive subgroup of the group of finitary permutations F Sym(Ω) of a set Ω. Does every transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G contain a transitive subgroup which has the cyclic-block property?

(Well-known problem). A finite group G is called an IYB-group if it is isomorphic to the permutation group of a finite involutive non-degenerate set-theoretic solution of the Yang–Baxter equation, or equivalently, G is isomorphic to the multiplicative group of a finite left brace. Assume that the Sylow subgroups of a finite soluble group G are IYB-groups. Is G an IYB-group?

As in 17.57, let r(m) = {r + km | k ∈ Z} for integers 0 ⩽ r < m; for r1(m1) ∩ r2(m2) = ∅ let the class transposition τr1(m1),r2(m2) be the involution which interchanges r1 + tm1 and r2 + tm2 for each integer t and fixes everything else, and let CT(Z) be the group generated by all class transpositions. Let CTk be the subgroup of CT(Z) generated by the class transpositions τr1(k),r2(k) for 0 ⩽ r1 ̸= r2 < k. Since τr1(k),r2(k) permutes the residue classes modulo k, the group CTk is isomorphic to the symmetric group Sk. Let CT(k) = ⟨CT2, CT3,..., CTk ⟩. Is it true that for k > 3 the group CT(k) is isomorphic to the symmetric group SN, where N is the least common multiple of the numbers 2, 3,..., k?

Let F be a non-abelian free pro-p group of finite rank. Can one find a finite collection U1,..., Un of open subgroups of F including F itself such that the only subgroup of F which is contained in Ui and is characteristic in Ui for every i is the trivial subgroup?

We call a group presentation finite if it represents a finite group. We say that a presentation is just finite if it is finite and is no longer finite on removal of any relation from it. Is it true that every finite group has a just finite presentation? Note that if a group has a balanced presentation, then it is just finite. A similar argument can be applied for some p-groups using the Golod–Shafarevich inequality.

Can some or all groups of the following sorts be written as homomorphic images of nonprincipal ultraproducts of countable families of groups? This is Question 18 in(G. M. Bergman, Pacific J. Math., 274(2015) 451–495). (a) Infinite finitely generated groups of finite exponent. (b) For an infinite set X, the group of those permutations of X that move only finitely many elements. It is known that no group of permutations containing an element with exactly one infinite orbit can be written as an image of such an ultraproduct(ibid.).

Suppose that U is a nonprincipal ultrafilter on ω, and B is a group such that every element b ∈ B belongs to a subgroup of B that is a homomorphic image of Z^ω/U. Must B then be a homomorphic image of an ultraproduct group(∏_{i∈ω} G_i)/U for some groups G_i? This is Question 19 in(G. M. Bergman, Pacific J. Math., 274(2015), 451–495). An affirmative answer would imply that every torsion group was such a homomorphic image for every U, and so would give positive answers to both parts of 21.11.

It is known that the group Zω has a subgroup whose dual is free abelian of rank 2ℵ0(see 17.24 in Archive). Does Zω have a subgroup whose dual is free ℵ0 abelian of still larger rank(the largest possible being 22)? This is Question 11 in(G. M. Bergman, Portugaliae Math., 69(2012) 69–84).

Suppose α is an endomorphism of a group G such that for every group H and every homomorphism f: G → H, there exists an endomorphism βf of H such that βf f = f α. Must α then be either an inner automorphism of G or the trivial endomorphism? This is Question 5 in(G. M. Bergman, Publ. Matem., 56(2012), 91–126).

Suppose B is a subgroup of the symmetric group S_Ω on an infinite set Ω. Will the amalgamated free product S_Ω*_B S_Ω of two copies of S_Ω with amalgamation of B be embeddable in S_Ω? This is a weakened form of the group case of Question 4.4 in(G. M. Bergman, Indag. Math., 18(2007), 349–403). It is known that S_Ω*_B S_Ω need not be so embeddable by a map respecting B(Algebra Number Theory, 3(2009), 847–879, § 10).

Let the width of a group(respectively, a monoid) H with respect to a generating set X mean the supremum over h ∈ H of the least length of a group word(respectively, a monoid word) in elements of X expressing h. A group(or monoid) is said to have finite width if its width with respect to every generating set is finite. (A common finite bound for these widths is not required.) Do there exist groups G having finite width as groups, but not as monoids? This is Question 9 in(G. M. Bergman, Bull. London Math. Soc., 38(2006), 429–440).

If X is a class of groups, let H(X) denote the class of homomorphic images of groups in X, let S(X) denote the class of groups isomorphic to subgroups of groups in X, let P(X) denote the class of groups isomorphic to(unrestricted) direct products of families of groups in X, and let Pf(X) denote the class of groups isomorphic to direct products of finite families of groups in X. By Birkhoff’s theorem, H(S(P(X))) is the variety of groups generated by X. If M is a class of metabelian groups, must H(S(Pf(M))) ⊆ S(H(P(S(M))))? This is Question 27 in(G. M. Bergman, Algebra Universalis, 26(1989), 267–283).

Suppose that G is a finite group, and A1, A2, A3 are subsets of G such that the multiplication map A1 × A2 × A3 → G is bijective. Must the subgroup ⟨A2 ⟩ generated by A2 have order divisible by the cardinality |A2 |? This is Question 8 in(G. M. Bergman, J. Iranian Math. Soc., 1(2020), 157–161). It is known(ibid.) that the corresponding statement is true for the subgroups ⟨A1 ⟩ and ⟨A3 ⟩. Moreover, |A2 | will at least divide the order of the least subgroup containing A2 and closed under conjugation by members of A1, and similarly of the least subgroup containing A2 and closed under conjugation by members of A3.

Suppose that S and M are groups of finite Morley rank, S is an infinite group, and M is a non-trivial connected group definably and faithfully acting on S.
