For every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X, must the range R(ν_f) = {∫_A f dμ : A ∈ Σ} of the associated vector measure ν_f be separable?

Suppose μ is a quasi-Radon probability measure. For every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X, must the range R(ν_f) = {∫_A f dμ : A ∈ Σ} of the associated vector measure be relatively norm compact in X?
context_brief: Norm compactness for quasi-Radon Pettis ranges

question_text: Suppose a Banach space X does not contain a copy of c_0. For every Pettis integrable function f: Ω → X, must the range R(ν_f) = {∫_A f dμ : A ∈ Σ} of the associated vector measure be relatively norm compact?

Does there exist a non-uniform Eberlein compact space K such that C(K) belongs to the class U of Banach spaces for which every Pettis integrable function f: [0, 1] → X is McShane integrable? Equivalently, are there non-uniform Eberlein compacta in the class K = {K : C(K) ∈ U}?
context_brief: Non-uniform Eberlein compacta in class K

question_text: Let f: Ω → X be a function on a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) with values in a Banach space X. If T_1 and T_2 are two topologies on Ω for which μ is quasi-Radon, and f is McShane integrable with respect to T_1, must f also be McShane integrable with respect to T_2?
context_brief: Topology dependence of the McShane integral

question_text: Characterize the Banach spaces X for which the closed unit ball B_X is contained in the range of some X-valued countably additive vector measure.
Let K be a weakly compact subset of c_0. Must there exist a c_0-valued countably additive vector measure whose range contains K?
context_brief: Weakly compact subsets of c_0 as vector-measure ranges

question_text: Let ν_1 and ν_2 be vector measures of finite variation with the same range R(ν_1) = R(ν_2), and assume that both variation measures |ν_1| and |ν_2| are perfect. Must ν_1 and ν_2 have the same Pettis differentiability behavior with respect to their own variations?
Let X be a Banach space that does not contain a copy of ℓ_1, and let ν be an X-valued vector measure whose integration operator I_ν: L^1(ν) → X is completely continuous. Must ν have finite variation?
Suppose ν is a non-atomic vector measure. Do there exist a set Γ and a vector measure ν̃: Σ → c_0(Γ) such that the associated spaces of integrable functions coincide, namely L^1(ν) = L^1(ν̃)?
Characterize when the norming set Γ = {γ_{g,x*} : g ∈ B_{L^∞(ν)}, x* ∈ B_{X*}} is a James boundary of L^1(ν), meaning that every f ∈ L^1(ν) attains its norm at some functional γ_{g,x*} in Γ.
If the dual unit ball B_{X^*} is weak*-sequentially compact, must the dual unit ball B_{L^p(μ,X)^*} of the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p(μ, X) also be weak*-sequentially compact?
context_brief: Weak-star sequential compactness in Lebesgue-Bochner duals

question_text: If a Banach space X is strongly weakly compactly generated, must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^1(μ, X) also be strongly weakly compactly generated?
If a Banach space X is strongly weakly K-analytic, or strongly weakly countably determined, must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p(μ, X) inherit the same corresponding property?
Characterize the Banach spaces X for which the vector-valued Lebesgue space L^p([0, 1], X), with 1 < p < ∞, has an unconditional basis.
For which separable Banach spaces X are the Hilbertian sum ℓ_2(X) and the Lebesgue-Bochner space L_2([0, 1], X) isomorphic as Banach spaces?
For which separable Banach spaces X does the Lebesgue-Bochner space L_1([0, 1], X) contain a subspace isomorphic to ℓ_2(X)?
context_brief: Copies of ℓ_2(X) inside L_1([0,1], X)

question_text: For which Banach spaces X are the spaces ℓ_∞(X) and L_∞([0, 1], X) isomorphic?

Does L^1[0, 1] have property (D_∞), meaning that every sequence of strongly measurable functions f_n: [0, 1] → L^1[0, 1] which is bounded in L^∞([0, 1], L^1[0, 1]) and converges scalarly in measure to 0 admits a subsequence that converges scalarly to 0 almost everywhere?

Are there infinite-dimensional reflexive Banach spaces with property (D_1), meaning that every sequence of strongly measurable functions f_n: [0, 1] → X which is bounded in L^1([0, 1], X) and converges scalarly in measure to 0 has a subsequence that converges scalarly to 0 almost everywhere?
Given a distinguished generating set for the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope, what analogue of the intersection condition holds?
How can one build a general polytope as a coset geometry of its automorphism group when a distinguished generating set is given?
Can one find a combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion for coverings that works beyond the regular and chiral cases?
Which polytopes P have the property that their monodromy group Mon(P) is a string C-group?
Does there exist a polytope P whose monodromy group Mon(P) is not a string C-group but that still has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover, or can one prove that no such polytope exists?
Given a string group generated by involutions, what are the minimal string C-groups that cover it?
What is the correct way to generalize the chirality group from two-orbit polytopes to k-orbit polytopes?
Given a polytope P, how can one determine the size of its monodromy group |Mon(P)|?
Which pairs of rooted polytopes have the property that their mix is itself a polytope?
For every k >= 1 and every n >= 3, does there exist a k-orbit n-polytope with no rank-2 section that is a digon?
Given a group Gamma, for which integers k >= 1 and n >= 3 is Gamma the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope or maniplex of rank n?

If a connected properly edge-colored n-regular graph satisfies the usual allowable-graph condition that every alternating i,j,i,j walk with |i-j| > 1 returns to its starting point, must it be the symmetry type graph of some maniplex?
Are there constructions of (n + 1)-polytopes from n-polytopes whose resulting symmetry type graphs differ from the families produced in Theorem 4.2 and from their duals?
Which combinatorial symmetry type graphs occur among convex polytopes, and which geometric symmetry type graphs occur among convex polytopes?
Do there exist polytopes P and Q such that the amalgamation class hP, Qi is nonempty and P has at least two non-isomorphic vertex-figures?
Whenever there is a rooted amalgamation of polytopes P and Q, is there always a universal rooted amalgamation of P and Q?
Which pairs of polytopes P and Q have a nonempty amalgamation class hP, Qi for which the number of flag orbits among polytopes in hP, Qi is bounded?
Which k-orbit polytopes P admit a universal k-orbit extension that covers every other k-orbit extension of P?
Given two polytopes P and Q, when does there exist a polytope whose facets are each isomorphic to either P or Q, and when can such a polytope be finite?
Describe all chiral polytopes of full rank.
Describe all chiral polytopes of nearly full rank.
For each symmetry type graph T, what is the largest n such that finite or infinite n-polytopes admit a faithful symmetric realization in Euclidean space E^d with symmetry type graph T?
context_brief: Maximal realization rank by symmetry graph

question_text: Describe all two-orbit polytopes of full rank.
For k <= d, find all k-orbit realizations in Euclidean space E^d of regular d-polytopes.
Determine the number N_k for each k, or improve the known bounds on N_k, where N_k bounds the dimensions in which geometrically k-orbit convex polytopes can exist.
context_brief: Dimension bounds for convex k-orbit polytopes

question_text: For which values of k and d does there exist a convex d-polytope with exactly k combinatorial flag orbits?
context_brief: Combinatorial flag orbits in convex polytopes

question_text: For which values of k and d does there exist a convex d-polytope with exactly k geometric flag orbits?
context_brief: Geometric flag orbits in convex polytopes

question_text: For which values of k and d is the following true: if a k-orbit d-polytope P is realized as a convex d-polytope, then P must be isomorphic to a geometrically k-orbit convex polytope?
context_brief: When convex realization preserves k-orbit geometry

question_text: Classify all two-orbit polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space H^3.
Classify all two-orbit 4-polytopes in hyperbolic 3-space H^3.
Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of k-orbit polytopes.
Which k-orbit d-polytopes admit a faithful realization in Euclidean space E^d as geometrically k-orbit polytopes?
Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of m-orbit polytopes.
Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of regular polytopes.
Develop a theory of realizations of regular polytopes in hyperbolic spaces.

Let (X, d) be a metric space, let 2^X denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X, meaning the weakest topology that makes each distance functional A -> d(x, A) continuous for every x in X. Characterize exactly when the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is a normal topological space.

For a metric space (X, d), it is known that if (X, d) is separable then the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is metrizable and therefore paracompact and normal. Is the converse true? Equivalently, is (2^X, T_W(d)) normal if and only if it is metrizable?
Suppose (X, d) is a uniformly discrete non-separable metric space. Must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be non-normal?
If (X, d) is a non-separable metric space, must its Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) contain a closed copy of the space omega_1 x (omega_1 + 1)?
Whenever a metric space (X, d) has non-normal Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)), must that hyperspace contain a closed copy of omega_1 x (omega_1 + 1)?
If (X, d) is completely metrizable, with no separability assumption, is that equivalent to some completeness-type topological property of the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d))?
Let X be a completely metrizable space. For every metric d compatible with the topology of X, must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be strongly Choquet, or at least strongly alpha-favorable?

Let X be a metrizable space. If, for every metric d compatible with the topology of X, the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is strongly Choquet or strongly alpha-favorable, must X itself be completely metrizable?

If a metric space (X, d) is pseudocomplete, must its Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) also be pseudocomplete? Likewise, if (X, d) is subcompact or base-compact, must (2^X, T_W(d)) inherit the corresponding property?
Given a metric space (X, d), characterize when the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is a Baire space, using properties of the underlying metric space (X, d).
Let (X, d) be a metric space such that each finite power X^n is a Baire space for every positive integer n. Must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) also be a Baire space?
If (X, d) is a Baire metric space, must its Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be a Baire space?
If (X, d) is a hereditarily Baire metric space, must its Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be a Baire space?
Let X be a metrizable space. If, for every metric d compatible with the topology of X, the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is a Baire space, must X itself be a Baire space?

Let X be a metrizable space. If, for every metric d compatible with the topology of X, the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is a Baire space, must the Vietoris hyperspace (2^X, T_V) also be a Baire space?
Let X be a metrizable space. If the Vietoris hyperspace (2^X, T_V) is a Baire space, must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be a Baire space for every metric d compatible with the topology of X?

Let R(x) = sum_{n>=0} s(n)x^n be a power series in Z[[x]] that is algebraic over Q(x) and unramified at x = 0. Suppose that for all sufficiently large primes p one has s(p) == 0 mod p. Characterize all such algebraic functions with this Fermat property, both in general and inside a fixed algebraic function field Q(x, U) where U is unramified at x = 0.

Let F be the abelian group of algebraic functions with the Fermat property. Let D be the subgroup generated by logarithmic derivatives U^(partial)(x) = xU'(x) of algebraic functions U(x), let Z[x] be the polynomial subgroup, and let P be the subgroup generated by finite sums of power-substituted algebraic functions U_j(x^{M_j}) with M_j >= 2. For an algebraic function U over Q(x) that is unramified at x = 0, let F_U = F intersect Q(x, U), D_U = D intersect Q(x, U), and P_U = P intersect Q(x, U). Determine the structure of the quotient groups F/(D + Z[x] + P), A_U = F_U/(D_U + Z[x]), and P_U = F_U/(D_U + Z[x] + P_U). In particular, determine the corresponding quotient in the purely rational case Q(x).

Let p(n) be the partition function, so that sum_{n>=0} p(n)x^n = product_{k>=1} (1 - x^k)^(-1). Define integers n_k by the power-product expansion sum_{n>=0} p(n)x^n = product_{k>=1} (1 + n_k x^k). Explore the arithmetic properties of the sequence (n_k). In particular, determine whether n(8k + 2), n(8k + 4), and n(8k + 6) are always negative while n(8k) is always positive for every k >= 1.

Let lambda_n(s) be the canonically indexed eigenvalues of the Mayer-Ruelle transfer operator for the Gauss continued-fraction map, indexed so that the labeling by n is canonical and corresponds to ordering by magnitude. For each nontrivial zero rho of the Riemann zeta function, let t(rho) be the integer M such that lambda_M(rho/2) = 1. Given a fixed integer M in N, determine what can be said about the set t^(-1)(M): whether it is infinite, how the conjectural distribution of Riemann zeros changes when restricted to that set, and how one can compute sets such as t^(-1)(1) effectively.

Let Z(s) = product_{n>=1} (1 - lambda_n(s)^2) be the Selberg zeta function written in terms of the canonically indexed eigenvalues lambda_n(s) of the Mayer-Ruelle transfer operator. For k in N, the order of vanishing of Z(s) at s = 1 - k equals dim_C(M_{2k}), where M_{2k} is the corresponding space of cusp forms for PSL_2(Z). Determine how the quantity dim_C(M_{2k}) is distributed among the individual factors in the product Z(1 - k) = product_{n>=1} (1 - lambda_n(1 - k)^2).

Let T(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n) be a norm form written in some integral basis of a proper degree-n extension of Q. Determine all functions f: Z -> C such that T(f(a_1), f(a_2), ..., f(a_n)) depends only on the value T(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n), rather than on the specific tuple (a_1, a_2, ..., a_n).

Let h(X) = X^3 - 3X + 1, let alpha be a root of h, let alpha' = alpha^2 - 2, and let K = Q(alpha). With respect to the integral basis {1, alpha, alpha'}, the norm form is T(a, b, c) = N(a + b alpha + c alpha') = a^3 - b^3 - c^3 - 3ab^2 - 3ac^2 + 3abc + 6b^2c - 3bc^2. Determine all functions f, h: Z -> C such that T(f(a), f(b), f(c)) = h(T(a, b, c)).

An uphill lattice path is a doubly infinite monotone path in R^2 made of unit steps from (a, b) to either (a, b + 1) or (a + 1, b), and a downhill lattice path is defined similarly with b - 1 in place of b + 1. For a finite set P of points in Z^2, call such a monotone lattice path friendly if the number of points of P on one side of the path equals the number on the other side, ignoring points that lie on the path itself. Is it true that every odd-sized finite set of lattice points has a friendly path?

Given an n x n square subdivided into n^2 unit squares in the usual way, call a line intersecting a unit square if the line and the unit square share a common point that is an interior point of the unit square. Determine the minimum number of lines needed so that every unit square is intersected. In particular, decide whether this minimum equals n - 1 for every n >= 3.

Let ?(x) be the Minkowski question mark function on [0, 1], defined by ?([0, a_1, a_2, a_3, ...]) = 2^(1-a_1) - 2^(1-(a_1+a_2)) + 2^(1-(a_1+a_2+a_3)) - ... for the regular continued-fraction expansion x = [0, a_1, a_2, ...]. Define rational functions Q_n(z) = B_n(z)z^(-n-1) by Q_0(z) = -1/(2z) and Q_n(z) = (1/2) sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (1/j!) (d^j/dz^j Q_{n-j-1}(-1)) (z^j - 1/z^(j+2)). Is it true that Lambda(t) = sum_{n>=0} Q_n'(-1)t^n/n! is an entire function and that int_0^infty Lambda(t)e^(-t) dt = int_0^1 x^2 d?(x)?
context_brief: Moments of the Minkowski question mark function

question_text: For n >= 2, let psi_n be the infimum of |Gamma|/n! over all finite subgroups Gamma of GL(n, R) for which there exists a Gamma-superflow. Here a Gamma-superflow is a flow whose vector field is a nonzero vector field Q(x) = (Q_1, ..., Q_n) with 2-homogeneous rational components, invariant under Gamma by gamma^(-1) o Q o gamma = Q for all gamma in Gamma, and unique up to scalar among invariant vector fields of minimal common-denominator degree. Is it true that psi_n = 2 for every n >= 3?

Let a(n) be Stern's diatomic sequence, defined by a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1, a(2n) = a(n), and a(2n + 1) = a(n) + a(n + 1). For L in N_0, define Q^(L)(N) = sum_{n=2^N+1}^{2^(N+1)} a(n)^L. Proposition 1 states that there is a unique algebraic number mu_L and a constant c_L such that Q^(L)(N)/2^N is asymptotic to c_L mu_L^N. Does there exist a function p(x) - analytic, continuous of bounded variation, or more generally a distribution - such that int_0^((1+sqrt(5))/2) x^L dp(x) = mu_L for every L >= 0?
context_brief: Moment representation for Stern sequence growth

question_text: Let vartheta(n) be the number of compositions of a positive integer n into powers of 2, and for each integer a let Theta(a) = lim_{k->infty} vartheta(2^k + a) in the 2-adic integers Z_2. Describe the arithmetic properties of the numbers Theta(a). In particular, determine whether Theta(a) is rational or algebraic over Q.
context_brief: 2-adic limits of the binary composition function

question_text: Let f: I -> R be a convex C^infinity function on an interval I, and for a < b in I define N(alpha, beta) = alpha(f(a) + f(b)) + beta f((a + b)/2) with 2alpha + beta = 1. Determine the best possible constants alpha* and beta* for which the upper Hermite-Hadamard-type inequality (1/(b - a)) integral_a^b f(t) dt <= N(alpha*, beta*) holds for every such smooth convex function and every choice of a < b in I. Equivalently, find the smallest universal endpoint weight alpha* such that alpha*(f(a) + f(b)) + (1 - 2alpha*) f((a + b)/2) always dominates the integral mean of every smooth convex function. The paper shows that N(1/4, 1/2) works for all convex integrable functions, and that the sharper candidate N(1/6, 2/3) is best possible only under the additional assumption that f'' is convex (equivalently, f^(4) >= 0), so the universal optimum for all smooth convex functions remains open.
context_brief: Best universal upper bound refining Hermite-Hadamard

question_text: Given a modulus of continuity ω, construct a compact set K such that the Green function g_{C\K} for the complement C\K with pole at infinity has modulus of continuity comparable to ω. More precisely, require the modulus ω(g_{C\K},·) to be similar to ω, for example by weak equivalence in the sense that there exist constants C1,C2>0 such that C1·ω(δ) ≤ ω(g_{C\K},δ) ≤ C2·ω(δ) for all sufficiently small positive δ.

Given a modulus of continuity ω, construct a compact set K for which the Green function g_{C\K} satisfies two-sided pointwise bounds in terms of the distance to K. Specifically, if δ=dist(z,K), require constants C1,C2,δ0>0 independent of z such that C1·ω(δ) ≤ g_{C\K}(z) ≤ C2·ω(δ) whenever δ ≤ δ0.

Find a compact set K contained in the real line for which the Green function g_{C\K} has two-sided Hölder behavior near K. That is, determine whether there exists α>0 and constants C1,C2>0 such that, for all z with sufficiently small δ=dist(z,K), one has C1·δ^α ≤ g_{C\K}(z) ≤ C2·δ^α.
context_brief: Two-sided Hölder Green function on R

question_text: Characterize the growth rates of the Markov factors M_n(K), where M_n(K) is the operator norm of differentiation on holomorphic polynomials of degree at most n with the uniform norm on an infinite compact set K, that determine the boundary of the 'zone of uncertainty' for the extension property. Here the extension property means the existence of a continuous linear extension operator from the Whitney function space E(K) to the space of infinitely differentiable functions on R^d.

Let (f_n) be a regular polynomial sequence, meaning f_n(z)=Σ_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j with d_n≥2 for every n and with positive constants A1,A2,A3 such that |a_{n,d_n}|≥A1, |a_{n,j}|≤A2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0≤j<d_n, and log|a_{n,d_n}|≤A3 d_n. Assume the generalized Julia set J(f_n) is a Cantor-type subset of the real line. Prove that the recurrence coefficients in the three-term recurrence for the equilibrium measure μ_{J(f_n)} are asymptotically almost periodic, in the sense that they converge to an almost periodic sequence up to an error tending to zero.

Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R, let μ_K be its equilibrium measure, and let P_n(x;μ_K) be the n-th monic orthogonal polynomial with zero set Z_n(μ_K)={x:P_n(x;μ_K)=0}. If U_n(μ_K)=inf{|x-x'|: x,x'∈Z_n(μ_K), x≠x'} denotes the minimal spacing between distinct zeros, determine whether there is a general relationship between this zero spacing and the smoothness of the Green function g_{C\K}; also determine whether there is a general relationship between that zero spacing and the Markov factors of K.
context_brief: Zero spacing, Green function, Markov factors

question_text: Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R that is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, and let μ be a measure with essential support ess supp(μ)=K whose isolated support points {x_n} satisfy Σ_n g_{C\K}(x_n)<∞. Suppose the logarithmic integrability condition ∫_K log(dμ/dμ_K) dμ_K(x) > -∞ holds, where μ_K is the equilibrium measure on K. Must μ then satisfy either the Widom condition limsup_{n→∞} W_n^2(μ)>0 or the Widom condition 2 liminf_{n→∞} W_n^2(μ)>0? Conversely, if μ satisfies a Widom condition, must the logarithmic integrability condition hold?

Does there exist a regular non-polar compact subset K of R that is not a Parreau-Widom set but whose Widom factors W_n(K)=||T_{n,K}||_{L^∞(K)}/Cap(K)^n remain bounded? More specifically, if K has zero Lebesgue measure, must the sequence (W_n(K)) be unbounded? The same questions are asked for the Widom-Hilbert factors (W_n^2(μ_K)) associated with the equilibrium measure μ_K.

Let K be a regular non-polar compact subset of R with leftmost endpoint α, and let μ_K be its equilibrium measure. Assume that μ_K([α,c]) is rational for every c∈R\K. Characterize such sets K. In particular, must every such K be a polynomial generalized Julia set, or equivalently must there exist a sequence (f_n) of admissible polynomials such that, with F_n=f_n∘f_{n-1}∘···∘f_1, the inverse-image sets F_n^{-1}([-1,1]) form a decreasing sequence and K=⋂_{n=1}^∞ F_n^{-1}([-1,1])?
context_brief: Rational equilibrium masses and generalized Julia sets

question_text: Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R such that the equilibrium measure μ_K coincides with a Hausdorff measure restricted to K. Must the Hausdorff dimension of K be equal to 0?
context_brief: When equilibrium measure is Hausdorff measure

question_text: For a regular polynomial sequence (f_n), find simple formulas for the Hausdorff dimension of the measure μ_{J(f_n)} supported on the generalized Julia set J(f_n). Here the Hausdorff dimension of a unit Borel measure μ is defined by dim(μ)=inf{HD(K): μ(K)=1}.
context_brief: Dimension formulas for Julia-set equilibrium measures

question_text: Let R be a commutative base ring, let A be an R-algebra, and let delta be either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation. Here an R-derivation is an R-linear map D: A -> A satisfying D(ab) = D(a)b + aD(b), and an R-E-derivation is an R-linear map delta: A -> A satisfying delta(ab) = delta(a)b + adelta(b) - delta(a)delta(b), equivalently delta = I - phi for some R-algebra endomorphism phi. For every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A, what is the radical r(delta(I)), where r(V) denotes the set of all a in A such that a^m belongs to V for all sufficiently large m?

Let R be a commutative base ring, let A be an R-algebra, and let delta be either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation. Which such maps have the property that their image Im delta = delta(A) is a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace of A? Here a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace V of A means that whenever a^m lies in V for every m >= 1, the products ba^m, a^m c, or ba^m c eventually lie in V in the corresponding left, right, or two-sided case.

Let R be a commutative base ring, let A be an R-algebra, and let delta be either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation. Which such maps send every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A to a corresponding left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace delta(I) of A? Here a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace V of A means that whenever a^m lies in V for every m >= 1, the products ba^m, a^m c, or ba^m c eventually lie in V in the corresponding left, right, or two-sided case.

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be either a locally finite K-derivation or a locally finite K-E-derivation. Here locally finite means that for each a in A, the K-submodule spanned by delta^i(a) for i >= 0 is finitely generated. Is the image Im delta = delta(A) always a two-sided Mathieu subspace of A, meaning that if a^m belongs to Im delta for every m >= 1, then ba^m c also belongs to Im delta for all sufficiently large m and all b, c in A?

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be either a locally nilpotent K-derivation or a locally nilpotent K-E-derivation. Here locally nilpotent means that for each a in A there exists m >= 1 such that delta^m(a) = 0. For every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A, must the image delta(I) be a corresponding left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace of A? Here a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace V of A means that whenever a^m lies in V for every m >= 1, the products ba^m, a^m c, or ba^m c eventually lie in V in the corresponding left, right, or two-sided case.

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be a locally finite K-derivation or K-E-derivation. Here locally finite means that for each a in A, the K-submodule spanned by delta^i(a) for i >= 0 is finitely generated. If e is an idempotent element of Im delta, meaning e^2 = e, must the principal ideal (e) generated by e be contained in Im delta?

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be a locally nilpotent K-derivation or K-E-derivation. Here locally nilpotent means that for each a in A there exists m >= 1 such that delta^m(a) = 0. For every choice of left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A and every idempotent e in delta(I), meaning e^2 = e, must the corresponding left, right, or two-sided ideal generated by e be contained in delta(I)?

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let (Lambda, *) be a monoid with unit e such that A has a K-algebra grading A = direct sum of A_lambda over lambda in Lambda, with each A_lambda a K-subspace and A_lambda A_mu contained in A_{lambda*mu} for all lambda and mu. Must the direct sum of all homogeneous components of degree different from e, namely the sum of A_lambda over all lambda != e, be a two-sided Mathieu subspace of A? Here a two-sided Mathieu subspace V means that if a^m belongs to V for every m >= 1, then ba^m c belongs to V for all sufficiently large m and all b, c in A.

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let z = (z1, z2, ..., zn) be commutative or noncommutative free variables. In the Laurent polynomial algebra A[z^{-1}, z], let M be the K-subspace consisting of all Laurent polynomials with no constant term. Is M always a two-sided Mathieu subspace of A[z^{-1}, z]? Here a two-sided Mathieu subspace V means that if f^m belongs to V for every m >= 1, then g f^m h belongs to V for all sufficiently large m and all g, h in the algebra.

For suitable perturbations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0 on the real line and suitable almost periodic initial data u_0(x), does the Cauchy problem have a unique global solution u(x,t) that evolves almost periodically in time?

For random n x n band matrices H with bandwidth w <= n and independent entries H_ij inside the band, can one prove the Fyodorov-Mirlin conjecture that the local eigenvalue statistics are in the GUE universality class when w is much larger than sqrt(n), but become Poisson when w is much smaller than sqrt(n), in both the real symmetric and complex Hermitian settings?

For random Schrodinger operators H = -Delta + V with random potential V, can one rigorously analyze the bulk spectral regime where eigenfunctions are expected to delocalize and eigenvalues are expected to follow random-matrix statistics, and can one construct and analyze models that exhibit the conjectured transition from Poisson statistics to random-matrix statistics at a mobility edge?

For Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure is supported on more than one interval, can one prove universality in the bulk and at all spectral edges, and can one also analyze parameter regimes in which intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open and close?

For random-matrix models that depend on external parameters p and undergo critical changes in the support of the equilibrium measure at values p_c, can one rigorously analyze the corresponding double-scaling and more general multi-scaling limits in which p approaches p_c while the matrix size n tends to infinity?

Can one obtain rigorous explicit formulas for Tracy-Widom distribution functions for general beta-ensembles beyond the classical invariant cases beta = 1, 2, and 4, including a rigorous completion of Rumanov's approach for all even beta > 0 and a rigorous verification of the asymptotic formulas proposed by Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal for general beta > 0?

For the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation with general initial data, can one prove full 3:2:1 KPZ universality in the strong sense proposed by Corwin, Quastel, and Remenik for solutions of the Cauchy problem, and can one identify the limiting process that arises in that scaling limit?
Can one analyze solutions of the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation simultaneously at more than one space-time point, rather than only through one-point statistics?
For last-passage percolation with general weights, can one prove the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling law, meaning time scale 3, spatial-correlation scale 2, and fluctuation scale 1 in the KPZ normalization?
For the longest increasing subsequence problem, can one prove KPZ-class fluctuation results when the permutation is sampled from distributions more general than the uniform distribution?
Can one explain the mechanism behind Tracy and Widom's solution of the asymmetric simple exclusion process with step initial data, and extend that method to more general initial data sets?

Can one develop a perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ-type interacting-particle models that plays a role analogous to KAM theory in integrable dynamical systems, so that persistence of integrability-like structure and robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena can be studied beyond exactly solvable models?

For the Toda algorithm applied to random Hermitian matrices, where the stopping time T^(1)(H) is used to compute the largest eigenvalue, can one prove universality for the centered and scaled stopping-time variable in the cases of beta = 1 invariant ensembles and beta = 1 or 2 Wigner ensembles?

For the QR algorithm applied to random matrices, can one control, as n tends to infinity, the bulk eigenvalue-ratio statistics |lambda_{j+1}/lambda_j| and |lambda_{j-1}/lambda_j| near the eigenvalue lambda_j closest to zero, together with the associated normalized eigenvectors, so as to prove the analogue of the Toda-algorithm universality theorem for QR?

For some eigenvalue algorithm A, can one prove a universality theorem for the deflation time T_{epsilon,n,A,E}, where T_{epsilon,n,A,E} is the smallest time at which the evolving matrix becomes approximately block diagonal to accuracy epsilon and the problem depends on statistics of both eigenvalues and eigenvectors?

Can one rigorously prove universality for one of the other numerical algorithms with random data discussed in the paper, especially the conjugate-gradient algorithm for solving a random linear system A x = b with both A and b random?

Can the orthogonal-polynomial-based sampling method developed by Olver, Nadakuditi, and Trogdon for invariant unitary ensembles be extended to orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles, while retaining its essentially machine-accuracy sampling behavior?

For the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line, i u_t = u_{xx} + 2 |u|^2 u for x >= 0 and t >= 0, with prescribed initial data u(x,0) = f(x) and oscillatory boundary forcing u(0,t) = e^{i w t}, can one compute the long-time asymptotic behavior of the solution u(x,t) for general real driving frequency w?

For the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line with oscillatory boundary forcing u(0,t) = e^{i w t}, can one show that as w decreases toward 0 the boundary drive excites k-gap solutions of periodic NLS?

Can the Bikbaev-Tarasov Backlund-transform method be adapted to solve the initial-boundary value problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation i u_t = u_{xx} - 2 |u|^2 u on the half-line with Robin boundary condition u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0, despite the singularities introduced when the solution is extended from x > 0 to x < 0?

For the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line with Robin boundary conditions and smooth matching initial and boundary data, can one prove that the initial-boundary value problem remains classical in x > 0 and t > 0 for a general class of smooth nonlinearities, rather than relying on the special Backlund-transform structure available only for the cubic focusing case?
More generally, what smoothness can be proved for solutions of initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations in arbitrary spatial dimension?

For the semiclassical focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation, can one solve the forward scattering problem for general smooth initial data and then implement the associated Riemann-Hilbert numerical methodology to compute the Cauchy problem in the small-dispersion limit epsilon = hbar down to 0?

For the Airy integral operator A_s on L^2(s, infinity), whose Fredholm determinant gives the edge-scaling distribution for the largest GUE eigenvalue, can one analyze the eigenfunctions u_tilde_j(s) asymptotically as s tends to infinity and also compute them accurately for finite s?

For perturbations of the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation of the form i u_tilde_t + u_tilde_xx + 2 |u_tilde|^2 u_tilde + epsilon |u_tilde|^ell u_tilde = 0 with decaying initial data, can one analyze the long-time behavior of solutions, especially in the case where the initial data correspond to a two-soliton solution of the unperturbed focusing NLS equation?

Can one use Riemann-Hilbert and nonlinear steepest-descent methods to give a fully rigorous proof of the asymptotic results obtained by Venakides, Deift, and Oba for the Toda shock problem, where the driven lattice settles into a one-gap periodic state for sufficiently strong driving?

If the exponential interaction in the Toda shock problem is replaced by a nearby force law F(x) so that the lattice equation becomes x_doubleprime_k = F(x_{k-1} - x_k) - F(x_k - x_{k+1}), can one analyze the general shock problem for suitably small perturbations F(x) of e^x and prove the numerically observed asymptotic behavior?

Can one give a rigorous and explicit mathematical solution of the diffraction problem for waves passing through two finite slits in the plane, the setting underlying Young's double-slit experiment in optics and the analogous double-slit experiment in quantum mechanics?

Do there exist overcomplete Gabor frames for L^2(R), meaning systems of the form {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} with g in L^2(R) and parameters a,b>0 that form a frame but not a Riesz basis, together with some ordering {f_k}_{k in I} of the frame elements, such that the ordered frame can be written as {f_k}_{k in I} = {T^k phi}_{k in I} for a bounded linear operator T and some vector phi?
context_brief: bounded operator representation of overcomplete Gabor frames

question_text: Assume an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} admits an ordering {f_k} for which {f_k}_{k in I} = {T^k phi}_{k in I} with bounded T. Must such a bounded-operator representation exist for both indexing choices I=N_0={0,1,2,...} and I=Z, or can the existence of a bounded representation depend on whether the ordered orbit is one-sided or two-sided?
context_brief: indexing dependence for Gabor orbit representations

question_text: Given an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z}, which orderings {f_k}_{k in I} of its elements have the property that the ordered frame can be represented as an operator orbit {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for some bounded linear operator T? In other words, can one characterize exactly which permutations or sequential arrangements of the same Gabor frame yield a bounded generating operator?
context_brief: characterizing admissible orderings of Gabor frames

question_text: Which overcomplete Gabor frames {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} admit at least one ordering {f_k}_{k in I} for which there exists a bounded linear operator T and a vector phi with {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I}? Equivalently, what conditions on the lattice parameters a,b>0 and the window g in L^2(R) determine whether some ordering of the frame can be generated by iterating a bounded operator?
context_brief: which Gabor frames admit some bounded ordering

question_text: Is there a single universal ordering rule {f_k}_{k in I} that works for every overcomplete Gabor frame that admits some bounded-operator orbit representation, so that whenever a frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} is of a type covered by the previous existence question, arranging its elements according to that one rule always yields {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for a bounded operator T?
context_brief: universal ordering for bounded Gabor representations

question_text: Let phi in L^2(R) and b>0 be such that the translate system {T_{kb} phi}_{k in Z} is an overcomplete frame. Although this system always has the two-sided representation {(T_b)^k phi}_{k in Z} with bounded translation operator T_b, is it possible to reorder the same frame into a one-sided sequence {f_k}_{k=0}^infty and find a bounded linear operator T such that {f_k}_{k=0}^infty={T^k phi}_{k=0}^infty?
context_brief: one-sided bounded representation for translate frames

question_text: Does there exist a separable Hilbert space H with an overcomplete frame {f_k}_{k=0}^infty whose vectors are uniformly bounded away from zero in norm and for which there is a bounded linear operator T from H to H such that f_k=T^k f_0 for every k>=0? Equivalently, can an overcomplete frame that does not decay in norm still be generated as a one-sided bounded operator orbit?
context_brief: norm-bounded-below overcomplete operator orbits in Hilbert space

question_text: Let RT(k) be the repetition threshold on a k-letter alphabet, and let FRT(k) be the finite repetition threshold, meaning that only finitely many factors of the critical exponent are allowed in the corresponding infinite word. Is it true that FRT(4) = RT(4) = 7/5?
A distinct square means a square factor considered up to shape, not merely by translated occurrence. Is every word of length n guaranteed to contain at most n distinct square factors?

Define the square density of a finite word w by ρsq(w) = #{x^2 in Σ+ such that x^2 is a factor of w} / |w|. Does there exist a mapping f: Σ* -> Σ* and a constant c > 1 such that, for every word w with ρsq(w) >= 1, the transformed word satisfies ρsq(f(w)) >= cρsq(w)?

A run is an occurrence of a repetition of exponent at least 2 that is maximal in the sense that it cannot be extended to the left or right while keeping the same type of repetition. Is every binary word of length n guaranteed to have at most n runs?

For an infinite word u, let Ru(n) be the size of the smallest window that contains every factor of length n of u, and define the recurrence quotient by ρ(u) = lim sup_{n->infinity} Ru(n)/n. For a Sturmian sequence of slope α, write ρ(α), and let S be the set of values taken by ρ(α) as α ranges over irrational numbers in [0,1]. What is the Hausdorff dimension of S, or of each interval S ∩ [a, a + 1]?

For an infinite word u, let Ru(n) be the size of the smallest window that contains every factor of length n of u, and define the recurrence quotient by ρ(u) = lim sup_{n->infinity} Ru(n)/n. How does this recurrence quotient behave for families of infinite words beyond Sturmian words, such as words of complexity 2n + 1, or even for more general infinite words?

For a uniformly recurrent infinite word, let P(n) denote the number of distinct palindromes of length n occurring as factors and let p(n) denote the usual factor complexity. When the upper bound P(n) + P(n + 1) = p(n + 1) - p(n) + 2 is attained, what is the structure of the corresponding Rauzy graphs?

A word is quasiperiodic if there exists another word x such that every position of the word lies inside some occurrence of x as a factor. Given a morphism f and a letter a such that a is the initial letter of f(a), is it decidable whether the infinite fixed point f^ω(a) is quasiperiodic?

In the Post Correspondence Problem, an instance (h, g) is a unique equality continuation instance if, for every word u and every pair of distinct letters a and b, the comparabilities h(ua) ⊲⊳ g(ua) and h(ub) ⊲⊳ g(ub) together imply h(u) = g(u). Is the Post Correspondence Problem decidable for this class of instances?

Given a Post Correspondence Problem instance (h, g), can one decide whether it satisfies the unique equality continuation property, namely that for every word u and every pair of distinct letters a and b, the comparabilities h(ua) ⊲⊳ g(ua) and h(ub) ⊲⊳ g(ub) imply h(u) = g(u)?

What is a complete characterization of solid bricks, where a brick is a nonbipartite matching covered graph with no nontrivial tight cuts and a matching covered graph is solid when every separating cut is tight? Equivalently for bricks, which nonbipartite matching covered graphs are free of nontrivial separating cuts, and what is the computational complexity of deciding from a given brick whether it is solid? In particular, is this decision problem in NP, and is it solvable in polynomial time?

Is every cubic solid brick odd-intercyclic? Here a graph is odd-intercyclic when any two odd cycles in it have a vertex in common, and the question asks whether every 3-regular solid brick must satisfy that odd-cycle intersection property.
context_brief: cubic solid bricks versus odd cycles

question_text: What is a complete characterization of K4-free bricks, meaning bricks for which the complete graph K4 is not a conformal minor? Equivalently, which bricks fail to be K4-based under the paper's definition that a matching covered graph is J-based exactly when J is a conformal minor of it, and J-free otherwise?

What is a complete characterization of C6-free bricks, where C6 denotes the triangular prism and a brick is C6-free when that graph is not a conformal minor? Equivalently, which bricks are not C6-based under the paper's conformal-minor framework?

Can one obtain a complete classification of homogeneous Riemannian manifolds with homogeneous geodesics (g.o. spaces, meaning homogeneous spaces in which every geodesic is an orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of the acting group) in dimension 7 and in all higher dimensions?

For a homogeneous Riemannian manifold that is not a geodesic-orbit space, can one give an explicit description of its homogeneous geodesics, rather than only reducing the problem to algebraic conditions or computationally expensive searches?

Can one prove in a representation-independent way that the geodesic-orbit property of a homogeneous space does not depend on the chosen coset presentation M = G/K or on the chosen Ad(K)-invariant reductive decomposition g = k + m, especially when one wants to show that the space is in no way naturally reductive?

Can the Riemannian results that characterize when an orbit of the form gamma(t) = exp(t(a + x)) . o is a geodesic by Lie-algebraic conditions, and that characterize when a curve built from several exponential factors is geodesic, be extended from the Riemannian setting to pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous manifolds?

Is every search for three-step or higher-step homogeneous geodesics reducible to the study of two-step homogeneous geodesics, so that products of three or more exponential factors introduce no essentially new phenomenon beyond the two-step case?
Is the single-machine scheduling problem 1||sum w_j T_j, which minimizes total weighted tardiness, fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p_max, the maximum processing time of any job?

Does the single-machine precedence-constrained scheduling problem 1|prec|sum w_j C_j admit a kernel whose size is polynomial in the gap between the optimum objective value and the lower bound given by the natural LP relaxation?
Are the single-machine throughput problems 1|r_j|sum U_j and 1|r_j|sum w_j U_j W[1]-hard when parameterized by p_max, the maximum processing time?
For single-machine makespan minimization with tau forbidden start and completion times, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by tau?

Consider P||C_max on parallel identical machines with high-multiplicity encoding, where there are p distinct processing times and both the processing-time values and the counts of jobs of each type are encoded in binary. Is this problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p?

For the three-machine precedence-constrained scheduling problem P3|prec, p_j=1|C_max, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the width of the partial order induced by the precedence constraints?
Are the parallel identical machine problems P|r_j, p_j=p|sum w_j U_j and P|r_j, p_j=p|sum U_j fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines?

In the just-in-time or interval-scheduling problem P|M_j, d_j-r_j=p_j|sum w_j U_j on parallel identical machines, where each job can be processed only on an allowed subset of machines and its processing time equals the length of its release-to-due-date window, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines?

Let p be the number of distinct processing times. Are each of the three preemptive parallel-machine problems P|pmtn,r_j|sum C_j, P|pmtn|sum U_j, and P|pmtn|sum T_j fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p?

For two identical parallel machines with preemption, equal processing time p for every job, and objective sum w_j T_j, is the problem P2|pmtn, p_j=p|sum w_j T_j W[1]-hard when parameterized by the common processing time p?
context_brief: Preemptive tardiness hardness on two machines

question_text: For the three-machine flow-shop makespan problem F3||C_max, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p_max, the maximum processing time?

For the three-machine job-shop makespan problem J3||C_max, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized jointly by p_max, the maximum processing time, and n_max, the maximum number of operations in a job?

Is there an algorithm that computes a (1+epsilon)-approximation for job-shop makespan minimization J||C_max in time f(m, epsilon) * poly(n), depending on the number of machines m and approximation parameter epsilon but only polynomially on the input size?

For the open-shop problem O|p_ij=1, ST_sd,b|C_max with unit-time operations and sequence-dependent setup times between g batches, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number g of batches?
context_brief: Batch setup times in open shop

question_text: For the open-shop throughput problem O|p_ij=1, r_j|sum w_j U_j with unit-time operations and release dates, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines?
In asymptotically flat general relativity, prove the weak cosmic censorship conjecture: for generic initial data for the Einstein evolution problem, naked singularities do not occur.

Let M be a compact 3-dimensional manifold. Prove that for generic vacuum initial data on M, the maximal vacuum Cauchy development equals the maximal vacuum extension, so generic vacuum spacetimes cannot be continued beyond their maximal Cauchy development.

For general initial data in general relativity, either prove the Penrose inequality relating apparent-horizon area and total mass, or give a counterexample showing that the inequality fails in the general case.

For the Einstein-Vlasov and related collisionless matter models, prove global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for small initial data, and prove existence and uniqueness for general spatially homogeneous solutions such as Bianchi type IX while also analyzing the large-data regime.
Prove nonlinear stability of the Kerr black hole under perturbations, so that initial data sufficiently close to Kerr evolve in a way that remains close to a member of the Kerr family.
Give a mathematically appropriate definition of a dynamical horizon that correctly captures the evolving boundary of a black hole in general relativity.
Provide a rigorous proof of the geodesic hypothesis in general relativity: ideal test particles of negligible mass move along spacetime geodesics.

Determine whether the conjectured nonlinear instability of Anti-de Sitter spacetime, in which weak turbulence transfers energy to high frequencies and can trigger black hole formation, changes qualitatively in models more general than spherically symmetric scalar-field collapse.

Classify asymptotically flat black holes in spacetime dimension higher than four and determine whether higher-dimensional black holes satisfy a uniqueness theorem analogous to the four-dimensional Kerr uniqueness results.
Determine whether higher-dimensional black holes are stable under gravitational perturbations, including the kinds of instabilities that do not occur in four-dimensional general relativity.
Show whether the singularity-resolution results obtained in loop quantum gravity for spatially homogeneous spacetimes extend to a substantially more general setting beyond symmetry-reduced models.

Prove a cosmic no-hair theorem for generic inhomogeneous spacetimes, showing that initially expanding solutions with positive cosmological constant approach de Sitter-like behavior under appropriate physical assumptions.
For the Bianchi type IX dynamical system, prove that the past attractor is exactly the Mixmaster attractor, rather than merely a subset of it.

Prove the BKL locality conjecture for generic inhomogeneous cosmological spacetimes, namely that the asymptotic approach to a generic spacelike singularity becomes effectively local along each timeline.
Prove that spike features arise in generic singular solutions of Einstein's equations and determine how those recurring spikes affect any eventual proof describing generic spacelike singularities.

Determine whether the qualitative structure of generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities is stable when one includes the matter fields expected in the early universe, rather than restricting to vacuum or highly simplified matter models.
Determine whether isotropic singularities are typical in modified theories of gravity, rather than being a special feature of only restricted models.
Determine when a four-dimensional spacetime can be reconstructed explicitly from its scalar curvature invariants, and identify the minimal set of such invariants needed for that characterization.
Give a rigorous mathematical definition of averaging in general relativity that is suitable for coarse graining geometry and matter on a curved spacetime.

Determine whether averaging can play an important dynamical role in cosmology and, in particular, identify the largest scale on which matter and geometry can be coarse-grained while the averaged evolution still exactly satisfies Einstein's equations.
Resolve the black hole information paradox by explaining whether and how information is preserved during black hole formation and evaporation in a theory compatible with quantum mechanics.
Explain the cosmological constant problem and dark energy within a consistent mathematical-physical framework that accounts for the observed late-time acceleration of the universe.
Formulate a fully consistent theory of quantum gravity that unifies general relativity with quantum mechanics and remains mathematically coherent in regimes where both are essential.
Determine how generic inflation is for generic initial data, rather than only for highly tuned or specially prepared cosmological initial conditions.
Determine the gravitational-wave waveforms emitted by binary black hole systems with sufficient precision to support optimal detection and accurate parameter extraction.

Understand the critical solutions and critical behavior that arise at the threshold of black hole formation in gravitational collapse within general relativity, especially beyond highly symmetric settings.

Let G be a simple graph of order n with m edges, and let μ1 ≥ μ2 ≥ ··· ≥ μn = 0 be the Laplacian eigenvalues of G. Define σ(G) to be the largest integer σ with 1 ≤ σ ≤ n such that μσ ≥ 2m/n, where 2m/n is the average degree of G. Characterize all graphs G for which σ(G) = 1.

In integer trigonometry, an angle with integer vertex has an LLS-sequence (a0, a1, a2, ...) and integer tangent Itan(BAC) = [a0; a1 : a2 : ...], while integer cosine is defined by Icos(BAC) = Isin(BAC) / Itan(BAC). Find an integer cosine rule for integer triangles stated entirely in these integer-geometric invariants.

For integer polygons, each angle has an LLS-sequence, and the LLS-sequence is the complete invariant of an integer angle in this setting. Classify all n-tuples of LLS-sequences that can occur as the angle data of integer n-gons.

A sail is the boundary of C \ LS, where C is a cone of a hyperplane arrangement and LS is the union of all subsets U similar to a chosen model subset S that avoid a chosen subset L. Classify all combinatorially possible types of faces that can occur on such sails, especially for Klein polyhedra where S is a basis n-simplex and L = Z^n intersected with the punctured cone C.

An n-dimensional simplex is called empty when its intersection with the integer lattice Z^n consists exactly of its vertices. Classify all empty simplices of dimension n up to affine integer-lattice congruence.

For an m-dimensional continued fraction in the geometric sense of the paper, determine which integer n-gons can occur as faces. This includes both faces at integer distance 1 from the origin and faces at integer distance greater than 1 from the origin.

Suppose k runners start together on a circular track of circumference 1 and run with distinct constant speeds. Is it true that, for every chosen runner, there exists a time when that runner is lonely, meaning at arc distance at least 1/k from every other runner?
Describe all finite two-dimensional sails, and thereby all corresponding continued fractions, in the geometric multidimensional-continued-fraction setting.
For polytopes of a fixed combinatorial type, describe the collections of sails of the associated cones arising from all such polytopes.
Does there exist an algorithm that decides whether a specified combinatorial type of fundamental domain can be realized by a periodic continued fraction?

If two Klein sails are not integer congruent, must their torus decompositions be different? Here a torus decomposition means the collection of integer-congruence types of the polyhedra in a fundamental domain together with their integer distances to the vertex of the cone.

Describe all torus decompositions that are realized by periodic two-dimensional continued fractions, where the torus decomposition records the integer-congruence types of polyhedra in a fundamental domain together with their integer distances to the cone vertex.

Must the torus decomposition of every algebraic sail in the sense of Klein contain at least one face that is integer congruent to a triangle, at least one face at integer distance 1 from the cone vertex, and at least one face at integer distance greater than 1 from the cone vertex?
Classify the continued fractions that correspond to the same cubic extension of the field of rational numbers Q.
For dimensions n >= 3, prove the existence of a cone whose sail realizes a single prescribed non-periodic combinatorial structure.
For n-dimensional continued fractions in dimensions n >= 3, determine which faces have the highest relative frequencies.
For every positive integer constant C, are there only finitely many pairwise integer non-congruent faces whose relative frequencies exceed C?
In dimensions n >= 3, is the sum of the relative frequencies of all possible faces finite?

If the sum of the relative frequencies of all possible faces is finite in dimensions n >= 3, find the correct higher-dimensional analogue of the Gauss map and compare its face frequencies with the frequencies defined by Möbius geometry.
Find a natural generalization of the Farey tessellation to higher-dimensional hyperbolic geometry.

Let K be a totally real cubic number field, and let y and z be elements of K with 0 < y, z < 1 such that 1, y, and z are linearly independent over Q. Does the Jacobi-Perron algorithm started from v = (1, y, z) always produce an eventually periodic continued fraction?
Study the geometric properties of the Markov spectrum.

Generalize continued fractions so that they describe 3-bridge knots, in analogy with the way ordinary finite continued fractions give a complete invariant of rational knots, also called two-bridge knots.

For an arbitrary diversity (X, δ) on n points, what is the smallest worst-case function f(n) such that every such diversity admits an embedding into some ℓ1 diversity (R^d, δ̂) with distortion at most f(n)? Equivalently, determine the optimal asymptotic upper bound for the minimal distortion required to embed any n-point diversity into ℓ1 when the target dimension d is unrestricted.

Can one design a hybrid embedding method for diversities that combines the advantages of Bourgain-style arguments, which give low-distortion embeddings for diameter diversities, with Bartal-style tree-based arguments, which work for Steiner diversities, in order to obtain stronger general ℓ1 distortion bounds for arbitrary diversities? In particular, is there a principled way to use a Bartal-type approach on parts of the problem while switching to a Bourgain-type approach on subproblems where tree methods fail?

Can expander-hypergraph methods be developed to prove nontrivial lower bounds on the distortion needed to embed diversities into ℓ1, analogous to the role that expander graphs play for metric embeddings into ℓ1? More specifically, can the connection between diversity embedding and hypergraph sparsest cut be turned into rigorous lower-bound constructions for diversity distortion?

Does every n-point diversity admit an ℓ1 embedding with distortion O(sqrt(n)) by a construction that depends only on the induced metric d(x, y) = δ({x, y}) and not on any additional diversity-specific information? Equivalently, is there an embedding procedure derived solely from the induced metric that matches the known barrier that no such metric-only method can do better than Ω(sqrt(n)) in general?

Let an abelian square be a factor uv of a finite word such that u and v have the same Parikh vector, and let two abelian squares be considered distinct when they are different factor strings. Suppose a word of length n over an arbitrary alphabet contains k distinct abelian square factors. Must there always exist a binary word of the same length n that contains at least k distinct abelian square factors?
context_brief: Maximum distinct abelian squares across alphabet sizes

question_text: For binary words of length n, let XNL(n) denote the maximum possible number of pairwise non-equivalent abelian square factors, where an abelian square is a factor uv with matching Parikh vectors and two abelian squares are non-equivalent when their Parikh vectors differ. Is XNL(n) always bounded above by a constant multiple of n^1.5?
context_brief: Maximum non-equivalent abelian squares in binary words

question_text: Does there exist an infinite word over a three-letter alphabet in which every abelian square has length exactly 2? Equivalently, is there an infinite ternary word containing no abelian square of length greater than two, so that the only possible abelian square types are the one-letter doubles aa, bb, and cc?
context_brief: Avoiding long abelian squares on three letters

question_text: For a binary linear word of length n, let MDL(n) be the minimum possible number of distinct abelian square factors. Is MDL(n) always equal to floor(n/4)? In addition, when n = 4k + 3, are the only binary words that attain exactly k distinct abelian squares the word a^(2k+1) b a^(2k+1) and its complement?
context_brief: Minimum distinct abelian squares in binary linear words

question_text: For a binary circular word of length n, let the count ignore abelian squares longer than the word itself, and let two abelian squares be considered distinct when they are different factor strings. Is the minimum number of distinct abelian square factors equal to (n - 1)/2 when n is odd and to (n - 2)/2 when n is even? Moreover, in the odd case are the only extremal circular words the conjugates and complements of a^n and a^(n-1)b, and in the even case are the only extremal circular words the conjugates and complements of a^k b^(n-k) with odd k?
context_brief: Minimum distinct abelian squares in binary circular words

question_text: Among all binary words of length n, what is the minimum possible total number of occurrences of abelian squares, where occurrences are counted with multiplicity rather than up to distinctness or equivalence?
context_brief: Minimum total abelian-square occurrences in binary words

question_text: For a general isolated hypersurface singularity in C^n defined by the germ of a holomorphic function F, the Mather-Yau theorem says that the singularity is determined up to biholomorphism by n and the isomorphism class of the Tjurina algebra T_F = C[[z_1, ..., z_n]]/(F, F_{z_1}, ..., F_{z_n}). How can one explicitly reconstruct the singularity from this Tjurina algebra?

Let X_n^d be the space of homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n with nonzero discriminant, and let Phi assign to each such form its associated form of degree n(d-2) on the dual space. For every regular GL_n-invariant function S on X_n^d, does there exist a rational GL_n-invariant function R on the space of degree n(d-2) associated forms, defined at every point of Phi(X_n^d), such that R composed with Phi equals S?

For every n >= 2 and d >= 3, prove both of the following conditions used to establish Conjecture 1.1: first, the morphism P∇|P X_n^d from P X_n^d // SL_n to Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n is a closed immersion, meaning an isomorphism onto a closed subset; second, the morphism PΨ from Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n to P C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)}^{ss} // SL_n is an isomorphism onto a closed subset of an affine open subset.

Let P∇ be the morphism induced by sending a degree-d form f to the span of its first partial derivatives in the Grassmannian Gr(n, C[z_1, ..., z_n]_{d-1}), and then passing to GIT quotients by SL_n. Is the image of P∇|P X_n^d normal for all n >= 2 and d >= 3?

For n >= 2 and d >= 3, can one find a homogeneous SL_n-invariant on C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} whose nonvanishing locus contains, as a closed subset, the set U_n^{n(d-2)} of degree n(d-2) forms F such that F^perp intersected with C[z_1, ..., z_n]_{d-1} is n-dimensional and has a basis with nonvanishing resultant?

Let Phi be the associated-form map from nondegenerate homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n to homogeneous degree n(d-2) forms on the dual space. Repeated application of this construction gives iterates such as Phi^2 when defined as rational maps between the corresponding spaces of forms. Is Phi^k a well-defined rational map for every positive integer k?

For the associated-form morphism Phi, define p to be the smallest positive integer such that Delta^p Phi extends from the nondegenerate locus X_n^d to a morphism on the entire affine space of degree-d forms. Compute this integer p.
Does there exist any pair (n, d) for which the minimal exponent p needed to extend Delta^p Phi to all degree-d forms is strictly greater than 1?

Given a block graph G, meaning a graph in which every block is a complete graph, and letting A(G) be its (0,1)-adjacency matrix, characterize exactly when G is nonsingular, that is, when A(G) is invertible (equivalently, G has full rank and nullity 0), as opposed to singular.
If G is a connected block graph in which every block has order at least 3, must the nullity of G be at most 1? Here nullity means the number of zero eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix A(G).
context_brief: Nullity bound for K2-forbidden block graphs

question_text: Let G1 and G2 be two connected nonsingular block graphs, and let v1 be a vertex of G1 and v2 be a vertex of G2. If one adds a new edge between v1 and v2 and the resulting graph is still a block graph, must the resulting block graph also be nonsingular?
context_brief: Edge-joining conjecture for nonsingular block graphs

question_text: Consider two Lagrangian fibrations φ : M 4 → B and φ′ : M ′ → B ′ . Assume that B and B ′ are affinely equivalent in the sense that there exists an affine diffeomorphism ψ : B → B ′ . Is it true that under these assumptions the corresponding Lagrangian fibrations are symplectomorphic?

Do local symplectic invariants exist for diffeomorphic degenerate singularities? How many and of what kind are they? This question makes sense even in the simplest case of one-degree- of-freedom systems.

Describe all the topological types of singularities that may appear in algebraically inte- grable systems with a small (≤ 3) degree of freedom. Next, describe the symplectic invariants of such singularities.
For integrable systems obtained by toric degeneration, describe the topology and geometry of the resulting singular fibers and of their small neighbourhoods.
In SYZ-type Lagrangian fibrations on Calabi-Yau 3-folds, describe the special singular fibers that occur at intersections of one-dimensional families of focus-focus singularities.
Construct a natural Hamiltonian system with a nonconstant potential on S 2 that admits a nontrivial polynomial integral of degree 5 and does not admit any nontrivial integrals of smaller degrees.
Construct new examples of natural Hamiltonian systems on higher dimensional mani- folds which are integrable in the class of integrals polynomial in momenta.
Construct stationary axially symmetric 4-dimensional Einstein metrics admitting Killing tensors of higher order.

In a symmetric space, is every Killing tensor a sum of symmetric products of Killing vectors? Equivalently, is it true that the algebra of all polynomial integrals of the geodesic flow in a symmetric space is generated by linear integrals?
Construct a natural Hamiltonian system on the 2-sphere with a nonconstant potential which is superintegrable by integrals of degree ≥ 3 and admits no nontrivial integral of degree one and two.
Does there exist a non-conformally flat metric on the sphere S n , n > 2, whose geodesic flow is maximally superintegrable (in the class of integrals which are polynomial in momenta)?
If a neighbourhood of the boundary of the billiard table Ω ⊂ R2 is foliated by caustics, then the billiard curve γ is an ellipse.
Assume that the exterior of an outer billiard table is foliated by invariant curves. Prove that the table is an ellipse.

(S. Tabachnikov) Let γ ⊂ RP2 be a smooth closed strictly convex curve, and let F be a smooth foliation by convex closed curves in its exterior neighbourhood, including γ as a leaf. The intersection of every tangent line to γ with the leaves of F define a local involution on this line, the point of tangency being a fixed point. Suppose that these involutions are projective transformations for all tangent lines of γ. Then γ is an ellipse, and the foliation consists of ellipses that form a pencil.
Prove the algebraic version of Birkhoff conjecture for outer billiards in a non-Euclidean surface of constant curvature.

Is it possible to choose the domain so that the dynamics of the corresponding billiard map are locally (near the 2-periodic orbit) conjugated to the dynamics of the rigid rotation through some angle α?
Are there plane billiards, other than ellipses, that possess rational caustics with two different values of the rotation numbers? Same question for outer billiards.
(V. Kaloshin) A q0 -rationally integrable billiard is elliptic.
(M. Bialy) Assume that a plane billiard has a family of rotational invariant circles with all the rotation numbers in the interval (0, 1/2). Then the billiard table is an ellipse.
Suppose that a billiard table has a sequence of convex caustics with rotation numbers converging to some number ω ∈ (0, 1/2). Does it imply that the table is an ellipse?
(M. Bialy) Are there multi-dimensional convex billiards, other than ellipsoids, having invariant hypersurfaces in the phase space? Same question for multi-dimensional outer billiards.

(A. Glutsyuk, S. Tabachnikov ) Given two nested closed convex hypersurfaces, assume that the billiard transformations on the set of oriented lines that intersect both hypersurfaces commute. Prove that the hypersurfaces are confocal ellipsoids.
For the generalized pentagram maps T_{I,J} on twisted polygons in projective space, is every map T_{I,I} integrable for every multi-index I?
Extend the action-angle theorem in a neighbourhood of a Liouville torus at singular points of the Poisson structure.
Determine obstructions to the global existence of action-angle coordinates on regular Poisson manifolds.
Which foliations with affine leaves can be described as the image of the moment map?

Consider a Poisson manifold M of even dimension such that it is symplectic on a dense set U ⊂ M . Assume that M is endowed with a toric action which is Hamiltonian on U . Is there an analog of Delzant theorem for the image of the moment map?
Problem 6.8 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Find natural examples of integrable systems in classical mechanics with non-trivial Duistermaat–Chern classes.
Assume that a classical integrable system (p1 , . . . , pn ) is given on M . Does there exist a quantum integrable system (P1 , . . . , Pn ) such that pj = σ(Pj )?

Problem 7.2 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Given a set of semiclassical operators that verify conditions 1 and 2 above, can one detect the independence axiom 3 in a purely spectral way? More precisely, can one tell from asymptotics of joint eigenvalues or eigenfunctions of (P1 , . . . , Pn ) that the principal symbols are almost everywhere independent?
Problem 7.3 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Write Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for focus-focus singularities in Berezin- Toeplitz quantisation.
Problem 7.4 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Define (and detect) the quantum Chern class.
Is a semitoric integrable system F = (J, H) uniquely determined up to symplectic equivalence by its semiclassical joint spectrum, and can one explicitly reconstruct the system from that spectrum?
Problem 7.7 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Is the singular Bohr-Sommerfeld formal power series in ~ a spectral invariant?

Problem 7.8 (Á. Pelayo). What information about the principal symbols f1 , . . . , fn of a quantum integrable system T1,~ , . . . , Tn,~ can be detected from their semiclasical joint spectrum? For instance, suppose that we know that a certain object – say, an integer z, or a matrix A – is a symplectic invariant of (M, ω, f1 , . . . , fn ). Can we compute this object from the semiclassical joint spectrum?
Problem 7.9 (Á. Pelayo). Can one detect from the joint spectrum of a quantum integrable system T1,~ , . . . , Tn,~ that a singularity is degenerate?
Problem 7.10 (Á. Pelayo). Can one make progress in counting the number of fixed points by studying the spectrum of the quantisation of µ : M → S 1 ?
What are necessary and/or sufficient conditions on a metric g such that every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable?

Let τ(n,t)=\frac{1}{n}\left(t-(t+n+1)\left(\frac{t}{1+t}\right)^{n+1}\right) for positive integers n and real numbers t>0. What is the maximum value of τ(n,t) over all pairs (n,t)\in \mathbb{N}\times(0,\infty)?
context_brief: Maximum of a gamma-function-related auxiliary expression

question_text: Let G be a graph. If P is a graph property and M is a matching of G whose induced subgraph <M> has property P, call M a P-matching. Write beta_P(G) for the maximum size of a P-matching in G and beta_P^-(G) for the minimum size of a maximal P-matching in G. For each P-matching family introduced in the survey, what nontrivial upper bounds can be proved for beta_P(G), and what nontrivial lower bounds can be proved for beta_P^-(G)?

Let G be a graph, let P be a graph property, and call a matching M of G a P-matching when the induced subgraph <M> has property P. For each P-matching family introduced in the survey, develop characterization theorems that determine exactly when a given matching M is a maximum P-matching, rather than merely a maximal one.

For a graph G and a graph property P, let beta_P(G) denote the maximum size of a matching M whose induced subgraph <M> has property P. Is there a graph parameter alpha_P, analogous to the Gallai identities for ordinary matchings, such that beta_P(G) + alpha_P(G) = |V(G)| for every graph G in the relevant class?

For a graph G and a graph property P, let beta_P(G) denote the maximum size of a P-matching in G, where a P-matching is a matching M whose induced subgraph <M> has property P. What Nordhaus-Gaddum type bounds can be proved for beta_P over a graph and its complement; specifically, what are the best possible lower and upper bounds for beta_P(G) + beta_P(G_bar) and for beta_P(G) * beta_P(G_bar)?

For a graph G and a graph property P, let beta_P(G) be the maximum size of a matching M whose induced subgraph <M> has property P. For the P-matching parameters introduced in the survey, what is the computational complexity of determining beta_P(G), and for which graph classes can beta_P(G) be computed in polynomial time or shown NP-complete?

A disconnected matching is a matching M such that |M| = 1 or the induced subgraph <M> is disconnected, and beta_dc(G) denotes the maximum size of a disconnected matching in G. What is the computational complexity of determining beta_dc(G), especially since the survey notes complexity results for several other matching varieties but leaves beta_dc unresolved?

Let F be a finite field of characteristic 2 such that the extension degree [F : F_2] is even, and let d be an invertible exponent over F (that is, gcd(d, |F^*|) = 1). Must there always exist a nonzero element a in F such that the Weil sum W_{F,d}(a) has magnitude at least 2*sqrt(|F|)? Equivalently, must there always exist a in F^* such that |W_{F,d}(a) - 1| >= -1 + 2*sqrt(|F|)?
context_brief: Sarwate-Pursley lower bound conjecture in characteristic 2

question_text: Let F be a finite field of characteristic p such that the extension degree [F : F_p] is not a power of 2, let l be the smallest odd prime divisor of [F : F_p], and let d be a nondegenerate invertible exponent over F. Is the p-adic valuation V_{F,d} of the Weil spectrum always at most ((l + 1)/(2l))*[F : F_p]?
context_brief: Conjectured upper bound for p-adic valuation of Weil spectra

question_text: Suppose F is a finite field and d is an invertible exponent over F such that the associated Weil spectrum {W_{F,d}(a) : a in F^*} has exactly three distinct values. Must that three-valued Weil spectrum always be symmetric, meaning that its two nonzero values are negatives of each other?
Let F be a finite field of characteristic p whose extension degree [F : F_p] is a power of 2. Is it impossible for any invertible exponent d over F to produce a three-valued Weil spectrum W_{F,d}?

Does Table 1 in the survey give a complete classification, up to the exponent equivalence relation of Definition 5.7, of all pairs (F, d) where F is a finite field, d is an invertible exponent over F, and the Weil spectrum W_{F,d} is three-valued?
context_brief: Completeness of the known classification of three-valued cases

question_text: Let F be a finite field of characteristic p with |F| > 2, and let d be an invertible exponent over F satisfying d == 1 mod (p - 1). Must there always exist a nonzero element a in F such that the Weil sum W_{F,d}(a) equals 0? Equivalently, under the same hypotheses, must the Dedekind determinant D_{F,d} = product_{a in F^*} W_{F,d}(a) vanish, or, equivalently again, must the number of solutions of the associated hyperplane-section system in Conjecture 11.4 equal q^(q-3) when |F| = q?

Let f : R^n -> R^m be a function that is Lipschitz continuous near a point x_bar, and assume every matrix in Clarke's generalized Jacobian of f at x_bar is surjective. If y_bar = f(x_bar), must there exist a continuous local selection s of the inverse image mapping f^{-1} near y_bar such that s(y_bar) = x_bar and s is calm at y_bar, meaning that for some constant gamma > 0 one has ||s(y) - x_bar|| <= gamma ||y - y_bar|| for all nearby y?

Is every 6-dimensional polytope 3-linked, in the sense that for every choice of three pairs of distinct vertices there exist three pairwise disjoint paths in its graph, each connecting one chosen pair?

Does the combinatorial 3-polytope FFS3 admit a decomposable geometric realization, where decomposable means representable as a Minkowski sum of two convex bodies that are not similar to one another? Equivalently, is every geometric realization of FFS3 indecomposable?

Let C_1 and C_2 be compact convex sets in a Hilbert space H. Must there exist a point x in H such that, if p_i is a projection of x onto C_i for i in {1,2}, then the normal vector x - p_i defines a supporting hyperplane that strongly exposes the singleton face {p_i} of C_i? Here a point p in a convex set C is strongly exposed by a linear functional f when f(p) = sup_{x in C} f(x) and every sequence (x_k) in C with f(x_k) approaching sup_{x in C} f(x) converges to p.

For nonconvex feasibility problems A intersection B != emptyset involving proximal sets, what can be proved about the dynamics and convergence of the continuous-time Douglas-Rachford flow associated with the operator T(x) = (lambda (2P_B - Id)(2P_A - Id) + (1 - lambda) Id)x in the limit lambda -> 0^+, especially in settings such as a subtransversal ellipse and a line or a p-sphere and a line where the discrete Douglas-Rachford method has complicated global behavior?

Given points a_1, ..., a_m in a Euclidean space X, can one write an explicit and neat formula or characterization for the unique minimizer of min_{x in X} max_{i in {1, ..., m}} ||a_i - x||, that is, for the center of the smallest Euclidean sphere containing all the points? More generally, what analogous description is available when X is an arbitrary normed or metric space, or when the maximum over the m distances is replaced by an arbitrary norm on R^m?

Let Omega be a finite family of convex polytopes in R^n.
