For each unit vector g in S^{n-1}, define C(g) to be the convex hull of all support faces Arg max_{x in P} <x,g> taken over P in Omega, and define F(Omega) = {C(g) : g in S^{n-1}}. Starting from Omega_0, iterate Omega_i = F(Omega_{i-1}). Which initial finite families Omega_0 have the property that this sequence eventually enters a 2-cycle, meaning that there exists N with Omega_{N+2} = Omega_N?

Does every convex 3-polytope admit a nonoverlapping net, that is, can one cut the polytope along some collection of edges so that the resulting connected surface unfolds into the plane without self-overlap?

Let S be a set, and let T ⊆ S be a subset. Classify those maps f : S → S with the property that for every α ∈ S, the set n ≥ 0 : f n (α) ∈ T has some nice structure, for example, it is the union of finitely many one-sided arithmetic progressions.

Fix integers N ≥ 1, d ≥ 2, and D ≥ 1. There is a constant C(N, d, D) such that for all degree d morphisms f : PN → PN defined over a number field K of degree [K : Q] = D, the number of K-rational preperiodic points is uniformly bounded,  # PrePer f, PN (K) ≤ C(N, d, D).
For all c ∈ Q, the set of periodic points Per(x2 + c, Q) contains no points of period strictly greater than 3.

Let X/C be a projective variety, let f : X → X be a polarizable endomorphism, and let Y be a subvariety of X which has no component contained entirely within the singular locus of X. question_text: Let Y0dyn (n) and Y1dyn (n) be the dynamical modular curves clas- sifying points, respectively cycles, of formal period n attached to the family of maps x2 + c, or xm + c, or some other natural 1-parameter family of rational maps on P1 such as bx + x−1 . question_text: Let f : A^N -> A^N be a morphism over an algebraic closure of Q, written as polynomial coordinate functions f = (f_1, ..., f_N). If there is no non-constant rational function g with g o f = g, then there exists a point whose forward orbit under f is Zariski dense.

Then for all ǫ > 0, the set (14.2) t ∈ Ck : δ(ft ) ≤ δ(f ) − ǫ is not Zariski dense in Ck . In particular, for one-parameter families, i.e., k = 1, the set (14.2) is finite. Let f : PN 99K PN be a dominant rational map. Is it true that there exists an integer ℓf satisfying 0 ≤ ℓf ≤ N such that23.

Let f : PN 99K PN be a dominant rational map de- fined over Q̄. (a) Let P ∈ PN (Q̄)f . The limit (15.3) defining αf (P ) converges. (b) The set αf (P ) : P ∈ PN (Q̄)f is finite. (c) Let P ∈ PN (Q̄)f . The arithmetic degree αf (P ) is an algebraic integer. (d) Let P ∈ PN (Q̄)f be a point whose orbit Of (P ) is Zariski dense in PN . Then αf (P ) = δf . Conjecture 15.3 is known for monomial maps, which are maps f = [f0 , . . . , fN ] such that their coordinate functions fi are monomials [215], and parts of the con- jecture are known in various other cases; see for example [128, 133, 134, 135]. We mayask for more refined information regarding the possible growth rates of h f n (P ) . The following is an arithmetic analogue of Question 14.16.

Let f : PN 99K PN be a dominant rational map defined over Q̄, and let P ∈ PN (Q̄)f be a point whose orbit Of (P ) is Zariski dense in PN . Is it true that there exist integers kf and ℓf with 0 ≤ ℓf ≤ N such that  (15.5) h f n (P ) ≍ δfn · nℓf · (log n)kf , where the implied constants depend on f and P , but not on n? Further, if δf > 1, is it true that kf = 0?  If f : PN → PN is a morphism, then (15.5) holds in the stronger form h f n (P ) = δfn ĥf (P ) + O(1); see Section 16. The situation is more complicated for general varieties. Sano [195] proves that if f : X → X is a morphism of a smooth projective variety defined over Q̄, and if P ∈ X(Q̄) satisfies αf (P ) > 1, then a version of (15.5) holds with kf = 0.

Let f : X 99K X be a dominant rational map of a smooth projective variety X defined over Q̄. (a) Let P ∈ X(Q̄)f . The limit (15.6) defining αf (P ) converges. (b) The set αf (P ) : P ∈ X(Q̄)f is finite. (c) Let P ∈ X(Q̄)f . The arithmetic degree αf (P ) is an algebraic integer. (d) Let P ∈ X(Q̄)f whose orbit Of (P ) is Zariski dense in X. Then αf (P ) = δf . The inequality (15.7) ᾱf (P ) ≤ δf for P ∈ X(Q̄)f relating arithmetic and dynamical degrees is true in the more general setting of.

Let f : PN → PN be a mor- phism of degree d ≥ 2 defined over a number field K. There is a constant C(f ) > 0 such that for all P ∈ PN (Q̄) that are wandering for f , we have24 C(f ) ĥf (P ) ≥  . K(P ) : K In order to state the next conjecture, we need a way to measure the arithmetic complexity of a rational map f : PN → PN defined over Q̄. It is not enough to simply use the coefficients of the polynomials defining f , since as we saw in Section 10, changing coordinates on PN has the effect of drastically changing the coefficients of f without affecting the underlying dynamical system. The solution is to view f as a point hf i in MN d , the space of “maps up to change-of-coordinates.” N The space Md is itself an algebraic variety, so we fix an embedding ι : MN L d ֒−→ P ,.

Let N ≥ 1, D ≥ 1, and d ≥ 2. There are positive constants c1 (D, N, d) and c2 (D, N, d) such that for all number fields K/Q with [K : Q] ≤ D, all degree d morphisms f : PN → PN defined over K, and all points P ∈ PN (K) whose orbit Of (P ) is Zariski dense in PN , we have ĥf (P ) ≥ c1 (D, N, d)hM (f ) + c2 (D, N, d). See [35, 34] for numerical evidence supporting Conjecture 16.3 in the case N = D = 1 and d ∈ {2, 3}, including conjectural values for the constants. We also note that the Zariski density assumption in Conjecture 16.3 is necessary. For ex- ample, the map f = [X 2 , Y 2 , γZ 2 ] has height roughly h(γ), while the f -orbit of the point P = [α, 1, 0] has canonical height ĥf (P ) = h(α), so we can make hM (f ) arbitrarily large while ĥf (P ) remains bounded. Ingram [116] and Looper [155] have proven weak versions of Conjecture 16.3 for polynomial maps f of P1 , where the constants depend also on the number of primes of bad reduction of f.

Let K(B) be the function field of an algebraic curve, let f : PN → PN be a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 defined over the field K(B), and let P ∈ PN K(B) . Is the canonical height ĥf (P ) always in Q? If not, give necessary and sufficient conditions for ĥf (P ) ∈ Q. Question 16.14 is open, even for N = 1, but the following result for local canon- ical heights is known.

Let f ∈ Cv (z) be a rational function of degree at least 2, and let Jf ⊂ P1Berk be the Julia set of f . Then Jf ∩ P1 (Cv ) is equal to the closure in P1 (Cv ) of the set of Type I repelling periodic points of f.

Let f ∈ Cv (z) with deg f = d ≥ 2. Can f have infinitely many periodic cycles of indifferent components that are not disks? If not, is there a bound in terms of d for the number of such cycles? Do the answers depend on the field Cv ?
Let K be a locally compact subfield of Cv , and suppose that the algebraic closure K̄ of K is dense in Cv . Let f ∈ K(z) be a rational function of degree at least 2. Then f has no wandering domains.

Let K ⊂ Cv be a discretely valued subfield whose algebraic closure K̄ is dense in Cv . Let p ≥ 0 be the residue characteristic of Cv , and let f ∈ Cv (z) be a rational function of degree at least 2. Suppose that there are no points ζ ∈ P1Berk at which f has local degree divisible by p. Then every wandering domain of f lies in the attracting basin of a Type II Julia periodic point.

Let f : PN → PN be a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 defined over Q, and let P ∈ PN (Q) be a point whose f -orbit Of (P ) is Zariski dense in PN . Then for every ǫ > 0, the set of primes p : #Of˜(P̃ mod p) ≥ p(1/2−ǫ)N is a set of density 1. 29This conjecture should probably be viewed as a provocation. A safer formulation would be to phrase it as the problem of classfiying all maps for which the conjecture fails to be true!.

Let f : PN → PN be a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 defined over Q, and let P ∈ PN (Q) be a point whose f -orbit Of (P ) is Zariski dense in PN . Under what conditions on f is it true that for every ǫ > 0, the set of primes p : #Of˜(P̃ mod p) ≤ p(1/2+ǫ)N is a set of density 1? There are a handful of published results giving upper bounds for the size of the orbit Of˜(P̃ mod p), including [105, 129, 201]. To illustrate, we quote an easily stated corollary from one of these papers.

Let K be a number field, let f (x) ∈ K(x) be a rational function of degree at least 2, and let α ∈ K be a point that is not periodic for f . Then (f, α) is eventually stable over K. One might be bold and ask if there is a uniform bound for the eventual stability predicted by Conjecture 19.4, but some care is needed,  since it is not hard to see that for any k ≥ 1, the constant C f (x), f k (α) in Definition 19.2 must be at least k.
Let K be a number field, let f : PN → PN be an endomorphism of degree at least 2 defined over K, and let P ∈ PN (K) be a point that is not periodic for f . Then (f, P ) is eventually stable over K.

Let K be a number field, let f : PN → PN be an endomorphism of degree at least 2 defined over K, and let X ( PN be a subvariety that is defined over K and irreducible over K. S (a) If the iterated forward orbit n≥1 f n (X) of X is Zariski dense in PN , is it true that (f, X) is eventually stable over K? Let f (x) ∈ Q(x) be a rational function of degree d ≥ 2, and for each prime p, let f˜p ∈ Fp (x) denote its reduction modulo p; see Section 12. (a) Is it true that the set (19.3) p : f˜p (x) is stable over Fp is a finite set? (b) Is it true that the set (19.4) p : f˜p (x) is eventually stable over Fp is a finite set? As a specific example, Jones [122, Conjecture 6.3] has conjectured that x2 + 1 is stable over Fp if and only if p = 3, i.e., for f (x) = x2 + 1, the set (19.3) is {3}. Ferraguti [76] has shown that under some Galois-theoretic assumptions, the set of stable primes (19.3) has density zero.

Then we have the following natural generalization of Conjecture 20.2.

Or is the set of such primes relatively sparse? There is a large literature studying the density of the support of sequences such as an − 1 and the Fibonacci sequence. In the dynamical setting, it is interesting to study the density of the support of orbits, as in the next theorem, which generalizes an earlier result of Odoni [178] for f (x) = x2 − x + 1. question_text: Let f : P^N -> P^N be a morphism of degree d >= 2 defined over Q, and assume that for every 1 <= n <= N + 1 the first coordinate function of f^n is not a constant multiple of X_0^(d^n). Then every wandering point P in P^N(Q) has only finitely many forward-orbit points that are integral relative to the hyperplane X_0 = 0; equivalently, if f^n(P) = [A_0(n), ..., A_N(n)] in primitive integral coordinates, then log|A_0(n)| / log max(|A_0(n)|, ..., |A_N(n)|) tends to 1 as n -> infinity.

Let f : PN → PN be a morphism of degree d defined over Q. (a) For which n ≥ 1 is it true that f has a point of exact period n in PN (Q) if and only if f has a point of exact period n in PN (R) and in PN (Qp ) for all primes p?

Let K be a number field, let X/K be a variety, let f : X → X be a morphism defined over K, let Y ⊂ X be a subvariety defined over K, and let P ∈ X(K). Let AK be the ring of adeles of K, and for any set S, let C(S) denote the adelic closure of S. Then   C Y ∩ Of (P ) = Y (AK ) ∩ C Of (P ).

Let K be a number field, let f (x), g(x) ∈ K[x] be polynomials of degree at least 2, and let a, b ∈ K. (a) Suppose that for all but finitely many primes p, the mod p orbits of a and b satisfy (22.1) Of˜(ã mod p) ∩ Og̃ (b̃ mod p) 6= ∅. Is it true that true that f and g have the same complex Julia sets? 33 If the answer is affirmative, does it suffice to assume that (22.1) holds for a set of primes of density 1? (b) Fix some ǫ > 0, and suppose that the intersection (22.1) has at least Npǫ elements for infinitely many primes p. Is it true that true that f and g have the same complex Julia sets? 33Aside from power maps and Chebyshev polynomials, having the same Julia set is more-or-less equivalent to f and g having a common iterate, up to symmetries of the Julia set.
For a holomorphic foliation on complex projective space, possibly with singularities, must every leaf accumulate at a singular point of the foliation?
For generic holomorphic foliations on the complex projective plane P2, what is the topology of a generic leaf?
For generic holomorphic foliations on the complex projective plane P2, are generic leaves dense?

Let F be a possibly singular foliation by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kähler manifold M, let T be an extremal positive ddc-closed current directed by F that gives full mass to the hyperbolic leaves, and for a universal covering map φ_a: D → L of a leaf define the Nevanlinna current τ_r^a. If Theorem 2.1 proves that τ_r^a converges to T for T-almost every a when all singularities of F are linearizable, does the same convergence still hold when the singularities are non-linearizable?

Does there exist an extremal positive ddc-closed current T directed by a foliation F for which one can estimate the speed at which the Nevanlinna currents τ_r^a converge to T in Theorem 2.1 when tested against smooth observables θ?

Let φ_a: D → L be the universal covering of a leaf, let A(r) = ∫_{D(r)} φ_a^*(ω), and define the associated Ahlfors current by σ_r^a := (1/A(r))(φ_a)_*[D(r)]. Does σ_r^a converge to the extremal positive ddc-closed current T as r tends to 1 for T-almost every base point a?

For a leaf parametrized by a universal covering map φ_a: D → L, Theorem 2.1 implies for T-almost every leaf that its Nevanlinna characteristic satisfies T(r) ≥ c log(1/(1-r)) for r close to 1. Does this lower bound hold for every leaf, and in particular does it hold for every leaf when the foliation admits no diffuse ddc-closed current?
context_brief: uniform lower bound for leaf growth

question_text: Let F be a foliation of degree d ≥ 2 with non-hyperbolic singularities. Describe the directed positive ddc-closed currents of F, and determine when F can admit diffuse positive closed currents directed by the foliation.

Let Bd be the parameter space of holomorphic foliations of degree d ≥ 2 and let Bc_d be the subset consisting of foliations that admit directed positive closed currents. Is Bc_d a countable union of proper analytic subsets of Bd?

For a generic foliation in Ad, the space of foliations on an affine chart C2 ⊂ P2 given by polynomial vector fields Z = P(z,w)∂/∂z + Q(z,w)∂/∂w with max(deg P, deg Q) = d, or for a generic foliation in Bd, the space of degree-d holomorphic foliations on P2, are generic leaves biholomorphic to the unit disc?
Let F be a holomorphic foliation on P2 with finite singular set Sing(F). Is it true that every leaf L of F meets Sing(F)?
Does there exist a Levi-flat hypersurface in P2 that is smooth or real analytic?

Assume F is a foliation of geometric degree d ≥ 2 on P2, the line at infinity is invariant, and all singularities are hyperbolic. Do all non-compact leaves of F, meaning all leaves except the compact curves, admit Green functions?

Let F be a foliation in Bd with d ≥ 2 that admits a non-zero positive closed current directed by F. What is the resulting function theory of its leaves, especially in terms of the existence and behavior of Green functions?
context_brief: function theory with directed closed currents

question_text: Construct a holomorphic minimal foliation, or a holomorphic minimal lamination, on a compact complex manifold that has uncountably many mutually singular extremal directed currents which are ddc-closed but not closed.

Let Z be a holomorphic vector field on C2. Can there be one positive-measure set of leaves whose universal covers are C and another positive-measure set of leaves whose universal covers are the unit disc?
context_brief: mixed parabolic and hyperbolic leaf types

question_text: Let Z be a holomorphic vector field on C2. If a non-pluripolar set of leaves is parabolic, must all leaves be parabolic?
Find conditions on a holomorphic vector field Z on C2 that guarantee every leaf is covered by the unit disc.

Let Z be a holomorphic vector field on Ck that is not the product of a polynomial vector field with a holomorphic function. For a leaf L with uniformization map φ whose source is either C or the unit disc, define the Nevanlinna currents τ_r^φ := (1/T(r))φ_*(log^+(r/|ζ|)). Must every cluster point of τ_r^φ be supported on the hyperplane at infinity, taking r → ∞ in the source-C case and r → 1 in the unit-disc case?

Let H be the space of entire maps from C to C or to P1 with the compact-open topology, and let U be the subset of maps h such that translates h(z+a_n) can approximate every f in H. What is the minimal possible growth of the Nevanlinna characteristic Th(r) = ∫_0^r (dt/t) ∫_{D(t)} h^*(ω) for maps h in U?

Let H be the space of entire maps as above, and let μ be a non-trivial probability measure on H that is invariant under the translation action h(z) ↦ h(z+a). What can be said about the measure μ(U) of the set U of universal maps with dense translation orbit?

Let M be a complex manifold of dimension n that is homogeneous under the action of a Lie group G, let 𝓜 be the space of holomorphic maps from M to Pn with the compact-open topology, and let G act on 𝓜 by precomposition. Under what conditions does this action admit a dense orbit?

In the setting where a Lie group G acts on the space 𝓜 of holomorphic maps from a homogeneous complex manifold M to Pn, extend Benjamin Weiss’s construction of non-trivial invariant probability measures to this broader action.
Investigate whether the dense-orbit and invariant-measure phenomena discussed above persist for biholomorphisms of Cn and for volume-preserving or symplectic automorphisms of Cn.

For holomorphic foliations on compact Kähler manifolds whose leaves have dimension greater than 1, what is the correct replacement for directed ddc-closed currents of bi-dimension (1,1) used in the one-dimensional case, so that one can develop an ergodic theory for such foliations?
Construct non-elementary holomorphic foliations F on Pk with leaves of dimension greater than 1 such that no leaf contains a compact curve.

Let F be a holomorphic foliation on the unit polydisc Dk ⊂ Ck whose leaves have dimension d > 1 and are tangent to holomorphic (1,0)-forms α1, ..., α_{k-d} that satisfy the Frobenius condition ∂α_j = Σ_{l=1}^{k-d} α_l ∧ β_{j,l}. Can F always be approximated by foliations on Ck or Pk? More precisely, can the forms α_j be approximated uniformly on compact subsets of Dk by entire forms, or by polynomial forms, that still satisfy the same Frobenius condition?

Let pi: X -> C^n be a ramified Riemann domain, where X is a possibly singular reduced complex space and pi is a holomorphic map whose fibers pi^{-1}({z}) are discrete for every z in C^n. Assume that for every point a in C^n there exists a neighborhood U of a such that pi^{-1}(U) is Stein, so X is locally Stein over C^n. Under these assumptions, what sufficient conditions or what necessary conditions guarantee that X itself is Stein? The paper states that this problem remains open even when X is non-singular.
context_brief: Levi problem for locally Stein ramified Riemann domains over C^n

question_text: Over RCA0, are the following four statements equivalent: (A) the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem for any finite number of trees; (B) Milliken's Ramsey theorem for strong trees on one finitely branching infinite tree with no terminal nodes; (C) the canonical partition theorem for colorings of a fixed finite graph inside the Rado graph; and (D) the statement that for every k >= 2, the Rado graph has the rainbow Ramsey property for k-bounded colorings?

Is the reverse-mathematical strength of the rainbow Ramsey theorem for edges in the Rado graph strictly greater than the reverse-mathematical strength of the rainbow Ramsey theorem for pairs of natural numbers?
context_brief: Rado graph edges versus pairs of naturals

question_text: Fix any graph G with three vertices and any k >= 2. Assuming over RCA0 the rainbow Ramsey theorem for k-bounded colorings of triples of natural numbers, does it follow that every coloring of copies of G in the Rado graph into countably many colors, with each color used at most k times, has a subgraph isomorphic to the Rado graph in which no two copies of G receive the same color?
context_brief: Triples of naturals versus three-vertex graphs

question_text: For each d, is the reverse-mathematical strength of the strong-tree version of the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem for d trees strictly weaker than the corresponding strength for d + 1 trees?
context_brief: Halpern-Lauchli strength by number of trees

question_text: For each d, is the reverse-mathematical strength of the strong-tree version of the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem for d trees strictly stronger than the reverse-mathematical strength of the somewhere dense matrix form for d trees?

Does the statement that the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem holds for any finite number of trees have the same reverse-mathematical strength as the statement that Milliken's theorem for colorings of finite strong trees holds?
Does the reverse-mathematical strength of Milliken's theorem depend on the height of the finite strong trees being colored?

Does the reverse-mathematical strength of either the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem or Milliken's theorem depend on the splitting properties of the underlying finitely branching trees; for example, are binary-branching trees weaker than ternary-branching trees, and are both weaker than trees whose branching is finite but unbounded?

What is the reverse-mathematical strength of the following statement: for every finite graph G and every k >= 2, every coloring of all copies of G in the Rado graph into countably many colors, with each color used at most k times, has a subgraph isomorphic to the Rado graph in which no two copies of G receive the same color?
context_brief: Strength of the Rado rainbow Ramsey property

question_text: For the Rado graph, does the rainbow Ramsey property for k-bounded colorings have the same reverse-mathematical strength as the rainbow Ramsey property for (k + 1)-bounded colorings?

Does the reverse-mathematical strength of the rainbow Ramsey theorem for the Rado graph coincide with the reverse-mathematical strength of Sauer's canonical partition theorem for colorings of a fixed finite graph inside the Rado graph?
context_brief: Rainbow theorem versus canonical partition theorem

question_text: When one colors copies of different finite graphs inside the Rado graph, do the resulting rainbow Ramsey theorems all have the same reverse-mathematical strength, or does that strength vary with the number of vertices in the finite graph being colored?
context_brief: Dependence on the finite graph being colored

question_text: Let M be a compact two-dimensional manifold, let X^r be the space of C^r vector fields on M, let Sigma^r be the subset of C^r-structurally stable vector fields, and let X_1^r = X^r \ Sigma^r with the induced C^r topology. Characterize the subset Sigma_1^r of vector fields in X_1^r that are structurally stable with respect to arbitrarily small perturbations that remain inside X_1^r.

Let X^r be the space of C^r vector fields on the sphere. Is every continuous arc in X^r arbitrarily well approximable by a continuous arc that meets only finitely many bifurcation points, meaning finitely many points outside the set of structurally stable vector fields where qualitative changes occur?

Do there exist invariant perfect sets, meaning nonempty compact invariant sets that are transversally totally discontinuous, for differential equations of class C^2 on orientable two-dimensional manifolds?

For second-order differential equations of the form x'' = f(x, x'), equivalently for first-order systems x' = y and y' = f(x, y), characterize structural stability and prove the genericity of structural stability in the spirit of Peixoto's results for vector fields on two-dimensional manifolds.

Let M be a compact n-dimensional manifold. If a C^r vector field on M has a nontrivial recurrent orbit through a point p in M, can that vector field be approximated arbitrarily closely in the C^s topology, with s <= r, by another vector field that has a periodic orbit through p?

Consider the Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem on a finite interval (0<x<L): u_t+u_x+u_{xxx}+u u_x=0 for t>0, with initial data u(x,0)=phi(x), and boundary data imposed through one of the four operator families B_k u=~h. In the notation used in the paper these families are built from B_1=(u(0,t),u(L,t),u_x(L,t)), B_2=(u(0,t),u_x(L,t),u_{xx}(L,t)), B_3=(u_{xx}(0,t),u(L,t),u_x(L,t)), and B_4=(u_{xx}(0,t),u_x(L,t),u_{xx}(L,t)), together with the lower-order boundary terms explicitly listed for B_{k,1} in the review. Is this problem globally well-posed in H^s(0,L) for some s>=0? Equivalently, can a solution blow up in finite time in some H^s(0,L) norm, or can one prove the global a priori bound sup_{0<=t<infty}||u(.,t)||_{L^2(0,L)}<infty that would yield global well-posedness?
context_brief: Global well-posedness for general finite-interval KdV IBVP

question_text: For the same finite-interval Korteweg-de Vries problem u_t+u_x+u_{xxx}+u u_x=0 on 0<x<L, t>0, with initial data u(x,0)=phi(x) and boundary condition B_k u=~h taken from the four operator families B_1, B_2, B_3, B_4 described above, is the initial-boundary value problem well-posed in the negative-regularity regime H^s(0,L) for some s<=-1? The review notes that the known local theory reaches s>=0, can be extended to -1<s<=0, and conjectures that the bounded-interval problem is ill-posed for every s<-1.

Consider the nonlinear Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem on a finite interval 0<x<L: u_t+u u_x+u_{xxx}=0, u(x,0)=phi(x), together with the boundary conditions u(0,t)=0, u(L,t)=0, and u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t). Is this nonlinear problem well-posed in H^s(0,L) for any Sobolev index s?

When N > 4 and the positive parameters a and b satisfy a^((N-4)/2) b < C1(N), do the conclusions of Theorem 1.1 still hold? In other words, for each sufficiently large lambda > 0 and each convex set C subset of L2(Omega) whose closure in L2(Omega) contains H1_0(Omega), does there exist some v* in C such that the associated Kirchhoff problem has at least three weak solutions, two of which are global minima in H1_0(Omega) of the corresponding energy functional?

For the new asymptotically conical (AC) G2-manifolds constructed by Foscolo, Haskins, and Nordstrom that are cohomogeneity-1 under an SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1) action, which of the locally defined G2-instantons near the singular orbit extend to globally defined G2-instantons on the whole manifold X, and, once the global solutions are classified and a nontrivial family is found, what global properties does the resulting moduli space have? In particular, what happens for the D7 family from [FHN18]?

Can one construct examples of nearly Kahler instantons on the known nearly Kahler 6-manifolds that occur as links of asymptotic cones of asymptotically conical G2-manifolds - namely S^6, CP^3, S^3 x S^3 (and finite quotients), and the flag manifold F2 - and, for any such nearly Kahler instanton, determine whether it occurs as the limit at infinity of a G2-instanton on an AC G2-manifold and, if it does, how many G2-instantons have that prescribed limit?

What is the local deformation theory of G2-instantons on asymptotically conical G2-manifolds? More specifically, can one understand the local geometry of their moduli space, prove a uniqueness result for the basic G2-instanton on R^7 with gauge group G2, decide whether deformations of symmetric G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds must preserve the same symmetries, and determine the properties of the natural projection from the moduli space of G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kahler instantons, including whether that projection is surjective?

For the two real 1-parameter families of irreducible G2-instantons described in Theorem 3 on the SU(3)-bundle Q over Lambda^2_-(CP^2), what is the limiting behavior of these G2-instantons as the parameter c tends to +infinity?

On the Bryant-Salamon G2-manifold R^4 x S^3, Proposition 6 gives a local 1-parameter family of SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons with gauge group SU(2) that extend smoothly over the singular orbit on the bundle P_id, and Theorem 5 shows that the member with parameter y_0 = 0 extends globally. Do any of the other local instantons from that family, namely those with y_0 != 0, also extend globally, and if they do, is their curvature necessarily unbounded at infinity?

Because the natural limits of G2-instantons on asymptotically locally conical (ALC) G2-manifolds are Calabi-Yau monopoles on Calabi-Yau cones, can one develop the theory and produce further examples of Calabi-Yau monopoles on Calabi-Yau cones or on asymptotically conical Calabi-Yau 3-folds that could arise as such limits?
context_brief: Calabi-Yau monopole limits on ALC ends

question_text: For the many asymptotically locally conical G2-manifolds that are close to a degenerate Calabi-Yau cone limit and are typically only U(1)-invariant, can one construct G2-instantons that are correspondingly close, in an appropriate sense, to Calabi-Yau monopoles on the limiting cone?

What is the deformation theory of G2-instantons on asymptotically locally conical G2-manifolds, how does it relate to the deformation theory of Calabi-Yau monopoles on asymptotically conical Calabi-Yau 3-folds, and what is the image of the natural projection from the moduli space of G2-instantons on an ALC G2-manifold to the space of Calabi-Yau monopoles on the asymptotic Calabi-Yau cone?

For irreducible SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant SU(2) G2-instantons on the BGGG G2-manifold R^4 x S^3 that extend smoothly on the bundle P_1, what happens in the unresolved parameter region 0 < f_1^+ - 1/2 < g_1^+ < f_1^+? In particular, which initial conditions in that region produce globally defined instantons with bounded curvature, which do not, and how should the corresponding existence and non-existence picture be completed for the broader Bogoyavlenskaya family of metrics?

How do G2-instantons on the Bogoyavlenskaya family of G2-manifolds behave as the underlying metric is deformed by changing the asymptotic circle size? In the large-circle limit, do these instantons converge to G2-instantons for the Bryant-Salamon metric on R^4 x S^3, and in the small-circle limit, what precise relation do they have to Calabi-Yau monopoles on the deformed conifold?

The moduli space M^BGGG_{P_1} of irreducible SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons on the BGGG manifold is non-compact. Can this moduli space be compactified, and what bubbling behavior occurs as one or both of the parameters f_1^+ and g_1^+ tend to infinity? In particular, does one obtain bubbling phenomena analogous to those proved for the Bryant-Salamon case, possibly related to anti-self-dual instantons on Taub-NUT?
For an arbitrary Jordan pair V, determine the full normal subgroup structure of the projective elementary group PE(V); equivalently, classify all normal subgroups of PE(V).

Determine whether the two theorems cited from [Lo5] continue to hold for broader classes of Jordan pairs: namely, whether PE(V) is perfect exactly when V has no simple factors isomorphic to (F2, F2), (F3, F3), or (H2(F2), H2(F2)), and whether PE(V) is simple exactly when V is simple and avoids those exceptional factors.
context_brief: Extend perfectness and simplicity criteria for PE(V)

question_text: Let I be an ideal of a Jordan pair V, let can: V -> V/I be the canonical map, and let PE(V, I) be the kernel of the induced surjective homomorphism PE(can): PE(V) -> PE(V/I). Describe the group PE(V, I) by explicit generators and relations.
context_brief: Generators and relations for relative group PE(V, I)

question_text: Assume V is defined over a field F and has a fully idempotent root grading R that is a division grading, meaning that every nonzero x in a root space V_alpha makes Q(x)|V_alpha invertible on the opposite root space. In the low-rank cases 2 <= rank R <= 4, is it true that whenever the Steinberg group St(V, R) is not centrally closed, every root space V_alpha must be one-dimensional over F and the field F must satisfy exactly the exceptional small-field restrictions listed in table (3.2.1)?

In the rank-one case, let J be a division Jordan algebra and let St(J) denote the rank-one Steinberg group defined in this section. Is St(J) centrally closed for every such J except the finite fields F_q with q in {2, 3, 4, 9}?
Let pi: St(V, R) -> PE(V) be the homomorphism from Theorem 2.11(a), and assume the root system R is irreducible of finite rank. Find sufficient conditions under which the kernel Ker(pi) is central.
context_brief: Centrality of the kernel of pi

question_text: For split root graded Jordan pairs V, can the basis-free presentation method pioneered by van der Kallen be generalized so that it treats the Steinberg group St(V, R) in a uniform, case-free way?

Consider the exterior Robin boundary value problem for the unit sphere in R^3: find a harmonic function w(φ, θ, r), defined for r > 1, 2π-periodic in θ, twice continuously differentiable, satisfying Laplace’s equation together with the boundary conditions lim_{r→1+} ||α w(φ, θ, r) + β ∂w/∂r(φ, θ, r) − h(φ, θ)||_{L^2(S)} = 0 and lim_{r→∞} w(φ, θ, r) = 0, where h ∈ L^2(S), S is the unit sphere, and α, β are chosen so that α − β(k + 1) ≠ 0 for every nonnegative integer k. For this problem, the boundary operator obtained from the solution formula is not a semigroup unless β = 0 (the Dirichlet case) or α = 0 (the Neumann case). In the semigroup setting for the Dirichlet and Neumann problems, the key tool relating approximation behavior and ergodic behavior is the interconnection theorem λR(λ; A^{-1})f = f − λ^{-1}R(λ^{-1}; A)f, where A is the infinitesimal generator of a semigroup. Does there exist an analogous interconnection relation for the Robin problem, or more generally when the relevant operator A is not the generator of a semigroup of operators, that could play the same role in establishing counterparts of the equivalences involving the resolvents and inverse/ergodic assertions from Theorems 1.1 and 2.1?
context_brief: Robin problem and non-semigroup resolvent interconnection

question_text: Develop an algorithmic procedure that, given an ordinary differential equation with the Painleve property, decides whether the equation can be solved in terms of one of the Painleve equations or an associated Painleve sigma-equation.

Develop a standard notation for Painleve transcendents that takes into account the wide variety of qualitatively different solutions that the Painleve equations possess and can distinguish those different solution families clearly.

Can numerical methods that exploit the integrable structure of the Painleve equations do better than standard Runge-Kutta methods and related generic ordinary-differential-equation solvers when computing Painleve solutions?

Because Painleve equations are integrable and are solvable by the isomonodromy method through an associated Riemann-Hilbert problem, how can that structure be used to build software for computing Painleve solutions numerically, including combining asymptotic information from the Riemann-Hilbert problem with efficient numerical codes to evaluate solutions at finite values of the independent variable?

Should numerical work on Painleve equations use integrable discretizations, namely discrete Painleve equations that tend to the associated continuous Painleve equations in an appropriate continuum limit, instead of relying only on generic discretizations of the differential equations?

Give a complete classification and a unified organizing structure for the major special properties of the Painleve equations, including Hamiltonian representations, exact solutions, Backlund transformations, associated isomonodromy problems, and asymptotic approximations with connection formulae, since the currently known results are still fragmentary and non-systematic.

Within the paper's standard ansatz for classical de Sitter solutions in 10d type II supergravity - namely a 10d metric globally written as a 4d de Sitter space-time times a 6d compact manifold, with Op/Dp sources, then further restricted to smeared solutions on 6d compact group manifolds with constant fluxes - is there any classical de Sitter solution whose sources are parallel, meaning that the sources lie along the same dimensions in the 10d space-time, or must every such putative solution be excluded?

For classical de Sitter solutions in the same standard type-II-supergravity ansatz, must every solution with intersecting Op/Dp sources be perturbatively unstable, in the precise 4d sense that at least one scalar field sits at a maximum of the scalar potential and is therefore tachyonic, equivalently giving the slow-roll parameter eta_V < 0?

Can a classical de Sitter solution in this standard type-II-supergravity setting simultaneously satisfy all four conditions needed for a controlled string-theory origin - large internal volume, small string coupling, a bounded number of orientifolds, and quantized fluxes - or is such a simultaneous regime impossible for every classical de Sitter solution?
context_brief: String-origin control of de Sitter solutions

question_text: Let F be a free group of rank at least 2, and let H be a finitely generated subgroup of the direct product F x F. The membership problem for H in F x F asks for an algorithm that, given a word in the generators of F x F, decides whether that word represents an element of H. Does such an algorithm always exist for every finitely generated subgroup H of F x F?
context_brief: Membership in direct products of free groups

question_text: Let G be a finitely presented group, and let H be a finitely generated subgroup of G whose membership problem in G is solvable, meaning there is an algorithm deciding whether a given word in G represents an element of H. Must the word problem in G itself then be solvable, that is, must there be an algorithm deciding whether a given word represents the identity element of G?

Suppose H is a hyperbolically embedded subgroup of G, meaning that there exists a relative presentation G = <X, H | R> for G with a strongly bounded relative presentation and a linear relative isoperimetric function. Let K be a finitely generated subgroup of H. If the membership problem for H in G is solvable, does it follow that the membership problem for K in G is also solvable?
context_brief: Membership transfer inside hyperbolically embedded subgroups

question_text: For the integral form of a Jack superpolynomial in superspace, defined by J^(alpha)_Lambda = sum_{Omega <= Lambda} v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) m_Omega, is every expansion coefficient v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) always a polynomial in alpha with integer coefficients?

Is there a combinatorial description, analogous to the one known in the ordinary Jack-polynomial setting, for the coefficients v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) appearing in the monomial expansion J^(alpha)_Lambda = sum_{Omega <= Lambda} v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) m_Omega of integral-form Jack superpolynomials?

Fix k >= 1 and N. For the space F_N^(k) of symmetric superpolynomials in N even variables and N odd variables that vanish whenever x_1 = x_2 = ... = x_{k+1}, do the Jack superpolynomials P^(alpha_{k,2})_Lambda(x_1, ..., x_N, theta_1, ..., theta_N) indexed by (k, 2, N)-admissible superpartitions form a basis of F_N^(k)?

What is the precise connection between admissible superpartitions, the associated Jack superpolynomials in superspace, and the basis states of irreducible Neveu-Schwarz modules in the minimal superconformal model M(2, 4p)?

For Macdonald superpolynomials in superspace, does the automorphism rho_{q,t} satisfy the second duality relation rho_{q,t}(P_Lambda(q, t)) = t^{|Lambda'a|} Q_{Lambda'}(t, q) for every superpartition Lambda?

For any two superpartitions Lambda and Omega of the same degree, does the normalized Macdonald superpolynomial satisfy the symmetry identity P_tilde_Lambda(u_Omega) = P_tilde_Omega(u_Lambda), where u_Lambda denotes the specialization determined by Lambda?

When the modified Macdonald superpolynomial H_Lambda(q, t) is expanded in the Schur superpolynomial basis as H_Lambda(q, t) = sum_Omega K_{Omega,Lambda}(q, t) s_Omega, are all coefficients K_{Omega,Lambda}(q, t) polynomials in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients?

Can one obtain explicit Littlewood-Richardson rules in superspace for the coefficients c^Gamma_{Lambda,Omega} and cbar^Gamma_{Lambda,Omega} that govern products of Schur superpolynomials and their dual variants?
For the ideal I_N^(k,r) spanned by Jack superpolynomials indexed by (k, r, N)-admissible superpartitions, is the inclusion I_N^(k,r) subseteq F_N^(k) actually an equality when r = 2?
context_brief: Equality of admissible Jack ideal and vanishing space

question_text: Does every closed Riemannian manifold contain a closed geodesic multinet that does not contain any non-trivial periodic geodesic? Here "closed" means there are no unbalanced (boundary) vertices, and a geodesic multinet is the version of a geodesic net that allows edge multiplicities and self-intersections.
Which 3-regular graphs G occur as the underlying graph of a closed geodesic net on the round 3-sphere? Here a closed geodesic net is a geodesic net with no unbalanced vertices.
Does every closed Riemannian manifold of dimension >= 3 admit a closed geodesic net whose underlying graph is a theta-graph, namely a graph with two vertices joined by three distinct edges?

For a fixed closed Riemannian manifold M, is there a function f_M, depending on the geometry and topology of M, such that every closed geodesic net on M of length L has at most f_M(L) balanced vertices?

Let Sigma be the set of all triples S of points in the Euclidean plane for which there exist geodesic multinets with exactly three unbalanced vertices located at S and with arbitrarily many balanced vertices. Is Sigma a measure-zero subset of (R^2)^3?

Is there a function f(n) such that every geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane with three boundary (unbalanced) vertices and with multiplicity of every edge at most n has at most f(n) balanced vertices?
Classify all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane that have exactly three unbalanced vertices.

Either construct an irreducible geodesic net in the Euclidean plane with four unbalanced vertices and more than 16 balanced vertices, or prove that no such geodesic net exists. Here irreducible means that no proper subset of its edges, together with the incident vertices, is itself a geodesic net with the same set of unbalanced vertices.

Do there exist geodesic nets in the Euclidean plane with exactly four unbalanced vertices and arbitrarily many balanced vertices? The conjecture further suggests that this may already hold when the four unbalanced vertices are the vertices of a square.
context_brief: Arbitrarily many balanced vertices from four boundary points

question_text: Is there a number N such that every irreducible geodesic net whose unbalanced vertices are exactly the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron has at most N balanced vertices?

Does there exist an integer N0 and an N0-tuple S of points in the Euclidean plane such that, for every N, there is a geodesic net whose set of unbalanced vertices is exactly S and whose number of balanced vertices is greater than N? Moreover, do such N0-tuples S form a subset of (R^2)^N0 of positive measure, or even a non-empty open subset?
context_brief: Fixed boundary set with unbounded complexity

question_text: Can the number of balanced vertices of a geodesic net in the Euclidean plane be bounded above by a function of only two quantities: the number of unbalanced vertices and the total imbalance? Here the total imbalance is the sum, over all unbalanced vertices, of the norms of their imbalance vectors.
Is there a function f such that every geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane with n unbalanced vertices, diameter D, and total length L has fewer than f(L/D, n) balanced vertices?

Let M be a complete Riemannian manifold. Does there exist a function f_M, invariant under rescaling of M, with the following property: whenever a geodesic net G on M has total length L, adjusted length L_tilde, diameter D, and n unbalanced vertices, the number of balanced vertices is at most f_M(L_tilde, L/D, n)? Here the adjusted length L_tilde is obtained by summing over all edges e_i the arclength integral of 1 / inj(e_i(s)), where inj(e_i(s)) is the injectivity radius of M at the point e_i(s). In particular, if M has injectivity radius inj > 0, must the number of balanced vertices be at most f_M(L / inj, L / D, n)?

Consider the layered geodesic-net construction G_n(phi) built from seven equally spaced outer vertices, an inner seven-vertex layer determined by a deviation parameter phi, and subsequent layers V_i produced by the paper's suspension-and-winging rules. For odd i, define the suspension angle phi_i(phi) as the angle OPv between the ray from the center O of the outer circle to the relevant hook P and the segment Pv for a vertex v in V_i. For even i, define phi_i(phi) as the angle OXv, where X is the third vertex of the equilateral triangle on the relevant outer pair P,Q and v lies in V_i. Does the derivative sequence phi_i'(0) ever repeat, or is it nonrepeating for all i?

In the same layered construction G_n(phi), is it true that for sufficiently small nonzero phi the finite sequence of suspension angles phi_0(phi), phi_1(phi), ..., phi_n(phi) never repeats a value? Equivalently, does this force G_n(phi) to be a geodesic net in which all edges have weight one, while still having 14 unbalanced vertices and, for large n, arbitrarily many balanced vertices?

For an irreducible Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP), is the squared coefficient of variation of the event-stationary inter-event time always at least 1? Equivalently, if T_1^alpha denotes the first inter-event time in the event-stationary version of the process, must c^2 = Var(T_1^alpha) / E[T_1^alpha]^2 satisfy c^2 >= 1 for every irreducible MMPP?

For an irreducible Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP), does the first inter-event time in the time-stationary version stochastically dominate the first inter-event time in the event-stationary version? In the paper's notation, if T_1^pi is the first inter-event time under time-stationary initialization and T_1^alpha is the first inter-event time under event-stationary initialization, must T_1^pi >=st T_1^alpha hold for every irreducible MMPP?
If a Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP) has event-stationary inter-event times with squared coefficient of variation c^2 equal to 1, must the process itself be a Poisson process?

For a Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP), if the squared coefficient of variation c^2 of the event-stationary inter-event times equals 1, does it follow that all modulating Poisson rates lambda_i are equal?

Do analogues of the two MMPP conjectures extend to general Cox processes under suitable regularity conditions? More specifically, for Cox processes satisfying appropriate regularity assumptions, must the squared coefficient of variation of the event-stationary inter-event time be at least 1 and must the time-stationary first inter-event time stochastically dominate the event-stationary first inter-event time?
context_brief: Cox-process extensions of the MMPP conjectures

question_text:
Let ψ be a function in L2(R). For integers j,k ∈ Z, define the dyadic dilates and translates
ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k). Call ψ an orthonormal wavelet if the collection {ψ_{j,k} : j,k ∈ Z} forms an orthonormal basis of L2(R).

Consider the set of all orthonormal wavelets as a subset of the unit sphere in L2(R). Is this set path connected in the L2(R) norm, meaning that for any two orthonormal wavelets ψ0 and ψ1 there exists a continuous map Ψ:[0,1]→L2(R) (continuous in the L2 norm) with Ψ(0)=ψ0, Ψ(1)=ψ1, and Ψ(t) an orthonormal wavelet for every t ∈ [0,1]?

Let ψ ∈ L2(R) be an orthonormal wavelet, and let ψ̂ denote its Fourier transform. Define the wavelet dimension function Dψ: R→N∪{0} by Dψ(ξ) := ∑_{j=1}^{∞} ∑_{k∈Z} |ψ̂(2^j(ξ+k))|^2.

Fix any function D:R→N∪{0} satisfying (D1) D is measurable and 1-periodic, (D2) D(ξ)+D(ξ+1/2)=D(2ξ)+1 a.e., (D3) ∑_{k∈Z} 1_Δ(ξ+k) ≥ D(ξ) a.e. where Δ = { ξ ∈ R : D(2^{−j} ξ) ≥ 1 for j ∈ N ∪ {0} }, and (D4) lim inf_{j→∞} D(2^{−j} ξ) ≥ 1 a.e.

Is the set { ψ ∈ L2(R) : ψ is an orthonormal wavelet and Dψ = D } path connected in L2(R) norm?

Let ψ ∈ L2(R). For integers j,k ∈ Z, define ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k). Call ψ a Parseval wavelet if ∑_{j,k∈Z} |⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩|^2 = ||f||^2 for all f ∈ L2(R).

Is the collection of Parseval wavelets path connected in the L2(R) norm?

Let f̂ denote the Fourier transform of f. Let H be either L2(R) or the Hardy space H2(R) = { f ∈ L2(R) : f̂(ξ) = 0 for ξ ≤ 0 }. For ψ ∈ L2(R), define ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k), j,k ∈ Z. Call ψ a Riesz wavelet for H if the wavelet system {ψ_{j,k} : j,k ∈ Z} is a Riesz basis of H.

Is the collection of Riesz wavelets (in this dyadic setting) path connected in the L2(R) norm?

Let f̂ denote the Fourier transform of f. Let H2(R) = { f ∈ L2(R) : f̂(ξ) = 0 for ξ ≤ 0 }. Let ψ ∈ L2(R), and define ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k), j,k ∈ Z. Call ψ a Riesz wavelet for H2(R) if the wavelet system {ψ_{j,k} : j,k ∈ Z} is a Riesz basis of H2(R).

Does there exist a Riesz wavelet ψ in H2(R) such that ψ belongs to the Schwartz class?

Let ψ ∈ L2(R) be an orthonormal wavelet with dyadic dilates/translates ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k) forming an orthonormal basis of L2(R). Let ψ̂ be the Fourier transform of ψ.

A wavelet set is a measurable set W ⊂ R such that {W+k}_{k∈Z} partitions R modulo null sets and {2^j W}_{j∈Z} partitions R modulo null sets.

Is it true that for every orthonormal wavelet ψ ∈ L2(R), there exists a wavelet set W such that W ⊂ supp ψ̂?

For ψ ∈ L2(R), define ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k), j,k ∈ Z. Call ψ a Riesz wavelet for L2(R) if {ψ_{j,k} : j,k ∈ Z} is a Riesz basis of L2(R).

Is the collection of all Riesz wavelets dense in L2(R) with respect to the L2 norm?

Let ψ be a Parseval wavelet, meaning ∑_{j,k∈Z} |⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩|^2 = ||f||^2 for all f ∈ L2(R), where ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k).

Define V(ψ) := span{ψ_{j,k} : j < 0, k ∈ Z}. Let D be the dilation operator (Df)(x) = √2 f(x).

Is it true that ⋂_{j∈Z} D^j(V(ψ)) = {0}?

Let ψ ∈ L2(R) and define ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k), j,k ∈ Z. A wavelet system is Bessel if there exists d < ∞ such that ∑_{j,k∈Z} |⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩|^2 ≤ d||f||^2 for all f ∈ L2(R).

Suppose ψ is a Bessel wavelet with bound < 1. Does there exist ψ′ such that {ψ_{j,k}} ∪ {ψ′_{j,k}} is a Parseval frame for L2(R)?
context_brief: Extending Bessel wavelets to Parseval frames

question_text:
For 0 < b < 1, define ψ_b ∈ L2(R) by ψ̂_b = 1_{(−1,−b)∪(b,1)}.

A frame wavelet is a function ψ whose dyadic wavelet system {ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k)} is a frame for L2(R) with bounds 0 < c ≤ d < ∞.

For what values of 1/8 < b ≤ 1/6 is ψ_b a frame wavelet?
context_brief: Frame property for a specific band-pass Fourier support

question_text:
Let A ∈ GL_n(R) be invertible and let Γ ⊂ R^n be a full rank lattice. For ψ ∈ L2(R^n), define ψ_{j,k}(x) := |det A|^{j/2} ψ(A^j x − k) for j ∈ Z and k ∈ Γ. Call ψ an orthonormal wavelet associated with (A,Γ) if {ψ_{j,k} : j ∈ Z, k ∈ Γ} is an orthonormal basis of L2(R^n).

For what dilations A and lattices Γ does there exist an orthonormal wavelet associated with (A,Γ)?

Let A ∈ GL_n(R) and let Γ ⊂ R^n be a full rank lattice. A measurable set W ⊂ R^n is an (A,Γ)-wavelet set if {W+γ}_{γ∈Γ} partitions R^n modulo null sets and {A^j W}_{j∈Z} partitions R^n modulo null sets.

Characterize pairs (A,Γ) for which an (A,Γ)-wavelet set exists.

Fix (A,Γ) with A ∈ GL_n(R) and Γ ⊂ R^n a full rank lattice. Suppose an orthonormal wavelet associated with (A,Γ) exists.

Must there also exist a minimally supported frequency (MSF) wavelet associated with (A,Γ), where MSF means |ψ̂| = 1_W for some measurable set W that is a wavelet set (tiles by translations and dilations, modulo null sets)?
context_brief: MSF wavelets vs existence of wavelets

question_text:
Let A ∈ GL_n(R) and Γ ⊂ R^n a full rank lattice. Let ψ be an orthonormal (or Parseval) wavelet associated with (A,Γ), and let ψ̂ be its Fourier transform.

Does Calderón’s formula ∑_{j∈Z} |ψ̂((A^T)^j ξ)|^2 = 1 hold for almost every ξ ∈ R^n?

Let Γ = Z^n and let A ∈ GL_n(R) be expansive, meaning all eigenvalues λ of A satisfy |λ| > 1. A function ψ ∈ L2(R^n) is well-localized if both ψ and ψ̂ have polynomial decay: ψ(x)=O(|x|^{−N}) and ψ̂(ξ)=O(|ξ|^{−N}) for some large N>0.

For what expansive dilations A do there exist well-localized wavelets associated with (A,Z^n), possibly with multiple generators?

A function ψ on R^n is r-regular for r = 0,1,2,… or ∞ if ψ is C^r and all partial derivatives up to order r decay polynomially: ∂^α ψ(x) = O(|x|^{−N}) as |x|→∞ for all |α| ≤ r, for some N>0.

Does there exist an ∞-regular wavelet construction in higher dimensions?

Schwartz class is the collection of all ∞-regular functions on R^n. Let A be an expansive dilation with integer entries (equivalently AZ^n ⊂ Z^n) and let Γ = Z^n.

Do Schwartz class wavelets exist for integer expansive dilations A and lattice Γ = Z^n?
context_brief: Schwartz class wavelets for integer expansive dilations

question_text:
Let ψ ∈ L2(R) be an orthonormal wavelet as in the dyadic definition, and assume ψ belongs to the Schwartz class (the collection of all ∞-regular functions).

Is the Fourier transform ψ̂ necessarily compactly supported?
context_brief: Fourier support of Schwartz class orthonormal wavelets

question_text: Let M be a compact connected Sasaki manifold with fixed underlying contact CR structure (D, J). Its Sasaki cone kappa(D, J) is the moduli space of Sasaki metrics with that fixed CR structure, and in the unreduced cone t^+(D, J) these structures come in rays under transverse scaling. Must every ray represented by a Sasaki metric of constant scalar curvature be isolated among the rays in the Sasaki cone?
context_brief: Isolation of cscS rays in the Sasaki cone

question_text: Let M be a compact connected Sasaki manifold with fixed underlying contact CR structure (D, J), and let its Sasaki cone be the cone of rays of Sasaki metrics compatible with that structure. Suppose the cone contains an extremal ray, meaning a ray represented by a Sasaki metric whose scalar curvature has transversely holomorphic gradient; constant scalar curvature Sasaki metrics are a special case of extremal metrics. Does it follow that the same Sasaki cone must contain at least one constant scalar curvature ray?
context_brief: From extremal rays to existence of a cscS ray

question_text: What is the minimax memory-bounded first-order oracle complexity T_{L,B}(d,M,epsilon) for minimizing a convex L-Lipschitz function F:R^d->R over the Euclidean ball {x: ||x|| <= B} when there exists an optimizer x* with ||x*|| <= B, and an algorithm is allowed T exact first-order oracle calls that each reveal F(x) and a subgradient at x but only M bits of state may be stored between oracle accesses? Equivalently, which query-memory pairs (T,M) are possible or impossible for this problem, preferably up to constant factors and at worst up to polylogarithmic factors in T and M?

In the regime where the dimension d is larger than polylogarithmic in 1/epsilon but smaller than polynomial in 1/epsilon, and only essentially linear memory is available between oracle calls, can convex L-Lipschitz optimization be solved with a number of first-order queries that is polynomial in d? More specifically, when the memory budget satisfies M = Theta(d polylog(LB/epsilon)) or M = O~(d), is T(d,M,epsilon) = O(poly d) achievable in that intermediate scaling regime?

Still in the regime d = Omega(log^c(1/epsilon)) and d = O(1/epsilon^c) for all c, is quadratic memory really necessary to obtain near-optimal query complexity for convex Lipschitz optimization? Concretely, can one have T(d, M = O(d^(2-delta)), epsilon) = O~(d polylog(1/epsilon)) for some delta > 0 while storing only subquadratic memory between first-order oracle calls?

Does there exist any query-memory tradeoff (T,M) for convex Lipschitz optimization with limited memory that lies polynomially inside the currently unknown region between the two known extremes, namely the gradient-descent regime with memory on the order of d log(LB/epsilon) bits and query complexity on the order of 1/epsilon^2, and the center-of-mass regime with query complexity on the order of d log(1/epsilon) and memory on the order of d^2 log^2(LB/epsilon)? Or is every tradeoff in that intermediate square impossible?

Does there exist a connected signed graph Γ = (G, σ) whose underlying graph G is not complete, whose adjacency spectrum is symmetric with respect to the origin, but which is not sign-symmetric, meaning Γ is not switching isomorphic to its negation -Γ = (G, -σ)?
Must every graph with exactly three distinct adjacency eigenvalues have at most three distinct vertex degrees?
Do there exist connected bipartite graphs with exactly four distinct adjacency eigenvalues and more than four distinct valencies?
Characterize all connected signed graphs whose adjacency spectrum consists of exactly two distinct eigenvalues.
Characterize all connected signed graphs whose spectral radius does not exceed sqrt(2 + sqrt(5)).

Does there exist a constant c such that every unsigned graph G with smallest adjacency eigenvalue at least -3 is c-integrable, meaning there is an integer matrix N such that c(A - floor(λ_min)I) = NN^T where A is the adjacency matrix of G and λ_min is its smallest eigenvalue?
Construct maximal signed graphs whose smallest adjacency eigenvalue is at least -3.
Develop a theory of signed Hoffman graphs analogous to the Hoffman graph machinery used for unsigned graphs.

For a simple connected unsigned graph Γ, determine the signature or signatures σ̄ that minimize spectral radius among all signatures on Γ, that is, satisfy ρ(Γ, σ̄) <= ρ(Γ, σ) for every signature σ of Γ.
Does every connected d-regular graph G admit a signature σ whose signed adjacency matrix has spectral radius at most 2 sqrt(d - 1)?
Are there 5-regular graphs that admit a signature attaining equality in Theorem 3.23, beyond the examples already constructed in the discussion leading up to Problem 3.24?
If Δ is the maximum vertex degree of a nontrivial graph G, does there always exist a signature σ such that the spectral radius of the resulting signed graph satisfies ρ(G, σ) < 2 sqrt(Δ - 1)?
If ρ is the spectral radius of a connected graph G, is there a signature σ such that the signed spectral radius satisfies ρ(G, σ) < 2 sqrt(ρ - 1)?
context_brief: spectral radius bound from unsigned spectral radius

question_text: For a signed graph consisting of 2k odd cycles of pairwise equal length and opposite signs, is the signature described in Proposition 3.27 the signature that minimizes spectral radius?
context_brief: minimizing spectral radius for paired odd cycles

question_text: Given a signed graph Γ = (G, σ), define a complement signed graph Γ̄ = (Ḡ, σ̄) whose underlying graph is the usual graph complement and for which useful spectral relations with the complete signed graph Γ ∪ Γ̄ hold.
Let N_α(d) denote the maximum number of equiangular lines in R^d with common angle α. Is it true that N_{1/5}(d) = 276 for 23 <= d <= 185, and N_{1/5}(d) = floor(3(d - 1)/2) for d >= 185?
Find a combinatorial interpretation of Seidel matrices that have exactly three distinct eigenvalues.
Do there exist Seidel matrices of order at least 14 with exactly three distinct eigenvalues whose switching class contains no regular graph?
context_brief: three-eigenvalue Seidel matrices without regular graph

question_text: Does every Seidel matrix with exactly three distinct rational eigenvalues contain a regular graph in its switching class?
For a graph Γ on n vertices, must its Seidel energy satisfy S(Γ) >= 2(n - 1), with equality at the complete graph K_n?
If a Seidel matrix S has rank n - 1, must there exist a 0-eigenvector of S whose entries are all ±1?

In the linear model where an algorithm for a transformation is a product of matrices R_t and each step R_t is block diagonal with n-2 identity blocks and one 2x2 unitary block acting on only two coordinates, let F be the normalized n x n Fourier transform, let G = [[0, F], [-F^*, 0]], and define X_alpha = (cos alpha) Id + (sin alpha) G on C^(2n). What is the true asymptotic lower bound, as alpha tends to 0, on the number of such two-coordinate unitary steps required to compute X_alpha? In particular, can one prove that computing X_alpha requires essentially Omega(n log n) steps rather than only the currently derived Omega(alpha^2 n log n) or Omega(alpha n log n) lower bounds?
context_brief: Asymptotic lower bound for computing X_alpha

question_text: Can one prove a lower bound for computing X_alpha in the same two-coordinate unitary-step model that is stronger than Omega(alpha n log n), possibly by choosing a nontrivial unitary representation Psi of U(n), composing the entropy-style potential Phi with Psi, and in particular exploiting the order-k determinant representation Psi_det^k(U) whose (I, J) entry is det U_{I,J}?
context_brief: Representation-theoretic route to stronger lower bounds

question_text: Even when the angle is fixed at alpha = pi/4 instead of tending to 0, can one prove a nontrivial lower bound for computing X_(pi/4) in the two-coordinate unitary-step model that is better than (1/(2 sqrt(2))) n log_2 n, which the paper states is the best bound obtainable from the vanilla entropy potential Phi?

For the mod-2 Steenrod algebra A_2 acting on the polynomial algebra P_d = F_2[x_1,…,x_d], determine a minimal generating set of P_d as a left A_2-module for every number of variables d ≥ 5. Equivalently, determine a basis of the quotient space QP_d = F_2 ⊗_{A_2} P_d, which is isomorphic to P_d / A_2^+ P_d, where A_2^+ is the augmentation ideal. In particular, the paper emphasizes that the five-variable case is not yet completely solved and that the general d ≥ 5 case remains open.
context_brief: Peterson hit problem in five or more variables

question_text: Let Tr_d denote Singer's algebraic transfer from GL_d-coinvariants of A_2-annihilated classes in H_*(B(ℤ/2)^d) to Ext^{d,d+*}_{A_2}(F_2,F_2). Is Tr_d a monomorphism for every rank d > 4? The paper states that Singer proposed injectivity for all positive integers d, but that this prediction is still unresolved in the range d > 4.
context_brief: Singer transfer injectivity beyond rank four

question_text: Does there exist a framed manifold of Kervaire invariant one in dimension 2^7 - 2 = 126? Equivalently, in the formulation recalled by the paper, does the class h_6^2 ∈ Ext^{2,2^7}_{A_2}(F_2,F_2) represent a stable homotopy element θ_6 : S^{126} → S^0? The paper notes that the cases i ≤ 5 are known to exist and the cases i ≥ 7 do not exist, leaving exactly i = 6 unresolved.

For every integer t ≥ 2, is the rank-5 Singer transfer Tr_5 an isomorphism in bidegree (5, 5 + (13·2^t - 5))? Using the reductions explained in the paper, this amounts to determining the GL_5-invariants of (QP_5)_{47}, where QP_5 = P_5/A_2^+P_5 for P_5 = F_2[x_1,…,x_5], and in particular understanding whether the invariant subspace of Ker((Sqg^0_*)(5,47)) vanishes. The paper also highlights a more interesting alternative in which this kernel has nontrivial GL_5-invariants and dim((QP_5)^{GL_5}_{47}) is not equal to 1.
context_brief: Whether the fifth Singer transfer stays an isomorphism for t at least two

question_text: Let B = ⊕_{n≥0} B_n be a semi-graded ring such that B is left noetherian, B_0 is left noetherian and contained in the center Z(B), each homogeneous piece B_n is finitely generated as a left B_0-module, and B satisfies the χ1 condition. If π : sgr-B → qsgr-B is the quotient from finitely generated semi-graded B-modules to the quotient by torsion modules, s is the degree-shift autoequivalence on qsgr-B, and Γ(π(B))_{≥0} := ⊕_{d≥0} Hom_{qsgr-B}(π(B), s^d(π(B))), does there exist an equivalence of categories qgr-B ≃ qgr-Γ(π(B))_{≥0} extending the Serre-Artin-Zhang-Verevkin theorem from finitely graded algebras to semi-graded rings?

Let A be a bijective skew PBW extension of an Ore domain R. Does A satisfy a Gelfand-Kirillov type description of its total ring of fractions, meaning that Q(A) is isomorphic to the total ring of fractions of a suitable multiparameter skew quantum polynomial algebra over Q(R), analogous to the quantum Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture? In addition, does taking centers commute with taking total fractions for such algebras, i.e. is Q(Z(A)) isomorphic to Z(Q(A))?
context_brief: Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture for bijective skew PBW extensions

question_text: Let K be a field and let A = K[x_1, ..., x_n; σ] be the skew polynomial ring in commuting variables satisfying x_i x_j = x_j x_i and x_i r = σ(r) x_i for every r in K, where σ is an automorphism of K of finite order. Give a matrix-constructive proof of the Quillen-Suslin theorem for A: for every finitely generated projective A-module, explicitly compute a basis. Equivalently, design an algorithm that, given an idempotent matrix F in M_s(A), constructs an invertible matrix U in GL_s(A) such that UFU^{-1} has block form [[0, 0], [0, I_r]], so the final r rows of U form a basis of the projective module generated by the rows of F.
context_brief: Constructive Quillen-Suslin algorithm for skew polynomial rings

question_text: Let B be a left semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebra with finite Gelfand-Kirillov dimension. Must B be a left noetherian domain? Here a left semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebra means a connected finitely semi-graded K-algebra B with finite left global dimension d such that Ext^i_B(B/B_{≥1}, B) = 0 for i ≠ d and Ext^d_B(B/B_{≥1}, B) ≅ B/B_{≥1}.
context_brief: Noetherian-domain question for semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebras

question_text: Let B be a semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebra over a field K of characteristic 0, and assume that B is left and right noetherian, generated in degree 1, and has global dimension 3. Is B cancellative in the Zariski cancellation sense, meaning that for every K-algebra C, any isomorphism B[t] ≅ C[t] forces B ≅ C?
context_brief: Zariski cancellation for semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebras

question_text: Which broad and mathematically natural classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds can be described explicitly? Here an affine Poisson manifold means a finite-dimensional manifold equipped with an affine atlas and a Poisson bi-vector P whose Schouten self-bracket [[P,P]] vanishes.

Can one construct smooth-atlas globalisations of the known Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetries Q_{1:6/2}(P)=O→r(γ_3)(P), Q_5(P)=O→r(γ_5)(P), and Q_7(P)=O→r(γ_7)(P)? In this notation, O→r is the graph-orientation map that sends a graph cocycle γ to a universal infinitesimal symmetry Q(P) of Poisson bi-vectors.

For a graph cocycle γ=Σ_a c_a·γ_a on n vertices, are combinatorial statistics of the constituent graphs—such as diameter distributions and vertex-valency distributions—stable across the full cohomology class [γ]=[γ+d(λ)] after arbitrary coboundary changes by graphs λ on n−1 vertices? Relatedly, what is the large-n and asymptotic behavior of the dimension of graph cohomology, especially near the bi-grading ray (n, 2n−2) that is relevant for Poisson-bracket symmetries, and is there a generating function for those dimensions?
context_brief: Stability and asymptotics of graph cocycles

question_text: How can Willwacher’s isomorphism grt ≃ H^0(Gra), between the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra and degree-zero cohomology of the relevant unoriented graph complex, be illustrated concretely at small vertex numbers such as n=4, 6, 8, 9, 10, ... where nontrivial cocycles already occur?

For the bi-grading ray (N, 2N), beginning at which N′>7 do nontrivial cocycles ω in the graph-complex kernel ker d exist, and beginning at which larger N′′ are those cocycles orientable to nonzero Kontsevich graphs built from wedges? Can one give explicit examples of new Poisson-bracket symmetries of the form Ṗ = (O→r(ω)(P))^m · O→r(γ)(P) using known cocycles γ and new cocycles ω on that ray?

For non-unique factorisations [[P,Q(P)]]=♦(P,[[P,P]]) of the Poisson-cocycle condition through Leibniz graphs, what is the topological structure of the resulting identities ♦₂−♦₁≡0? Equivalently, if one forms a meta-graph whose vertices are Leibniz graphs and where adjacency means that two Leibniz graphs have expansions sharing a Kontsevich oriented graph, what are the genus, diameter, typical cycle length, and related invariants of these meta-graphs, and how does the iterative generation algorithm saturate them?

Do there exist universal infinitesimal symmetries Q(P) of Poisson structures that are nonlinear, proper, valid for all finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds, and not produced from graph cocycles through Kontsevich’s orientation morphism O→r?

If a graph cocycle γ generates the formal flow P(ε)=exp(ε O→r(γ)(P)·∂/∂P⃗)P|_{ε=0} on Poisson bi-vectors, does that graph-defined power series converge and determine a globally well-defined Poisson structure at every point of an arbitrary affine Poisson manifold?

What are the Liouville-integrability and possible super-integrability properties of the nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems Ṗ = Q(P) that arise from known Kontsevich graph symmetries of Poisson bi-vectors?

Does the evolution equation Ṗ = Q(P) for Poisson structures itself carry a Poisson or Hamiltonian formulation on the jet space of Poisson bi-vector components, meaning that one can write Q(P)=π(χ(P)) for some variational Poisson structure π and variational covector χ, possibly χ=δH/δP for a well-defined Hamiltonian functional?

Consider the two-parameter family of Poisson brackets on R^3 defined by {f,g}_{a,ρ}(x,y,z)=ρ(x,y,z)·det(∂(a,f,g)/∂(x,y,z)), where a is a smooth function and ρ is a density in the chosen coordinates. Is this class preserved by any Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry Ṗ=Q(P), and for a given symmetry does there exist an induced evolutionary system ȧ=A([a],[ρ]), ρ̇=R([a],[ρ]) whose pushforward under τ:(a,ρ)↦{·,·}_{a,ρ} equals Q(P([a],ρ))?
context_brief: Preservation of Nambu-type brackets on R^3

question_text: Which two-parameter Poisson brackets {·,·}_{a,ρ} on R^3 remain invariant under a fixed Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry, meaning Q({·,·}_{a,ρ})≡0 at every point? More generally, which Poisson bi-vectors P satisfy both the Jacobi identity [[P,P]]=0 and the invariance condition Q(P)=0 for a chosen symmetry Q?

Do there exist infinitesimal symmetries Q(P) of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds that are simultaneously nonlinear, proper, and nontrivial in Poisson cohomology, meaning they are not of the form [[P,X]] up to terms proportional to [[P,P]]? If no such examples exist, what mechanism forces all currently known universal Poisson cocycles, including those produced from nontrivial graph cocycles by O→r, to become ∂_P-trivial?

For a fixed affine Poisson manifold (M^r_aff,P), how many of the countably many universal symmetries obtained by applying O→r to wheel cocycles and their iterated commutators in ker d are globally nonzero sections of Λ^2TM^r_aff rather than vanishing identically?

For a fixed affine Poisson manifold (M^r_aff,P), how large is the family of trivialising vector fields X=X(γ) associated with graph cocycles γ∈ker d? Is the vector space of these vector fields locally complete enough to approximate arbitrary vector fields on the manifold, so that the exponentials of the trivialising fields could effectively imitate a smooth structure on the affine Poisson manifold?

Suppose a classical model has a Poisson bracket {·,·}_P and an infinitesimal symmetry Q that acts nontrivially on that Poisson structure. After quantisation, must there always be a corresponding well-defined response either on the Hilbert space of states, on the operator algebra of observables, or on both?
context_brief: Quantised response to a classical symmetry

question_text: How does the graph complex act on the space of deformation-quantisation star-products, especially under gauge transformations ⋆⇄⋆′, when the leading Poisson bi-vector in a Kontsevich star-product ⋆ = × + ħ{·,·}_P + o(ħ) is shifted by a graph-generated symmetry Q(P)=O→r(γ)(P) to P+εQ(P)+o(ε)? Can this action be described explicitly and illustrated by examples?

How do graph-complex symmetries Ṗ=O→r(γ)(P) act on the Ikeda–Izawa Poisson σ-model, whose Feynman path-integral expansion encodes the Kontsevich star-product? In addition, does that σ-model possess symmetries that do not originate from graph cocycles γ in ker d?
context_brief: Graph symmetries in the Poisson sigma-model

question_text: Do universal infinitesimal symmetries Ṗ=Q(P) of classical Poisson structures survive under Batalin–Vilkovisky quantisation, where the classical master equation [[P,P]]=0 is replaced by iħΔP + 1/2[[P,P]] = 0?

Is there a universal extension of the Kontsevich construction from affine Poisson manifolds to the commutative but non-associative calculus of cyclic words with pair-of-pants multiplication in formal noncommutative or super-geometry, such that it remains well defined for the full family of graph-encoded symmetries Q∈sym([[P,P]]=0) of Poisson structures?

Let M be the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on R^d, defined by M f(x) = sup_{r>0} (1/m(B(x,r))) ∫_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy, where B(x,r) is the open ball of center x and radius r, and let the uncentered maximal operator be defined analogously by taking the supremum over all open balls that contain x. Is the map f -> |∇M f| bounded from the Sobolev space W^{1,1}(R^d) to L^1(R^d)? Equivalently, for every f in W^{1,1}(R^d), is M f weakly differentiable and does there exist a universal constant C = C(d) such that ||∇M f||_{L^1(R^d)} <= C ||∇f||_{L^1(R^d)}? The same question is asked for the uncentered maximal operator.

For a one-dimensional real-valued function f of bounded variation, let M be the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. Must the total variation decrease under M, in the sharp form Var(M f) <= Var(f)? If that sharp inequality fails, can Kurka's existing bound with constant 240004 be substantially improved?

For alpha >= 0, define the one-dimensional non-tangential maximal operator by M^alpha f(x) = sup_{(y,t): |x-y| <= alpha t} (1/(2t)) ∫_{y-t}^{y+t} |f(s)| ds, so that alpha = 0 gives the centered maximal operator and alpha = 1 gives the uncentered maximal operator. For functions f : R -> R of bounded variation, does the sharp inequality Var(M^alpha f) <= Var(f) hold for every 0 <= alpha < 1/3? If not, what is the smallest alpha for which that inequality is valid?

Suppose f is a radial function in W^{1,1}(R^d). The known uncentered result says that the uncentered Hardy-Littlewood maximal function of f is weakly differentiable and satisfies an L^1 gradient bound of the form ||∇M̃ f||_{L^1(R^d)} <= C ||∇f||_{L^1(R^d)}. Does the analogous statement remain true for the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator M acting on radial functions?

Let M_S be the spherical maximal operator on R^d, defined by taking at each x the supremum over r > 0 of the average of |f| on the sphere S^{d-1}(x,r). For dimensions d >= 2, is M_S bounded as an operator from W^{1,p}(R^d) to W^{1,p}(R^d) throughout the full endpoint range 1 < p <= d/(d-1)?

Let phi be a nonnegative integrable convolution kernel on R^d with integral 1, let phi_t(x) = t^{-d} phi(x/t), and define the convolution-type maximal operator by M_phi f(x) = sup_{t>0} (phi_t * |f|)(x). For a one-dimensional function f of bounded variation, does there always exist a finite constant C(phi) such that Var(M_phi f) <= C(phi) Var(f)? For which kernels phi can one prove the sharp constant C(phi) = 1?

For 0 <= beta < d, define the centered Hardy-Littlewood fractional maximal operator by M_beta f(x) = sup_{r>0} m(B(x,r))^{beta/d - 1} ∫_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy, and define the uncentered fractional maximal operator analogously by taking the supremum over balls that contain x. When 0 <= beta < 1 and q = d/(d-beta), is the map f -> |∇M_beta f| bounded from W^{1,1}(R^d) to L^q(R^d)? The same question is asked for the uncentered fractional maximal operator.

For 0 < beta < 1 and q = d/(d-beta), a known result proves that if f is radial and belongs to W^{1,1}(R^d), then the uncentered fractional maximal function is weakly differentiable and satisfies ||∇M̃_beta f||_{L^q(R^d)} <= C ||∇f||_{L^1(R^d)}. Does the analogous statement hold for the centered fractional maximal operator M_beta acting on radial functions?

For a sequence f : Z -> R, define the one-dimensional discrete centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal function by M f(n) = sup_{r>=0} (1/(2r+1)) sum_{k=-r}^r |f(n+k)|, where the supremum is over nonnegative integers r. If f has bounded variation on Z, must the sharp inequality Var(M f) <= Var(f) hold? If not, can Temur's bound with constant 294912004 be substantially improved?

For 0 < beta < 1, define the one-dimensional discrete centered fractional maximal operator by M_beta f(n) = sup_{r>=0} (2r+1)^{beta-1} sum_{k=-r}^r |f(n+k)|, where the supremum is over nonnegative integers r, and let q = 1/(1-beta). If f : Z -> R has bounded variation and M_beta f is not identically infinite, is there a universal constant C such that the q-variation of M_beta f satisfies Var_q(M_beta f) <= C Var(f)?

Let Omega be a bounded open convex subset of R^d with Lipschitz boundary and 0 in its interior. For 0 <= beta < d and f : Z^d -> R, define the discrete centered fractional maximal operator associated to Omega by M_{Omega,beta} f(n) = sup_{r>=0} N(0,r)^{beta/d - 1} sum_{m in Omega(0,r)} |f(n+m)|, where N(x,r) counts lattice points in the Omega-ball Omega(x,r). When 0 <= beta < 1 and q = d/(d-beta), does every discrete function f satisfy ||∇M_{Omega,beta} f||_{ell^q(Z^d)} <= C(d,Omega,beta) ||∇f||_{ell^1(Z^d)}? More generally, does inequality (6.4) hold for all alpha <= beta and q = d/(d-beta+alpha)? The paper asks the analogous questions for the uncentered operator as well.

Let M be the one-dimensional centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. Is the derivative map f -> (M f)' continuous from W^{1,1}(R) to L^1(R)? In other words, whenever f_j converges to f in W^{1,1}(R), must the derivatives of the centered maximal functions converge in L^1(R) as well?

Let M̃ be the one-dimensional uncentered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, and let BV(R) denote the Banach space of functions f : R -> R of bounded total variation with norm ||f||_{BV(R)} = |f(-infinity)| + Var(f). Is the map M̃ : BV(R) -> BV(R) continuous?

Let M be the one-dimensional centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, and let BV(R) denote the Banach space of functions f : R -> R of bounded total variation with norm ||f||_{BV(R)} = |f(-infinity)| + Var(f). Is the map M : BV(R) -> BV(R) continuous?

For 0 < beta < 1, let M_beta be the one-dimensional centered fractional maximal operator and let q = 1/(1-beta). Is the derivative map f -> (M_beta f)' both bounded and continuous from W^{1,1}(R) to L^q(R)?

How can one build a unified mathematical framework for analyzing nature-inspired optimization algorithms so as to derive rigorous information about their convergence, rate of convergence, stability, and robustness?
context_brief: Unified analysis of convergence and stability
