For a fixed pair of vertices in a graph G, compare interlacing for resolvent centrality RC(i, alpha) = [(I - alpha A)^(-1)]_ii, defined for alpha in (0, 1/rho(A)), and for exponential subgraph centrality SC(i, beta) = [e^(beta A)]_ii. Say that two vertices interlace when the corresponding centrality values are equal for some parameter value. Is it always true that the number of interlacing values for resolvent centrality is less than or equal to the number of interlacing values for subgraph centrality for that same vertex pair?

Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective varieties over a field K, and let D1 be an admissible subcategory of Db(X1) and D2 an admissible subcategory of Db(X2). Must every exact fully faithful functor F: D1 -> D2 be of Fourier-Mukai type?

Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective varieties over a field K, and let D1 and D2 be admissible subcategories of Db(X1) and Db(X2). If F: D1 -> D2 is an exact equivalence, does there exist a Fourier-Mukai equivalence between D1 and D2?

The derived Torelli theorem for Enriques surfaces says that if X1 and X2 are smooth projective surfaces over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2, X1 is an Enriques surface, and Db(X1) is equivalent to Db(X2), then X1 is isomorphic to X2. Does this theorem remain true in characteristic 2 for some or all of the three characteristic-2 families of Enriques surfaces: classical, singular, and supersingular Enriques surfaces?

Let X be an Enriques surface and let Db(X) = <Ku(X, L), L> be the semiorthogonal decomposition defined by a collection L of exceptional line bundles. Does the Serre functor S_{Ku(X,L)} admit an explicit and computable description beyond the abstract description coming from the general theory of admissible subcategories?
context_brief: Serre functor of Enriques Kuznetsov component

question_text: Let X be an Enriques surface and let Ku(X, L) be the Kuznetsov component determined by a collection L of exceptional line bundles in a semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X) = <Ku(X, L), L>. Is Ku(X, L) indecomposable?

Let X be an Enriques surface and let Ku(X, L) be the Kuznetsov component in a semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X) = <Ku(X, L), L>. Do the Fourier-Mukai existence questions from Questions 1.7 and 1.8 have a positive answer when D_i is taken to be a Kuznetsov component Ku(X_i, L_i) of an Enriques surface?
context_brief: Fourier-Mukai questions for Enriques Kuznetsov components

question_text: If X is a cubic threefold and Ku(X) is the Kuznetsov component appearing in the standard semiorthogonal decomposition of Db(X), is Ku(X) indecomposable?
Is a cubic fourfold X rational if and only if its Kuznetsov component Ku(X) is equivalent to the bounded derived category of a K3 surface?

Let X be a Calabi-Yau threefold given as a complete intersection of one cubic hypersurface and two quadric hypersurfaces in P^6. Is it possible to prove a stronger Bogomolov inequality for slope-semistable torsion-free sheaves on X, analogous to the inequalities proved in the cited quintic and quadric-quartic cases, in a way that implies inequality (4.5)?
context_brief: Bogomolov inequality for a P^6 complete intersection

question_text: Let (X, H) be a smooth complex projective polarized variety. Does there always exist a class gamma in the numerical Chow ring of the form gamma = e^{-B} * (1, 0, Gamma, gamma_3, ..., gamma_n) together with an upper semicontinuous function f^gamma: R -> R such that every gamma-tilt-semistable object E satisfies the quadratic inequality Q_{s,q}(E) >= 0 for all (s, q) in Delta with q > f^gamma(s)?
Can the categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds, namely Theorem 5.4, be proved by using the extension techniques for Fourier-Mukai equivalences that are discussed in Section 3.1?
context_brief: Alternative proof strategy for cubic-threefold Torelli

question_text: For a prime Fano threefold of index 1 or 2, when does its Kuznetsov component admit Serre-invariant stability conditions?

Suppose D is an admissible subcategory of Db(X) that admits Serre-invariant stability conditions and has numerical Grothendieck group N(D) of rank 2. Is there a unique orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on D under the action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R)?

Let X be a cubic threefold. If sigma is any stability condition on the Kuznetsov component Ku(X), is sigma in the same orbit as the explicitly constructed stability conditions sigma(s, q, mu)? Equivalently, is every stability condition on Ku(X) Serre-invariant?
context_brief: All stability conditions on Ku(X) for a cubic threefold

question_text: Let Y1 be the prime Fano threefold of index 2 and degree 1, equivalently the degree-6 hypersurface in the weighted projective space P(1,1,1,2,3) known as the Veronese double cone. Is there a unique orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on Ku(Y1) under the action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R)?
context_brief: Serre-invariant stability on the Veronese double cone

question_text: Let Y1 be the Veronese double cone, namely the prime Fano threefold of index 2 and degree 1. Does the categorical Torelli theorem hold for Y1?
context_brief: Categorical Torelli for the Veronese double cone

question_text: Let X1 and X2 be prime Fano threefolds of index 1 and degree 10, so in particular Gushel-Mukai threefolds. If there is a Fourier-Mukai type equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2), must X1 and X2 be birational?
context_brief: Birational categorical Torelli for Gushel-Mukai threefolds

question_text: If X is a quartic threefold, are the stability conditions sigma(s, q, mu) on its Kuznetsov component Serre-invariant for some choice of (s, q)?
context_brief: Serre invariance on quartic-threefold Kuznetsov components

question_text: For quartic threefolds, is there a categorical Torelli theorem, and does a birational categorical Torelli theorem hold?
context_brief: Categorical Torelli questions for quartic threefolds

question_text: Let X1 and X2 be cubic fourfolds. If there is an equivalence Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) between their Kuznetsov components, does it follow that X1 and X2 are birational?
context_brief: Birational categorical Torelli for cubic fourfolds

question_text: Let X1 and X2 be Gushel-Mukai fourfolds, and suppose there is an equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) that commutes with the degree shift functors of X1 and X2. What additional assumptions on Phi are sufficient to conclude that X1 and X2 are isomorphic?
context_brief: Refined Torelli question for Gushel-Mukai fourfolds

question_text: If X1 and X2 are Gushel-Mukai varieties of the same dimension and their Kuznetsov components are equivalent, must X1 and X2 be birational?
context_brief: Birational categorical Torelli for Gushel-Mukai varieties

question_text: For a nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion model in which each population diffuses and moves according to a detection-kernel-smoothed combination of all population densities, determine whether time-dependent solutions exist in a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions, especially for top-hat detection kernels.
For the same nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion model, determine when spatially non-constant steady states exist under zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or periodic boundary conditions.
context_brief: nonconstant steady states for nonlocal multispecies dynamics

question_text: Characterize the qualitative properties of spatially non-constant steady states in the nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion model driven by kernel-based perception of population densities.
context_brief: qualitative structure of nonconstant steady states

question_text: Determine whether time-dependent and steady-state solutions of the nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion model remain well defined as the perceptual radius R tends to 0+, and whether the nonlocal model converges meaningfully to its local counterpart in that limit.
context_brief: local limit of nonlocal multispecies dynamics

question_text: Determine in what sense time-dependent solutions exist for the nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion model under boundary conditions other than periodic ones, with special attention to how the detection kernel should be defined near the boundary.
context_brief: boundary conditions for kernel-based multispecies dynamics

question_text: For the multispecies movement model in which populations respond to dynamic densities of landscape marks left by other populations, determine whether time-dependent solutions exist in a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions and a top-hat detection kernel, and whether those solutions remain well defined as R tends to 0+.

For the same landscape-mark model, determine whether spatially non-constant steady states exist in a bounded periodic domain with a top-hat detection kernel, and whether those steady states persist in the local limit R -> 0+.

Describe the qualitative properties of spatially non-constant steady states in the landscape-mark memory model, compare them with those of the simpler nonlocal multispecies perception model, and determine whether introducing an explicit cognitive-map variable creates genuinely new dynamics.
context_brief: dynamics added by explicit scent-mark memory

question_text: Determine in what sense solutions exist for the landscape-mark memory model under zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions in a bounded domain with a top-hat detection kernel.
context_brief: nonperiodic boundary conditions for scent-mark model

question_text: For the multispecies movement model in which populations remember conflict zones and avoid them through a dynamic cognitive map, determine whether time-dependent solutions and spatially non-constant steady states exist in a bounded periodic domain with a top-hat kernel, describe their qualitative properties, and determine whether the solutions remain well defined as R tends to 0+.
context_brief: conflict-zone memory model well-posedness and steady states

question_text: Determine in what sense time-dependent solutions exist for the conflict-zone memory model under zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions in a bounded domain with a top-hat detection kernel.

Compare the solutions of the conflict-zone memory model with magnitude-based cognitive maps against the analogous model in which the cognitive map is formulated as a probability-like quantity, and determine what substantive differences this modeling choice creates.
context_brief: compare magnitude and probability conflict memories

question_text: Determine how adding birth and death processes changes the dynamics, existence theory, and spatially non-constant steady-state profiles of the dynamic-memory movement models introduced in Section 2.2.2.

For the consumer-resource system in which consumers move according to a top-hat-kernel perception of resource density, determine whether time-dependent solutions exist in a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions.
For the conflict-zone memory model extended with a diffusive memory-smearing term, determine whether time-dependent solutions exist in a bounded periodic domain with a top-hat detection kernel.
Determine whether solutions of the memory-smearing model converge to solutions of the conflict-zone memory model as the memory-diffusion coefficient epsilon_i tends to 0+.

For the extension in which conflict memories are generated from nonlocal conflict encounters through a top-hat detection kernel, determine whether time-dependent solutions exist in a bounded periodic domain.
context_brief: periodic well-posedness with nonlocal conflict generation

question_text: For the same nonlocal conflict-generation memory model, determine whether spatially non-constant steady states exist in a bounded periodic domain and describe their qualitative properties.
context_brief: steady states with nonlocal conflict generation

question_text: Determine how adding nonlocal information gathering to conflict-memory dynamics changes space-use outcomes by comparing the qualitative properties of non-constant steady states in the nonlocal conflict-generation model against those in the local conflict-zone memory model.
context_brief: space-use effect of nonlocal conflict perception

question_text: Determine in what sense solutions exist for the nonlocal conflict-generation memory model under zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions in a bounded domain with a top-hat kernel.

For the consumer-resource extensions in which consumers follow a dynamic cognitive map of resource locations, determine whether time-dependent solutions and spatially non-constant steady states exist in a bounded periodic domain with a top-hat detection kernel, and describe the qualitative properties of those steady states.

Compare the qualitative structure of non-constant steady states among the three consumer-resource formulations that use direct resource perception, a memory variable growing with resource density, and a memory variable growing with both consumers and resources.

For the scalar diffusion-advection model whose advective potential is the population density evaluated tau time units in the past, determine how the existing analysis changes when homogeneous Neumann boundary data are replaced by periodic or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary data.
context_brief: boundary-data dependence in discrete-delay self-memory model

question_text: Determine how adding top-hat-kernel nonlocal perception to the scalar discrete-delay movement model changes the analysis and dynamical outcomes, especially in a one-dimensional periodic domain where no kernel truncation at the boundary is needed.

Determine under what conditions there exists a unique solution to the delayed diffusion-advection model whose growth term includes a spatially nonlocal population average, under homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions and, more generally, in higher dimensions or with other boundary conditions.
Determine under what conditions a unique solution exists for the time-dependent delayed diffusion-advection model with nonlocal maturation effects under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions.
context_brief: time-dependent Dirichlet problem with delayed advection and nonlocal maturation

question_text: Determine under what conditions a unique solution exists for the consumer-resource system in which consumers move according to the resource gradient from tau time units in the past, under homogeneous Neumann boundary data and in higher spatial dimensions.

Determine in what sense solutions exist for discrete-delay movement models of the forms (2.20) and (2.24) when top-hat-kernel nonlocal perception is added on top of the explicit time delay, especially under periodic boundary conditions.
context_brief: time delays combined with top-hat perception

question_text: Determine whether discrete-delay movement models with top-hat-kernel nonlocal perception converge to corresponding local delayed models as R tends to 0+, and characterize the qualitative differences between the local and nonlocal delayed systems.

Determine under what conditions a unique solution exists for the distributed-delay movement model with a general spatiotemporal kernel that includes the heat-equation Green function as a special case, under homogeneous Neumann boundary data.

Determine how a dynamic cognitive map interacts with discrete or distributed time delays, how that combination changes space-use outcomes, and whether standard bootstrapping arguments can prove existence and uniqueness for bounded-domain problems that combine nonlocal perception with such delays.
context_brief: dynamic maps combined with discrete or distributed delays

question_text: Determine what distinct roles short-term and long-term memory play in movement models, including their effects on well-posedness and steady-state structure, and whether using both memory layers can produce space-use phenomena that cannot arise with only one memory compartment.

Determine whether a movement model that includes both short-term and long-term memory can be meaningfully connected to the time-since-last-visit concept and whether it predicts movement more accurately than comparable models with only one memory compartment.
context_brief: memory compartments and time since last visit

question_text: Determine how prioritizing one information channel over another affects space-use patterns and persistence outcomes, including whether models can explain why avoiding predation may take priority over foraging and what changes when that priority is reversed.
context_brief: prioritization of information in movement decisions

question_text: Determine in what sense solutions exist for the one-dimensional learning model in which a starvation-dependent switch turns foraging attraction on and off relative to home attraction, despite the presence of irregular higher-order coefficients.

Determine how to incorporate nonlocal perception into the starvation-driven learning model and characterize the differences in solution behavior between using learning alone, perception alone, and both mechanisms together.
context_brief: learning model combined with nonlocal perception

question_text: Determine whether a starvation-driven switch between foraging and home attraction can generate nontrivial spatiotemporal dynamics or patterns, whether such switching helps or harms the species biologically, and what alternative satisfaction measures can drive similar behavioral modification.
For every previously introduced model whose existence theory is still open, determine whether necessary or sufficient conditions guarantee uniqueness of the solution once existence is obtained.

Determine under what conditions the nonlocal models from Section 2.2.2 admit solutions under homogeneous Neumann or Dirichlet boundary conditions when the perceptual kernel is explicitly truncated near the boundary, and compare those results against the periodic case.
context_brief: nonperiodic boundary theory with truncated kernels

question_text: Construct perceptual kernels that remain biologically reasonable near domain boundaries while also supporting rigorous mathematical analysis of the resulting nonlocal movement equations.

Determine what biological predictions are made by evaluating knowledge-based movement models using the net-growth measure based on reaction terms, including whether there are optimal cognition-related parameter ranges and how those predictions compare with a null model that lacks cognition-based movement.

Formulate useful eigenvalue problems for movement models that include memory and nonlocal perception together with population dynamics, and determine how the key eigenvalues depend on perceptual radius, advection speed, diffusion rates, and memory uptake or decay rates.
context_brief: eigenvalue problems for memory and nonlocal perception

question_text: Determine whether the foraging-success and foraging-efficiency measures lead to consistent predictions about optimal strategies in knowledge-based movement models, including the nonlocal perception model studied in [16].
context_brief: compare foraging success and foraging efficiency

question_text: Develop measures of foraging success that go beyond simple overlap with resource density by incorporating metabolic or other costs so that successful foraging can be evaluated as a genuine component of fitness.

Determine whether the pack-fitness framework of form (4.8) can be extended to movement models with other cognitive mechanisms, and how the resulting fitness changes with perceptual kernel choice or perceptual radius.
context_brief: fitness-function analysis for other cognitive mechanisms

question_text: For movement models that include cognitive movement mechanisms, explicit resources, and birth-death processes all at once, determine whether different proposed success measures agree about which strategies are optimal.
context_brief: comparing success measures in full cognitive-resource-demographic models

question_text: Determine which knowledge-based strategies are optimal for the two static-memory resource-tracking models that use resource-to-average-resource and resource-to-population ratios, and compare those predictions with the optimality results already known for the original nonlocal perception model.
context_brief: optimal strategies in ratio-based resource-memory models

question_text: Determine how the new modeling components introduced in the review affect the stability of constant steady states, what kinds of spatial or spatiotemporal patterns can occur, what mechanisms generate those patterns, and how those patterns connect to both simulations and biological observations.
context_brief: pattern classification across new modeling components

question_text: Determine whether travelling-wave solutions exist for the nonlocal aggregation-segregation model with detection kernels from Section 2.3, and if they do, compute or estimate how wave speed depends on kernel shape, perceptual radius, and advection or diffusion parameters.
context_brief: travelling waves in nonlocal self-memory model

question_text: Determine whether travelling-wave solutions exist for the scalar movement model whose advection depends on the population density tau time units in the past, with or without a birth-death term, and if they do, compute or estimate the dependence of wave speed on tau, advection, and diffusion.
context_brief: travelling waves in discrete-delay movement model

question_text: Determine whether travelling-wave solutions exist for the distributed-delay movement model with temporal kernels of the forms introduced in equation (2.27), and if they do, compute or estimate how wave speed depends on the delay parameter and on advection and diffusion rates.
context_brief: travelling waves in distributed-delay movement model

question_text: Determine whether travelling-wave solutions exist for the nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion system driven by detection kernels, and if they do, compute or estimate how wave speed depends on kernel choice, perceptual radius, and advection or diffusion parameters.
context_brief: travelling waves in nonlocal multispecies system

question_text: Determine whether travelling-wave solutions exist for the nonlocal system in which a single species moves using an explicit dynamic cognitive map, and if they do, compute or estimate how wave speed depends on kernel choice, perceptual radius, and other parameters, and whether the result extends to multiple interacting species.
context_brief: travelling waves with dynamic cognitive-map variable

question_text: For the bounded one-dimensional nonlocal movement problem with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and a truncated top-hat detection kernel, determine whether there is a critical domain length below which only the trivial steady state exists and above which a positive steady state appears, and determine how that threshold depends on perception and movement parameters.
context_brief: critical domain size under nonlocal perception

question_text: Develop a general numerical technique that can efficiently solve the nonlocal movement problems from Section 2.2.2 under boundary conditions that are not periodic.
context_brief: general numerical methods for nonperiodic nonlocal problems

question_text: Determine how unequal diffusion rates, advection rates, perceptual radii, and perceptual kernels change the broad pattern-formation insights already known for implicit-memory models, including whether the current qualitative trends remain valid and when they break down.
context_brief: parameter sensitivity of implicit-memory pattern results

question_text: Extend the current understanding of pattern formation and dynamics from two interacting populations to systems with three or more interacting populations, where oscillatory or more complicated behavior may arise.
What is a general classification or characterization of geodetic graphs, where a graph is geodetic when every pair of distinct vertices is connected by a unique shortest path (a unique geodesic)?

Let G be a graph homeomorphic to the Petersen graph. If each path in G made of two successive segments is a geodesic, each cycle of G containing five segments has odd length, and all cycles of G containing six segments have equal length, are these three conditions not only sufficient but also necessary for G to be geodetic?

Let G be a graph homeomorphic to a Moore graph of diameter d and degree k >= 3, with the Moore graph distinct from K_n for n >= 5. If each path of G composed of d successive segments is a geodesic, each cycle of G containing 2d + 1 segments has odd length, and all cycles of G containing 2d + 2 segments have equal length, are these three conditions not only sufficient but also necessary for G to be geodetic?

Can it be proved rigorously that the total number of geodetic graphs of diameter d >= 2 that are homeomorphic to the Petersen graph is (d + 3)C5, meaning the number of combinations of d + 3 elements taken 5 at a time?

Is it possible to devise a computer program that runs on a modern computer in real time, enumerates all natural solutions of the geodetic system of Diophantine equations associated with the Hoffman-Singleton graph, and thereby generates and determines the general number of all geodetic graphs of diameter d >= 2 that are homeomorphic to the Hoffman-Singleton graph?

Do the geodetic systems of Diophantine equations associated with K4, the Petersen graph, and the Hoffman-Singleton graph share a hidden common structure in the distribution of their variables that would make it possible to construct the corresponding system for generating every geodetic graph homeomorphic to the still-undiscovered Moore graph with k = 57, including that graph itself?
Do there exist infinitely many strongly regular geodetic graphs, or any strongly regular geodetic graphs that are not Moore graphs?

How does changing the topology of connections in a computer network influence the quality of network performance when the network is modeled by geodetic graphs, especially in terms of systemic hierarchy, diameter, vertex connectivity, reliability, cost, flexibility of topological change, and the number of graphs of a given diameter that represent the same network topology?
Can one determine a single model together with an adequate optimization technique that simultaneously accounts for many different characteristics of computer-network operation quality?

Let G be a locally-finite simple geodetic graph and let t be a natural number. If C is an embedded cycle whose diameter exceeds t and whose length is minimal among all such paths in G, must C contain a geodesic subpath of length t + 1?

Let μ be a non-negative finite Borel measure on R^3 representing an extended nuclear charge distribution, with total charge μ(R^3) ≤ 1. Consider the Dirac-Coulomb operator D0 - μ * |x|^{-1}, where D0 is the free Dirac operator and μ * |x|^{-1} is the electrostatic potential generated by μ. Denote by λ1(D0 - μ * |x|^{-1}) the lowest eigenvalue of this operator in the spectral gap (-1, 1). Is this eigenvalue always minimized, among all such charge distributions with the same total charge, when the entire charge is concentrated at one point, so that λ1(D0 - μ * |x|^{-1}) ≥ λ1(D0 - μ(R^3)/|x|) = sqrt(1 - μ(R^3)^2)?

Let M ≥ 2 point nuclei with charges θ1, ..., θM ≥ 0 and positions R1, ..., RM in R^3 satisfy Σ_{m=1}^M θm ≤ 1. Consider the multi-center Dirac-Coulomb operator D0 - Σ_{m=1}^M θm/|x - Rm|, and let λ1 denote its lowest eigenvalue in the spectral gap (-1, 1). Is this eigenvalue always at least as large as the lowest gap eigenvalue for the single-center Coulomb field carrying the same total charge, namely does λ1(D0 - Σ_{m=1}^M θm/|x - Rm|) ≥ λ1(D0 - (Σ_{m=1}^M θm)/|x|) = sqrt(1 - (Σ_{m=1}^M θm)^2) hold for every choice of M, positions, and charges with total charge at most 1?

Let μ be a non-negative Borel measure on R^3 with total charge μ(R^3) ≤ 1, and let f: R^3 → R^3 be a contraction for the Euclidean norm. Write f_*μ for the pushforward of μ under f, so f_*μ represents a version of the same charge distribution moved closer together by the contraction. If λ1(D0 - ν * |x|^{-1}) denotes the lowest eigenvalue in the spectral gap (-1, 1) of the Dirac-Coulomb operator generated by a charge distribution ν, does every Euclidean contraction fail to increase this eigenvalue, i.e. does λ1(D0 - μ * |x|^{-1}) ≥ λ1(D0 - (f_*μ) * |x|^{-1}) always hold?

For the space-homogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation in the regime gamma + 2s < 0, do global-in-time classical solutions exist? The paper identifies this very soft potential regime as unresolved even though homogeneous well posedness is understood when gamma + 2s >= 0.
context_brief: Homogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann, very soft potentials

question_text: Can one prove a short-time existence theory for the inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials and algebraically decaying initial data? The open case singled out in the paper is hard potentials gamma > 0 with initial data behaving like f_0 <= <v>^{-q}.
context_brief: Short-time existence with algebraic decay and hard potentials

question_text: For the inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation with a physically meaningful collision kernel, do global classical solutions exist for generic initial data? This is the unconditional global well posedness problem outside perturbative or near-equilibrium regimes.
context_brief: Global classical well posedness for generic inhomogeneous data

question_text: In the space-homogeneous Boltzmann or Landau equation with gamma + 2s < 0, can one obtain an a priori L-infinity bound for classical solutions? The paper presents this missing estimate as the key obstruction in the very soft potential case.
context_brief: A priori L-infinity bounds in the very soft potential case

question_text: For every classical solution f : [0, T] x R^3 -> [0, infinity) of the space-homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation with initial data f_0, is the pointwise bound f(t, v) <= sqrt(250 / (9 pi)) max_w f_0(w) valid for all (t, v) in [0, T] x R^3? If true, this would rule out finite-time blow-up through a universal L-infinity estimate.

Suppose f : (-infinity, 0] x R^3 -> [0, infinity) is a smooth classical solution of the space-homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation, satisfies 0 <= f(t, v) <= 1 everywhere, and for every time t there is a constant C_t with integral f(v) <v>^{-1} dv <= C_t. Must f be a stationary Maxwellian?

Can one prove the hydrodynamic bounds (3.1), (3.2), and (3.3) for solutions of the inhomogeneous Landau and Boltzmann equations without assuming them a priori? Establishing those unconditional regularity estimates would imply global smooth solutions for arbitrary initial data.

Can the Boltzmann equation, or the Landau equation, develop implosion-type singularities analogous to the singularities studied for compressible Euler or compressible Navier-Stokes? The paper presents this as a plausible alternative to unconditional regularity and notes that such singularities would invalidate the universal hydrodynamic bounds.

For a classical solution of the kinetic equation f_t + v · grad_x f = a_ij(t, x, v) partial_{v_i v_j} f on [0, 1] x B_1 x B_1 with uniformly elliptic coefficients lambda I <= {a_ij} <= Lambda I, does a Krylov-Safonov-type interior Holder estimate hold? In other words, must there exist alpha > 0 and C, depending only on dimension and ellipticity, such that ||f||_{C^alpha((1/2, 1) x B_{1/2} x B_{1/2})} <= C ||f||_{L^infinity([0, 1] x B_1 x B_1)}?

For a classical solution of the nonlocal kinetic equation (5.2) with bounded source term h and symmetric kernel K satisfying the two-sided fractional ellipticity bounds lambda |v' - v|^{-d-2s} <= K(t, x, v, v') <= Lambda |v' - v|^{-d-2s}, does a Krylov-Safonov-type interior Holder estimate hold? Specifically, can one prove the bound stated in Conjecture 8.2 with constants depending only on dimension, lambda, and Lambda?

Find a variational, ideally geodesic, formulation for the motion of an ideal incompressible fluid in a fixed domain with sources and sinks. The formulation should specify how boundary flux data, transported vorticity entering through source parts of the boundary, exterior forcing, and any fluid-memory effects enter the action principle for Euler-type motion.
context_brief: Euler equations with sources and sinks

question_text: Extend the geodesic and Hamiltonian Euler-Arnold framework from Lie groups to Lie groupoids in a way that also covers elasticity theory, not only multiphase and vortex-sheet fluid models.

Describe the differential geometry of the Lie groupoid of multiphase or generalized volume-preserving diffeomorphisms equipped with its source-wise right-invariant L2 metric, including sectional curvature, Ricci curvature, and conjugate points, analogously to Arnold's description for D_mu(M).

Determine whether Arnold's geodesic framework can be extended from the diffeomorphism group D(M) to the semigroup Map(M) so that it captures both smooth solutions and their continuations past shock formation for Burgers-like and compressible fluid equations.

Find a variational formulation for systems of material particles moving in R^d with d > 1 that stick on collision, for both potential and non-potential flows, and that remains flexible enough to describe shock formation and evolution in multidimensional Burgers dynamics.

Describe a mechanical or fluid model whose configuration space is D_mu(M) and whose kinetic energy defines an L2 left-invariant metric, and identify whether any physically meaningful systems realize this type of invariance.
Determine whether the incompressible Euler equations are ill-posed in the Besov spaces B^1_{infinity,q} for 1 < q < infinity.

For a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold M and a volume-preserving H^s diffeomorphism phi of M, determine whether phi lies in the image of the L2 exponential map on D_mu^s(M) and whether there exists an energy-minimizing L2 geodesic from the identity to phi.
Determine whether the L2 action functional for two-dimensional ideal hydrodynamics satisfies the Palais-Smale condition.
Determine whether D_mu^s(M) admits a closed L2 geodesic when M is a compact surface of genus at least two or a bounded planar domain with at least two holes.

Explain in what precise sense the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group D_mu(M), equipped with the right-invariant L2 metric, fails to be an infinite-dimensional locally symmetric Riemannian space, and relate that failure to the gap between sectional-curvature intuition and hydrodynamic stability.

Determine whether particle trajectories of Euler flows are analytic in time in arbitrary dimension, and how that analyticity depends on the presence and analyticity of boundaries. This includes clarifying the status of Yudovich-class trajectories, which are known to be Gevrey regular but not known to be analytic.
Prove that for any compact analytic two-dimensional Riemannian manifold with analytic boundary, the set of generalized minimal flows is nonempty and is a proper subset of the Yudovich space.
Prove that for every generalized minimal flow u(x,t), the vorticity level sets curl u(x,t)=const are real-analytic curves.
Prove that any generalized minimal flow admits a background region B0 on which the vorticity is constant, with the remaining vorticity organized into blob regions separated from that background.

Define anisotropic function spaces adapted to ideal hydrodynamics that have higher regularity along flow lines than across them, and prove existence and uniqueness theorems for Euler dynamics in those spaces in any dimension.
Determine the sharp regularity of generalized minimal flows within anisotropic function spaces tailored to flow-line geometry.

Quantify how the L2 exponential map on D_mu^s(M) fails to be Fredholm for compact Riemannian three-manifolds, for example in terms of essential spectrum or another measurement of non-compactness in the derivative of the exponential map.

Determine the order of the first conjugate point along any L2 geodesic in D_mu^s(M) starting at the identity, and decide whether the existence of conjugate points is related to Arnold's stability criterion for stationary flows.
Show that the absolute complexity C(gamma(t)) of any L2 geodesic gamma(t) in D_mu^s(M) is bounded above by an exponential function of time and initial H^s speed.
Show that a typical L2 geodesic in D_mu^s(M) has absolute complexity growing linearly in time.
Quantify the aging phenomenon of ideal fluids, preferably by constructing a Lyapunov function on fluid velocities that is nondecreasing along Euler evolution except on a slim exceptional set.

For a periodic channel flow initially close to a monotone plane-parallel profile and containing a kink in one initial vorticity level set, show that the kink persists under Euler evolution and does not smooth out over time.

Investigate the properties and relations of the entropy quantities H_epsilon, H_{epsilon,delta}, H_tilde_epsilon, and H_tilde_{epsilon,delta} introduced for compact sets and probability measures in metric or Hilbert spaces.
context_brief: Entropy notions for sets and measures

question_text: Explain why ensembles of Euler solutions can exhibit decreasing epsilon-entropy over time, despite the underlying Hamiltonian and Liouville-type structure of ideal fluid dynamics.
Prove that the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation is non-integrable under at least one reasonable notion of infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian integrability.

Justify the observed tendency of generic two-dimensional Euler flows with small numerical viscosity to approach integrable point-vortex configurations, and design a dissipation model that produces this asymptotic integrable dynamics.

Study the dynamics and bifurcations of systems with a small number of point vortices on manifolds such as half-planes, quarter-planes, hemispheres, quarter-spheres, disks, tori, cylinders, and half-cylinders.

Study the first non-integrable point-vortex systems on non-orientable surfaces, and describe the corresponding Casimirs and finite-dimensional approximations for area-preserving diffeomorphism groups of those surfaces.
Prove that the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equation admits wandering solutions.
Remove the current smoothness restrictions in KAM-based arguments and prove non-transitivity and non-mixing properties for the three-dimensional Euler equation in full generality.

For an integrable Hamiltonian system on a compact 2n-dimensional manifold, determine how complicated the dynamics can be on singular submanifolds where the n commuting first integrals lose functional independence, including whether chaotic behavior can occur on such tiny singular sets.
context_brief: Chaos on singular loci of integrable systems

question_text: Explain the paradox that generic steady three-dimensional Euler fields appear topologically regular while Beltrami fields can realize arbitrarily complicated topology, and determine the natural notion of genericity for steady fields.

Construct a hierarchy of higher helicity-type invariants for divergence-free vector fields so that when all lower invariants vanish, the first nonzero invariant gives a lower bound for the field's energy.

Find a direct reduction from the three-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation to the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation through singular solutions, and similarly relate the three-dimensional compressible Euler equation to singular solutions supported on one-dimensional submanifolds.
context_brief: Singular reductions of NLS and Euler

question_text: Describe the differential geometry of shape spaces carrying the nonlocal H^{-1/2} metrics that arise from dynamic free boundaries or vortex sheets in hydrodynamics.

Extend the symplectomorphism and Kahler-map properties of the Madelung transform to wave functions that are allowed to vanish, and explain the quantization-condition controversy in momentum-map terms for the relevant semidirect product action.
Explain the correspondence between bouncing-droplet dynamics and quantum-particle behavior by combining averaging arguments with the Madelung transform.
Find a more natural mechanism for energy dissipation in the proposed infinite mechanical cascade model that does not rely on inserting explicit friction by hand.

Determine whether a mechanism analogous to the proposed chamber-and-damper apparatus can explain cascades in real hydrodynamics, and whether one can choose the parameters n_i, m_i, and r_i so that the model functions as intended, ideally with an analogue in two-dimensional ideal fluid flow.

Let A007908(m) be the decimal string obtained by concatenating the positive integers 1, 2, 3, ..., m in order, and let A001292 be the increasing sequence formed from every cyclic permutation of those strings. Ignoring the trivial first term A001292(1) = 1, does A001292 contain any nontrivial perfect power, meaning a term equal to a^k for some positive integer a and exponent k >= 2? Equivalently, how many terms of A001292 are perfect powers if Kashihara's conjecture says that there are no nontrivial ones?

Let A352991 be the OEIS sequence obtained by listing, in increasing order, all decimal concatenations coming from distinct permutations of the first m positive integers for varying m. If a term A352991(n) is a perfect power and is greater than 1, must it always be a perfect square and never a higher-order perfect power c^k with k >= 3? Equivalently, are there no nontrivial cubes, fourth powers, or other higher perfect powers anywhere in A352991?

Let B^(H): L2(0,1) -> l2 be the Hausdorff moment operator defined by [B^(H) z]_j = integral_0^1 t^(j-1) z(t) dt for j = 1, 2, .... The inverse problem B^(H) z = y is known to be ill-posed of type I, and there exists an infinite-dimensional subspace of the data space l2 on which the inverse of B^(H) is continuous. Which infinite-dimensional subspace is it?
context_brief: Continuous inverse subspace for the Hausdorff moment operator

question_text: Let J: L2(0,1) -> L2(0,1) be the integration operator [Jx](s) = integral_0^s x(t) dt for 0 <= s <= 1, and let A := B^(H) o J: L2(0,1) -> l2. Is the inverse problem Ax = y moderately ill-posed, in the sense that there exist constants C > 0 and kappa > 0 such that C i^(-kappa) <= sigma_i(A) for all i in N, or is it instead exponentially ill-posed?
context_brief: Ill-posedness degree of the composite Hausdorff moment operator

question_text: Let A map L2(0,1) into an arbitrary Hilbert space Y, assume A is a Hilbert-Schmidt operator with non-closed range, and let k in L2([0,1] x [0,1]) be the kernel of A* A: L2(0,1) -> L2(0,1). If k has limited smoothness, meaning that k is not infinitely many times continuously differentiable on the whole closed unit square [0,1] x [0,1], under what conditions can the operator equation Ax = y nevertheless be severely ill-posed, in particular exponentially ill-posed?
context_brief: Severe ill-posedness with only limited kernel smoothness

question_text: For the composite operator A = B^(H) o J : L2(0,1) -> l2, what are the singular functions u_i(A) in L2(0,1) and v_i(A) in l2?
context_brief: Singular functions of the composite operator

question_text: Let H_n = (1/(i+j-1))_(i,j=1)^n be the n x n truncation of the infinite Hilbert matrix. For any fixed index i, does sigma_i(H_n) converge to pi as n -> infinity? If not, what is the asymptotic behavior of sigma_i(H_n) as n increases?
context_brief: Fixed-index singular values of truncated Hilbert matrices

question_text: Let H = (1/(i+j-1))_(i,j=1)^infinity be the infinite Hilbert-matrix operator on l2, and let H_n be the n x n Hilbert-matrix truncation extended to an operator on l2 by filling the remaining rows and columns with zeros. How does the operator norm ||H - H_n||_(L(l2,l2)) behave as n increases?
context_brief: Operator-norm gap between Hilbert matrix and truncations

question_text: Consider the finite triangular-grid regions called (a,b)-benzels, tiled by five trihex prototiles: a right-pointing stone, a left-pointing stone, and three bone orientations. Let T003(a,b) count tilings that allow no stones and all three bone orientations. For k >= 2, what exact formula governs T003(k(3k-1)/2, k(3k+1)/2)? More weakly, is there a recurrence or other counting method that is substantially more efficient than brute-force enumeration for these bone-only benzels?

Let T012(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T012(3n, 3n) = 2^n n! for every n >= 1?
context_brief: left stones two bones diagonal formula

question_text: Let T012(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T012(3n+1, 3n+2) = 2^n n! for every n >= 1?
context_brief: left stones two bones offset formula

question_text: Let T013(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and all three bone orientations are allowed. Whenever the Conway-Lagarias invariant of the (a,b)-benzel is negative or zero, must a type-013 tiling exist?

Let T102(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which right stones are allowed, left stones are forbidden, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that for all k >= 0 and n >= 1, except (k,n) = (0,1), one has T102(n+3k, 2n+3k-1) = product_{i=1}^k ((2i)! (2i+2n-2)!)/((i+n-1)! (i+n+k-1)!)?

Let T103(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which right stones are allowed, left stones are forbidden, and all three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T103(n, 2n-3) = (3n+3)(3n-7)!/((n-5)! (2n-1)!) for every n >= 5, with the same formula also yielding 0 for n = 3 and n = 4 if one formally interprets 1/(-1)! and 1/(-2)! as 0?

Let T103(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which right stones are allowed, left stones are forbidden, and all three bone orientations are allowed. Whenever the Conway-Lagarias invariant of the (a,b)-benzel is positive or zero, must a type-103 tiling exist?

Let T(n) = T112(3n, 3n), where T112(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that for every n >= 1 the second quotient T(n) T(n+2) / T(n+1)^2 equals 256(2n+3)^2(4n+1)(4n+3)^2(4n+5) / (27(3n+1)(3n+2)^2(3n+4)^2(3n+5))?
Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. What formula governs T112(3n+1, 3n+1) for n >= 1?

Let T(n) = T112(3n+1, 3n+2), where T112(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that for every n >= 1 the quotient T(n) T(n+3) / (T(n+1) T(n+2)) equals 65536(2n+3)(2n+5)^2(2n+7)(4n+3)(4n+5)^2(4n+7)^2(4n+9)^2(4n+11) / (729(3n+2)(3n+4)^3(3n+5)^2(3n+7)^2(3n+8)^3(3n+10))?
Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. What formula governs T112(3n-1, 3n) for n >= 1?

Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T112(n+2, 2n+1) equals the nth large Schroder number for every n >= 1?

Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T112(n+2, 2n) equals the number of royal paths in a lattice of order n for every n >= 1?

Let T113(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Whenever a+b is congruent to 1 modulo 3, is it true that T113(a,b) = 1, so that the region has exactly one tiling?
context_brief: unique all-tiles tiling when a+b=1 mod 3

question_text: Let T113(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-4), defined for n >= 5, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

Let T113(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-3), defined for n >= 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

Let T113(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum of all tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-4; 3), defined for n >= 5, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

Let T113(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum of all tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-3; 3), defined for n >= 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

For tilings of a finite simply-connected region in the hexagonal grid by stones and bones, there are two natural local 2-flip moves: one replaces two oppositely oriented stones by two bones, and the other replaces a stone-and-bone pair by a stone of the same orientation together with a bone of a different orientation. Can every such tiling be transformed into every other such tiling by a finite succession of these 2-flips?

Let T_n be the triangular region of hexagonal cells with n cells on each side. When stones alone are used as tiles, Conway, Lagarias, and Thurston showed that T_n is tileable exactly for n congruent to 0, 2, 9, or 11 modulo 12. As n tends to infinity through those congruence classes, does the number of stone tilings of T_n converge 2-adically to 0?
context_brief: 2-adic limit for stone tilings of triangular regions

question_text: Does there exist a membership-query algorithm that runs in time polynomial in the number of variables n, the target decision-tree size s, and 1/epsilon, and that properly learns any size-s decision tree over {0,1}^n to error at most epsilon under the uniform distribution? The learner should output a decision-tree hypothesis, and the problem remains open even if the learner is allowed to be only weakly proper, meaning it may return a decision tree whose size is not restricted to s.
context_brief: Polynomial-time proper learning of decision trees

question_text: Can a proper learning algorithm for size-s decision trees vary its amount of greediness across levels of the constructed tree, by searching over different numbers k of highly influential variables at different steps, in a way that preserves high accuracy while improving the runtime to polynomial time? In particular, is it enough to use k = polylog(s) near the top of the tree and then switch to constant k lower down?

Is there a way to choose the first ell levels of the learned decision tree all at once, for ell on the order of log log s, while examining only polylog(s) candidate choices at each step, so that the resulting proper learning algorithm for size-s decision trees runs in polynomial time? Equivalently, can the structural search space for these multi-level splits be reduced enough that the total number of subproblems stays polynomial in s?

If variable influence alone is not enough to identify a small set of near-optimal splitting choices when properly learning decision trees, does there exist a slightly higher-order splitting criterion that is still efficiently computable and is strong enough to recover such a small candidate set, thereby enabling a polynomial-time proper learning algorithm?

Can one design a polynomial-time proper learner for size-s decision trees under the additional assumption that the unknown target function is monotone? Ideally, can such an algorithm avoid membership queries and use only random examples while still properly learning the monotone decision-tree target?

As an intermediate step toward polynomial-time proper learning of decision trees, can one efficiently learn the target using a hypothesis class that is more expressive than decision trees but still retains their desirable interpretability properties, such as branching programs or generalized decision trees whose internal nodes branch on halfspace outcomes?

For integers k > 1 and D > 3, let chi_k(D) be the maximum chromatic number of G^k over all graphs G with maximum degree at most D, and let omega_k(D) be the corresponding maximum clique number of G^k. Is it always true that chi_k(D) = omega_k(D) for every such pair (k, D)?

For each integer t, does there exist a threshold Delta_t such that every graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) > Delta_t satisfies omega(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t? If such a threshold exists, can the same conclusion be strengthened from the clique number of G^2 to the coloring, list-coloring, painting, or Alon-Tarsi parameters of G^2, namely chi(G^2), chi_l(G^2), chi_p(G^2), or chi_AT(G^2)?
context_brief: Defect below Delta squared in graph squares

question_text: If G is a planar graph of maximum degree Delta(G), must the chromatic number of its square satisfy chi(G^2) <= floor(3 Delta(G) / 2) + 1 whenever Delta(G) > 8, together with the sharp small-degree cases stated by Wegner's planar graph conjecture?

Let G be a minor-closed class of graphs that excludes K_{3,t} for some positive integer t. Does there exist a threshold Delta_0 such that every graph G in this class with Delta(G) > Delta_0 satisfies both chi(G^2) <= chi_l(G^2) and chi_l(G^2) <= floor(3 Delta(G) / 2) + 1?

Does there exist an integer D such that every 2-degenerate graph G with Delta(G) > D satisfies chi(G^2) <= 5 Delta(G) / 2? More generally, does there exist an integer D such that every graph G with Delta(G) > D and maximum average degree mad(G) < 4 also satisfies chi(G^2) <= 5 Delta(G) / 2?

If G is a graph of maximum degree Delta, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= 5 Delta^2 / 4 when Delta is even and chi_s(G) <= (5 Delta^2 - 2 Delta + 1) / 4 when Delta is odd? Equivalently, is the Erdos-Nesetril conjecture on strong edge coloring always true?
If a bipartite graph G has bipartition (A, B), maximum degree Delta_A on side A, and maximum degree Delta_B on side B, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= Delta_A Delta_B?
context_brief: Strong edge coloring of bipartite graphs

question_text: If a graph G has maximum degree Delta and contains no cycle of length 5, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= Delta^2?
If G is a subcubic bipartite graph with no 4-cycle, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= 7?
Let G be a bridgeless subcubic graph. If G is neither the Wagner graph nor the graph obtained from K_{3,3} by subdividing one edge, must chi_s(G) <= 9 hold?

For subcubic graphs, do the following stronger strong-edge-coloring bounds hold: first, if G is bridgeless and has more than 13 vertices, then chi_s(G) <= 8; second, if G has girth at least 5, then chi_s(G) <= 7?
Does there exist a constant C such that every planar graph G of girth g > 5 and maximum degree Delta satisfies chi_s(G) <= ceil(2 g (Delta - 1) / (g - 1)) + C?
context_brief: Planar strong edge coloring with girth

question_text: Does every graph G satisfy the total-coloring bound chi''(G) <= Delta(G) + 2?
If a graph G has maximum degree Delta, must its L(2,1)-labeling number satisfy lambda_{2,1}(G) <= Delta^2?

Fix integers k > 3 and Delta > 3. For all but finitely many connected graphs G of maximum degree Delta, is the list-chromatic number of the k-th power bounded by chi_l(G^k) <= sum_{i=1}^k Delta (Delta - 1)^(i-1) + 1 - k, and does the same bound also hold for the painting number chi_p(G^k)?
context_brief: Higher graph powers list coloring and painting

question_text: Given a projective variety X with mild singularities and a maximal rationally connected (MRC) fibration phi: X -> Y defined only up to birational modification of the base, under what assumptions can one choose a birational model of Y so that the MRC fibration is represented by a holomorphic morphism rather than merely an almost holomorphic rational map?
If a compact Kahler manifold X has positive holomorphic sectional curvature, must X be projective and rationally connected?
context_brief: Yau conjecture on positive holomorphic sectional curvature

question_text: Let (X, g) be a compact Kahler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature, and assume the invariant ntf(X, g), defined using truly flat tangent vectors, equals dim X. Must h^0(X, Omega_X^q) vanish for every q > 0, and is X automatically projective?
context_brief: Projectivity from semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature

question_text: Can the structure theorem proved for smooth projective varieties with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature, including the locally trivial MRC fibration and the splitting description of the universal cover, be generalized to compact Kahler manifolds?
context_brief: Extending the semi-positive curvature structure theorem

question_text: Let (X, g) be a compact Kahler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Is the fundamental group of X an extension of a finite group by Z^(2m)? After passing to a suitable finite etale cover X* -> X and considering the Albanese map alpha: X* -> Alb(X*), does the fiber F carry a Kahler metric g_F with ntf(F, g_F) = dim F, and is F projective and rationally connected?
context_brief: Fundamental group and Albanese fibers under semi-positive curvature

question_text: Let (X, g) be a compact Kahler manifold with semi-positive or semi-negative holomorphic sectional curvature, and let V be the set of appropriate truly flat tangent vectors. Does V determine an integrable subbundle of TX? Can one find a complementary subbundle W with TX = W (+) V? In the semi-positive case, can one construct an MRC fibration f: X -> Y with W = TX/Y? In the semi-negative case, can one construct the Iitaka fibration f: X -> Z associated with K_X with V = TX/Z?
context_brief: Truly flat tangent vectors and induced fibrations

question_text: Do blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces admit positive holomorphic sectional curvature? More broadly, can one classify all varieties of a fixed dimension, for example dimension two or three, with semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature, and can one identify an algebraic-geometric analog of semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature?
context_brief: Classification and algebraic analogs of holomorphic sectional curvature

question_text: If X is a smooth projective variety with pseudo-effective tangent bundle and phi: X -> Y is its holomorphic MRC fibration, must phi be locally trivial?
context_brief: Local triviality for MRC fibrations with pseudo-effective tangent bundle

question_text: If X is a rationally connected manifold with pseudo-effective tangent bundle, is its anti-canonical divisor -K_X big?
context_brief: Positivity of -K_X under pseudo-effective tangent bundle

question_text: Let X be a compact Kahler manifold with pseudo-effective tangent bundle. After replacing X by a suitable finite etale cover and considering the Albanese map X -> Alb(X), can one prove that the fiber F has big anti-canonical divisor or is projective, and is this Albanese map an MRC fibration of X?
context_brief: Albanese fibers for compact Kahler manifolds with pseudo-effective tangent bundle

question_text: Does the blow-up of a Hirzebruch surface at four general points have pseudo-effective tangent bundle, and what can be said about blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces at special points?
context_brief: Blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces and pseudo-effective tangent bundles

question_text: Suppose phi: X -> Y is an almost holomorphic map between smooth projective varieties, pi: Gamma -> X resolves its indeterminacy, D is an effective divisor on Gamma such that (Gamma, D) is klt, and -pi_*(K_{Gamma/Y} + D) is nef. Under these relative anti-canonical assumptions, can one obtain a structure theorem, and in particular can one choose a holomorphic morphism X -> Y' that is birationally equivalent to the original map phi: X -> Y?
context_brief: Structure theorems from nef relative anti-canonical divisors

question_text: What general structure results can be proved for smooth projective varieties with pseudo-effective anti-canonical divisor?

Let (X, Delta) be a klt pair with smooth X and nef -(K_X + Delta). Does there exist an orbifold morphism rho: (X, Delta) -> (R, Delta_R) such that (R, Delta_R) is a klt pair with smooth R and c_1(K_R + Delta_R) = 0, the general orbifold fibers are slope rationally connected, and the fibration is locally trivial with respect to pairs?
context_brief: Slope rationally connected quotient structure theorem

question_text: For measure differential equations on a manifold, where the non-variational setting uses probability vector fields that have only an abelian monoid structure rather than a Lie algebra structure, can one develop a mathematically useful control theory at the level of the induced flows instead of at the level of solutions, by leveraging geometric control techniques?
context_brief: Flow-level control for measure differential equations

question_text: When a multi-agent system is represented across several limiting descriptions, including microscopic dynamics, mean-field limits, graph limits, and embedding-based representations, how do optimal control problems behave under those limiting procedures? In particular, when passing between these scales, what properties of the control problem are preserved, changed, or lost?
context_brief: Control under mean-field and graph limits

question_text: In the Kantorovich formulation of multi-agent control, where solutions are represented as measures on the space of continuous curves and related to the classical Lagrangian and Eulerian formulations, how can one characterize sparse or parsimonious controls and derive necessary and sufficient optimality conditions within that framework?
context_brief: Kantorovich formulation and parsimonious optimal control

question_text: Which finite distributive lattices occur as congruence lattices of SPS lattices, where an SPS lattice is a finite slim planar semimodular lattice and 'slim' means that the lattice has no M3 sublattice? Equivalently, determine necessary and sufficient conditions for a finite distributive lattice D to be representable as Con L for some finite slim planar semimodular lattice L.
context_brief: Characterization of congruence lattices of SPS lattices

question_text: Let D be a finite distributive lattice that is the glued sum D^h u B2 of a finite distributive lattice D^h with B2, and let L be a patch lattice, meaning a rectangular lattice whose corners are dual atoms; equivalently, patch lattices are exactly those rectangular lattices L for which Con L is a glued sum of a finite distributive lattice Con^h L with B2. Which properties of the finite distributive lattice Con^h L characterize exactly when D is the congruence lattice of a patch lattice L?
context_brief: Characterization problem for congruence lattices of patch lattices

question_text: In fixed-budget best arm identification, a bandit instance mu belongs to the class S of instances with a unique best arm, the learner uses exactly n samples, and then outputs an estimate I_hat_n of the best arm; the resulting error probability is p_{mu,n} = P_mu(I_hat_n != I*(mu)), where I*(mu) is the unique arm with the largest mean. Is there a natural algorithm class A and a well-defined instance-dependent function Gamma*_fb: S -> R such that every algorithm in A satisfies lim inf_{n->infinity} n / log(1/p_{mu,n}) >= Gamma*_fb(mu), while some algorithm in A also satisfies the matching upper bound lim sup_{n->infinity} n / log(1/p_{mu,n}) <= Gamma*_fb(mu), so that Gamma*_fb exactly characterizes the asymptotic complexity of the fixed-budget setting?

In the same fixed-budget best arm identification setting, does there exist an algorithm, other than uniform sampling itself, that performs uniformly no worse than uniform sampling for every bandit instance mu in S? The comparison is the asymptotic fixed-budget error exponent discussed in the paper, namely whether the algorithm can achieve a lower or equal value of lim sup_{n->infinity} n / log(1/p_{mu,n}) than the uniform-sampling benchmark for every instance.

For two-armed Bernoulli bandits in the fixed-budget setting, Kaufmann et al. (2016) show that an optimal sampling vector exists, but that vector depends on the unknown means of the two arms and therefore is not available a priori. Is there an algorithm that can still achieve asymptotic optimality in this setting without requiring prior knowledge of those unknown arm means?

Let CTCS(n) be the critical beta-splitting continuous-time random tree on n leaves, and let D_n^(1) and D_n^(2) denote the heights of two leaves whose positions in the interval-splitting representation are r_n apart on the underlying cyclic order. Define the correlation coefficient by rho(n, r_n) = (E[D_n^(1) D_n^(2)] - E[D_n]^2) / Var(D_n), where D_n is the height of a uniform random leaf. If log r_n / log n converges to a limit alpha in [0, 1], prove that rho(n, r_n) converges to 1 - alpha.

In the original interval-splitting version of the critical beta-splitting model, where leaves keep their deterministic left-to-right labels instead of being randomly relabeled, analyze the distribution of the height of a designated leaf i(n) in both the discrete-time tree DTCS(n) and the continuous-time tree CTCS(n).

Let D*_n be the height of the random tree CTCS(n), meaning the maximum leaf height in the continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree on n leaves. Show that D*_n / log n converges in probability to a constant c, and determine the value of c.

Let L*_n be the height of the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n), meaning the maximum number of edges from the root to a leaf. Show that L*_n / log^2 n converges in probability to a constant c, and determine the value of c.

For a fixed finite clade shape chi, let N_n(chi) be the number of copies of chi that appear as fringe clades in DTCS(n). Prove that n^(-1) Var(N_n(chi)) converges to a limit sigma^2(chi), and prove the corresponding central limit theorem for N_n(chi).

Let Lambda_n be the total branch length of the continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree CTCS(n), where each edge length is its time duration. Prove that n^(-1) Var(Lambda_n) converges to 6/pi^2, and prove the corresponding central limit theorem for Lambda_n.

For the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n), study combinatorial properties of fringe clades, including the number K_n of distinct clade shapes that appear in a realization, the largest clade shape that appears more than once, and the smallest clade shape that does not appear at all.

Let a(n, m) be the occupation probability that the harmonic descent chain started from n ever visits state m, and let a(m) = lim_{n->infinity} a(n, m). Find explicit bounds for |a(n, m) - a(m)|. In particular, prove the following ansatz for every nonnegative sequence f(j) with polynomial growth: if sum_{i>=2} a(i) f(i) converges, then sum_{i=2}^n a(n, i) f(i) converges to sum_{i>=2} a(i) f(i); if sum_{i>=2} a(i) f(i) diverges, then sum_{i=2}^n a(n, i) f(i) is asymptotic to sum_{i=2}^n a(i) f(i).

Let N_m^(n) be the number of clades of size m in DTCS(n). Study the joint distribution of the vector (N_m^(n), 2 <= m <= n) in enough detail to compute covariances and derive central limit theorems for statistics built from these clade counts.

Study the distributions, variances, and limit laws of the balance indices discussed for DTCS(n), including the Colless index, quadratic Colless index, B1 index, B2 index, s-hat shape index, total cophenetic index, variance of leaf heights, rooted quartet index, and related indices, rather than only their first-order expectations.

Repeat the empirical data studies comparing the critical beta-splitting model with real phylogenetic trees on a substantially larger dataset, and extend those comparisons to additional tree-shape indices beyond the small-scale studies reported in the paper.

Let Phi be a functional on the fringe tree. Suppose a central limit theorem is known for the stationary fringe process sum_{i=0}^{m-1} Phi(T_i), where T_i is the re-rooted local weak limit tree at leaf i. Does the analogous central limit theorem necessarily hold for the finite-tree statistic sum_{i=1}^n Phi(T_i^(n)) on DTCS(n)?

For the explicit inductive growth algorithm that builds CTCS(n+1) from CTCS(n) by choosing a random bud and either adding a side-bud or extending to a bud-pair, determine whether there exists a useful martingale that can be exploited to analyze the model.

Let Lbar_n be the drawn length of the cladogram representation of DTCS(n), meaning the total vertical length in the standard cladogram drawing convention. Prove the correct asymptotic growth rate of Lbar_n, in particular the conjectured rough order n log^4 n.

For the standard cladogram drawing of DTCS(n), study the drawn width profile process W(h), h >= 0, where W(h) counts the number of vertical line segments that cross the strip (h, h+1), equivalently the number of clades with drawing height at most h that arise from splits of clades with drawing height at least h+1.

For DTCS(n), let SS_n^(alpha) be the sum over all clades of the alpha-th power of the clade size. Develop a detailed analysis of SS_n^(alpha) as a function of alpha, including asymptotics and phase changes across the ranges of alpha discussed in the paper.

Study the scaling limit of the branchpoint structure in the fringe process associated with the critical beta-splitting model, viewed after rescaling as a point process describing branchpoint locations near a typical leaf.

Determine whether there exist discrete random-tree models that look superficially different from the critical beta-splitting model but have the same continuum limit CTCS(infinity), in the sense of converging to the same exchangeable-partition-based infinite random tree object.

Clarify the precise mathematical relationship between the infinite critical beta-splitting tree CTCS(infinity) and the beta(2,1) coalescent, including which structural correspondences are exact, which hold only asymptotically, and how the shared subordinator description should be interpreted.

In the inductive growth description of CTCS(n), let p_up be the limiting probability of branch extension and let p_diag be the limiting probability of side-bud extension. Because the analysis suggests p_up = p_diag, determine whether this identity is a consequence of an underlying symmetry of the random tree shape.

Given a weighted simple graph G = (V, E, omega) with geodesic distance d_G and a fixed epsilon > 0, what are the optimal upper and lower bounds on the cardinality of an epsilon-net L subseteq V for the metric space (V, d_G)? Here an epsilon-net means a landmark set that is both epsilon-sparse and an epsilon-sample of the graph.

Given a weighted simple graph G = (V, E, omega), design an algorithm that constructs an epsilon-net for G using fewer landmarks than the currently available methods while also running faster than those existing algorithms.

Let G = (V, E, omega) be a weighted simple graph, let W = V be the witness set, and let L subseteq V be an epsilon-net used to build the filtered Dowker complex Dow_alpha(W, L). Determine how to choose epsilon and how to select the epsilon-net L so that, for sufficiently large alpha, the one-dimensional persistence diagram PD_1(Dow_alpha(W, L)) has as many points as the genus of G. Assuming such an epsilon-net is given, bound the bottleneck distance between PD_1(VR_alpha(G)) and PD_1(Dow_alpha(W, L)) in terms of the cycle lengths of G and epsilon.

Let G = (V, E, omega) be a weighted graph with landmark and witness sets L, W subseteq V, and let Dow_alpha(W, L) denote the associated Dowker complex filtration. If G' = (V, E, omega') has the same vertices and edges but a different weight function, how can one bound the bottleneck distance between the persistence diagrams of the Dowker complexes of G and G' in terms of the supremum distance between omega and omega'? Also, if L and L' are both epsilon-nets for G, what conditions on these landmark sets guarantee that Dow_alpha(W, L) and Dow_alpha(W, L') have the same homotopy type?

Fix integers m and k with k <= m. Let A be an n x m binary matrix whose columns are distinct nonzero vectors a_1, ..., a_m in {0,1}^n, let x and y be independent uniformly random n x t binary matrices, and for each i define m_i^A(x) = sum_j <a_i, x_j>_2, the number of columns x_j whose parity on the subset encoded by a_i is odd. When A consists of all binary vectors of Hamming weight at most k, can one compute exactly the probability that m_i^A(x) = m_i^A(y) for every i?

For the same Computational Problem in which one must evaluate the probability that m_i^A(x) = m_i^A(y) for all i, which families of binary-column sets A admit an exact solution, and which families of A admit an efficient algorithm for computing that probability?

When the input consists of an arbitrary binary matrix A with distinct nonzero columns, is the Computational Problem of determining the probability that m_i^A(x) = m_i^A(y) for all i an NP-complete problem?

For which families of binary-column sets A can one efficiently approximate, rather than exactly compute, the probability in the Computational Problem that two independent random binary matrices x and y satisfy m_i^A(x) = m_i^A(y) for every i?

Consider the cardinality-based 4-uniform hypergraph s-t cut problem in which every 1-vs-3 hyperedge split has penalty w_1 = 1 and every 2-vs-2 split has penalty w_2. What is the computational complexity of this problem in the regime w_2 > 2?

In a 4-uniform hypergraph with distinguished nodes s and t, suppose one must separate s from t while minimizing the number of 1-vs-3 hyperedge splits and forbidding every 2-vs-2 split; equivalently, consider the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem obtained as the limit w_2 -> infinity with w_1 = 1. What is the computational complexity of this problem?

Given a directed acyclic graph G and an integer k >= 0, does there exist a complete sequence of front- and back-edge eliminations that transforms G into the required bipartite directed acyclic graph while incurring total elimination cost at most k?

Given a directed acyclic graph G and an integer k >= 0, does there exist a complete sequence of vertex eliminations, where eliminating a vertex j adds all edges from each predecessor of j to each successor of j and costs |P_j| times |S_j|, whose total cost is at most k?
Given a directed acyclic graph G together with integers M >= n and O >= 0, can the graph be reversed using persistent memory at most M and computational cost at most O?

Let M be a real n x n matrix with spectral radius lambda = rho(M) < 1, partitioned into an l x l block array, and let delta be a delay matrix with zero diagonal and entries in {0,1,...,k}. If M(delta) is the asynchronous-update operator induced by those communication delays, is it always true that rho(M(delta)) <= lambda^(1/(k+1))? If not, does there exist some universal bound f(lambda, k) in (0,1) such that rho(M(delta)) <= f(lambda, k)?

For graphs that are close to trees, such as graphs with few cycles or sparse graphs of large diameter, is there a structural characterization of the minimum-cardinality (n-k)-contingent zero-forcing sets, meaning vertex sets that remain zero-forcing after any deletion of at most k edges?
For graphs with few cycles or for sparse graphs with large diameter, is there an efficient algorithm for computing a minimum-cardinality (n-k)-contingent zero-forcing set?

Among graphs that exhibit structural properties typical of power grids, what is the typical order of magnitude of the smallest (n-k)-contingent zero-forcing set as a function of the numbers of vertices and edges?

Let V_{d1,...,dk} be the Segre-Veronese variety of partially symmetric rank-one tensors in P(S^{d1}V1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S^{dk}Vk). For each r, the r-th secant variety σ_r(V_{d1,...,dk}) has expected dimension min{r dim(V_{d1,...,dk}) + r - 1, ambient dimension}. Which Segre-Veronese varieties are r-defective (that is, have secant variety of smaller than expected dimension), and what are the actual dimensions of their secant varieties?

For products of projective spaces (and, more generally, other interesting classes of varieties), classify special line bundles in the sense that there exists r ≥ 1 for which r generic double points fail to impose independent conditions on the line bundle.

Given a variety X, a line bundle L on X, and an integer r, determine whether there exists a 0-dimensional subscheme X ⊆ X that is a disjoint union of degree-2 schemes such that the reduced subscheme X_red imposes independent conditions on L while X itself does not.
For a homogeneous polynomial f ∈ S^dV, let X be a minimal apolar scheme for f (that is, deg(X)=cR_X(f) in the apolar setting). Must the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity satisfy reg(X) ≤ d?
Determine the maximal possible Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity reg(X) of an irredundant scheme X that is apolar to a form f ∈ S^dV.

For f ∈ S^dV, let X be the scheme associated to a generalized additive decomposition (GAD) of minimal length. Is reg(X) ≤ d? More generally, which conditions on f guarantee existence of a GAD whose associated scheme has low regularity?
Develop general lower bounds for the degree of higher secant varieties, analogous in spirit to the lower-bound framework used for second secant varieties.

Classify low-dimensional varieties whose second and/or third secant variety has minimal degree; more generally, for a fixed r, construct varieties X such that σ_r(X) is a hypersurface of the smallest possible degree.

Fix n and d, and let D_{n,d} be the generic number of eigenscheme points for degree-d forms in n+1 variables. Let E_{n,d} denote the Zariski-closed locus in the symmetrized product (PV)^(·D_{n,d}) (equivalently in Hilb_{D_{n,d}}(PV)) consisting of eigenconfigurations that occur as eigenschemes X_f of some f ∈ S^dV. Determine defining equations (in the broad Zariski-closed-condition sense) for E_{n,d}.
When a non-reduced scheme X occurs as the eigenscheme of a tensor, what degrees can the irreducible components of X have, and which schemes can appear as such irreducible components?

For non-symmetric tensors in V⊗d, each choice of contracted d-1 factors defines an eigenscheme, and the eigencompatibility variety EC_{n,d} records d-tuples of schemes that can simultaneously occur from one tensor. Determine the dimension and defining equations of EC_{n,d}.
Given real vector spaces V1,...,Vd with dim(Vi)=ni+1, does there exist a tensor T ∈ V1⊗···⊗Vd such that all c(n) critical points (equivalently singular tuples in the cited setup) are real?
For probability tensors, determine which counts of real critical points can occur among the aEDdeg(S_{n1,...,nd}) critical points.
Compute EDdeg(σ_2(v_d(P^1))), i.e., the Euclidean distance degree of the secant variety of the rational normal curve in P^d.
context_brief: ED degree of secant rational normal curve
