Zavorotnyi proved that the fourth moment I2(T) of the Riemann zeta function has the asymptotic I2(T) = T P4(log T) + O(T^(2/3 + epsilon)), where P4 is a specific polynomial of degree 4. Improve the exponent in this error term.

Suppose Ik(T) = T P_{k^2}(log T) + O(T^(1/2 + epsilon)) conjecturally, where P_{k^2} is a polynomial of degree k^2, and define the error term by Ek(T) = Ik(T) - T P_{k^2}(log T). Determine the optimal exponents theta_k for which Ek(T) = O(T^(theta_k + epsilon)) should hold for each integer k, especially for k >= 3, and decide whether the Multiple Dirichlet Series method can justify the correct conjectural values.

For the shifted moment Mk(T, alpha) = integral from 0 to T of the product over i of |zeta(1/2 + t + alpha_i)|^(2k_i) dt, Chandee proved an upper bound of the shape Mk(T, alpha) <<_{k,epsilon} T (log T)^(k_1^2 + ... + k_m^2 + epsilon) times the product over i < j of min{1/|alpha_i - alpha_j|, log T}^{2 k_i k_j}, under the stated hypotheses on the shifts alpha_i(T). Use Harper’s method to remove the epsilon from this bound.

Soundararajan proved the lower bound I3(T) >= (20.26 a3 / 9!) (1 + o(1)) T (log T)^9 for sufficiently large T. Improve the constant 20.26, ideally all the way to the conjecturally best value 42, and likewise improve the corresponding lower-bound constants for Ik(T) when k > 3.
context_brief: Lower bounds for cubic and higher moments

question_text: Assuming the ternary additive divisor conjecture, prove an omega theorem for the sixth moment I3(T) of the Riemann zeta function by showing that there exists Theta > 0 such that I3(T) = T P9(log T) + Omega(T^Theta), where P9 is a polynomial of degree 9.

Assume the Riemann Hypothesis and a smoothed quaternary additive divisor conjecture. Starting from the conjectured asymptotic I4(T) ~ C4 T (log T)^16 for the eighth moment of the Riemann zeta function, derive the full main term up to an error of size o(T) or a power saving, obtain a shifted analogue, and asymptotically evaluate the smoothed shifted integral of product_{j=1}^4 zeta(1/2 + a_j + it) zeta(1/2 + b_j - it) when |a_j| and |b_j| are << 1/log T and omega is supported in [c1 T, c2 T].
context_brief: Full main term for the eighth moment

question_text: The CFKRS recipe gives a conjectural full asymptotic formula for Ik(T). Make this recipe rigorous for the fourth moment, by proving the asymptotic formula for I2(T) with a power-saving error term using the recipe method itself.

Can the conjectural lower-order terms for Ik(T), attributed to CFKRS and to Diaconu-Goldfeld-Hoffstein, be recovered by refining the splitting conjecture in the Gonek-Hughes-Keating hybrid Euler-Hadamard product?

Let f run over holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of weight k_f <= T. Prove asymptotic formulas, with the best possible error terms, for the third and fourth moments of the central values L(1/2, f), normalized by L(1, ad f), in particular aiming for sums of the shape T^2 P3(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(1+epsilon)) for the cubic moment and T^2 P6(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(4/3+epsilon)) for the quartic moment.

Heath-Brown proved a Weyl-strength twelfth-moment bound for the Riemann zeta function, Jutila proved an analogous sixth-moment result in the t-aspect for L(1/2 + it, f) with f a Hecke-Maass cusp form, and complementary twelfth-moment results are known for Dirichlet L-functions in the level aspect. Prove the analogous Weyl-strength bound for the sixth moment of L(1/2, f tensor chi).
context_brief: Sixth moment of twists of Maass forms

question_text: Jutila proved a Weyl-strength twelfth-moment bound for Hecke-Maass cusp forms of level 1 with spectral parameter at most T. Prove a level-aspect analogue in which one sums over Hecke-Maass cusp forms of level q and bounded spectral parameter.

For a Hecke-Maass cusp form f of level 1 and fixed spectral parameter t_f, Good proved that the second moment in t has the form integral from 0 to T of |L(1/2 + it, f)|^2 dt = T P1(log T) + O_{t_f,epsilon}(T^(2/3 + epsilon)). Make the dependence on t_f in the error term explicit, determine whether the error can be made independent of t_f when T >= t_f^(3/2 + delta) for some delta > 0, and obtain the analogous statement for holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of weight k_f.
context_brief: Uniformity in spectral or weight aspect

question_text: Use the work of Humphries and Khan to compute weight-aspect upper bounds for the sixth moment of L(1/2, f tensor g) when f and g vary over primitive forms of level 1 and weights k and ell, under the conditions |k - ell| = O(1) and K < k + ell <= 2K.
context_brief: Weight-aspect sixth moment for Rankin-Selberg L-values

question_text: Let chi_{8d} denote the quadratic character attached to the fundamental discriminant 8d, with d ranging over odd squarefree integers 0 < d < X. Young proved a first-moment asymptotic of the form sum L(1/2, chi_{8d}) = X P(log X) + O(X^(1/2 + epsilon)). Improve this by reducing the exponent 1/2, ideally toward a secondary term of size c X^(1/4) plus a smaller error.
context_brief: First moment of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions

question_text: Let chi_{8d} denote the quadratic character attached to the fundamental discriminant 8d, with d ranging over odd squarefree integers 0 < d < X. Determine a polynomial P of degree 10 such that sum L(1/2, chi_{8d})^4 = X P(log X) + o(X), decide whether the error term can be improved to a power saving, and determine whether the Multiple Dirichlet Series method can recover at least the initial coefficients of P.
context_brief: Fourth moment of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions

question_text: Fix a prime p > 2 and a power q of p. Let L(u, f, psi) be the Artin-Schreier L-function attached to a rational function f in F_q(x) and an additive character psi. For the families AS_d^ord = {f = h/g : h, g in F_q[x], (g,h)=1, g squarefree, deg f = max(deg h, deg g) = d, deg g in {d, d-1}}, AS_d^0 = {f in F_q[x] : deg f = d, (d,p)=1}, and AS_d^{0,odd} = {f in F_q[x] : deg f = d, f(x) = -f(-x), (d,2p)=1}, with q fixed and d -> infinity and with M_k denoting the k-th moment of L(q^(1/2), f, psi), compute the listed low moments and extend the 1-level density of zeros beyond the currently stated support ranges: for AS_d^ord, compute M1 through M6 and prove 1-level density for support of phi-hat inside (-1-delta, 1+delta) or (-2-delta, 2+delta); for AS_d^0, compute M1 through M4 and prove 1-level density for support inside (-(2-2/p)-delta, 2-2/p+delta); for AS_d^{0,odd}, compute M1 and M2 and prove 1-level density for support inside (-(1-1/p)-delta, 1-1/p+delta).

Investigate how zero-density estimates depend on available moment bounds for the Riemann zeta function. In particular, Ingham’s method uses the fourth moment integral over [T, 2T] of |zeta(1/2 + it)|^4 dt; determine whether other nontrivial moments, such as Heath-Brown’s twelfth-moment estimate, can be used in zero-density arguments, and whether analogous arguments can be generalized to other L-functions.
Chandee and Soundararajan proved, under the Riemann Hypothesis, that |zeta(1/2 + it)| is bounded by exp((C0 + o(1)) log t / log log t) with C0 = (log 2)/2. Reduce the constant C0 in this bound.

Let S(t) = (1/pi) arg zeta(1/2 + it). Carneiro, Chandee, and Milinovich proved, under the Riemann Hypothesis, that |S(t)| <= (C0 + o(1)) log t / log log t with C0 = 1/4. Reduce the constant C0 in this estimate.

Let f be a Hecke-Maass cusp form of level 1 with spectral parameter t_f. Prove the Weyl-strength subconvex estimate L(1/2 + it, f) <<_epsilon ((1 + |t_f - t|)(1 + |t_f + t|))^(1/6 + epsilon) uniformly, including the conductor-dropping regimes where t_f - t or t_f + t is small relative to max{t_f, |t|}.

For k >= 3, let D_{k,2}(x, h) = sum_{n<=x} d_k(n) d_2(n+h), and let M_{k,2}(x, h) denote the main term in the known asymptotic formula. Prove an omega theorem for the error D_{k,2}(x, h) - M_{k,2}(x, h).
context_brief: Omega theorem for shifted divisor sums

question_text: Topacogullari proved that for 1 <= h << x^(2/3), D_{3,2}(x, h) = x P3(log x) + O(x^(8/9 + epsilon)), where P3 is a degree-3 polynomial whose coefficients depend on h, and analogous results are known for D_{2,3}(x, h). Improve both the admissible range of h and the size of the error term, derive exact simple formulas for the coefficients of P3, and determine numerically whether |D_{3,2}(x, h) - x P3(log x)| has size about sqrt(x).

Asymptotically evaluate each of the following additive-divisor correlations: sum_{n<=x} d3(n) d3(n+1); sum_{n<=x} d(n) d(n+1) d(n+2); for every kappa in (0,1), sum_{n<=x} d_kappa(n) d(n+1) d(n+2); and for every kappa in (2,3), sum_{n<=x} d_kappa(n) d3(n+1).

For distinct positive integers h1, ..., hr with r >= 3 and integers k1, ..., kr >= 1, find a conjectural asymptotic formula for sum_{n<=x} d_{k1}(n+h1) d_{k2}(n+h2) ... d_{kr}(n+hr), analogous to the Hardy-Littlewood style conjectural asymptotic for sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n+h1) ... Lambda(n+hr).

Fix an integer k >= 3 and a small epsilon_0 >= 0. Asymptotically evaluate the mean value integral from 0 to T of (sum_{m <= T^(2+epsilon_0)} d_k(m) / m^(1/2+it)) (sum_{n <= T^(2+epsilon_0)} d(n) / n^(1/2-it)) dt.

Let g be a primitive cusp form of weight k for Gamma_0(N), normalized so that its first Fourier coefficient is 1 and written as g(z) = sum_{n>=0} lambda_g(n) n^((k-1)/2) e(nz). Let F(x,y) be a smooth weight function supported on (X/4, 4X] x [Y/4, 4Y], satisfying the derivative bounds stated in the paper, and define the shifted convolution sum D_g(ell_1, ell_2; h) = sum_{ell_1 m +/- ell_2 n = h} lambda_g(n) lambda_g(m) F(ell_1 m, ell_2 n) for coprime ell_1 and ell_2. Determine how the explicit constant in the known asymptotic upper bounds depends on k and N, and in the full modular-group case prove a weight-uniform asymptotic upper bound useful for Rankin-Selberg moment problems with large weights.
context_brief: Shifted convolution sums for cusp forms

question_text: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup, let R_Gamma = k[[Gamma]] be its local semigroup ring, and let G_Gamma = gr(R_Gamma) be its associated graded ring. Is there a way to compute the Betti numbers b_i(G_Gamma) or the graded Betti numbers b_{i,j}(G_Gamma) by taking homology of simplicial complexes naturally attached to Gamma?
context_brief: simplicial models for tangent-cone Betti numbers

question_text: For integers e and m with 3 <= e < m, let R(e,m) be the supremum of rho(Gamma) over all numerical semigroups Gamma with embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = e + 1 and multiplicity mult(Gamma) = m, where rho(Gamma) is the number of relations, meaning the cardinality of a minimal presentation of Gamma. Determine the value of R(e,m).
context_brief: maximal number of relations at fixed edim and multiplicity

question_text: For integers m > 3, let R(3,m) denote the supremum of rho(Gamma) over numerical semigroups Gamma with edim(Gamma) = 4 and mult(Gamma) = m. Is it true that R(3,m) = floor(2 + 2*sqrt(m))?

For integers e and m with 3 <= e < m, define the combinatorial upper bound C(e,m) as follows: choose the integer r such that binom(e+r-1, r-1) <= m < binom(e+r, r), set s = m - binom(e+r-1, r-1), and define C(e,m) = binom(e+r-1, r) + s^{<r>} - s, where s^{<r>} is the Macaulay-shift quantity coming from the unique binomial expansion of s used on the page. Determine exactly which pairs (e,m) satisfy R(e,m) = C(e,m), where R(e,m) is the supremum of rho(Gamma) for numerical semigroups Gamma with edim(Gamma) = e + 1 and mult(Gamma) = m.
context_brief: when the Elias-Robbiano-Valla bound is sharp

question_text: For integers e and m with 3 <= e < m, let T(e,m) be the supremum of t(Gamma) over all numerical semigroups Gamma with embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = e + 1 and multiplicity mult(Gamma) = m, where t(Gamma) is the type of Gamma, namely the number of pseudo-Frobenius numbers of Gamma. Determine T(e,m).
context_brief: maximal type at fixed edim and multiplicity

question_text: For a numerical semigroup Gamma = <g1 < g2 < ... < ge>, define its width by width(Gamma) = ge - g1. For each positive integer w, let W(w) be the supremum of rho(Gamma) over all numerical semigroups Gamma with width(Gamma) = w, where rho(Gamma) is the number of relations in a minimal presentation of Gamma. Determine W(w).
context_brief: maximal number of relations at fixed width

question_text: Let Gamma = <g1 < g2 < ... < ge> be a numerical semigroup, and let its interval completion be the numerical semigroup Gamma_tilde = <g1, g1 + 1, g1 + 2, ..., ge>. Let R_Gamma = k[[Gamma]] and G_Gamma = gr(R_Gamma), and similarly define G_{Gamma_tilde}. Is the first Betti number of the associated graded ring always monotone under interval completion, that is, does b_1(G_Gamma) <= b_1(G_{Gamma_tilde}) always hold?
context_brief: first tangent-cone Betti number under interval completion

question_text: If Gamma is a numerical semigroup and width(Gamma) is the difference between its largest and smallest minimal generators, is the first Betti number of the associated graded ring G_Gamma always bounded above by binom(width(Gamma)+1, 2)?
context_brief: quadratic width bound for first tangent-cone Betti number

question_text: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup, and let Gamma_tilde be its interval completion generated by all integers from the smallest minimal generator g1 through the largest minimal generator ge. Is the number of relations of Gamma always at most the number of relations of Gamma_tilde, that is, does rho(Gamma) <= rho(Gamma_tilde) always hold?
context_brief: number of relations under interval completion

question_text: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup. Is the number of relations rho(Gamma) in a minimal presentation of Gamma always bounded above by binom(width(Gamma)+1, 2), where width(Gamma) is the difference between the largest and smallest minimal generators of Gamma?
context_brief: quadratic width bound for number of relations

question_text: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup, let Gamma_tilde be its interval completion, and let R_Gamma = k[[Gamma]] and R_{Gamma_tilde} = k[[Gamma_tilde}] be the corresponding local semigroup rings. Is it true for every homological degree i that the Betti numbers of the local semigroup ring do not decrease under interval completion, i.e. b_i(R_Gamma) <= b_i(R_{Gamma_tilde}) for all i?
context_brief: all local-ring Betti numbers under interval completion

question_text: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup. For each homological degree i > 1, is the i-th Betti number of the local semigroup ring R_Gamma always bounded above by binom(width(Gamma)+1, i+1)?
context_brief: binomial width bound for higher local Betti numbers

question_text: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup, let Gamma_tilde be its interval completion, and let G_Gamma = gr(k[[Gamma]]) and G_{Gamma_tilde} = gr(k[[Gamma_tilde]]) be the associated graded rings. Is it true for every homological degree i that b_i(G_Gamma) <= b_i(G_{Gamma_tilde})?
context_brief: all tangent-cone Betti numbers under interval completion

question_text: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup. For every homological degree i, is the i-th Betti number of the associated graded ring G_Gamma always bounded above by binom(width(Gamma)+1, i+1)?
context_brief: binomial width bound for tangent-cone Betti numbers

question_text: For each positive integer e, let S(e) be the supremum of rho(Gamma) over all symmetric numerical semigroups Gamma with embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = e, where a numerical semigroup is symmetric when for every integer x not in Gamma one has Frob(Gamma) - x in Gamma. Determine S(e).
context_brief: maximal number of relations in symmetric semigroups

question_text: For each positive integer e, let S(e) be the supremum of rho(Gamma) over symmetric numerical semigroups Gamma with embedding dimension e. Is S(e) finite for every e?
context_brief: Bresinsky boundedness problem for symmetric semigroups

question_text: For each positive integer e, let A(e) be the supremum of the type t(Gamma) over all almost symmetric numerical semigroups Gamma with embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = e. Here Gamma is almost symmetric if for every integer x not in Gamma, either Frob(Gamma) - x lies in Gamma or both x and Frob(Gamma) - x are pseudo-Frobenius numbers of Gamma. Determine A(e).
context_brief: maximal type in almost symmetric semigroups

question_text: For each positive integer e, let A(e) be the supremum of the type t(Gamma) over almost symmetric numerical semigroups Gamma with embedding dimension e. Is A(e) finite for every e?
context_brief: boundedness of type in almost symmetric semigroups

question_text: Let Gamma be a nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroup with embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = 5. Is it always true that the type t(Gamma) is at most 5, and is equality possible only when Gamma is almost symmetric?
context_brief: type bound for 5-generated nearly Gorenstein semigroups

question_text: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup with canonical reduction and embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = 4. Is its type always bounded by 4, that is, must t(Gamma) <= 4 hold?
context_brief: type bound under canonical reduction in edim four

question_text: If Gamma is an almost symmetric or nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroup, are there upper bounds for the Betti numbers b_i(R_Gamma) of its local semigroup ring R_Gamma that depend only on the embedding dimension edim(Gamma)?
context_brief: Betti-number bounds in almost or nearly Gorenstein families

question_text: Let Gamma be a nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroup that is not almost symmetric, and assume edim(Gamma) = 4. Is it true that the number of relations rho(Gamma) can only be 5 or 6?
context_brief: relation counts for non-almost-symmetric nearly Gorenstein semigroups

question_text: Fix an embedding dimension e and let F be a family of numerical semigroups with that fixed embedding dimension. For each i = 1, ..., e - 1 define B_i(F) = sup{ b_i(R_Gamma) | Gamma in F }, where R_Gamma is the local semigroup ring of Gamma. Must it be true that the quantities B_i(F) are either all finite or all infinite?
context_brief: uniform finite-versus-infinite behavior of Betti-number suprema

question_text: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup with embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = 4. Is the type t(Gamma) bounded above by some function of rho(Gamma), where rho(Gamma) is the number of relations in a minimal presentation?
context_brief: bounding type by number of relations in edim four

question_text: Let Gamma = <g1, ..., ge> be a numerical semigroup and let p be a pseudo-Frobenius number of Gamma. An RF-matrix of p is an e x e matrix (a_ij) with a_ii = -1, a_ij in N for i != j, and sum_j a_ij g_j = p for every row i; subtracting two rows gives a relation in ker(phi), called an RF-relation. Are all minimal relations of a numerical semigroup RF-relations?
context_brief: whether every minimal relation comes from RF-matrices

question_text: A numerical semigroup Gamma is called cyclotomic if the polynomial P_Gamma(z) determined by the Hilbert series H_Gamma(z) = P_Gamma(z)/(1-z) is a product of cyclotomic polynomials. Is a numerical semigroup a complete intersection if and only if it is cyclotomic?

Let Gamma be a complete intersection numerical semigroup, let R_Gamma = k[[Gamma]], let m be the maximal ideal of R_Gamma, let G_Gamma = gr(R_Gamma), and let HF_{G_Gamma}(j) = dim_k(m^j/m^{j+1}) be the Hilbert function of the associated graded ring. Is this Hilbert function always non-decreasing as j increases?
context_brief: Rossi problem for complete intersection semigroups

question_text: Characterize exactly those pairs (e,m) of positive integers for which there exists a complete intersection numerical semigroup Gamma with embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = e and multiplicity mult(Gamma) = m.
context_brief: existence of complete intersections by edim and multiplicity

question_text: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup, let Frob(Gamma) denote its Frobenius number, let edim(Gamma) denote its embedding dimension, and let eta(Gamma) be the number of elements gamma in Gamma with gamma < Frob(Gamma). Is Wilf's inequality always true, namely Frob(Gamma) < edim(Gamma) * eta(Gamma)?

Let A_Gamma = k[Gamma] be the graded semigroup ring of a numerical semigroup Gamma, let f be a minimal generator of the toric ideal defining A_Gamma, let eta(Gamma) be the number of elements gamma in Gamma with gamma < Frob(Gamma), and let g1, ..., g_{edim(Gamma)} be the minimal generators of Gamma. Must every such f satisfy deg(f) <= edim(Gamma) * (eta(Gamma) - 1) + sum_i g_i + 1?
context_brief: weak Wilf bound for degrees of minimal toric generators

question_text: Given a Hilbert space H, a closed linear operator A acting on H, and a datum g in the range of A, under what assumptions does the inverse problem Af = g admit at least one solution f in the closure of the Krylov subspace K(A, g) = span{g, Ag, A^2 g, ...}? The question also asks for conditions that control whether the Krylov solution is unique and, if Krylov approximants fn are constructed by an abstract truncation algorithm, how quickly fn converges to f.
context_brief: General Krylov solvability for Friedrichs-type inverse problems

question_text: Assume (A0, A~0) is a joint pair of abstract Friedrichs operators on a Hilbert space H, meaning that A0 and A~0 are closed and densely defined, A0 is contained in (A~0)* =: A1, A~0 is contained in (A0)* =: A~1, and A1 + A~1 is a bounded self-adjoint operator with strictly positive bottom. Suppose further that the hypotheses g ∈ ran A ∩ dom A* and A* g ∈ Dqa(A* A) hold in a way that yields a unique solution of the auxiliary problem A* A f = A* g lying in K(A* A, A* g). What additional assumptions are needed to upgrade this auxiliary Krylov solvability to standard Krylov solvability of Af = g for a chosen closed realization (A, A*) of (A0, A~0), that is, to ensure the solution belongs to K(A, g)?
context_brief: From auxiliary Krylov solvability to standard Krylov solvability

question_text: Investigate when the inverse problem Af = g is Krylov-solvable for the prototypical Friedrichs operator on H = L^2(R) given by dom A = H^1(R) and Af = -f' + f, and more generally for first-order operators of the form A = -d/dx + c(x) where c : R -> C is chosen so that c(x) + overline{c(x)} is a positive bounded function separated from zero. The problem is to identify suitable assumptions on the datum g and, in the variable-coefficient case, on the coefficient c under which Krylov solvability holds.
context_brief: Krylov solvability for one-dimensional Friedrichs operators

question_text: Investigate the Krylov solvability of the inverse problem Af = g for the classical Friedrichs operator on a bounded Lipschitz domain Ω ⊂ R^d defined by Af = Σ_{k=1}^d ∂k(B_k f) + C f, where each coefficient matrix B_k lies in W^{1,∞}(Ω, M_r), each B_k is self-adjoint, and C lies in L^∞(Ω, M_r) with C + C* + Σ_{k=1}^d ∂k B_k > μ 1 almost everywhere for some μ > 0. The goal is to determine what assumptions on the coefficient matrices B_k and C lead to Krylov-solvable inverse problems of this Friedrichs type.
context_brief: Krylov solvability for classical Friedrichs differential operators

question_text: Characterize the Krylov intersection and Krylov reducibility for Friedrichs operators. In the bounded setting, the Krylov intersection is I(A, g) = K(A, g) ∩ A(K(A, g)^⊥); in the unbounded setting, when the Krylov subspace is defined, the corresponding expression is I(A, g) = K(A, g) ∩ A(K(A, g)^⊥ ∩ dom A). Krylov reducibility asks whether K(A, g)^⊥ is also invariant under A, equivalently whether A K(A, g)^⊥ ⊂ K(A, g)^⊥. The problem is to determine these structures both for abstract Friedrichs operators on Hilbert space and, concretely, for the classical Friedrichs differential operator.
context_brief: Krylov intersection and reducibility for Friedrichs operators

question_text: Consider a perturbation A~ f~ = g~ of an inverse problem Af = g induced by a Friedrichs operator A, where A~ is close to A and g~ is close to g in a suitable sense. Determine when the Krylov subspaces K(A, g) and K(A~, g~) stay close in the weak-gap metric dbw on closed subspaces of a separable Hilbert space, when such perturbations preserve Krylov solvability, when they destroy or create it, and what additional conclusions hold when the perturbation also preserves the Friedrichs character of the operator.
context_brief: Perturbations, weak-gap closeness, and stability of Krylov solvability

question_text: Consider gradient descent on a convex function f: R^d -> R that is L-smooth, meaning that its gradient exists and is L-Lipschitz. Starting from an initial point x0 in R^d, the iterates are defined by x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t nabla f(x_t), and f* = inf f with x* denoting a minimizer. What is the best anytime convergence rate for the individual-iterate error f(x_T) - f* that can be guaranteed uniformly over all such objectives by choosing a stepsize sequence (eta_t)_{t=0}^infinity? In particular, does there exist a stepsize sequence and an exponent alpha > 1 such that, for every horizon T in N and every L-smooth convex function f, the error f(x_T) - f* is bounded up to a universal constant factor by L ||x0 - x*||^2 / T^alpha, with the guarantee available in an anytime, monotonically decreasing form across all T?
context_brief: Anytime acceleration for gradient descent on smooth convex objectives

question_text: Prove that the Riemann zeta function zeta(s) has at least one nontrivial zero rho = beta + i gamma whose positive imaginary part gamma is irrational.
Prove that the positive imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are not all rational multiples of one another.
Show that gamma_1, the imaginary part of the first nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function, is irrational.
Obtain upper bounds for 1/|zeta'(rho)| as rho ranges over the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

Let H be a Hilbert space and D be a dictionary in H. For f in A_1(D), where A_1(D) is the closure in H of the finite expansions f = sum_{k in Lambda} a_k g_k with g_k in D and sum_{k in Lambda} |a_k| <= 1, consider the Power-Relaxed Greedy Algorithm defined by T_0^r(f)=0, T_1^r(f)=G_1(f), and for m >= 2 by T_m^r(f) = (1 - 1/m^alpha) T_{m-1}^r(f) + (1/m^alpha) g(R_{m-1}^r(f)), where g(R_{m-1}^r(f)) is a dictionary element maximizing the inner product with the current residual. Does there exist some exponent alpha_0 > 1 such that for every f in A_1(D) one has ||f - T_m^r(f)|| <= C m^{-alpha_0/2} for all m, i.e. a decay rate strictly better than the m^{-1/2} scale obtained from the known alpha = 1 result?
context_brief: Power-Relaxed Greedy Algorithm in Hilbert spaces

question_text: For a Hilbert space H with dictionary D and for f in A_1(D), can one replace the averaging schedule 1/m in the Relaxed Greedy Algorithm or 1/m^alpha in the Power-Relaxed Greedy Algorithm by another function 1/h(m) so that the resulting iterates T_m^r(f) = (1 - 1/h(m)) T_{m-1}^r(f) + (1/h(m)) g(R_{m-1}^r(f)) satisfy an approximation bound strictly better than the bound of Theorem 3.1, namely ||f - G_m^r(f)|| <= 2 / sqrt(m)?
context_brief: Alternative averaging schedule for relaxed greedy updates

question_text: In a quasi-Banach space, does the equivalence between almost-greedy bases and semi-greedy bases remain true for general Markushevich bases, without assuming that the basis is Schauder? Here, almost-greedy means that greedy projections approximate as well as the best coordinate projections up to a uniform constant, while semi-greedy means that for each greedy set A, the best approximation inside span{x_n : n in A} is bounded by a constant times the best |A|-term approximation error.
context_brief: Almost-greedy versus semi-greedy in quasi-Banach spaces

question_text: Suppose a basis has Property (A), meaning that moving the largest-magnitude coefficients to new coordinates and changing their signs in the admissible way does not change the norm. Must such a basis be unconditional? Equivalently, is Property (A) by itself strong enough to force greediness, rather than merely 1-almost-greediness?

Is 1-almost-greediness equivalent to 1-semi-greediness for bases in Banach spaces, and also for bases in quasi-Banach spaces? In other words, when a basis attains the isometric constant 1 for almost-greedy approximation, must it also attain the constant 1 for semi-greedy approximation, and conversely?

For the Haar system in L^p with 1 < p < infinity, can one find an equivalent norm under which the Haar basis becomes exactly 1-greedy, rather than merely (1 + epsilon)-greedy for each fixed epsilon > 0?
context_brief: Exact 1-greedy renorming of the Haar system in L^p

question_text: Let B be a C-semi-greedy basis in a quasi-Banach space. Does there always exist an equivalent renorming of the space under which B becomes 1-semi-greedy?

Let d >= 1, let 0 < gamma < 1 (with gamma >= 1/2 when d = 1), let sigma > d/2, and let E_j denote the isolated eigenvalues, counted with algebraic multiplicity, of the semiclassical Schrödinger operator -hbar^2 Delta + V on L^2(R^d) with complex-valued potential V in L^{gamma + d/2}(R^d). If delta(E) := dist(E, [0, infinity)), does there exist a constant C_{gamma,sigma,d} such that for every hbar > 0 one has sum_j |E_j|^{-sigma} delta(E_j)^{gamma + sigma} <= C_{gamma,sigma,d} hbar^{-d} int_{R^d} |V(x)|^{gamma + d/2} dx?

Let d >= 2, let gamma > 0, let 0 <= sigma <= d/2, and let E_j denote the isolated eigenvalues, counted with algebraic multiplicity, of the semiclassical Schrödinger operator -hbar^2 Delta + V on L^2(R^d) with complex-valued potential V. If delta(E) := dist(E, [0, infinity)), does there exist a potential V in L^{gamma + d/2}(R^d) for which the eigenvalue sum sum_j |E_j|^{-sigma} delta(E_j)^{gamma + sigma} grows strictly faster than hbar^{-d} as hbar -> 0?

Consider the nonlocal eigenvalue bounds sum_j |E_j|^{alpha} (delta(E_j) / |E_j|)^{beta} <= C_{alpha,beta,gamma,d} (hbar^{-d} int_{R^d} |V(x)|^{gamma + d/2} dx)^{alpha/gamma} for the eigenvalues E_j of the semiclassical Schrödinger operator -hbar^2 Delta + V with complex-valued potential V, where delta(E) := dist(E, [0, infinity)). In the six parameter regimes currently listed in the paper -- (a) alpha = 1/2, beta = 1, 0 < gamma < d/(2(2d-1)), d >= 2; (b) alpha > (d-1)gamma/(d/2-gamma), beta = 1, d/(2(2d-1)) <= gamma <= 1/2, d >= 2; (c) alpha = beta > 2gamma with gamma > 1/2 under the truncation |E_j|^gamma <= hbar^{-d} int |V|^{gamma + d/2}; (d) 0 < alpha < gamma(gamma + d/2), beta > 2gamma with gamma > 1/2 under the truncation |E_j|^gamma >= hbar^{-d} int |V|^{gamma + d/2}; (e) alpha = beta = gamma + d/2 with gamma >= 1/2 for d = 1 or gamma > 0 for d >= 2 under the truncation |E_j|^gamma <= hbar^{-d} int |V|^{gamma + d/2}; and (f) alpha > gamma, beta = gamma + d/2 with gamma >= 1/2 for d = 1 or gamma > 0 for d >= 2 under the truncation |E_j|^gamma >= hbar^{-d} int |V|^{gamma + d/2} -- for which values of d, alpha, beta, and gamma is this bound sharp up to a factor of hbar^{epsilon} for arbitrary epsilon > 0, and can the parameter region where such bounds hold be enlarged?
context_brief: Sharpness and extension of nonlocal bounds

question_text: For eigenvalue sums associated with semiclassical Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials, when a bound of order hbar^{-d} fails as hbar -> 0, is the resulting violation of the hbar^{-d} scale power-like or only logarithmic, and if the growth is power-like what is the optimal exponent?
For semiclassical Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials, does the violation of locality occur for generic potentials V, or only for specially chosen potentials?

For eigenvalue sums of the form sum_j |E_j|^{-sigma} delta(E_j)^{gamma + sigma} associated with semiclassical Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials, how does the hbar-growth exponent depend on the choice of potential V, and what role does the threshold sigma = d/2 play in determining whether an hbar^{-d} bound is valid or violated?
context_brief: Potential dependence and sigma = d/2 threshold

question_text: What is the deeper conceptual reason that Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials can violate locality, or equivalently the Weyl-type locality behavior that underlies the usual hbar^{-d} semiclassical scale?

Let X be an ordered Banach space, and suppose that every increasing net in X that has a supremum x in X is norm convergent to x. Must it then follow that every increasing sequence or net in X that is order bounded from above is norm convergent?
If every increasing order-bounded sequence in an ordered Banach space X has a supremum, does it follow that X is normal?

Let X be a separable ordered Banach space such that every order-bounded increasing sequence in X has a supremum. Is that already enough to conclude that every order-bounded increasing sequence in X is norm convergent, without assuming separately that the cone X+ is normal?
Let X be an ordered Banach space. If every weakly convergent increasing net in X is norm convergent, must the cone X+ be normal?
Characterize those ordered Banach spaces X whose cone X+ is non-normal but for which every increasing weakly convergent sequence is nevertheless norm convergent.
context_brief: Sequential Dini property with non-normal cone

question_text: Let H be a Hilbert space over C and let A : D(A) ⊆ H → H be the infinitisimal generator of a bounded semigroup on H. Assume further that A−1 exists as a densely defined, closed operator. Is A−1 the infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup?

This problem, arising in the theory of Gaussian open quantum systems, consists in proving that a dissipative operator G which is quadratic in creation and annihilation operators (or, after a unitary transformation, a differential operator quadratic in partial derivatives ∂j and multiplication by coordinates xk ) generate an analytic semigroup. The solution has applications in the proof of strong positivity, irreducibility and regularity properties of Gaussian open quantum systems. Let aj , a∗k be the annihilation and creation operators on ℓ2 (Nd ; C) that are defined by closure from their action on the canonical orthonormal basis (e(n1 , . . . , nd ))n∈Nd , which is given by √ aj e(n1 , . . . , nd ) = nj e(n1 , . . . , nj−1, nj − 1, . . . , nd ), √ a∗k e(n1 , . . . , nd ) = nk + 1 e(n1 , . . . , nk−1, nk + 1, . . . , nd ). Let H, Lℓ be the closures of operators defined on the canonical basis by d d ζj ∗ ζ¯j X X ∗ κjk ∗ ∗ κjk H = Ωjk aj ak + aa + aj ak + a + aj , j,k=1 2 j k 2 j=1 2 j 2 d X Lℓ = (v ℓk ak + uℓk a∗k ) ℓ = 1, . . . , 2d, k=1 where Ω := (Ωjk )1≤j,k≤d = Ω∗ and κ := (κjk )1≤j,k≤d = κT ∈ Md (C) are d × d complex matrices with Ω Hermitian and κ symmetric, V = (vℓk )1≤ℓ≤2d,1≤k≤d , U = (uℓk )1≤ℓ≤2d,1≤k≤d are 2d × d complex matrices ζ = (ζj )1≤j≤d ∈ Cd . It is not difficult to show (see e.g. [38, Proposition 4.9]) that the closure of the operator G defined on the canonical basis by 2d 1X ∗ G = −iH − Lℓ Lℓ 2 ℓ=1 generates a C0 contraction semigroup P = (Pt )t≥0 on ℓ2 (Nd ; C). Suppose that the non-degeneracy condition (block-matrix form)  T   T V V V TU  V   K= V U = >0 U∗ U ∗V U ∗U holds, then sufficient conditions for P to be an analytic semigroup are also available. The problem it to find a classification of the set of parameters Ω, κ, U, V, ζ for which P is analytic. Alternatively, by the unitary correspondence of the above basis with multidimensional Hermite polynomials (multiplied by exp(−|x|2 /2) normalized), one can formulate the problem with differential operators 1 ∂ ∗ 1 ∂ aj = √ xj + , ak = √ xk − . 2 ∂xj 2 ∂xk In this case strict positivity of K implies     1 −1 1 1 K >0 1 1 −1 1 from which one P2dfinds the strong ellipticity condition for the self-adjoint part G0 = −(1/2) ℓ=1 L∗ℓ Lℓ of G d X U ∗ U + V T V − V T U − U ∗ V jk z j zk > ǫkzk2  Re j,k=1 for z = (zj )1≤j≤d ∈ Cd . Thinking of spectra of G0 and H one wonders if the semigroup P generated by P is analytic when K > 0 and H is bounded from below or from above.

Let Ω be a Polish space. We call a semigroup T = (T (t))t≥0 of contractions on Cb (Ω) a transition semigroup if (i) for every f ∈ Cb (E) we have T (t)f → T (s)f locally uniformly whenever t → s and (ii) for every t ≥ 0 and every uniformly bounded sequence (fn )n∈N ⊂ Cb (Ω) that converges locally uniformly to f , we have that T (t)fn converges locally uniformly to f . Is there a characterization of the generators of such a semigroup akin to the Lumer–Phillips theorem?
Let A and B be generators of C0 semigroups. Under which condition does C := A2 + B 2 generate an analytic semigroup?

Let (T (t))t≥0 be a not necessary strongly continuous semigroup on a Banach space X and consider the following condition. (i) (0, ∞) ∋ t 7→ T (t) ∈ L(X) is analytic. (ii) t 7→ T (t) is analytic on a sector containing R+ (iii) kT (t)k ≤ Metω , dtd T (t) ∈ L(X) and k dtd T (t)k ≤ Mt etω for some constants ω, M. Under which assumption added to (i), (ii) or (iii) does there exist a sectorial operator A generating (T (t))t≥0 ?
context_brief: Existence of a generator for analytic semigroups

question_text: Let A and B be the generators of two communicating C0 -semigroups on a Banach space and let G be the generator of the corresponding product semigroup. Find (the most general) conditions implying D(G) = D(A) ∩ D(B).

Let A and B be generators of C0 -semigroups on a Banach space X. (i) Define the sum C = A + B such that C becomes a (maximal) closed operator on X and Cx = Ãx + B̃x for all x ∈ X and some extrapolated operators A and B. (ii) Find assumptions on A and B such that C remains a generator on X, thereby unifying known perturbation results.

For unbounded linear operators A(t) on a Banach space X and for a starting time t0 , characterize the well-posedness of the non-autonomous Cauchy problem ẋ(t) = A(t)x(t) for t ≥ t0 x(t0 ) = x0 by Hille-Yosida type condition for an operator G generating an evolution semigroup on X = C0 (R, X) or X = Lp (R, X).
Is a C0-semigroup with generator A immediately norm continuous if and only if ||R(is, A)|| tends to 0 as |s| tends to infinity?
context_brief: Characterization of immediate norm continuity by the resolvent

question_text: Consider "non- C0 -semigroups", e.g., bi-continuous semigroups, and describe appropriate regularization properties.

Call a C0-semigroup T on a Banach space X asymptotically analytic if there exist an analytic C0-semigroup S on a Banach space Y, a bounded linear operator P from X to Y, and, for every f in X, an element g in Y such that T(t)f = S(t)g + w(t) for all t >= 0 with ||w(t)|| = o(||S(t)g||) as t -> infinity. Which C0-semigroups are asymptotically analytic? As a first step, what can be proved in the special case Y = X and P = I, and more generally which C0-groups governing second-order equations and which non-analytic semigroups governing functional differential equations are asymptotically analytic?

Let E := Lp (Ω, µ) for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and a σ-finite measure space (Ω, µ) and let (Tt )t∈[0,∞) ⊆ L(E) be a strongly continuous semigroup on E such that Tt is a positive kernel operators for each t > 0, meaning that there exists a measurable function kt : Ω × Ω → R+ such that Z (Tt f )(y) = kt (y, x)f (x)dµ(x) Ω for almost every y ∈ Ω. Assume that (Tt )t∈[0,∞) is mean ergodic, meaning that the limit 1 T Z lim Tt f dt T →∞ T 0 exists in E for all f ∈ E. Does it follow that (Tt ) is strongly convergent, i.e. limt→∞ Tt f exists for all f ∈ E?
context_brief: Tauberian Theorem for Semigroups of Kernel Operators

question_text: Prove or disprove that the non-analytic growth bound ζ(T ) of a C0 -semigroup T coincides with the critical growth bound ωcrit (T ).
Let (T (t))t≥0 be a C0 -semigroup with growth bound ω0 := inf{ω ∈ R : kT (t)k ≤ M ω · etω for t ≥ 0} Find condition such that ω0 is a minimum, i.e., kT (t)k ≤ M0 · etω0 for t ≥ 0 .
context_brief: Precise growth behaviour in terms of the growth bound

question_text: Let (T (t))t≥0 be a bounded C0 -semigroup on a (complex) Banach space X, and let A denote its generator. Suppose that σ(A) ∩ iR = ∅ and that there exists α > 0 such that k(is − A)−1 k = O(|s|α) as |s| → ∞. Find β ∈ depending on the geometric properties of the space X (for instance its Fourier type, its type or its cotype) such that log(t)β/α −1 kT (t)A k = O , t → ∞. t1/α
context_brief: Fine scale of the growth behaviour

question_text: Let E = Lp(Omega, mu) for 1 <= p < infinity over a sigma-finite measure space, and let (T_t) be a strongly continuous semigroup of positive kernel operators on E. If (T_t) is irreducible, meaning that for all nonzero positive f and g in E there exists t >= 0 with T_t f wedge g != 0, must (T_t) be expanding, meaning that T_t f > 0 almost everywhere for every t > 0 and every nonzero positive f in E?
Let E be a Banach lattice and let C : E → E be a positive quasinilpotent compact operator. Do there exist positive operators, A, B : E → E such that C = AB − BA with one of A and B compact?
Use the Perron Frobenius spectral theory of positive C0 -groups to characterize unitary C0 -groups on a Hilbert space H that are unitarily isomorphic to a Koopman group on an L2 -space.
context_brief: Characterizing Koopman groups on Hilbert spaces

question_text: Let M be a von Neumann algebra equipped with a normal, semi-finite, and faithful trace τ and p ∈ [1, ∞). Let (etA )t∈[0,∞) be an individually eventually positive C0 - semigroup on Lp (M, τ ). Is s(A) = ω0 (A)?

Let (e^{tA}) be a C0-semigroup on a Hilbert space H, where -A is associated with a form a: V x V -> H with form domain V contained in H, and let C be a closed convex subset of H. Characterize, in terms of a and V, when C is individually eventually invariant under the semigroup and when C is uniformly eventually invariant under the semigroup.

Let (Omega, mu) be a sigma-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Omega), and let a: V x V -> C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form. Let A be the associated operator on L2(Omega), so that -A generates a bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Omega). If L-infinity-boundedness means that there exists M > 0 such that ||T(t)f||_infinity <= M ||f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega) and all t >= 0, can this L-infinity-boundedness property be characterized directly in terms of the sesquilinear form a?

Let (Omega, mu) be a sigma-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Omega), let a: V x V -> C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, let -A generate the associated bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Omega), and assume that (T(t)) is L-infinity-bounded in the sense that there exists M >= 1 with ||T(t)f||_infinity <= M ||f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega). Must there exist a function g in L-infinity(Omega) with g > 0 mu-almost everywhere and 1/g in L-infinity(Omega) such that ||g T(t)f||_infinity <= ||g f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega) and all t >= 0?

Let (Omega, mu) be a sigma-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Omega), let a: V x V -> C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, let -A generate the associated bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Omega), and assume that (T(t)) is L-infinity-bounded. Characterize exactly when there exists a function g in L-infinity(Omega) with g > 0 mu-almost everywhere and 1/g in L-infinity(Omega) such that ||g T(t)f||_infinity <= ||g f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega) and all t >= 0.
context_brief: Characterization of L∞ -contraction for a weight

question_text: Let (Omega, mu) be a sigma-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Omega), let a: V x V -> C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, let -A generate the associated bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Omega), and suppose there exists a function g in L-infinity(Omega) with g > 0 mu-almost everywhere and 1/g in L-infinity(Omega) such that ||g T(t)f||_infinity <= ||g f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega) and all t >= 0. How can one find or explicitly construct such a weight g?
Consider the following properties of the generation A of a C0 -semigroups (T (t))t≥0 . (i) rg A closed. (ii) rg(1 − T (t)) closed for one t > 0. Does assertion (ii) imply assertion (i)?

Let (T (t))t≥0 be a contraction semigroup with generator A on a Hilbert space H. Consider the following properties: (i) There exists m ≥ 0 such that k(λ − A)xk ≥ m| Re λ|kxk for all Re λ < 0 and all x ∈ H. (ii) There exists m1 > 0 such that kT (t)xk ≥ m1 kxk for all t ≥ 0, x ∈ H. Does assertion (i) imply assertion (ii)?

Characterize injective C0-semigroups via the backward uniqueness property, and apply the resulting criteria to non-autonomous Cauchy problems u'(t) = A(t)u(t) with sectorial A(t) by analyzing the corresponding evolution semigroup.
Does every bounded C0-semigroup on a Hilbert space have a bounded rational calculus?
When is a C0-semigroup on a Hilbert space similar to a contraction semigroup?

Let B be a Banach space. Let P be a projection on a finite-dimensional Banach subspace of B. Let L0 + λL be a generator of C0 -semigroup Utλ on B for all λ ∈ [0, λsup ). Let Ut0 leave both PB and its complement (I − P)B invariant, let PLP = 0. Denote Lt ≡ (Ut0 )−1 LUt0 . Let the integrals Z t Z tk−1 dt1 . . . dtk PLt1 . . . Ltk P, k = 1, . . . , n + 1 −∞ −∞ be finite for all t ⩾ 0. If is it possible to find such a λ-dependent operator r n,λ on PB , which is polynomial in λ, and λ-dependent semigroup un,λ t on PB, whose generator is polynomial in λ, such that P(U 0t )−1 U λt P = un,λ t r n,λ + O(λ2n+2 ), λ → +0 λ2 λ2 for all t > 0 ? Let us emphasize that we do not assume here asymptotic behaviour to be uniform in t, it is just assumed for each fixed t > 0. If there are counterexamples, what further restrictions should be assumed to obtain such an asymptotic estimate? Relevance. This problem is important for the derivation of perturbative corrections to Markovian quantum master equations. It seems to be a possible direction of generalization of the classical results by E.B. Davies to higher orders of perturbation theory in λ and seems to be held in a simple example discussed in . It also seems to be necessary for strict perturbative derivation of master equations recently obtained by A.S. Trushechkin .

Let L be the closure on UC_b(R, R) of the differential operator (Lf)(x) = a(x)f''(x) + b(x)f'(x) + c(x)f(x), where a, b, c are bounded uniformly continuous real-valued functions and a(x) >= a_0 > 0 for all x. Find an explicitly given Chernoff function S(t) for L such that S is Chernoff-equivalent to the semigroup (e^{tL}), there exist a dense subspace D and constants M > 0, q > 1, n_0 > 0 with ||e^{tL}f - S(t/n)^n f|| <= M / q^n for all n >= n_0 and all f in D, and the formula for S(t) depends explicitly on a, b, c, f, and x without hiding the unknown semigroup inside the definition.

Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system with length function ell and reflection set T = {wsw^-1 : s in S, w in W}. It is known that sum_{u in W} x^{ell(u)} is a rational generating function. Determine whether sum_{t in T} x^{ell(t)} must also be a rational generating function.

Let (W1,S1) and (W2,S2) be Coxeter systems, and let u,v in W1 and w,z in W2 be such that the Bruhat intervals [u,v] and [w,z] are isomorphic as posets. Must the corresponding Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials agree, i.e. must P_{u,v}(q) = P_{w,z}(q)?

Let (W1,S1) and (W2,S2) be Coxeter systems, let J1 subseteq S1 and J2 subseteq S2, let u,v in W1^{J1} and w,z in W2^{J2}, and let f : [u,v] -> [w,z] be a poset isomorphism such that f([u,v]^{J1}) = [w,z]^{J2}. Must the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials satisfy P_{u,v}^{J1,q}(q) = P_{w,z}^{J2,q}(q)?

Let W be a Weyl group of type A and let u <= v in W. Suppose [u,z] is a hypercube decomposition of the Bruhat interval [u,v] in the sense defined in the paper. Does the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) always equal the polynomial P~_{u,v,z}(q) produced from that hypercube decomposition?
Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system and let u <= v in W. If ~Phi_{u,v}(c,d) denotes the complete cd-index of the Bruhat interval [u,v], must all coefficients of ~Phi_{u,v} be nonnegative?

Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system and let u <= v in W. Must there always exist another Coxeter system (W',S') and an element w in W' such that the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) can be realized as P_{e,w}(q)?

Given a Coxeter system (W,S) and u <= v in W, construct an explicit combinatorial model for the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q), namely a set M(u,v) and statistic s : M(u,v) -> N such that P_{u,v}(q) = sum_{a in M(u,v)} q^{s(a)}, in a genuinely combinatorial rather than merely recursive way.
For n >= 5, let L(sigma) be the odd inversion number of a permutation sigma in S_n, and let L_n(x) = sum_{sigma in S_n} x^{L(sigma)}. Is the polynomial L_n(x) always symmetric and unimodal?

Let (W,S) be a finite Coxeter system and let u <= v in W. Writing the R-polynomial in the form ~R_{u,v}(t) = Q_{u,v}(t^2) when ell(u,v) is even and ~R_{u,v}(t) = t Q_{u,v}(t^2) when ell(u,v) is odd, must the polynomial Q_{u,v}(t) always be log-concave?
For a graph G, let tau(G; x) be the polynomial defined by tau(G; x) = sum_{pi in Pi(V)} a(G[pi]) x^{|pi|}. Does tau(G; x) have only real roots for every graph G?
Let sum_{i=0}^d h_i t^i be a symmetric monic polynomial with nonnegative coefficients and only real roots. Must there exist a simplicial convex polytope whose h-vector is (h_0, ..., h_d)?

Let sum_{i=0}^d h_i t^i be a polynomial with only real roots such that h_0 = 1 and h_0 < h_1 < ... < h_k for some 0 <= k <= d. Must there exist a simplicial complex whose f-vector is (h_0, h_1 - h_0, ..., h_k - h_{k-1})?
Let W be a Weyl group and let [u,v] be a Bruhat interval in W. Is the rank generating function of [u,v] always log-concave?
Let A(n,k) be the Eulerian number counting permutations in S_n with k descents, and form the infinite matrix A = (A(n+1,k))_{n,k in N}. Is this matrix totally positive?
context_brief: Total positivity of the Eulerian matrix

question_text: For all i,j,r in N, consider the square submatrix of the Eulerian matrix A = (A(n+1,k))_{n,k in N} cut out by rows i, i+1, ..., i+r and columns j, j+1, ..., j+r. Is its determinant always a monotonically increasing function of i?
context_brief: Monotone total positivity for Eulerian minors

question_text: A fullerene is a convex, 3-regular polytope consisting only of pentagonal and hexagonal facets. For a feasible integer n, meaning a positive even integer n >= 20 with n != 22, let C_n denote the set of all fullerenes with exactly n vertices, considered up to graph isomorphism as fullerene isomers. Can one design a computationally efficient procedure that samples uniformly from the fullerene isomers in C_n, so that every isomer in C_n is selected with the same probability?
context_brief: Uniform random generation of fullerene isomers

question_text: A fullerene is a convex, 3-regular polytope consisting only of pentagonal and hexagonal facets. For a feasible n, meaning a positive even integer n >= 20 with n != 22, let T_n be the unique dual graph of such a fullerene. A generalized Stone-Wales (gSW) path in T_n is a path (v_1, ..., v_{2w}) of odd length 2w - 1 such that v_1 and v_{2w} have degree 5, v_2 and v_{2w-1} have degree 6, all vertices are distinct, and (v_i, v_{i+2}) is an edge for every i = 1, ..., 2w - 2. Since a gSW operation can be applied only when such a path exists, which fullerene isomers do not permit any generalized Stone-Wales operation at all?
context_brief: Classification of fullerenes without gSW moves

question_text: A fullerene is a convex, 3-regular polytope consisting only of pentagonal and hexagonal facets. For a feasible n, meaning a positive even integer n >= 20 with n != 22, let T_n be the unique dual graph of such a fullerene. If A is the adjacency matrix of T_n and D is its degree matrix, define the (alpha, beta)-character by ch_{alpha,beta}(T_n) := tr(exp(alpha A + beta D)). For alpha and beta in (0, 1), does equality of this character exactly characterize graph isomorphism among dual fullerenes, meaning that for all feasible n_1, n_2 and dual fullerenes T_{n_1}, T_{n_2}, one has T_{n_1} ≃ T_{n_2} if and only if ch_{alpha,beta}(T_{n_1}) = ch_{alpha,beta}(T_{n_2})?

A fullerene is a convex, 3-regular polytope consisting only of pentagonal and hexagonal facets. Let C_n denote the set of all fullerenes with exactly n vertices, and let T_n be a random dual graph of a fullerene in C_n. For any dual fullerene graph G with adjacency matrix A and degree matrix D, define its (1/2, 1/4)-character by ch_{1/2,1/4}(G) := tr(exp((1/2)A + (1/4)D)). Does the normalized quantity [ch_{1/2,1/4}(T_n) - min_H ch_{1/2,1/4}(H)] / [max_H ch_{1/2,1/4}(H) - min_H ch_{1/2,1/4}(H)] converge as n tends to infinity, where the minimum and maximum are taken over dual graphs H of fullerenes in C_n? If the limit exists, what is its explicit form or limiting distribution?
context_brief: Limiting law for normalized fullerene characters

question_text: Let Σ_{n+1,2d} = C_0 ⊆ ··· ⊆ C_{k(n,d)-n} = P_{n+1,2d} be the filtration of cones of degree-2d forms in n+1 variables obtained from the Gram-matrix construction along projective varieties V_i containing the Veronese variety. For a strictly separating intermediate cone C_i appearing in the strict inclusions of filtration (6), determine a practical membership test for C_i, preferably one stated as an intrinsic property of a representing Gram matrix rather than by directly checking local positive semidefiniteness on the underlying variety.

For a strictly separating intermediate cone C_i in the filtration between the sum-of-squares cone Σ_{n+1,2d} and the cone P_{n+1,2d} of positive semidefinite forms, explicitly describe its dual cone C_i^∨ = {L in Hom(R[X], R) | L(f) ≥ 0 for all f in C_i}.

For a strictly separating intermediate cone C_i, interpret the dual cone C_i^∨ in homogeneous truncated moment terms. Concretely, determine what kind of homogeneous truncated moment sequences or representing measures correspond to membership in C_i^∨, in analogy with the identification of P_{n+1,2d}^∨ as the cone of homogeneous truncated moment sequences that admit representing measures supported on the unit sphere S^n.

For each i in {0, ..., k-n}, let Λ_i := {α_s + α_t | 0 ≤ s, t ≤ n+i} ⊆ I_{n+1,2d} ⊆ N_0^{n+1}. Determine how the dual cone C_i^∨ is related to the Λ_i-truncated moment problem, where one asks whether a truncated multisequence indexed by Λ_i admits a non-negative Borel representing measure.

When cone filtrations between Σ_{n+1,2d} and P_{n+1,2d} are built by ordering the monomials of I_{n+1,d}, which structural properties of the chosen monomial order determine whether adjacent cones become equal or remain strictly separated, and how do those order-theoretic properties control the resulting pattern of equalities and inequalities in the filtration?
context_brief: Effect of monomial order on cone filtrations

question_text: Let G be a 3-connected cubic graph with a blue-red vertex coloring. Write B and R for the subgraphs induced by the blue and red vertices. A crumby coloring is one with maximum degree Delta(B) <= 1, minimum degree delta(R) >= 1, and no path with 3 edges in R. Since the original conjecture asserting that every 3-connected cubic graph has such a coloring is false, what relaxation of the conditions imposed on the red induced subgraph R is sufficient to guarantee that every 3-connected cubic graph admits a blue-red coloring of this type?

For a graph G, let chi_l(G) be the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L admits a proper L-coloring, and let chi*_l(G) be the least integer k such that for every k-list-assignment L, the graph G admits an L-packing of size k, meaning k pairwise-disjoint L-colorings. Does there exist a graph G for which the list packing number exceeds the list-chromatic number by at least 2, that is, chi*_l(G) > chi_l(G) + 1?

For every graph G, is the list packing number chi*_l(G) always at most twice the list-chromatic number chi_l(G)? Equivalently, if chi_l(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment admits a proper coloring and chi*_l(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment admits k pairwise-disjoint proper colorings, must chi*_l(G) <= 2 chi_l(G) hold for all graphs G?

Let G be a cubic planar graph and let L be a 3-list-assignment on G, meaning each vertex has a list of three allowed colors. An L-coloring is proper if adjacent vertices receive different colors, and two L-colorings are disjoint if every vertex receives different colors in the two colorings. Must every such 3-list-assignment admit two disjoint proper L-colorings?

Let G be a cubic planar graph and let L be a 3-list-assignment on G. Is it always possible to choose three pairwise-disjoint proper L-colorings, that is, three proper colorings from the given vertex lists such that each vertex receives three different colors across the three colorings?

For cubic bipartite graphs equipped with a 3-list-assignment, two disjoint proper colorings are known to exist. Does every cubic bipartite graph with a 3-list-assignment also admit three pairwise-disjoint proper list-colorings?
For a graph G with maximum degree Delta(G), is the list packing number always at most Delta(G) + 1? In other words, must chi*_l(G) <= Delta(G) + 1 hold for every graph G?
Does there exist a planar graph G whose list packing number chi*_l(G) is at least 6?
Is the list packing number of every planar graph at most 7? That is, does chi*_l(G) <= 7 hold for every planar graph G?
If G is a triangle-free planar graph, is its list packing number always at most 4? In other words, must chi*_l(G) <= 4 hold for every triangle-free planar graph G?

Let v be a vertex of a graph G. Is the list packing number of G always at most two more than the list packing number of the vertex-deleted graph G \ v? Equivalently, must chi*_l(G) <= chi*_l(G \ v) + 2 hold for every graph G and every vertex v of G?

Let e be an edge of a graph G. Is the list packing number of G always at most two more than the list packing number of the edge-deleted graph G \ e? Equivalently, must chi*_l(G) <= chi*_l(G \ e) + 2 hold for every graph G and every edge e of G?
Fix an integer k > 2. Given a graph G as input, is deciding whether chi*_l(G) <= k complete for the complexity class Pi^P_2?

Fix an integer k >= 1 and let n = 4k + 1. Choose a set S subseteq {1, 2, ..., 2k} of size k, let the complementary set {1, ..., 2k} \ S be used on the second layer, and define the extended Petersen graph XP(2n, S) on vertex set Z_n x {1, 2} with layer edges determined by circular distance d(x, y) = min{|x - y|, n - |x - y|} and matching edges x1x2 for x in Z_n. Is every extended Petersen graph, except the Petersen graph itself, Class 1, meaning that its chromatic index equals its maximum degree?

Does there exist a constant c >= 0 such that every non-complete graph G of order n with minimum degree delta(G) >= n/2 + c has rainbow connection number rc(G) = 2? In particular, does the weaker threshold delta(G) >= n/2 already imply rc(G) = 2?
Does there exist a 5-edge-connected 5-regular graph that is Class 2, that is, a 5-regular graph whose edges cannot be colored with only 5 colors?

An r-graph is an r-regular graph G such that every odd vertex set X subseteq V(G) is joined to its complement by at least r edges. Such a graph is poorly matchable if any two of its perfect matchings intersect. Is there a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph?

Can one characterize exactly which subcubic K3-free graphs are Class 2? Equivalently, is it possible to describe all K3-free graphs of maximum degree at most 3 whose chromatic index is 4 rather than their maximum degree?

Let v1, ..., vn be a linear ordering of the vertices of a graph G, and for each vertex vi define d-(vi) = |{j < i : vivj in E(G)}| and d+(vi) = |{j > i : vivj in E(G)}|. A Type-A order is one in which every vertex v satisfies that d-(v) is odd or 0. Can it be decided in polynomial time whether a graph G admits a Type-A order or a Type-B order, where a Type-B order requires that each vertex either has d-(v) odd or 0, or else has d-(v) even and d+(v) = 0?
Under the same definitions of Type-A and Type-B vertex orders for a graph G, if G admits a Type-A order or a Type-B order, can such an order be found in polynomial time?

Let S be a semigroup and let X be any set. A semigroup conjugacy relation on S is partition-covering if, for every partition of X, one can put a semigroup structure on X whose conjugacy classes are exactly the blocks of that partition. For the standard semigroup conjugacy relations ∼o, defined by a ∼o b when there exist g,h in S with ag = gb and bh = ha; ∼p, defined by a ∼p b when there exist u,v in S with a = uv and b = vu; and ∼tr, the epigroup relation defined using idempotent powers a^ω and b^ω together with elements g,h satisfying ghg = g, hgh = h, hg = a^ω, gh = b^ω, and ga^(ω+1)h = b^(ω+1), must every partition arise as the set of conjugacy classes of some semigroup?

For semigroup elements a and b, define a ∼p b to mean that there exist u and v in the semigroup with a = uv and b = vu. If a semigroup embeds into a group, must this relation ∼p be transitive on that semigroup?

For semigroup elements a and b, define a ∼p b when there exist u and v in the semigroup with a = uv and b = vu. If a semigroup has the property that ∼p is transitive in every variant of that semigroup, where the variant at an element c has multiplication x ◦ y = xcy, must ∼p already be transitive in the original semigroup?

Define Otto conjugacy on a semigroup S by a ∼o b if there exist elements u and v in S such that au = ub and va = bv. Does there exist a semigroup S for which ∼o is a congruence and the quotient semigroup S/∼o fails to be cancellative?

Define Otto conjugacy on a semigroup S by a ∼o b if there exist elements u and v in S such that au = ub and va = bv. Is there a finite semigroup S for which ∼o is a congruence and the quotient semigroup S/∼o is not cancellative?

Does there exist an infinite family of semigroup conjugacy relations that are first-order definable, that agree with ordinary group conjugacy on every group, and that form a strict chain under inclusion?

Does there exist an infinite family of semigroup conjugacy relations that are first-order definable, that agree with ordinary group conjugacy on every group, and that form an antichain under inclusion, so that no one of the relations contains another?

Is there any semigroup conjugacy relation that is not partition-covering, meaning that there exists some partition of some set that cannot be realized as the conjugacy classes of a semigroup for that relation?

Let ∼g denote ordinary group-style conjugacy inside subgroups of a semigroup, and let ∼u denote unit conjugacy, where a ∼u b means that some unit u satisfies u^(-1)au = b and ubu^(-1) = a. Is ∼u the smallest semigroup conjugacy relation that is strictly larger than ∼g, in the sense that every conjugacy relation different from ∼g must already contain ∼u?
context_brief: whether unit conjugacy is minimal above group conjugacy

question_text: Let H be Green’s H-relation on a semigroup, let ∼tr be the epigroup conjugacy relation, and let ∼p∗ be the transitive closure of the relation a ∼p b defined by factorizations a = uv and b = vu. Must every pair of H-related elements that are ∼tr-conjugate also be ∼p∗-conjugate, that is, is ∼tr ∩ H contained in ∼p∗ for all semigroups?
context_brief: whether tr∩H is contained in p-star

question_text: Let ∼g denote subgroup conjugacy inside a semigroup, let U(S) be the group of units, and let ∼u be unit conjugacy. If one also requires Green’s H-relation, so that one compares ∼u ∩ H with ∼g, are these two relations equal for every semigroup having fewer than 13 elements?
context_brief: small-semigroup threshold for u∩H equals g

question_text: For each of the semigroup conjugacy relations ∼o, ∼tr, ∼p∗, ∼n, and ∼u, what is the largest natural number n for which intersecting that relation with Green’s H-relation always gives exactly subgroup conjugacy ∼g on every semigroup with at most n elements?
context_brief: largest size bound for relation∩H equals g

question_text: Is there an epigroup for which the relation ∼tr, intersected with Green’s H-relation, is not contained in the transitive closure ∼p∗ of the factorization relation a ∼p b defined by a = uv and b = vu?
context_brief: epigroup counterexample for tr∩H versus p-star

question_text: Is there a semigroup conjugacy relation that is first-order definable, agrees with ordinary group conjugacy on every group, is different from ∼g, and is nevertheless strictly contained in the relation ∼u ∩ H obtained by intersecting unit conjugacy with Green’s H-relation?

Given a continuous graph Gamma=(V,E) and a radius r>0, does there always exist a finite predetermined discretization of points of Gamma, such as endpoints together with finitely many subdividing points on edges, that preserves the r-independence number alpha_r(Gamma) by guaranteeing that some maximum r-independent set can be chosen entirely from that finite point set?

For the maximum r-independent set problem on a continuous graph, does every yes-instance admit a polynomial-size certificate, equivalently a solution whose relevant point locations can be encoded with polynomially bounded rational data?

For the maximum r-independent set problem on a continuous graph Gamma, how does computational complexity depend jointly on the radius r and on the structure of the underlying graph, beyond the known cases where some small radii and sufficiently large radii are polynomial-time solvable while many other rational radii are NP-hard?

Let G be a combinatorial graph, let alpha(G) denote the size of a maximum independent set of G, and let alpha_1(Gamma(G)) denote the largest size of a 1-independent set in its continuous counterpart Gamma(G), where points of the continuous edges may be chosen as set members and any two chosen points must be at distance at least 2. Is n/2 a tight universal upper bound on the ratio alpha_1(Gamma(G))/alpha(G), and how does this ratio behave on special graph classes?

For every rational radius r>0, does there exist a polynomial-time approximation algorithm for the maximum r-independent set problem on continuous graphs whose approximation ratio is bounded below by an absolute constant independent of the input graph?

Let alpha_r(Gamma) be the maximum size of a set of points in a continuous graph Gamma whose pairwise distances are at least 2r, and let beta_r(Gamma) be the minimum number of radius-r balls whose union covers all points of Gamma. For a continuous graph with n endpoints, what bound holds for alpha_r(Gamma)+beta_r(Gamma) as a function of n and r, and is that bound tight?

For a combinatorial graph G and its continuous counterpart Gamma(G), let beta(G) be the minimum vertex-cover size in G and let beta_1(Gamma(G)) be the minimum number of radius-1 balls centered anywhere on Gamma(G) that cover all points of the continuous graph. What is the largest possible ratio beta(G)/beta_1(Gamma(G)) over all graphs G; in particular, is this ratio always at most 2?

For the hard instances of the minimum r-cover problem on continuous graphs, namely when r is a non-unit fraction, what lower bounds on approximation hardness can be proved for computing the minimum number of radius-r balls needed to cover the graph?

Let K_n be the complete graph on n vertices and let Gamma(K_n) be its continuous counterpart in which each edge is a unit-length interval. If chi_{1/2}(Gamma(K_n)) denotes the minimum number of colors needed for a cover of Gamma(K_n) by radius-1/2 balls such that intersecting balls receive different colors, what is the exact value of chi_{1/2}(Gamma(K_n))?

Is every continuous planar graph (1/2,3)-colourable, meaning that all points of the graph can be covered by radius-1/2 balls that can be colored with at most three colors so that any two intersecting balls receive different colors? Equivalently, can one prove that three colors always suffice, or exhibit a continuous planar graph that forces at least three colors and certify that lower bound?

Does the severe inapproximability known for the chromatic number of combinatorial graphs persist for the 1/2-chromatic number of continuous graphs, or does allowing radius-1/2 balls on continuous edges make the problem asymptotically easier to approximate?

Given a continuous graph Gamma, can one derive informative lower and upper bounds for chi_{1/2}(Gamma), the minimum number of colors in a valid radius-1/2 ball cover, as a function of the chromatic number chi(Gamma's combinatorial counterpart) and the number n of endpoints, or as a function of other polynomial-time computable graph parameters?

Let the 1-bramble number of a continuous graph Gamma(G) be defined as the maximum order of a family of subtrees of Gamma(G) that pairwise come within distance 1, where the order is the minimum number of points needed to hit every subtree in the family. For a fixed small integer k>0, is there a tractable algorithm to decide whether the 1-bramble number of Gamma(G) is at most k?

For the minimum r-cover problem on continuous graphs, where one must cover every point of the graph by radius-r balls centered anywhere on the graph, what is the complexity when r is an algebraic real number? More specifically, if r is algebraic and not a unit fraction, must the problem be NP-hard?

What is the maximum integer N for which there exists a packing array PA(N,14,9), meaning an N x 14 array with entries from {0,1,...,8} such that every 2-column subarray contains each ordered pair of symbols at most once?

Does there exist a skew weighing matrix W(18,9), meaning an 18 x 18 matrix with entries in {0,1,-1} such that W W^T = 9I, each row and column has exactly 9 nonzero entries, distinct rows are orthogonal, and the matrix is skew-symmetric (W^T = -W)?

Does there exist a balanced ternary design BTD(17,17;8,2,12;12,8), meaning an arrangement of 17 elements into 17 blocks of cardinality 12 that can be represented by a 17 x 17 incidence matrix with entries in {0,1,2}, where each element appears with total multiplicity R = 12, appearing with multiplicity 1 in exactly 8 blocks and multiplicity 2 in exactly 2 blocks, and every pair of distinct elements appears together exactly 8 times?

Does there exist a balanced ternary design BTD(12,26;3,5,13;6,5), meaning an arrangement of 12 elements into 26 blocks of cardinality 6 that can be represented by a 12 x 26 incidence matrix with entries in {0,1,2}, where each element appears with total multiplicity R = 13, appearing with multiplicity 1 in exactly 3 blocks and multiplicity 2 in exactly 5 blocks, and every pair of distinct elements appears together exactly 5 times?

Does there exist a symmetric weighing matrix W(21,9), meaning an 21 x 21 matrix with entries in {0,1,-1} such that W W^T = 9I, each row and column has exactly 9 nonzero entries, distinct rows are orthogonal, and the matrix is symmetric?

What is the maximum integer m for which there exists an equidistant permutation array with parameters (12,8,m), meaning an m x 12 matrix whose rows are permutations of 0 through 11 and such that every pair of distinct rows differs in exactly 8 positions?

Let n >= 3 and let Omega be an open subset of R^n. If f: Omega -> R^n is a homeomorphism that belongs to the Sobolev space W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n), is it true that f can be approximated in the W^{1,p} Sobolev norm by a sequence of diffeomorphisms, or by a sequence of piecewise affine homeomorphisms? Determine whether the answer depends on the exponent p, including whether positive results hold for all p or only in ranges such as p > n - 1, and whether counterexamples exist for smaller p.
Let n >= 3, let Omega be an open subset of R^n, and let f: Omega -> R^n be a piecewise affine homeomorphism. Can f be approximated by diffeomorphisms in the Sobolev norm?

In higher dimensions, does there exist a counterexample to the Ball-Evans approximation problem at some exponent p >= floor(n/2)? Equivalently, can one construct a Sobolev homeomorphism in such a regime that cannot be approximated by diffeomorphisms or piecewise affine homeomorphisms in the relevant Sobolev norm?

Let Omega be an open subset of R^2, let f: Omega -> R^2 be a homeomorphism with Jf > 0 almost everywhere, let p >= 1, and let a > 0. Define E1(f) = integral_Omega (|Df(x)|^p + 1 / Jf(x)^a) dx and E2(f) = integral_Omega (|Df(x)|^2 + |Df(x)|^2 / Jf(x)) dx. Can one find a sequence of diffeomorphisms that approximates f both in the Sobolev norm and in the value of E1 or E2?

Let f be a homeomorphism in W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n) such that Jf = 1 almost everywhere, so the deformation is incompressible. Can f be approximated in the Sobolev norm by incompressible diffeomorphisms, or by piecewise affine incompressible homeomorphisms?

Let f be a homeomorphism in the second-order Sobolev space W^{2,q}(Omega, R^n) with q >= 1. Can one approximate f in the W^{2,q} Sobolev norm by diffeomorphisms, or by piecewise affine homeomorphisms?

Let n >= 3, and let Omega and Omega' be bounded open subsets of R^n. Consider the class of Sobolev maps f in W^{1,p}(Omega, Omega') that arise as weak W^{1,p} limits of homeomorphisms fk from Omega onto Omega'; that is, fk converges weakly to f in W^{1,p}. Consider also the class of Sobolev maps f in W^{1,p}(Omega, Omega') that arise as strong W^{1,p} limits of homeomorphisms fk from Omega onto Omega'. Are these two classes equal?
context_brief: Weak versus strong closure for homeomorphisms

question_text: Let n >= 3, and let Omega and Omega' be bounded open subsets of R^n. Consider the class of Sobolev maps f in W^{1,p}(Omega, Omega') that arise as weak W^{1,p} limits of diffeomorphisms fk from Omega onto Omega'. Consider also the class of Sobolev maps f in W^{1,p}(Omega, Omega') that arise as strong W^{1,p} limits of diffeomorphisms fk from Omega onto Omega'. Are these two classes equal?
context_brief: Weak versus strong closure for diffeomorphisms

question_text: Let n >= 4 and p = floor(n/2). If Omega is a connected open subset of R^n and f is a homeomorphism in W^{1, floor(n/2)}(Omega, R^n), is it possible for the sets where the Jacobian is positive and where the Jacobian is negative to both have positive measure?

Let n >= 4 and 1 <= p < floor(n/2). Is it possible to construct a homeomorphism f of the ball B(0, R) that belongs to W^{1,p}(B(0, R), B(0, R)), satisfies the boundary condition f(x) = x for every x on the boundary ∂B(0, R), and has Jacobian Jf < 0 almost everywhere on [0, 1]^n?
context_brief: Mostly negative Jacobian with identity boundary

question_text: Let n >= 3 and assume floor(n/2) < p <= n - 1, or in the special case n = 3 assume 1 <= p <= 2. If Omega is a connected open subset of R^n and f in W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n) is continuous, open, and discrete, is it possible for both sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} to have positive measure?
context_brief: Jacobian sign for continuous open discrete maps

question_text: Let n >= 6 and 1 <= q <= floor(n/2)/2. If Omega is a connected open subset of R^n and f is a homeomorphism in W^{2,q}(Omega, R^n), is it possible for both sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} to have positive measure?
context_brief: Jacobian sign in second-order Sobolev class

question_text: Let n >= 3 and 1 <= q < n/2. Is it possible to construct a homeomorphism in the Sobolev space W^{2,q} whose Jacobian vanishes almost everywhere? The same question is also asked for homeomorphisms whose first derivative belongs to the space BV, that is, whose first derivative has bounded variation.
context_brief: Vanishing Jacobian in W2,q or BV

question_text: Does every closed simply-connected 4-manifold admit a trisection in which one of the three 4-dimensional pieces is a 4-disk? Equivalently, is every closed simply-connected 4-manifold representable by a trisection having a 4-dimensional sector diffeomorphic to the 4-disk, rather than merely by a trisection in which all three sectors are higher-genus 4-dimensional handlebodies?

Can one develop an algorithmic procedure that converts generalized Kirby diagrams representing non-orientable 1-handles into gems of the corresponding 4-manifolds? In addition, do the resulting gems admit gem-induced trisections in enough generality that gem methods would then provide an estimation of trisection genus for all closed 4-manifolds, including the non-orientable setting?

Suppose one starts with a gem of the compact 4-manifold consisting only of the handles of index at most two. Can one construct from it a gem of the associated closed 4-manifold even when the original gem contains no rho3-pair and no rho4-pair? More specifically, can one recognize or create the combinatorial structures needed to pass from the bounded handlebody stage to the closed manifold stage without assuming the special pair configurations used in Proposition 9?
context_brief: closing gems without rho3 or rho4 pairs

question_text: Let M be a compact 4-manifold, and form the double of M by taking a Kirby diagram of M and adding a 0-framed meridian to each framed component, which yields a Kirby diagram of the double. For the resulting 5-colored graph produced by the paper's construction, can one modify that graph in a standard way so as to create rho3-pairs satisfying the hypotheses of Proposition 9, thereby giving a direct gem-theoretic route to the double?

Can one characterize classes of gems for which the trisections arising from those gems actually realize the trisection genus of the represented 4-manifolds? In other words, beyond merely producing or bounding trisections from gems, which combinatorial or topological conditions on a gem guarantee that the trisection obtained from it has minimum possible genus for the underlying 4-manifold?

Which closed simply-connected 4-manifolds admit a 5-colored graph Γ in G_s^(4) and a cyclic permutation ε of the color set such that g_{ε0,ε2,ε4} = 1 and g_{ε1,ε3,ε4} = 1 and the associated T(Γ, ε) is a gem-induced trisection, so that the trisection genus equals the second Betti number β2(M)? More generally, can one characterize topologically the 4-manifolds that admit gems satisfying the hypotheses used in Proposition 26, or at least identify broad classes of manifolds that do so?

Let M be a compact 4-manifold with boundary homeomorphic to a connected sum #m(S1 ⊗ S2), with m > 0, and let Mbar be the associated closed 4-manifold obtained by attaching the corresponding 4-dimensional handlebody. Theorem 13 states that if M admits a gem-induced trisection, then Mbar admits a trisection with the same central surface and therefore gT(Mbar) <= gGT(M). Under what conditions on a gem of M does equality hold, so that the trisection genus of Mbar is exactly the G-trisection genus of M?

Do there exist transcendental entire functions with infinitely many zeros that satisfy either of the following Fermat-type functional equations on the complex plane: (f'(z))^2 + (f''(z))^2 = (f(z))^2, or f(z + c1)^2 + f(z + c2)^2 = f(z)^2 where c1 and c2 are distinct nonzero constants?
How can one describe all transcendental meromorphic solutions of the difference equation f(z + c1)^2 + f(z + c2)^2 = f(z)^2, where c1 and c2 are fixed distinct nonzero constants?

For Polyak's heavy-ball method with update x_{t+1} = x_t - gamma*nabla f(x_t) + beta*(x_t - x_{t-1}), applied to scalar objective functions f: R -> R that are L-smooth and mu-strongly convex (the one-dimensional case of F_{mu,L}), does there exist a tuning of the step size gamma and momentum parameter beta that achieves acceleration, or is acceleration impossible even in dimension 1?
