question_text: Let d be the Fubini-Study metric on the complex projective plane CP^2. Does there exist a sequence of nonnegatively curved polyhedral metrics d_n on CP^2 that converges to d?

Let O_3 be the octahedron graph. A metric space X satisfies O_3-comparison if every labeling of six points x, x', y, y', z, z' in X by the vertices of O_3 admits a model configuration in Hilbert space in which the three diagonal distances xx', yy', zz' do not decrease and all edge lengths do not increase. Does every geodesic CAT(0) space satisfy O_3-comparison?
In Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension, does there exist a discrete cocompact isometric action generated entirely by elements of finite order?
context_brief: Hyperbolic actions generated by finite-order elements

question_text: In Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension, does there exist a discrete cocompact isometric action generated entirely by central symmetries?
context_brief: Hyperbolic actions generated by central symmetries

question_text: In Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension, does there exist a discrete cocompact isometric action generated entirely by rotations around subspaces of codimension k?
context_brief: Hyperbolic actions generated by codimension-k rotations

question_text: Let Ω be a round spherical disc of radius α < π/2 on the unit sphere S^2, and let Ω′ be a convex domain in S^2 with the same area as Ω. Show that there exists a bi-Lipschitz map from Ω′ to the Euclidean plane whose Lipschitz constants are 1 and α/sin(α), that is, a (1, α/sin(α))-bi-Lipschitz map.

Let X be a complete length CAT(0) space, not assumed locally compact, and let K be a compact subset of X. Is the closed convex hull of K, meaning the intersection of all closed convex subsets of X that contain K, necessarily compact?
context_brief: Compactness of convex hulls in CAT(0)

question_text: Let T be the 2-dimensional torus. A homeomorphism h: T -> T is called simple if it is supported on an embedded open disc, and the disc norm of h is the least number of simple homeomorphisms whose composition equals h. Do there exist homeomorphisms of T with arbitrarily large disc norm?
Does there exist an embedding of the closed 4-ball D^4 into S^2 x R^2 such that the projection map from D^4 to S^2 induced by the first factor is open?

Let M be a closed surface of genus 2 with a Riemannian metric of nonpositive curvature. Is it true that, with probability 1, a random geodesic in M eventually enters the subset where the curvature is strictly negative?

Let (M, g) be a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold, let p be a point of M, and let h be the pullback of g to the tangent space T_pM along the exponential map exp_p: T_pM -> M, allowing h to degenerate where exp_p fails to be regular. Does the possibly degenerate tensor h determine the pointed manifold (M, g, p) uniquely up to isometry?
context_brief: Ambrose problem for exponential pullback metrics

question_text: Call a body V in R^3 an optical fiber if it is bounded by two plane figures F1 and F2 together with a smooth tube Σ, and every light ray entering V through one end and reflecting perfectly on the interior walls exits through the other end with probability 1, while every light ray starting inside V exits through one of the ends with probability 1. Must every such optical fiber admit a slicing into plane figures that meet the walls at right angles?

Does there exist an optical fiber in R^3, in the sense of a reflective tube body with the almost-sure entrance and exit property described above, whose two planar ends are not congruent to each other?

For each dimension n, does there exist a positive constant epsilon_n such that every open subset of R^n with volume at most epsilon_n admits an embedding into the unit ball that increases the lengths of all curves, equivalently a length-increasing embedding?

Consider the one-dimensional Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated model (FA-1f) on Z, where each site updates only when at least one nearest neighbor is infected, and where the reversible equilibrium measure pi is the Bernoulli product measure with infected density q in (0,1). For any such q and any local observable f depending on finitely many sites, does the law of the process started from any initial distribution nu that almost surely contains at least one infected site satisfy lim_{t->infinity} |E_nu[f(eta(t))] - pi(f)| = 0?

In the one-dimensional FA-1f model on Z with infection density q > 0, suppose the initial distribution nu has exponentially decaying probability of containing no infected site in a symmetric interval around the origin, namely nu(no infected vertices in [-ell, ell]) = O(e^{-kappa ell}) for some kappa > 0. Under that assumption, is the convergence of the law at time t to the Bernoulli(q) equilibrium measure pi exponentially fast for every q > 0?

Let a kinetically constrained model have bootstrap-percolation stable configurations E, and for each beta in E let pi_beta denote the product Bernoulli equilibrium measure pi conditioned on the event that the bootstrap percolation limit BP(eta) equals beta. Must every stationary measure mu of the kinetically constrained model admit a decomposition mu = integral_E pi_beta dmu_star(beta) for some probability measure mu_star on E?

Let the vertices of the complete graph K_m be linearly ordered and identified with {1,2,...,m}. Two independent edges ij and st are called nested when i < s < t < j or s < i < j < t. Determine the smallest integer m such that every 2-coloring of the edges of this ordered complete graph contains a monochromatic non-nested matching of size n.

Consider a random 4-regular graph G defined as the union of two uniformly random cycles on the same vertex set. Is G also a.a.s. 3-choosable, meaning that G is properly colorable for every assignment of lists of three allowed colors to its vertices?

Let G be a random 4-regular graph, and let P_G = product over all edges uv in E(G) of (u - v), where the variables correspond to the vertices of G. In this 4-regular setting, the only relevant monomial for the Alon-Tarsi method is the product over all vertices v in V(G) of v^2. Is it true that the coefficient of P_G at that monomial is a.a.s. non-zero?
Let G be a disjoint union of cycles, and let H be a disjoint union of copies of K_4. Is the graph G union H 4-colorable?

A strong edge coloring assigns colors to the edges of a graph so that any two edges that are adjacent or adjacent to a common edge receive distinct colors; equivalently, it is a proper coloring of the square of the line graph. Let chi'_s(G) denote the smallest number of colors in such a coloring. Diamond-free claw-free cubic graphs can be obtained from cubic graphs by truncation, meaning that each vertex is replaced by a triangle, and T(G) denotes the cubic graph obtained by truncating a cubic graph G. Is every diamond-free claw-free cubic graph strongly 6-edge-colorable? Equivalently, is chi'_s(T(G)) = 6 for every cubic graph G?
context_brief: Strong edge coloring of truncated cubic graphs

question_text: A proper vertex coloring is called a 2-homogeneous coloring when exactly 2 colors appear in the open neighborhood of every vertex. If a cubic graph admits a 2-homogeneous coloring, are 4 colors always sufficient?
context_brief: Color bound for 2-homogeneous colorings of cubic graphs

question_text: A proper vertex coloring is called a 2-homogeneous coloring when exactly 2 colors appear in the open neighborhood of every vertex. Are there only finitely many connected bridgeless cubic graphs that do not admit a 2-homogeneous coloring?
context_brief: Finiteness of cubic graphs without 2-homogeneous colorings

question_text: Let G = (V, E) be a directed graph, let A be a non-trivial Abelian group, and let f map E into A. The boundary of f is the map partial f from V to A defined by partial f(x) = sum of f(e) over edges leaving x minus the sum of f(e) over edges entering x. The graph G is called A-connected if for every map b: V -> A with total sum 0 there exists a map f: E -> A - {0} such that b = partial f; an A-nowhere-zero-flow is such an f with partial f = 0. A graph is called almost-A-connected when all boundaries are admissible except partial f = 0. A snark is a cubic non-3-edge-colorable cyclically 4-edge-connected graph with girth at least 5, and it is bicritical if removing any two distinct vertices produces a 3-edge-colorable graph. Is every bicritical snark almost-Z_2^2-connected and almost-Z_4-connected?
Find an example of a nontrivial graph cocycle action on a Poisson bracket, meaning an action that produces a family of inequivalent Poisson structures not related by a coordinate change.

For the tetrahedral graph cocycle action on the space of Nambu-Poisson brackets, determine whether the action is nontrivial or instead trivial in the sense of being generated only by a coordinate change.
Determine whether the gamma_3-flow is nontrivial, that is, whether the induced change of a Poisson bivector is more than a coordinate change along a vector field X_{gamma_3}^d on R^d.

Assume that in dimension d+1 the tetrahedral Kontsevich graph flow on a Nambu-Poisson bracket is trivial, meaning the flow Q_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗4}) can be written as the Schouten bracket [[P, X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3})]] for some vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}. Determine whether that trivializing vector field can always be constructed as a linear combination of descendants, in dimension d+1, of the two-dimensional 'sunflower' graph.

If the trivializing vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} for the tetrahedral flow in dimension d+1 can be constructed from sunflower descendants, determine whether it is enough to use the union of two classes of dimension-(d+1) descendants: first, descendants of the previously known dimension-d solution X_{gamma_3}^d, and second, descendants of vanishing one-vector micro-graphs defined over R^d.
context_brief: Descendants of prior solution and vanishing graphs

question_text: Determine whether the vanishing micro-graphs that are indispensable for constructing and analyzing the dimension-(d+1) problem arise only by taking descendants of an underlying vanishing set already present in dimension d-1, rather than from genuinely new vanishing mechanisms appearing for the first time in higher dimension.
What is the group-theoretic and topological mechanism of vanishing for Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations?
Find two perfect squares such that both their sum and their difference are also perfect squares.
Find three perfect squares whose sum is itself a perfect square, with the additional condition that the sum of the squares of any two of the three numbers equals the square of the remaining one.
Find a right triangle all of whose side lengths are perfect squares.

Divide 10 into two numbers so that, after dividing each number by the other, adding the two quotients, squaring that sum, and multiplying by one of the two numbers, the result is a prescribed given number.
Divide 10 into two numbers so that if each number is multiplied by its own square root and the two results are added, the total equals a prescribed given number.
Find three proportional perfect squares whose sum is also a perfect square.
Find two perfect squares such that the product of one of them with their sum equals the square of the other.
Find four perfect squares such that multiplying the first by itself, then by the second, then by the third, and then by the fourth yields back the same four numbers.
Find two perfect squares whose sum is 10 and such that adding the square root of each number to that number again produces perfect squares.
Find a perfect cube such that adding 1 dirham to it produces another perfect cube.
Find two perfect cubes such that dividing each by the other and adding the two quotients gives a perfect square.
Find a perfect square such that dividing it and another number by each other, adding the resulting quotients, and multiplying by one of the numbers produces a perfect square.

Divide 10 into two numbers so that if the smaller number is divided by the larger, that quotient is added to the larger number, and the resulting total is multiplied by the smaller number, the outcome is a prescribed given number.
Find a perfect square such that subtracting from it 10 times its square root and then 10 dirhams still leaves a perfect square.
Find two inheritances where the first equals 10 dirhams minus the square root of the second inheritance, and the second equals 5 dirhams minus the square root of the first inheritance.
Find a number that has a square root and remains a square after adding 10 dirhams and also after subtracting 10 dirhams.
Find a perfect square such that adding its square root and 2 dirhams still gives a perfect square, and subtracting its square root and 2 dirhams also gives a perfect square.
Find a perfect square such that squaring it and then increasing the result by 10 times its square root and by 10 dirhams produces a number that itself has a square root.
Find a perfect square such that subtracting its square root from it, then multiplying the remainder by its square root, gives back the original square.

Find two numbers whose difference equals 10 times the square root of the smaller number, and such that dividing each by the other and adding the two quotients yields the square root of the smaller number.
Find a perfect cube whose difference from its square is a perfect square.
Given a number, divide it into two parts so that dividing the original number by each part and by their difference, then summing those three quotients, produces a prescribed given number.
Given a prescribed number, divide it into two parts so that one part is a perfect cube and the other part is a perfect square.
Given a prescribed number, divide it into two parts so that both parts are perfect cubes.

Find a perfect square such that subtracting one third of the square and its square root from that square leaves a quantity whose square root, multiplied by 10, equals one third of the original square plus its square root.
Determine the number of garments when the total price is a given number of dirhams and the price of a single garment plus the square root of the number of garments equals another given number.
Find three perfect cubes whose product is a prescribed given number.

Determine the fixed monthly salary of an employee, measured in dirhams, when the employee worked for a number of days equal to the square root of that salary and received a predetermined amount of money for the month.
Divide 10 into two numbers such that dividing each by the other and adding the two quotients gives back one of the two numbers.

Divide 10 into two numbers such that dividing the larger by the smaller and multiplying by the larger, then dividing the smaller by the larger and multiplying by the smaller, yields two results whose difference is a prescribed fixed number.

Fix r > 0. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. For the planar case where M is a circle of radius R > r, determine the structure of a maximal distance minimizer for M (equivalently, decide what the minimizers are) in the parameter range r < R < 4.98r.
context_brief: MDM for a circle (horseshoe conjecture range)

question_text: Fix r > 0. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. Let M be an R-stadium, defined as the boundary of the R-neighborhood of a segment. For parameters satisfying r < R < 5r, describe the set of maximal distance minimizers for this R-stadium. Additionally, determine (i) the supremum of constants C such that there exists a maximal distance minimizer for a Cr-neighborhood that is not a horseshoe, and (ii) the infimum of constants c such that for any closed curve with minimal radius of curvature cr, every maximal distance minimizer is a horseshoe.
context_brief: MDM for a stadium; horseshoe thresholds

question_text: Fix r > 0 and a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for M is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. For dimensions d \ge 3, must every maximal distance minimizer \Sigma be representable as a union of finitely many injective curves?

Fix r > 0. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. Suppose \Sigma is an r-minimizer for some compact set M. Consider the maximal distance minimization problem with target set taken to be B_r(\Sigma). Is \Sigma the unique r-minimizer for B_r(\Sigma)?
context_brief: MDM uniqueness under induced target set

question_text: Fix r > 0 and a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for M is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. Define a point x \in \Sigma to be energetic if there exists y \in M such that |xy| = r and B_r(y) \cap \Sigma = \emptyset, and let G_\Sigma denote the set of energetic points of \Sigma. Does G_\Sigma determine a minimizer \Sigma (for the given M and r)?

Fix r > 0 and let M \subset \mathbb{R}^2 be a finite set with |M| = n. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for M is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. Let G_\Sigma be the set of energetic points of \Sigma, where x \in \Sigma is energetic if there exists y \in M such that |xy| = r and B_r(y) \cap \Sigma = \emptyset. How does an explicit description of a minimizer \Sigma depend on M in terms of the degrees of the resulting equations? Under the simplifying assumption that the points of M have rational coordinates, what is the largest degree of the extension of \mathbb{Q} generated by the set of energetic points G_\Sigma?
context_brief: Algebraic complexity of MDM for finite planar sets

question_text: Let A \subset \mathbb{R}^d be compact. The Steiner problem considered here is: find a closed set St of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(St)) such that St \cup A is connected; such a minimizer is called a Steiner set, and if St is connected it is called a Steiner tree (in particular, this holds when A is finite). For dimensions d \ge 3, does there exist a finite set of terminals A such that there are two different Steiner trees St_1 and St_2 connecting A, but the directions of all segments incident to terminals are the same (equivalently, the two trees coincide in a neighborhood of the terminals)?
context_brief: Non-uniqueness with codirected terminal edges in d>=3

question_text: Let A \subset \mathbb{R}^d be a bounded set (not assumed closed). Consider the optimization problem: find a set S such that H^1(S) is minimal among all sets with S \cup A connected. Is it possible that this problem has no solution for some bounded A \subset \mathbb{R}^d, i.e., that the infimum of H^1(S) over admissible S is not attained? (Equivalently, is the closedness assumption on A necessary for solvability in this formulation?)
context_brief: Existence of Steiner solutions for non-closed bounded inputs

question_text: For Euclidean space \mathbb{R}^d with d \ge 2, determine the Steiner ratio. Here, for a finite set A of points in the Euclidean plane, a minimum spanning tree (MST) is a shortest connection of A by segments whose endpoints lie in A, and the Steiner ratio is the infimum (over finite point sets) of the ratio: (total length of a Steiner tree for A) divided by (total length of an MST for A). What is the Steiner ratio in \mathbb{R}^d for d \ge 2?
context_brief: Gilbert-Pollak / Steiner ratio in Euclidean spaces

question_text: Let St be a Steiner tree in Euclidean space, let A be its terminal set, and fix x and r > 0 so that Br(x) contains no terminal points, that is, A ∩ Br(x) = ∅. Assume moreover that the tree has finite length inside Br(x). For t = 1/2, or more generally for t ∈ (0, 1), what is the largest possible number of intersection points between the tree and the sphere ∂Btr(x)?

Let St be a Steiner tree in Euclidean space, let A be its terminal set, and fix x and r > 0 so that Br(x) contains no terminal points, that is, A ∩ Br(x) = ∅. Assume moreover that the tree has finite length inside Br(x). A branching point of a Steiner tree is a non-terminal vertex of degree 3. For t = 1/2, or more generally for t ∈ (0, 1), what is the largest possible number of branching points of St that can lie inside Btr(x)?
Let St ⊂ Rd with d > 2, and additionally assume that St is full. What is the maximum possible value of H1(St ∩ Btr(x)) / r for t ∈ (0, 1)?
context_brief: Normalized local length of full Steiner trees

question_text: Let A \subset \mathbb{R}^d be a compact totally disconnected set for which there exist at least two different Steiner trees connecting A (call them S and T). A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. Can one of the Steiner trees (for example S) also arise as a solution to a maximal distance minimization problem (for some choice of r > 0 and some compact target set M)?
context_brief: When a Steiner tree can be an MDM

question_text: Let Ω ⊂ Rd and consider a random N-point input in Ω. Does the length of a Steiner tree for that input have asymptotics βN^((d−1)/d), where β is a constant depending on Ω and the random model?

Let Ω ⊂ Rd and consider a random N-point input in Ω. Can one obtain bounds of the form β1N^((d−1)/d) ≤ EH1(St) ≤ β2N^((d−1)/d) that distinguish the Steiner tree problem from the minimum spanning tree, the rectilinear Steiner tree, and the traveling salesperson problem? In the same random setting, what are good upper and lower bounds for the Steiner ratio?
Is it true that one can always connect n points in a rectangle of side lengths √3 and (n − 1) by a set of length at most √3(n − 1) + o(1)?
context_brief: Worst-case Steiner tree length in a thin rectangle

question_text: For n terminals, consider full Steiner topologies, meaning the underlying abstract graphs of full Steiner trees. How many different full Steiner topologies may simultaneously give a shortest solution to the Steiner problem for the same terminal set?

In \mathbb{R}^3, consider a regular n-gon lying in the plane x = 1 and centered at (1, 0, 0). Let Q be the set of its vertices. Let f be a homothety with center at the origin and scale factor \lambda, where \lambda is small enough, and consider the terminal set \bigcup_{k \in \mathbb{N}} f^k(Q). What is the structure of the Steiner tree connecting this terminal set?
Does there exist a non-planar example of a unique full Steiner tree that has infinitely many branching points?
context_brief: Unique full nonplanar Steiner tree with infinitely many branch points

question_text: Classify the elementary-equivalence classes of the tracial matrix ultraproduct MU as U ranges over ultrafilters on N, and also classify the elementary-equivalence classes of the C*-norm matrix ultraproduct MU.
For every Connes embeddable non Gamma II1 factor N, determine whether there exists an embedding pi: N -> MU such that the relative commutant N' intersect MU is exactly C.
A non Gamma factor N is called pseudocompact when N is elementarily equivalent to MU for some ultrafilter U. Determine whether the free group factor L(F_n) is pseudocompact for n >= 2.
Determine whether there exists a group von Neumann algebra L(G) that is pseudocompact, and whether there exists an icc non inner amenable group von Neumann algebra L(G) that is not pseudocompact.
If N is a finite-index subfactor of the matrix ultraproduct MU, determine whether N must itself be isomorphic to a matrix ultraproduct.

Let SU be the ultraproduct of the symmetric groups with normalized Hamming distance, viewed trace-preservingly inside MU, and let W*(SU) be the von Neumann subalgebra of MU generated by SU. Determine whether W*(SU) contains a copy of a matrix ultraproduct.
Determine whether there exists a separable II1 factor N that admits an existential embedding of L(F2) into N but is not isomorphic to a nontrivial free product.
Determine whether there exist II1 factors N and M such that N is strongly solid, M contains an existential copy of N, and M nevertheless admits a Cartan subalgebra.

Determine whether there exists a group G that contains an existential inclusion of F2 such that L(G) is not isomorphic to L(F_n) for some n in N; in particular, determine whether a non-elementary surface group G can satisfy L(G) not isomorphic to L(F_n).
Let M be a separable II1 factor containing an existential copy of a nonamenable biexact II1 factor N. Determine whether M must be prime.
Let N be a nonamenable II1 factor with the Haagerup property and suppose N is existentially included in M. Determine whether M can have property (T).

Let N be a II1 factor with the Haagerup property, and let B be a property-(T) subalgebra of the ultrapower NU. Determine whether there exist finite-dimensional subalgebras M_n subset N such that B is contained in the ultraproduct product n->U M_n.
Determine whether there exists an existential inclusion of L(F2) into MU, and whether the random embedding is existential in the Haar-sampling sense.

Determine whether there exists a countable group G such that L(G) is an existentially closed II1 factor, and whether there exists an existentially closed II1 factor that is not isomorphic to any group von Neumann algebra.
Determine whether there exists a sequence of separable non Gamma factors N_i whose ultraproduct product i->U N_i has property Gamma.

Determine whether there exists a pair of Connes embeddable non Gamma factors that are not elementarily equivalent, and whether there are continuum many pairwise non-elementarily-equivalent non Gamma factors.
Determine whether there exists an icc non inner amenable group G such that its group von Neumann algebra L(G) is not elementarily equivalent to L(F2).

A II1 factor is called super McDuff when N' intersect NU is a II1 factor. Determine whether there exist two non-elementarily-equivalent Connes embeddable super McDuff II1 factors, and whether there are continuum many such factors.
Determine whether there exist two property-Gamma II1 factors that are not McDuff and are not elementarily equivalent, and whether there are continuum many such examples.
Determine whether the group von Neumann algebra L(F) of Thompson's group F is super McDuff.
If a II1 factor M is McDuff and decomposes as M congruent N1 tensor N2, determine whether at least one tensor factor N1 or N2 must also be McDuff.
For a non Gamma II1 factor, determine whether there exists one with a unique sequential commutation orbit of Haar unitaries and with sequential commutation diameter exactly n for a prescribed n in N.
Determine whether there exists a property-(T) II1 factor with a unique sequential commutation orbit of Haar unitaries.
context_brief: Sequential commutation in property T factors

question_text: Determine whether there exists a II1 factor N with no diffuse relative-(T) subalgebras and with a unique sequential commutation orbit, and whether such an N can additionally have the Haagerup property.

Determine whether there exists a II1 factor N with h(N) = 0 but continuum many sequential commutation orbits, and whether there exists a II1 factor N with h(N) = 0 that is not generated as a von Neumann algebra by a single sequential commutation orbit.

Let M = N1 *_B N2. Suppose u_i are Haar unitaries in N_i with E_B(u_i^k) = 0 for all k in N, and suppose v_i are Haar unitaries in MU such that u_i and v_i are sequentially commuting equivalents and E_{B^U}(v_i^k) = 0 for all k in N. Determine whether v1 and v2 must be freely independent.
If N is a non-prime II1 factor, determine whether N has a unique sequential commutation orbit.
For a separable II1 factor N and its amplification N^t, determine whether N and N^t have the same number of sequential commutation orbits.
If u and v are independent unitaries in the ultrapower NU, determine whether they can be lifted to sequences of pairwise independent unitaries in N.
If u and v are freely independent unitaries in the ultrapower NU, determine whether they can be lifted to sequences of pairwise k-independent unitaries in N for every k.

Let M be a separable subfactor with two embeddings pi_i: M -> NU. Suppose phi_n: N -> N is a sequence of unital completely positive maps whose ultrapower Phi = (phi_n)^U conjugates pi1 to pi2. Determine whether there must exist a unitary u in NU that conjugates pi1 and pi2.
Determine whether there exists a nonamenable separable II1 factor N such that any pair of embeddings of N into NU are conjugate by a unitary in NU.

If a Connes embeddable separable II1 factor N has the property that any pair of embeddings of N into RU are conjugate by an automorphism of RU, determine whether N must be isomorphic to the hyperfinite factor R.
Determine whether the free group factors L(F_n) are elementarily equivalent for different values of n.
Let N be a Connes embeddable separable II1 factor. Determine whether N admits an embedding into RU whose commutant is a factor.
Let N0 be an index-2 subfactor of an ultrapower NU. Determine whether N0 must be isomorphic to an ultraproduct product i->U N_i of index-2 subfactors N_i subset N.
Determine whether an ultrapower NU of a II1 factor can ever be isomorphic to a group von Neumann algebra.
context_brief: Ultrapowers as group von Neumann algebras

question_text: Determine whether there exists a II1 factor N such that the 1-bounded entropy h(NU) of its ultrapower is infinite while h(N) = 0.
If a II1 factor N satisfies ((N' intersect NU)' intersect NU) = N, determine whether N must be isomorphic to the hyperfinite factor R.
For an arbitrary II1 factor M, determine whether the tensor product M2(C) tensor M always embeds into MU.

A II1 factor N is solid if every subalgebra A subset N whose commutant in N is diffuse is amenable, and N is U-solid if every subalgebra A subset N whose commutant in NU is diffuse is amenable. Determine whether solidity and U-solidity are equivalent for II1 factors.
Determine whether there exist II1 factors N and M that are elementarily equivalent as II1 factors but not elementarily equivalent when viewed as C*-algebras.
Determine whether there exists a II1 factor N such that the ultrapower NU has non-full fundamental group.

Suppose N1, N2, M1, and M2 are separable II1 factors with NU1 tensor NU2 congruent MU1 tensor MU2. Determine whether, up to permuting the indices, each N_i must be elementarily equivalent to the corresponding M_i.
context_brief: Tensor-product rigidity up to elementary equivalence

question_text: Suppose I and J are finite sets and {N_i}_{i in I}, {M_j}_{j in J} are separable II1 factors such that the free products *_i in I NU_i and *_j in J MU_j are isomorphic. Determine whether I and J must be bijective and, up to permutation, the corresponding factors must be mutually elementarily equivalent.
context_brief: Free-product rigidity up to elementary equivalence

question_text: Given an absolutely convergent real series sum x_n, define its achievement set E(x_n) to be the set of all subsums sum_{n in A} x_n over subsets A of the natural numbers. What characterizations of the four possible topological types of E(x_n) - finite set, multi-interval set, Cantor set, and Cantorval - can be given directly in terms of the generating sequence (x_n)?

Let x_n = 1/2^n + (-1)^n/3^n. What is the topological type of the achievement set E(x_n), that is, is the set of all subsums of this series a finite set, a multi-interval set, a Cantor set, or a Cantorval?
Let (x_n) be the sequence defined by x_{2n-1} = 1/2^(2n-1) and x_{2n} = 1/2^(2n+1). What is the topological type of the achievement set E(x_n) of all subsums of this series?
Does there exist a sequence (x_n) for which the ratio x_{n+1}/x_n has a limit as n tends to infinity and whose achievement set E(x_n) is a Cantorval?
Suppose a positive series has remainder terms r_n = sum_{i>n} x_i satisfying r_n > x_n for every n. Must there exist a subsequence (x_{n_k}) whose achievement set E(x_{n_k}) is a Cantorval?
For a geometric sequence (q^n)_{n in N} with q in (1/2, 1), does there always exist a subsequence (q^{n_k})_{k in N} whose achievement set E(q^{n_k}) is a Cantorval?

Consider a multigeometric series (k_1, ..., k_m; 1/n) with integer coefficients k_i, with none of k_1, ..., k_m divisible by n, and let Sigma = {sigma_0 < ... < sigma_{n-1}} be the set of all subsums of {k_1, ..., k_m}, assumed to have exactly n elements. If the achievement set E(k_1, ..., k_m; 1/n) has positive Lebesgue measure and sigma_i is congruent to t_i modulo n with t_i < n, must the set of residues {t_i} equal {0, 1, ..., n-1}?
For every achievable Cantor set C, do there exist achievable Cantor sets C' and C'' such that the algebraic sum C + C' is again a Cantor set while C + C'' is a Cantorval?
For every achievable Cantor set C, do there exist achievable Cantorvals D' and D'' such that C + D' is a Cantorval while C + D'' is an interval?
For every achievable Cantorval D, do there exist achievable Cantorvals D' and D'' such that D + D' is a Cantorval while D + D'' is an interval?
Let C(a_n) be a central Cantor set determined by its ratios of dissection (a_n). If the difference set C(a_n) - C(a_n) has nonempty interior, must 0 belong to the interior of C(a_n)?
Is the Palis dichotomy generically true for central Cantor sets, meaning that the relevant sum or difference set generically either has measure zero or contains an interval?
Can every infinite achievable set be decomposed as the algebraic sum of two achievable sets of Hausdorff dimension 0?
Suppose E(x_n) is an achievement set such that E(x_n) + E(x_n) is a Cantor set. Must the Hausdorff dimension of E(x_n) be at least one half of the Hausdorff dimension of E(x_n) + E(x_n)?
Is the boundary of every achievable Cantorval itself an achievable set?
Do there exist two achievable Cantorvals E(x_n) and E(y_n) whose union E(x_n) union E(y_n) is a closed interval?
Do there exist achievable Cantorvals whose boundaries have positive Lebesgue measure?
Is there an achievable Cantorval E such that the Hausdorff dimension of its boundary Fr E is equal to 1? Is there an achievable Cantorval E such that the Hausdorff dimension of Fr E is equal to 0?

Is there an analogue of the Nymann-Saenz Lemma for endpoints of interval components of an achievable Cantorval? More concretely, if E(x_n) is a Cantorval and a and b are left endpoints of two distinct interval components of E, must there exist epsilon > 0 such that E intersect [a - epsilon, a] is a translate of E intersect [b - epsilon, b]?
Characterize which achievement sets in R^2 are homeomorphic to each other; equivalently, classify planar achievement sets up to homeomorphism.
context_brief: Achievement sets on the real plane

question_text: Find reasonable sufficient conditions ensuring that the planar achievement set E(x_n, y_n) has nonempty interior.
context_brief: Achievement sets on the real plane

question_text: For parameters p, q in (0, 1), characterize the two-dimensional achievement set E(p^n, q^n) consisting of all subsums of the vector series sum (p^n, q^n).
context_brief: Achievement sets on the real plane

question_text: Given an absolutely convergent series x = (x_n), let F_x(t) be the cardinality of the set of {0,1}-subseries representations of t. For which subsets C of {0, 1, 2, ..., omega, c} does there exist a sequence x whose cardinality function F_x has range exactly C?
Does there exist a sequence x for which the range of the cardinality function F_x contains an unbounded sequence of natural numbers but contains neither omega nor c?
Is it true that the set {t in R : F_x(t) = c} or the set {t in R : F_x(t) = omega}, whenever nonempty, must contain a Cantor set?

A sequence (x_n) is called a minimal representation of a Cantorval or a multi-interval set if removing any infinite subsequence changes the topological type of the achievement set. For an achievable Cantorval E, is it true that (x_n) is a minimal representation for E exactly when x_n < r_{n+1} for only finitely many n, as is already known for achievable multi-interval sets?
If A is a Borel subset of [0, infinity) containing 0, does there exist a Borel subset B of the real line whose center of distances C(B) is exactly A?
If C is a compact subset of [0, infinity) containing 0, does there exist a compact set K subset R whose center of distances C(K) is exactly C?

Let C be the central Cantor set generated by the fast convergent geometric sequence (q^n) with q in (0, 1/2), and let E(q^n) denote the adjoint Cantorval obtained by adjoining the gaps removed at odd-numbered steps. Compute the center of distances C(E(q^n)).
Do there exist fast convergent sequences (x_n) such that the adjoint Cantorval E(x_n) is achievable?

For an even integer m, which non-bipartite triangle-free graph with m edges has the largest spectral radius? Equivalently, among all non-bipartite graphs G with m edges and no C_3 subgraph, determine the extremal graph maximizing lambda(G).
For an even integer m, which non-bipartite graph with m edges, containing neither C_3 nor C_5 as a subgraph, has the maximum spectral radius?
Fix k >= 2 and an even integer m. Among all non-bipartite graphs with m edges that avoid every odd cycle C_3, C_5, ..., C_{2k+1}, which graph has the largest spectral radius?

Fix k >= 1. Does there exist an integer N(k) such that every non-bipartite graph G in G(m, {C_3, C_5, ..., C_{2k+1}}) with even m >= N(k) satisfies one of the three exact spectral extremal descriptions in Conjecture 2.11, according to the congruence class of m - (2k - 1) modulo 3?

Fix r >= 1. For all sufficiently large m, must every B_{2,r+1}-free graph G with m edges satisfy lambda(G) <= sqrt(m), with equality only for complete bipartite graphs? Here B_{2,r+1} = K_2 \/ ((r+1)K_1) is the book graph obtained from K_{2,r+1} by adding an edge between the two vertices of degree r+1.
For fixed r >= 1 and m edges, which B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graph has the largest spectral radius?

Fix r >= 1 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is a B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graph with m edges, is it true that lambda(G) is at most rho(m, r), where rho(m, r) is the largest root of x^3 - x^2 - (m - 1)x + m - 2r - 1 = 0, with equality exactly when m == 1 mod r and G is isomorphic to K^+_{r,(m-1)/r}?

Fix k >= 2. If G has m edges and contains neither C_{2k+1} nor C_{2k+2}, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2, for all sufficiently large m?
context_brief: Long odd and even cycle conjecture

question_text: Fix k >= 2. If G has m edges and contains neither theta_{1,2,2k-1} nor theta_{1,2,2k}, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2, for all sufficiently large m?
Fix k >= 3 and write m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k with 1 <= l <= k - 1. Which graph in G(m, theta_{1,2,2k-1}) union G(m, theta_{1,2,2k}) has the largest spectral radius?

For integers q >= p >= 3, what is the maximum spectral radius among graphs in G(m, theta_{1,p,q})? Equivalently, characterize the extremal graphs with m edges that avoid the theta graph formed by three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, p, and q between the same two endpoints.

Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is F_{k,3}-free, where F_{k,3} = K_1 \/ kK_2 is the friendship graph made of k triangles sharing a common vertex, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2?
For each t >= 5, what is the maximum spectral radius among all F_t-free graphs with m edges, and which extremal graphs attain that value, where F_t = K_1 \/ P_{t-1} is the fan graph on t vertices?

Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is F_{2k+1}-free or F_{2k+2}-free, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2?
For integers q >= p >= r >= 2, how can one characterize the graphs in G(m, theta_{r,p,q}) that have the largest spectral radius?

Fix k >= 2. Does there exist m_0 such that whenever m >= m_0 and G avoids both theta_{1,p,q} and theta_{1,r,s}, with q >= p >= 3, s >= r >= 3, p + q = 2k + 1, and r + s = 2k + 2, then for each residue class l with 1 <= l <= k - 1 and m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k, the graph G satisfies lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality only for that graph?

Fix k >= 2. Does there exist m_0 such that whenever m >= m_0 and G is F_{k,3}-free, then for each residue class l with 1 <= l <= k - 1 and m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k, the graph G satisfies lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality only for that extremal graph?

Fix k >= 2. Does there exist m_0 such that whenever m >= m_0 and G is F_{2k+2}-free, then for each residue class l with 1 <= l <= k - 1 and m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k, the graph G satisfies lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality only for that extremal graph?

Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is W_{2k+1}-free, where W_{2k+1} is the odd wheel on 2k+1 vertices, must the extremal graph for lambda(G) depend only on the residue class of m + k(k+1)/2 modulo k, taking the complete join K_k \/ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 in the divisible case and S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k} in the other residue classes?

Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G avoids every wheel W_t of order t >= 2k + 1, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2?
Let r >= 3 and let G be a K_{r+1}-free graph with m >= r + 1 edges. Must the sum of squares of the two largest adjacency eigenvalues satisfy lambda_1(G)^2 + lambda_2(G)^2 <= 2m(1 - 1/r)?
Fix r >= 3 and write m = ar + b with a a non-negative integer and 1 <= b <= r. Among all non-r-partite K_{r+1}-free graphs with m edges, which graph has the largest spectral radius?

Fix k >= 1 and r >= 3. For all sufficiently large m, if G is B_{r,k+1}-free, where B_{r,k+1} = K_r \/ (k+1)K_1 is the generalized book graph, must lambda(G) be at most sqrt(2m(r - 1)/r), with equality only for complete regular r-partite graphs?

Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is W_{2k+2}-free, where W_{2k+2} is the even wheel on 2k+2 vertices, must lambda(G) be at most sqrt(4m/3), with equality only for regular complete 3-partite graphs?
Given a color-critical graph F with chromatic number chi(F) = r + 1, determine the F-free graphs with m edges that attain the maximum spectral radius.

Fix a color-critical graph F with chromatic number chi(F) = r + 1 >= 4. For all sufficiently large m, what is the extremal graph with maximal spectral radius among all non-r-partite F-free graphs with m edges?
Does every doubly connected periodic Fatou component of a meromorphic function have to be a Herman ring, rather than some other kind of doubly connected periodic component?
context_brief: Characterization of doubly connected periodic Fatou components

question_text: A Siegel disk is guaranteed by the presence of a suitable periodic point, namely a Siegel point. Is there an analogous kind of point or other intrinsic dynamical marker whose existence would guarantee that the map has a Herman ring?

Which rational maps, especially in low degrees such as 3 and 4, admit Herman rings? More specifically, can one give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a Herman ring in terms of the map's degree, the configuration of critical orbits, and combinatorial data, and can one describe the associated parameter slices using tools such as Teichmuller theory and quasiconformal deformation theory?
context_brief: Classification of rational maps with Herman rings

question_text: How are Herman rings created or destroyed when a rational or transcendental map is perturbed, and what is the structure and size of the parameter sets in natural families for which Herman rings occur?

What geometric regularity can the boundary components of a Herman ring have? In particular, under what hypotheses are these boundaries Jordan curves or quasicircles, when can they have fractal structure, what can be said about their Hausdorff dimension or Lebesgue measure, and can a Herman-ring boundary ever have positive area?

Can one develop an obstruction theory and identify structural conditions under which a transcendental map with a Herman ring can be conformally mated with the action of a Fuchsian group or a subgroup of PSL(2, Z) on the upper half-plane? More specifically, when can a topological mating between the map and the group action be defined, when can that topological mating be promoted to a conformal one, and what dynamical feature distinguishes the resulting correspondence map when the function has a Herman ring?
context_brief: Conformal matings in the transcendental setting

question_text: Must every rational map that has a Herman ring also have buried Julia components, or are additional global dynamical or topological assumptions needed before the existence of a Herman ring forces buried Julia components to appear?
Does there exist a root-finding method, for instance among generalizations of Newton, Konig, or Chebyshev type methods, whose Fatou set contains a Herman ring?

Given a periodic Herman ring H of period p for a meromorphic function, can one prove an upper bound on p in terms of the number h of H-relevant poles, complementing the known lower bounds? This is especially asked for meromorphic maps with finitely many poles and at least one omitted value, such as functions of the form E(z)/((z-z0)(z-z1)...(z-zp)) where E is an entire function omitting a finite point.
context_brief: Upper bounds on period from relevant poles

question_text: For a meromorphic function with a stable Baker omitted value, can there be infinitely many Herman rings whose periods vary, even though for each fixed period p >= 3 the number of p-periodic Herman rings is known to be finite? In particular, can this happen when the Baker omitted value is the only accumulation point of the critical values?
context_brief: Infinitely many periods with stable bov

question_text: For each natural number n, is there a finite upper bound on the number of distinct geometric or combinatorial configurations that an n-cycle of Herman rings of period n can realize?
If a meromorphic function with an omitted value has a quasi-nested wandering domain, must that function necessarily have no Herman rings?
If a general transcendental meromorphic function has a finite omitted value, does that condition alone force the map to have no Herman rings of any period?
context_brief: Finite omitted values obstructing Herman rings

question_text: Can the K-moduli construction for K-semistable log Fano pairs be extended beyond characteristic 0, in particular to fields of positive characteristic or even to an arithmetic setting over Z, despite the current lack of general tools such as resolution of singularities and the minimal model program in those settings?
context_brief: K-moduli in positive and arithmetic settings

question_text: For integers n and d with 3 <= d <= n + 1, is every smooth degree d hypersurface in projective space P^{n+1} K-stable?
For integers n and d with 3 <= d <= n + 1, describe the K-moduli space H^K_{n,d} that parametrizes K-semistable degree d hypersurfaces of dimension n.
Given positive integers d_1, ..., d_k with k + 2 <= sum_i d_i <= n + k, is a general complete intersection of multidegree (d_1, ..., d_k) K-stable?

Let M_{d,r}(C) be the moduli space of rank r polystable vector bundles with fixed determinant of degree d on a smooth projective curve C of genus g, in the case gcd(r, d) = 1 so that M_{d,r}(C) is a smooth Fano variety. Is M_{d,r}(C) K-stable for every such curve C, and can one give a modular interpretation of the limiting points of the K-moduli space X_g that contains [M_{d,r}(C)] and is birational to M_g?
If X is a smooth Fano threefold with Picard rank rho(X) = 1, must X be K-semistable?
context_brief: Fano threefolds of Picard rank one

question_text: If X is a smooth Gushel-Mukai Fano variety of dimension n with 3 <= n <= 6, must X be K-stable?

Let X be a Fano variety. Can one give a purely algebraic proof that if X is K-semistable then its tangent sheaf T_X is semistable with respect to the polarization -K_X, and also a purely algebraic proof that if T_X is polystable then there exists a quasi-etale cover f: Y -> X with Y = product_i X_i and T_Y = f^*(T_X) = direct-sum_i T_{X_i}, where each T_{X_i} is stable with respect to -K_Y?

Let X be a Fano variety and let 0 -> Omega_X^[1] -> E -> O_X -> 0 be the canonical extension determined by the image of c_1(X) in H^1(X, Omega_X^[1]). Can one give a purely algebraic proof that if X is K-semistable then E is semistable with respect to -K_X, and if X is K-polystable then E is polystable with respect to -K_X?

Let x in X be a symplectic singularity. Must the minimizer of the normalized volume be given by a Kollár component E over x, where a Kollár component means an exceptional divisor E extracted by a projective morphism Y -> X with (Y, E) purely log terminal and -E ample over X? If so, must its discrepancy satisfy A_X(E) = r n for r = 1 or 2, and must the underlying log Fano pair (E, Delta_E) be K-polystable?
If x in X is a singular point of dimension n, must its normalized volume satisfy vol-hat(x, X) <= 2 (n - 1)^n, with equality only for the A_1 singularity?

Fix a klt pair (X, Delta). Is there a positive constant epsilon such that for every (K_X + Delta)-nonnegative birational map X --> X' and every point x in X', the normalized volume vol-hat(x, X', Delta') is at least epsilon?
context_brief: Local volume lower bounds in MMP

question_text: Let x in (X = Spec(R), Delta) be a germ of a klt singularity, let a_bullet be a graded sequence of m_x-primary ideals, let c = lct(X, Delta; a_bullet), and let LCP(X, Delta + c a_bullet) be the set of valuations v with c = A_{X,Delta}(v) / v(a_bullet). Are all valuations in this set quasi-monomial, and more strongly, does there exist a log smooth model (Y, E) -> X such that LCP(X, Delta + c a_bullet) is contained in QM(Y, E) and forms a cone over a connected convex set?
context_brief: Valuations computing lct of graded ideals

question_text: Develop software to generate benchmark parameterized linear systems that are generally accepted as relevant in practice and suitable for theoretical analysis.
For each class of parameterized benchmark linear systems, develop theoretically and practically fast algorithms.

Algebraic Multigrid Analysis for Theoretical Computer Scientists: Show that for polynomially bounded SWCDDM matrices $M$, Algebraic Multigrid runs in time $~O(nnz(M))$ to compute an (implicitly represented) symmetric matrix $Z$, which can be applied in $O(nnz(M))$ time, and satisfies the condition that $ Omega(1) M^-1 Z O(1) M^-1$. In particular, the constants are independent of the problem size $n$.

Polynomially decaying eigenvalues: Fix constants $epsilon > 0$ and $p > 0$. Let $A_n C^n x n$, $n>= 1$, be a sequence of random positive definite matrices constructed via A_n = U Lambda_n U*, where U C^n x n is Haar unitary, Lambda_n = diag 1^-p, 2^-p, ..., n^-p . Let $b_n = A_n z_n$ be a sequence of random vectors where $z_n C^n$ is distributed uniformly on the sphere. What is the asymptotic behavior of $T_ CG(A_n,b_n,epsilon)$ compared with $T_ RCD(A_n,b_n,epsilon)$ as $n -> infinity$?
Can we solve an $(n,k,0,kappa)$ linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy using $~ O(k^omega + nnz(A)kappa)$ arithmetic operations?

Find the smallest $p>0$ such that we can solve an $n x n$ linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy using $~ O(T_A*bar kappa_p)$ arithmetic operations, where $bar kappa_p$ is the $p$-averaged condition number of the singular values of $A$, whereas $T_A$ is either $n^2$ or $nnz(A)$.
What is the complexity of solving $(n,0,l,kappa)$ linear systems, and how is this affected by the model of computation (direct access vs matrix-vector product)?

Let $A$ be an $n x n$ random matrix with i.i.d. Gaussian (or Rademacher, or Bernoulli) entries, and take any $n$-dimensional vector $b$. Is it possible (conditioned on a high-probability event) to solve the linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy faster than $O(n^omega)$?
What is the bit complexity of solving $(n,k,l,kappa)$ linear systems? In particular, does the $~ O(k^omega + n^2kappa)$ running time for $(n,k,0,kappa)$ systems extend to the Word-RAM model?
What is the bit complexity of solving an $n x n$ linear system with $nnz(A)$ non-zeros? In particular, does the $~ O(n* nnz(A))$ runtime extend to the Word-RAM model.
Several specific open problems that exist in this context are mentioned in~. More generally, try to extend the approach in~ to other types of PDEs or preconditioners.
Develop a descriptive convergence bound for GMRES applied to nonnormal linear algebraic systems, that particularly describes the (transient) behavior early in the iteration.

Find an interesting (nonselfdajoint resp. nonsymmetric) model problem, where the theoretical result on the eigenvalue distribution of the preconditioned matrix indeed corresponds to the actual convergence behavior of GMRES (e.g., $M^-1A$ has $m$ eigenvalue clusters and an acceptable approximate solution is obtained by GMRES in $ O(m)$ steps). Determine which particular properties of the problem implied this correspondence.

Explain the convergence acceleration of GMRES after the initial (transient) phase that is observed in some convection-diffusion model problems such as the one in~. In particular, explain whether or not the speed of convergence can be related to eigeninformation (i.e., eigenvalue location and eigenvector conditioning) of the discretized convection-diffusion operators.

Taking the above recurrences to represent the CG or steepest descent algorithm, determine conditions on $A$ that will insure that the norms of the vectors $r_k$ drop below the machine precision in finite precision arithmetic or show some examples where they do not.

Show that the CG and Lanczos algorithms do or do not behave similarly in finite precision arithmetic when used to solve a symmetric positive definite linear system. This will, of course, depend on the implementation of each method, so use standard good implementations of both.

How many bits of precision are necessary to guarantee that CG applied to an $n$ by $n$ SPD linear system $Ax=b$ obtains an approximate solution with normwise backward error at most $epsilon$ in $n$ (or fewer) steps?

Analyze the Lanczos algorithm under general models of inexact matrix-vector multiplication and/or the use of a preconditioner. Progress is made if these bounds generalize Paige's analysis and/or provide new, easier to understand, insight into the behavior of the algorithm.

Extend Paige's analysis of the Lanczos algorithm to the block Lanczos algorithm. The exact analysis will depend on the use of an orthogonalization scheme used within blocks, so either specify certain assumptions on the accuracy of the scheme, or analyze a standard ``good'' algorithm.

Deterministic Pseudospectral Shattering: Give a provably correct and efficient deterministic algorithm for the following task: on input $A C^n x n$ and $delta>0$, output a perturbation $E$ with $ |E | delta$ such that $kappa_eig(A+E) C(delta/n)^c$, where $C,c$ are universal constants. In this context, efficient means $O(n^3 ^c(n/delta))$ arithmetic operations, either in exact arithmetic or, more ambitiously, in finite arithmetic with $O( ^c(n/delta))$ bits of precision.

Deterministic Minami Perturbation: Minami showed that if $A$ is $n x n$ Hermitian tridiagonal and $E$ is a random diagonal matrix with independent absolutely continuous entries, then $gap(A+delta E) C(delta/n)^c$ for some constants $C,c$ depending on the distribution of the entries. Give an efficient deterministic algorithm for finding such a perturbation. Here, efficient means faster than the parent algorithm in which it is used, so $O(n^3 ^c(n/delta))$ for diagonalization and, ambitiously, $O(nnz(A) ^c(n/delta))$ or $O(nnz(A) ^c(n)/delta^c)$ for Krylov methods.
Give a provable randomized algorithm for backward error diagonalization or Schur form with runtime $O(n^3 ^c(n/delta))$ that only uses $O( (n/delta))$ bits of precision.

For a given $A ^n x n$, let $ V$ denote an approximate invariant subspace of dimension $d$ of $A$, in the sense that there exists some $d$-dimensional invariant subspace $ V$ of $A$ such that $ ( V, V)$ is small. Let $ W$ be some other subspace of dimension $r<n-d$. Suppose the columns of $Q$ form an orthonormal basis for the (generically) $d+r$ dimensional space $ Q = V + W$. Provide conditions that will ensure that $d$ eigenvalues of $Q*AQ$ approximate the $d$ eigenvalues of $A$ associated with the invariant subspace $ V$. Impose assumptions about the eigenvalues of $A$ corresponding to $ V$, as needed.

Let $Q$ be an orthonormal basis for a Krylov space for arbitrary $A ^n x n$ with random starting vector $b$. Is $kappa_V(Q*AQ)$ bounded (by a polynomial in $n$) with high probability? Or is $ [ _ (Q*AQ)]$ (the expected value of the area in $ $ of the $epsilon$-pseudospectrum) bounded by $ (n) ^beta$ for $beta$ close to 2? (This problem is open even when $A$ is a circulant shift matrix.)

Consider a non-Hermitian $A ^n x n$ and suppose $Q ^n x k$ has orthonormal columns. We know that the Ritz values (eigenvalues of $Q*AQ$) are located in the numerical range, $W(A) = v*Av: |v |_2=1 $, a closed, convex subset of $ $ that contains the eigenvalues of $A$ (and, potentially, points far from these eigenvalues). What can be said (deterministically or probabalistically) about the distribution of the Ritz values across $W(A)$ for $1<k<n$? What if $Q$ is restricted to be a basis for a Krylov subspace? What if $Q$ is the basis for a random subspace?
Give a ``TCS-style'' analysis of MR$^3$ which proves its correctness and convergence under easily verifiable conditions on the input.

Let $B$ be an $n x n$ (upper) bidiagonal matrix. Is there an algorithm that, in $O(kn)$ operations, can produce $k$ triples $(sigma_i,v_i,u_i)$ such that $sigma_i >= 0$, $v_i, u_i C^n$ are unit vectors, and, for machine precision $epsilon$, $ |Bv_i-sigma_iu_i |_2 = O(epsilon n |B |_2)$; $|v_i^Hv_j|$, $|u_i^Hu_j| = O(epsilon n)$ if $i != j$.

Consider a general nonnormal matrix $A = V Lambda V^-1$ with largest eigenvalue magnitude $lambda_1$ and finite eigenvector condition number $kappa_V = |V | |V^-1 |$. Is there an algorithm that uses $ ( (nkappa_V),1/epsilon)$ matrix-vector products with $A$ and returns $lambda$ so that $|lambda - lambda'| epsilon |lambda_1|$, where $lambda'$ is any eigenvalue of $A$ with $|lambda' | (1-epsilon) lambda_1$?
Prove stronger theoretical bounds for GECP applied to $K$, by exploiting the structure of the kernel $K$.
Does the QRCP algorithm typically used in practice satisfy the above, or a similar, bound.

Consider selecting $r = O(k)$ uniformly random row indices $I$ and then choosing column indices $~J$ so that $A(I,:) A(I,~J) ~T$. What are sufficient conditions on $r$ and on the kernel $f$ which guarantee that | _~J A - A |_F <= c(n, m, k) | _J A - A |_F with high probability, where $c(n, m, k)$ grows at most logarithmically in its arguments? In other words, when does column selection on a random subset of the rows perform similarly to column selection on the full matrix?

Consider $n$ positive real numbers $lambda$, and consider the set of all $n x n$ orthonormal matrices $S$. Prove a tightness bound(s) between the (1) trace error of the optimal column subset selection of the worst case matrix $K$ possessing eigenvalues $lambda$: x_k (lambda) := _V S _ [n], | | = k K - K_:, K_ , ^-1 K_ ,: _K=V^ -> p diag(lambda) V and (2) the objective yielded by volume sampling any such $K$: y_k (lambda) := (E_ k-DPP(K) K- K_:, K_ , ^-1 K_ , :) _K=diag(lambda) = (k+1) e_k+1 (lambda)e_k(lambda) which is dependent on $lambda$ alone in terms of the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_k$.

Sketch-and-solve: Let (A R^n x d ) be a full-rank matrix, (B R^n x p ) be a matrix, and let (Omega R^n x k ) be an oblivious subspace injection with dimension $d$ and injectivity (1-epsilon ). Let (~ X = (Omega^ -> p A)^+(Omega^ -> p B) R^d x p ) be the sketch-and-solve approximation to the ordinary least-squares solution $X = A^+B$. (Here, $^+$ denotes the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse.) Prove or disprove: Does it necessarily hold that [ |A ~ X - B |_ F <= (1+O(epsilon)) _X R^d x p |AX - B |_ F? ]

Randomized SVD: Let (A R^n x d ) be a matrix, fix $r > 0$, and let (Omega R^n x k ) be an oblivious subspace injection with dimension $r$ and injectivity (1-epsilon ). Let $~A = (AOmega)(AOmega)^+A$ denote the randomized SVD approximation to $A$, and let $A_r$ be the best rank-$r$ approximation to $A$ with respect to the Frobenius norm. Prove or disprove: Does it necessarily hold that [ |A - ~A |_ F <= (1+O(epsilon)) |A-A_r |_ F? ]

Regression in the $\ell_p$ norm: Consider the $ell_p$ linear regression problem minimize_x R^d |Ax - b |_ell_p for a matrix (A R^n x d ) and a vector (b R^n ). For a sketching matrix (Omega R^n x k ), the sketch-and-solve solution is [~ x argmin_x R^d |(Omega^ -> p Ax)-(Omega^ -> p b) |_ell_p. ] Formulate a generalization of the OSI property to the $ell_p$ regression problem which ensures that this procedure succeeds to constant-factor accuracy [ |A ~ x - b |_ell_p <= const* _x R^d |Ax - b |_ell_p. ]

Nelson--Nguyen conjecture: Subspace embedding properties of sparse random matrices: Prove or disprove the Nelson--Nguyen conjecture: A SparseStack embedding with parameters $ = O(( r) / epsilon)$ and $k = O(r / epsilon^2)$ is an oblivious subspace embedding with parameters $alpha = 1 - epsilon$ and $beta = 1+epsilon$.

Subspace injection properties of sparse random matrices: Assume the condition $r O(n/ n)$ relating the subspace dimension $r$ and the ambient dimension $n$. Prove or disprove: A SparseStack embedding with parameters $ = O(1)$ and $k = O(r)$ is an oblivious subspace injection with parameter $alpha = const$. More specifically, do parameters $ = 4$ and $k = 2r$ suffice to achieve the OSI property (for all sufficiently large $r$)?

Rerandomized subsampled trigonometric transforms: Assume that $n = Omega( r)$. Prove or disprove: The rerandomized SRHT of dimension $k = O(r/epsilon^2)$ is an oblivious subspace embedding with $alpha = 1-epsilon$ and $beta = 1+epsilon$.

Given any choice of $m$-node tree tensor network (e.g., tensor train or Tucker) and choice of ranks (dimensions of edges in the tensor network), let the set of representable tensors in this tensor network be $S R^d_1 x *s x d_n$. Find a polynomial-time algorithm that takes as input any tensor $A R^d_1 x *s x d_n$ and yields an approximation $X S$ such that [ |X-A |_F^2 < (m-1) _Y S |Y-A |_F^2, ] or show that an $(m-1)$-approximation is optimal under complexity-theoretic assumptions.
What is the asymptotic error $epsilon_m*$ as a function of $m$ and $delta$?

In the planar magnetic billiard model, where a particle moves inside a billiard table along Larmor circles determined by a strong constant magnetic field, is every totally integrable magnetic billiard necessarily the circular billiard?

Let N be a smooth convex curve in R^2, and consider the Minkowski billiard in the unit ball of the norm N, defined by the generating function L(s0, s1) = N(gamma(s1) - gamma(s0)) with gamma parameterized by N-arc length. If this Minkowski billiard is totally integrable, must the norm N be Euclidean?

Consider Newton's equation u'' = -V'_u(u,t) with V periodic in both u and t. Besides the special case V = V(nu + mt), for which the system is known to be totally integrable near infinity, are there other potential functions V for which the system is totally integrable at infinity?

Consider the elliptic equation Delta u = -V'_u(u, x1, ..., xn), where V is 1-periodic in u, x1, ..., xn. Suppose that for every rotation vector alpha in R^n there exists a foliation of T^(n+1) by graphs of minimal solutions of slope alpha. Does it follow that V does not depend on u?
Let (N, g) be an orientable closed hyperbolic surface. Is the Hofer-Zehnder capacity of the unit disk cotangent bundle (D^*N, d lambda) finite?

If N is a closed hyperbolic surface and Omega_i are embedded simply connected billiard tables in N, does there exist a sequence Omega_i for which the length of the shortest closed billiard trajectory Omega_i-sys tends to infinity as i tends to infinity?

For a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism on a closed symplectic manifold, is it true that either the number of periodic orbits is finite or the number P(T) of primitive periodic orbits of period at most T grows at least quadratically, in the sense that lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2?

Does the quadratic lower bound lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2 hold for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism on a standard symplectic torus? More generally, does it hold on every aspherical closed symplectic manifold?
If a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of CP^n has infinitely many periodic orbits, must those periodic orbits satisfy the quadratic growth bound lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2?
Find physically interesting infinite-dimensional billiard systems, ideally arising from equations of mathematical physics such as fluid dynamics or other Euler-Arnold type geodesic equations.

Do there exist nontrivial integrable pensive billiards, meaning pensive billiard systems with a nonzero delay function for which one can exhibit explicit choices of boundary curve and delay that yield integrable dynamics?

Construct a continuous theory for particles with positive and negative mass, or equivalently for billiards in pseudo-Euclidean metrics, and determine whether the resulting Euler-like equations for a fluid of negative density exhibit interesting phenomena.
Characterize which fiber-wise convex domains in T^*S^n arise as billiard domains W_T associated with convex billiard tables T in R^(n+1).
Characterize which C^0-Hamiltonian self-maps of a fiber-wise convex domain W in T^*S^n arise as billiard maps of convex billiard tables.

Let M be a closed manifold that is not a K(pi,1), and let Sigma be a closed connected hypersurface in T^*M that is a regular energy level of a Hamiltonian H: T^*M -> R. Is there always some epsilon > 0 such that almost all energy levels of H in the interval (c - epsilon, c + epsilon) carry a contractible periodic orbit of H?

Within the class of tiling billiards in periodic tilings, is there a finite list of generic archetypal behaviors? In particular, does a general dichotomy hold in which typical trajectories are either dense in open sets or integrable in the sense of being periodic or linearly escaping?

Describe the dynamics of generic trajectories in parallelogram tiling billiards, where the plane is tiled by parallelograms with side vectors a_vec = (a, 0) and b_vec = (b sin alpha, b cos alpha) and the dynamics depends on the parameters alpha in (0, pi) and m = a/b.
Provide examples of real-world systems from areas such as physics, mechanics, biology, or economics that can be modeled as locally conformal symplectic flows or maps.

For the locally conformal symplectic cotangent-bundle equations of motion dot x = partial_p H + (p dot dot x - H) eta_p_bar and dot p = -partial_x H + f p - (p dot dot x - H) eta_x_bar, is there a physical example realizing this framework, and what is the physical or mechanical meaning of these equations?

Assume eta_p_bar = 0 so that eta is pulled back from the base manifold, and assume H is a Tonelli Hamiltonian so that the equations become dot x = partial_p H and dot p = -partial_x H + f p - L(x, dot x) eta_x_bar. What physical interpretation, if any, should be assigned to the term -L(x, dot x) eta_x_bar?
For a projective billiard, when does the system possess an invariant symplectic form, and when does it admit a variational description?

Given a closed immersed submanifold M of Euclidean space, estimate from below the number of generalized n-periodic billiard trajectories, meaning inscribed n-gons with vertices on M that have extremal perimeter, in terms of the topology of M and the immersion.

Study the complexity function of polygonal symplectic billiards, where the complexity p(n) counts the number of length-n subwords arising from symbolic codings of billiard trajectories by polygon sides.
Do there exist chaotic symplectic billiards in convex C^1-smooth domains?
How restrictive is the condition that the characteristic curves on a smooth hypersurface in standard symplectic space are planar?

In a domain with smooth boundary in Euclidean space, fix a generic interior point P and consider the time-t front consisting of light rays emitted from P in all directions, reflected specularly at the boundary, and evolved for time t. Does this time-t front become dense as t tends to infinity?
Prove Ivrii's conjecture for 3-periodic multidimensional outer symplectic billiards with respect to a strictly convex closed hypersurface.

When a smooth convex closed curve is approximated by n-gons and the quality of approximation is measured by the area of the symmetric difference, is the resulting function of n related to some billiard-like dynamical system?

How can one characterize the optical symplectic transformations of the space of oriented lines, namely the local symplectic transformations realizable by finite collections of mirrors, inside the full space of symplectic transformations of the space of oriented lines?

For a compact Riemann surface X of genus g >= 2 and the moduli space SU_X(r) of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, let L denote the determinant line bundle on SU_X(r). The base locus of the linear system |L| consists of those bundles E such that h^0(X, E ⊗ M) ≠ 0 for every line bundle M of degree g-1 on X. Beyond the examples constructed by Raynaud, for which other ranks r do such base points occur, can this base locus have positive dimension, and can one obtain a reasonable upper bound for its dimension?
context_brief: Base locus of the determinant linear system

question_text: For the same determinant line bundle L on SU_X(r), is the square linear system |L^2| always base-point free?

Given a vector bundle E in SU_X(r), does there exist an etale covering π: Y → X such that the theta divisor of the pullback bundle, θ(π^*E) = { M in J^{g(Y)-1}(Y) | h^0(Y, π^*E ⊗ M) ≥ 1 }, is a proper divisor rather than the whole Jacobian J^{g(Y)-1}(Y)?
context_brief: Etale covers and pullback theta divisors

question_text: Let X be a non-hyperelliptic curve, and let θ: SU_X(2) \dashrightarrow |2Θ| be the theta map sending a rank-2 semistable bundle E with trivial determinant to the divisor { L in J^{g-1}(X) | h^0(X, E ⊗ L) ≥ 1 }. Is this map always an embedding?
context_brief: Embedding property of the rank-2 theta map

question_text: Can one find a direct proof of the Verlinde formula for dim H^0(SU_X(r), L^k), namely dim H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) = (r/(r+k))^g ∑_{S⊎T=[1,r+k], |S|=r} ∏_{s∈S, t∈T} |2 sin(π(s-t)/(r+k))|^{g-1}, for example by applying Riemann-Roch once the needed Chern numbers of the moduli space are understood?
context_brief: Direct proof of the Verlinde formula

question_text: Let U^*_X(k) be the moduli space of semistable vector bundles on X of rank k and degree k(g-1), let Θ_k = { F in U^*_X(k) | h^0(X, F) ≠ 0 }, and let M = O(Θ_k). For the tensor-product map τ_{k,r}: SU_X(r) × U^*_X(k) → U^*_X(kr), the pullback of the canonical theta divisor defines a linear map ϑ_{k,r}: H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) → H^0(U^*_X(k), M^r)^*. Is ϑ_{k,r} always an isomorphism, equivalently, is |L^k| spanned by the divisors Θ_F = { E in SU_X(r) | h^0(X, E ⊗ F) ≠ 0 } as F ranges over U^*_X(k)?
context_brief: Strange duality for generalized theta functions

question_text: As the smooth curve X of genus g varies, the flat projective bundle with fibers |L_X^k| over the moduli space M_g defines a projective representation ρ_{r,k}: Γ_g → PGL(H^0(SU_X(r), L^k)), where Γ_g = π_1(M_g, X) is the mapping class group. What is this representation?
context_brief: Mapping-class-group representation from the projective connection

question_text: Can one construct a flat Hermitian metric H_X on H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) such that the image of the projective monodromy representation ρ_{r,k} is contained in the projective unitary group PU(H_X)?
context_brief: Unitary structure on the projective connection

question_text: Is there a sufficiently simple and flexible way to realize the generalized theta functions in H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) as holomorphic functions, analogous to how classical theta functions describe sections of O(kΘ) on a Jacobian?
context_brief: Holomorphic realization of generalized theta functions

question_text: Let f : C^n -> V be a finite morphism from complex affine n-space onto a normal affine variety V. Must V be contractible?

Classify, up to the equivalence relation p = beta o q o alpha where alpha is a polynomial automorphism of C^2 and beta is an affine automorphism of C, all primitive polynomials p(x, y) in two complex variables that have a fiber isomorphic to C^*.

Let A be an Artin local ring over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, finite-dimensional over k. Is the length of the module of Kahler differentials always at least l(A) - 1, and does equality hold exactly when A is isomorphic to k[x]/x^n?

Let A be an Artin local ring over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, and let M be a finitely generated A-module. If D(M) denotes the A-module of k-derivations from A to M and s(M) denotes the socle of M, is l(D(M)) always at least l(M) - l(s(M)), and does equality hold exactly when A is isomorphic to k[x]/x^n and M is free?

Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let R be a finitely generated noetherian K-algebra domain, let L = Q(R), and let delta be a K-derivation of R. If X_delta^f denotes the abelian group of all delta-integral factors occurring for delta-integral elements of L, must X_delta^f be a finitely generated abelian group?

Classify all K-derivations delta of general type on the polynomial ring R = K[x, y], where "general type" means that A_0 = {x in R : delta(x) = 0} and L_0 = {xi in Q(R) : delta(xi) = 0} both equal K, and describe such derivations in terms of the delta-integral ring A generated by delta-integral elements.

Let A be a purely inseparable form of the polynomial ring k^[n] over a field k, meaning that A becomes isomorphic to K^[n] after base change to the perfect closure K of k. If A is k-rational, or more strongly if its quotient field is birationally contained in k^[n], must A already be a trivial form?
context_brief: Purely inseparable forms of affine space

question_text: Let (A, M) be a regular local ring and let B = A[a/b], where a is in M \ M^2, b is in M^2, and gcd(a, b) = 1 so that B is regular. Under what conditions is the ideal MB a complete intersection in B?

Suppose a polynomial p in two variables over C has smooth, irreducible, rational zero set. Must p be a factor of a field generator, equivalently, does there exist a polynomial q such that the generic fiber of pq is rational?
context_brief: Rational zero sets and field generators

question_text: Classify all rational cuspidal plane curves and all elliptic cuspidal plane curves.
What is the maximal possible number of cusps among rational cuspidal plane curves?
Can one prove that there is no counterexample (f, g) to the Jacobian Conjecture with both f and g lying in the subring C[Y, XY, X^2Y, X^3Y - X]?
Let X be a smooth contractible complex affine algebraic surface of log-general type. Does X contain any once-punctured curve?
Let X be a smooth contractible complex affine algebraic surface of log-general type. Does X contain only finitely many once-punctured curves, up to isomorphism?

Let X be a smooth contractible algebraic surface with a proper embedding X -> C^N, let phi(x) = ||x||^2 on X, and for sufficiently large R let X_R = {phi < R^2}, so that X_R is a strictly pseudoconvex domain in X with real-algebraic boundary. If X is not isomorphic to C^2, must X_R fail to be biholomorphic to a bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain in C^2?
If a homology sphere S occurs as the boundary of a strictly pseudoconvex domain in C^2, must S be diffeomorphic to the 3-sphere S^3?
context_brief: Homology spheres bounding domains in C^2

question_text: Must every smooth Q-acyclic surface of log-general type be rigid?

Let X be a smooth Q-acyclic surface of log-general type, and let (V, D) be a minimal SNC-completion with X = V - D, where V is smooth projective and D is a simple normal crossings divisor. Must K_V (K_V + D) = 0, equivalently, since D is a rational tree, must the logarithmic Chern number c_1^2(X) = (K_V + D)^2 equal -2?

Is the set of all Eisenbud-Neumann diagrams of the boundary divisors D arising from minimal smooth SNC-completions of contractible surfaces, or of acyclic surfaces, or of Q-acyclic surfaces, of log-general type finite?
Let X be a smooth acyclic surface such that for every non-constant regular function p in C[X] there exists q in C[X] with F = (p, q) : X -> C^2 a proper morphism. Must X be isomorphic to C^2?
For n > 3, does there exist a smooth contractible hypersurface in C^n whose logarithmic Kodaira dimension is of general type?
Let p in C[x_1, ..., x_n] define a contractible hypersurface X = {p = 0} in C^n. Must p be an isotrivial polynomial, meaning that its generic fibers are pairwise isomorphic hypersurfaces in C^n?
Which polynomials on C^2 are projectively isotrivial, in the sense that their generic fibers all have isomorphic smooth projective models?
If X = {p = 0} is a contractible hypersurface and X has an isolated singular point, must p be equivalent, up to an automorphism of C^3, to a quasihomogeneous polynomial?
Over a field k of positive characteristic, classify all regular injections of the affine line A^1_k into the affine plane A^2_k.
