source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let f (z) be analytic in a simply-connected domain D. It is known that f (z) can be expanded in a series of Faber polynomials ∞ X f (z) = an Pn (z). n=0 Find the domain of variability V of an as f (z) runs through all functions analytic in D, and having positive real part there. It is known that if D is a circle, V is a circle; and if D is an ellipse, then V is an ellipse, see Royster [677]. (W. C. Royster)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: If z1 = 1, and the zi are arbitrary complex numbers for 2 ≤ i ≤ n, then Atkinson [35] proved that max |Sk | > c 1≤k≤n with c = 13 . What is the best value for the constant c?

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: We consider the range of the random function ∞ X F (z) = ±an z n n=0 P (F chosen at random in the natural way) defined in D, where |an |2 = ∞. Is the image of w = F (z) with probability one (a) everywhere dense in the plane? (b) the whole plane? (c) does it contain any given point with probability one? If an = nλ , (b) holds if λ > 12 , and (a) holds if − 21 < λ < + 12 . (J. P. Kahane)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let f (z) = n=0 an z n X fn (z) = ak z k , k=0 and let Γn be the modulus of the largest zero of fn (z). Then Kakeya (no citation) showed that lim inf n→∞ Γn ≤ A, with A√= 2. What is the best possible value of A? Clunie and Erdös [162] have shown that 2 < A < 2.

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Is it possible to express each K-quasiconformal map in 3-space as the composition of two quasiconformal maps with maximal dilatation less than K? The corresponding plane result is true. (F. W. Gehring)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Suppose that f is a plane K-quasiconformal mapping of the unit disc D onto itself. Show that there exists a finite constant b = b(K) such that m(f (E)) ≤ b{m(E)}1/K for each measurable set E ⊂ D. Here m denotes plane Lebesgue measure. Such an inequality is known (see [303]) with the exponent K replaced by a constant a = a(K). (F. W. Gehring)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: It was proved by Boyarskiı̆ [111] that the partial derivatives of a plane K-quasiconformal mapping are locally L-integrable for 2 ≤ p < 2 + c, where c = c(K) > 0. Show that this is true with c = K−1 . The example f (z) = |z| K −1 .z shows that such a result would be sharp. (F. W. Gehring)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Show that each quasiconformal mapping of Rn onto Rn has a quasiconformal extension to Rn+1 . This has been established by Ahlfors when n = 2 and by Carleson when n = 3. (F. W. Gehring)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Suppose that f is an n-dimensional K-quasi-analytic function. Show that the partial derivatives of f are locally L-integrable for n ≤ p ≤ n + c, where c = c(K, n) > 0. This was shown by Gehring [297] to be true if f is injective. (F. W. Gehring)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: One part of Nevanlinna theory is devoted to the following problem. How does the geometric structure of a simply connected Riemann covering surface of the sphere influence the value distribution of the meromorphic function generating the surface? It is suggested that one also consider halfsheets among the constituent pieces of such surfaces, which have an infinite number of branch points on their boundary. A typical example is the covering surface generated by ez − z. It contains a right half-plane with a second order branch point at 2πin for each integer n. (F. Huckeman)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: (Boundary values of Cauchy integrals). Let γ be a C 1 curve in the plane and let f be a continuous function on γ. Put Z f (t) F (z) = dt (z ∈ / γ). γ −z t Does F have non-tangential boundary values almost everywhere on γ? This is a very old question which has been studied quite extensively, especially by Russian mathematicians. It is known that the answer is ‘yes’ if slightly greater smoothness is assumed for γ or f (see e.g. Havin [380] for an outstanding contribution to this subject). Suppose now that γ is a Jordan curve and let φ be a conformal map from the unit disc onto the inside of γ. Does F ◦ φ belong to H p for some p < 1, or perhaps to the class N of functions with bounded Nevanlinna characteristic? (A. Baernstein)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let f (z) be analytic and bounded for ℜzP> 0. Suppose that |α| < 12 π and that (rn ) is a sequence of positive integers with rn = ∞. Show that the exponential type of f on the sequence zn = rn eiα is equal to the type of f on the ray z = reiα . (Proofs by Boas [102] and by Levinson [516] for α = 0 do not seem to work for |α| > 14 π.) (J. Korevaar)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let Γ be a Jordan curve and suppose that z = 0 lies inside it. Wermer [786] showed that when Γ has infinite length, the powers z n , n 6= 0 span all of C(Γ). One can indicate conditions on Γ under which the powers z n , n 6= n1 , . . . , nk , form a spanning set (see Korevaar and Pfluger, [488]). Under what conditions on Γ can one omit an infinite set of powers, and still have a spanning set? (J. Korevaar)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: For what sets Ω of lattice points (mk , nk ) do the monomials xmk y nk span L2 orPC0 on the unit square 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1? It is conjectured that the condition mk nk = ∞ is sufficient for sets Ω in an angle εx ≤ y ≤ x/ε, ε > 0. Hellerstein [425] has shown that the condition is not necessary. (J. Korevaar)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: (Two constant theorems for the polydisc) Let F (z1 , z2 ) be defined for |z1 ≤ 1, |z2 | ≤ 2 except when z1 = z2 and |z1 | = |z2 | = 1. Suppose that F is plurisubharmonic in |z1 | < 1, |z2 | < 1 and that F (z1 , z2 ) ≤ log |z1 −z 2| , whenever the left hand side is defined. Further, suppose that F (z1 , z2 ) ≤ 0 for {|z1 | = |z2 | = 1, z1 6= z2 }. Does it follow that F (z1 , z2 ) ≤ 0 for |z1 | < 1, |z2 | < 1? (L. A. Rubel, A. Shields)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Suppose that |zk | = 1 (1 ≤ k < ∞). Put m X Al = lim sup zkl . m→∞ k=1 It is easy to see that there is a sequence zk , for which Al < cl for all l, and Clunie [160] proved Al > cl 2 for infinitely many l. Is there a sequence for which Al = o(l) as l → ∞? (P. Erdös)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Suppose that A and B are disjoint linked Jordan curves in R3 which lie at a distance 1 from each other. Show that the length of A is at least 2π. The corresponding result with a positive absolute constant instead of 2π is due to Gehring [298]. (F. W. Gehring)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let E = {|z| < 1}, let 0, a > 0, b = |b|eiβ (−π < β ≤ π) be distinct points of E; and let K be the family of continua K with the properties that {a, b} ⊂ K ⊂ E \ {0} and E \ K is connected. On any K ∈ K there is a continuous function arg z; we thus subdivide K into homotopy classes {Kn } according to the value of V (K) = arg b − arg a ∈ {β + 2nπ, n ∈ Z}. Let us call K ∈ K a natural continuum if K is a trajectory of a quadratic differential a with the following properties: (a) 0, a, b are simple poles of σ, and there is no other pole of σ in E; (b) σ is real on ∂E. There are many problems that then arise, for example: (i) Do all homotopy classes contain natural continua? (There are many in Kn when |β + 2nπ| < 2π.) (ii) Find all natural continua in K. (iii) How does the modulus of E \ K vary when K runs through the natural continua in Kn ? (F. Huckemann)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let K be a compact set of positive measure in C. Does there necessarily exist a non-constant analytic function in C \ K with f (∞) = 0 such that [f (z) − f (ζ)]/[z − ζ] 6= ±1 for any z, ζ ∈ C \ K? Conceivably, the hypotheses even imply the existence of non-linear analytic functions f with |f (z)f (ζ)|/|zζ| bounded, but this is a well-known unsolved problem. Of course one can pose more general problems again such as requiring that the difference quotient omit all values in some pre-assigned plane set. (These problems arise in the use of variational methods.) (D. Aharonov and H. S. Shapiro)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: For a domain D in C, define ρ(x, y) = sup{|f (x) − f (y)| : x, y ∈ D; f analytic in D; |f ′ | ≤ 1 in D}. If D is convex, then ρ(x, y) = |x − y|, but not otherwise. Clearly ρ(x, y) ≤ L(x, y), the infimum of the lengths of paths in G that join x to y. What can be said about ρ for general D, in terms of the geometry of D? (L. A. Rubel)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Suppose that f (z) is continuous in a domain D and that either R (i) |ζ−z|=r f (ζ) dζ = 0 for all z ∈ D and 0 < r ≤ r(z), or (weaker), h R i (ii) limr→0 r −2 |ζ−z|=r f (ζ) dζ = 0 for all z ∈ D. Does it follow that f (z) is analytic in D? (see e.g. [809], [808]). (D. Gaier and L. Zalcman)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let f (z) be continuous on D, and let α be a fixed number with 0 < α ≤ 1. If, for each z in {|z| < 1}, Z f (ζ) dζ = 0, |ζ−z|<α(1−|z|) is f necessarily analytic in D? What happens if we are given that f is continuous only in D? (L. Zalcman)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Suppose that n X n X a1 > 0, 0 ≤ an ≤ n, n ≥ 1, bn = aν , cn = bν . ν=1 ν=1 P Then P (an /cn )α < ∞ if α > 21 . For what other functions f (t) is it true that fP(cn /an ) < ∞? Is it true, for Pinstance, that (under some smoothness condition on f) f (cn /an ) converges with 2 f (n )? The analogous result for cn /bn was obtained by P Borwein [107], that P if xf (x) is positive and non-increasing for x ≥ a > 0 and f (n) < ∞, then f (cn /bn ) < ∞. (W. K. Hayman)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let µ(t) be a continuous monotonic increasing function of t for t ∈ [0, 1] and let ω1 (h, µ), ω2 (h, µ) denote its modulus of continuity and modulus of smoothness respectively. It is known that, if ω1 (h) = O(h) (h → 0), or ω2 (h) = O(h(log 1/h)−c ) (h → 0), where c > 12 , then µ(t) is absolutely continuous (w.r.t. Lebesgue measure). It is also known that each of these conditions is essentially best-possible. Are they simultane- ously best possible? More precisely, is it true that given any function φ(t) ↑ ∞ as t ↓ 0, there is a continuous, monotonic increasing singular function µ(t) such that ω1 (h) = O(hφ(h)) (h → 0) and ω2 (h) = O(h(log 1/h)− 2 ) (h → 0)? (J. M. Anderson)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let P (θ) = N n=1 e iλn θ be a finite Dirichlet series with exponents γ 6= m γn for m 6= n. What can be said about P µ ≡ inf |P (θ)|? A trivial argument shows that µ ≤ (N − 1)1/2 . In fact, |P |2 P = N + 2 m6=n cos(λm − λn )θ. If w(θ) = |P |2 − N ≥ −c, then let h(θ) = c + w(θ) = 2 bn cos(δn θ), where the bn are positive integers. Then Z T Z T 1 1 bn = lim h(t) cos(δn t) dt ≤ lim h(t) dt = c. T →∞ 2T −T T →∞ 2T −T Thus c ≥ 1. The problem arises in prediction theory where µ ≤ (N − 1)1/2 is adequate. If the λn are rational, then the problem reduces to a problem on polynomials with coefficients 0 and 1. (S. Rudolfer and W. K. Hayman)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: The Hankel matrices of a function f having a Taylor expansion f (z) = a0 + a1 z + . . . are defined by Hp(n) = (aij ); aij = an+1+j−2 ; 1 ≤ i, j ≤ p + 1. (n) If f belongs to the Pick-Nevanlinna class (Det Hp ≥ 0, all n, p), then all the poles of f are simple and they lie on the positive real axis. Denote by (n) (n) ε1 ≥ ε2 ≥ . . . ≥ ε(n) p ≥0 (n) the eigenvalues of Hp . Then (n) 1 lim sup(εj )1/n = , n→∞ λj where λj is the j-th pole, where the poles are numbered in order of increasing modulus. What can be said about the eigenvalues under less restrictive conditions? (R. Bouteiller)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: (Subadditivity problem for analytic capacity) Prove or disprove the existence of a constant M such that γ(K1 ∪ K2 ) ≤ M {γ(K1 ) + γ(K2 )} for all compact sets K1 , K2 in C. Even the case where γ(K2 ) = 0 is open. For background, see Garnett [290]. (J. Korevaar)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Define the Harnack function Hz0 (z) for a Green domain D relative to z0 ∈ D to be the supremum of all positive harmonic functions h on D to be the supremum of all positive harmonic functions h on D which satisfy h(z0 ) ≤ 1. If Kζ (z) is the Martin kernel for D relative to z0 , K(ζ0 ) = 1 for all ζ in the Martin boundary ∆1 , then Hz0 (z) = sup{Hζ (z) : z ∈ D, ζ ∈ ∆1 }. In particular for D the unit disc, the boundary ∆1 may be identified with the unit circle T and, if z0 = 0, then Kζ (z) is the Poisson kernel with pole at ζ ∈ T . In this case, Kζ = H0 along the radius to ζ. Using the Riemann mapping functions, this property may be described for simply connected D as follows: for each ζ ∈ ∆1 , Kζ touches Hz0 along a Green line for D issuing from z0 . Does this property continue to hold for D multiply connected? (M. Arsove and G. Johnson)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: A bounded simply-connected domain D is said to be conformally rigid if there is some ε > 0 such that if f is a conformal self-map of D satisfying |f (z) − z| < ε, then f (z) ≡ z. Clearly, if each prime end of D is a singleton, then D is not conformally rigid. Show the converse. (P. M. Gauthier)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let U be an open set in the plane and λU a be the harmonic measure at the point a with respect to U . Then Øksendal [616] showed that λU a is singular U with respect to area measure. Is it also true that λa is singular with respect to β-dimensional Hausdorff measure for all β > 1? The same question can be asked for the Keldysh measure µU a at a ∈ K with respect to U a compact set K. Øksendal showed that µa is singular with respect to area measure. (B. Øksendal)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let D be the unit disc cut along p radial slits from the outer boundary, all of the same given length. Let u be the harmonic measure of {|z| = 1} in D. Find the configuration of slits which makes u(0) minimal, when p is fixed. (A. A. Gonchar, communicated by M. Essén)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let K ⊂ C be compact and let x0 ∈ K be a non-peak point for R(K), the uniform limits on K of rational functions with poles outside K. Will there always exist a continuous curve Γ in K terminating at x0 ? It is easy to see that if P∞ n −n−1 ≤ |z − x | ≤ 2−n }, and M n=1 2 M1 (An (x0 ) \ K) < ∞, where An (x0 ) = {z : 2 0 1 denotes 1-dimensional Hausdorff content, then Γ can be chosen to be a straight line segment. In this case, Øksendal [615] showed that the integrated Brownian motion starting at x0 stays inside K for a positive period of time, almost surely. There is an example of a compact set K and a non-peak point x0 ∈ K such that no straight line segment terminating at x0 is included in K. (B. Øksendal)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: A domain D ⊆ Rn is said to be linearly accessible, if each point in the complement of D can be joined to ∞ by a ray which does not meet D. Let g( · , x0 ) be the Green’s function for D with pole at x0 in D. Is {x : g(x, x0 ) > t} linearly accessible for 0 < t < ∞. This conclusion is valid in R2 . (J. Lewis)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let U be a connected open set in Rn . Brelot and Choquet [113] showed that the set of points on the boundary of U which are accessible from the interior by (finite length) rectifiable paths supports harmonic measure. It is natural, in view of polygonal path connectedness of finely open sets, to ask if the same is true for finely open sets and the Keldysh measure. (T. Lyons and B. Øksendal)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let D be a bounded strictly pseudo-convex domain in Cn , n > 1, with smooth boundary. Denote by A∞ (D) the class of functions analytic in D, continuous on D, all of whose derivatives are continuous on D. Let E be a closed subset of the boundary of D which is not a set of uniqueness for A∞ (D), i.e. there exists a function f 6≡ 0, which belongs to A∞ (D) such that f vanishes exactly on E and all of the derivatives of f vanish on E. Is every closed subset of E a set of non-uniqueness for A∞ (D)? This is true in the case of the unit disc in C. (A. -M. Chollet)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let K ⊂ Cn be a compact set and let P0 (K) be the set of all polyno- mials on K. The P -hull of K, the polynomial convex hull of K, is defined by P -hull K = {z ∈ Cn : |p(z)| ≤ sup |P (z)| for all p ∈ P0 (K)}. k Let P (K) be the uniform closure of P0 (K) in C(K), the continuous function on K. Let Šilov Bd (P (K)) denote the Šilov boundary of the uniform algebra P (K). Determine all compact sets K ⊂ Cn (n > 1) such that Šilov Bd (P (K)) = Boundary (P -hull K). For n = 1, every compact set K ⊂ C has this property. For n > 2, examples of K are compact sets and closed spheres. (S. Kilambi)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: (i) (One-dimensional version.) Let E be a compact set in R; and, for each x ∈ E, let δx > 0 be given. Let Ix = (x − δx , x + δx ). For what values of cPcan one always find a disjoint collection of such intervals, {Ixj } say, such that j |Ixj | ≥ c|E|? It is known that this is possible for c = 21 , but is impossible in general for c > 32 . (ii) (n-dimensional version.) Let E be a compact set in Rn ; and let K be an open bounded symmetric convex set in Rn . For each x ∈ E, let δx > 0 be given; and let Kx = x + δx K, the dilation of K by a factor δx , centred at x. For Pof c can one always find a disjoint collection of such sets, {Kx } say, what values such that j |Kxj | ≥ c|E|? If c(K) denotes the best value, it is known that −n 2 ≤ c(K) < 1. The facts in (i) and (ii), together with some sketchy information on c(Qn ) (where Qn is the n-cube) and c(Sn ) (where Sn is the n-sphere), are given in [777], but there is no information on the correct asymptotic behaviour of c(Qn ) or c(Sn ). The problem has applications to the best constants in results concerning the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function. (P. L. Walker)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let φt (z) = etz − 1, φ1t = φt and φn+1 t = φt ◦ φnt for n ≥ 1; it follows that t φ1t (−1) = e−t − 1 = −t + − . . . , 2! −t −1) φ2t (−1) = et(e − 1 = −t2 + . . . etc. Are the coefficients in these formal power series for {φnt (−1)}∞ n=1 uniformly bounded by 1 in modulus? (P. J. Rippon)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: It is known that any quasi-conformal homeomorphism of B n = {x : x ∈ Rn , |x| < 1} onto a Jordan domain D in Rn can be extended to a homeomorphism of B n onto D. If ∂D is rectifiable (in the sense that Λn−1 (∂D) < ∞), is f |∂B n absolutely continuous (in the sense that Λn−1 f (E) = 0 for every set E in ∂B n with |E| = 0)? One can also ask the analogous question about f −1 . When n = 2, the answer to both questions is ‘yes’ for conformal mappings, but ‘no’ for quasi-conformal mappings. When n = 3, Gehring [299] has proved that, if in addition the function f has a quasi-conformal extension to Rn , then f |∂B n is absolutely continuous; but, even in this special case, it is not known if f −1 |∂D is absolutely continuous. (A. Baernstein II)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let Γ be a closed Jordan curve in the extended plane, and suppose that ∞ ∈ Γ. Let f1 , f2 map the upper and lower half-planes, respectively, onto the two different domains in C bounded by Γ, with f1 (∞) = f2 (∞) = ∞. Then, if h = f2−1 ◦f2 , h is a homeomorphism of R onto R. It is known that Γ is a quasi-circle if and only if h is quasi-symmetric (that is, there exists a constant c such that 1 h(x + t) − h(x) ≤ ≤c c h(x) − h(x − t) for all x, t ∈ R). Can one characterise the function h for general Jordan curves Γ? In particular, can every function h : R → R be generated in this fashion? (L. Bers; communicated by A. Baernstein II)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let E ⊂ [0, 1] be a compact set on the positive real axis 2 2 2  in R ; and let E have positive conformal 2-capacity, that is M ∆(E, ∂B (2); R ) > 0 where ∆(E, ∂B 2 (2); R2 ) is the family of all curves joining  E to ∂B 2 (2) and M (∆) is the 2-modulus of ∆. Is it true that M ∆(E, F ; R ) = ∞, where F = R \ E? (A. A. Gonĉar; communicated by M. Vuorinen)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Is it true that, for any polynomial P with complex coefficients, the mapping f 7→ P ∗ (D)(P f ), where P ∗ (z) = P (z), is a bijection of E onto E? The proposer can prove that this is true when P is a homogeneous polynomial; and D. J. Newman told the proposer that he could prove the injectivity half of the conjecture, but the proposer has seen no details of the proof. The conjecture would follow if one could show that the partial differential equation P ∗ (D)(P f ) = z α where P ∗ (z) = P (z), has a solution f that is entire and of exponential type for every multi-index α. (H. S. Shapiro)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: For n ≥ 2 and α > 0, let  2 α Tdα f (ξ) = 1 − |ξ| fˆ(ξ) R R2 + where R > 0 and f ∈ S(Rn ). Is it true, for all f ∈ L2n/(n+1) (Rn ) and all α > 0, that TRα f (x) → f (x) a.e. as R → ∞? When n = 2 and {Rj } is a lacunary sequence tending to ∞, Carbery [135], Córdoba and López-Melero [174] and also Igari [456] have shown that the answer is ‘yes’. When n ≥ 3, the more ‘elementary’ problem of norm convergence remains unsolved. (See also [136], [173], [681].) (A. Carbery)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let Γ be a Fuchsian group in D, and let i(z) ≡ z. Is it true that X Y |γ ′ (0)| ≥ |γ(0)|2 ? γ∈Γ γ∈Γ, γ6=i Note that this is an equivalent formulation of a problem connecting the Bergman kernel function and the capacity function of a Riemann surface. (N. Suita; communicated by Ch. Pommerenke)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let W be a hyperbolic Riemann surface, Gω the Green’s function with pole ω ∈ W, and Γ = {[γn ]} the fundamental group. Let Γ̃ be the subgroup of equivalence classes [γ] such that, for every ω ∈ W, the harmonic conjugate G∗ω of Gω changes by an integral multiple of 2π on a representative path in [γ]. Certainly [Γ, Γ] ⊳ Γ̃ ⊳ Γ. Is it true that, if [Γ, Γ] 6= Γ̃, then W is necessarily of the form V \ A where V is a hyperbolic surface and A 6= ∅ is a relatively closed subset of zero logarithmic capacity? The conjecture is true if Γ̃ = Γ and V is the unit disc; and it is false if [Γ, Γ] = Γ̃. (The conjecture arises from work in [735].) (K. Stephenson)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: A continuous mapping f : B n → Rn , where B n = {x : x ∈ Rn , |x| < 1}, and n ≥ 2, is said to be proper if f −1 (K) is a compact subset of B n whenever K is a proper subset of f (B n ). Let Bf = {z : z ∈ B n , f is not a local homeomorphism at z}. Is it true that, if (i) n ≥ 3, (ii) f : B n → Rn is proper and quasi-analytic, and (iii) Bf is compact then f is necessarily injective? Note that the mapping f (z) = z 2 , where z ∈ B 2 , shows that the conjecture is false when n = 2. The conjecture is known to be true in the special case that f (B n ) = B n , n ≥ 3. The conjecture is a special case of a more general open problem in [773]. (M. Vuorinen)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let V be the zero set of some analytic function in a strictly pseudo- convex domain Ω in C2 . If V has finite area inside Ω, is it necessarily true that V is the zero set of some bounded analytic function on Ω? Bo Berndttson (no citation) has shown that the answer is ‘yes’ when Ω is the ball; and easy examples show that the answer is ‘no’ for strictly pseudo-convex domains in C when n > 2. Skoda ([719], [720]) and independently Henkin [433] have shown (under some cohomology condition on Ω) for all n that V is the zero set of a function of Nevanlinna class only if V satisfies the Blaschke condition. (R. Zeinstra)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: For a Hadamard gap sequence {nk }∞ k=1 , nk+1 /nk ≥ q > 1, is it true that the measure in [0, 2π[ of the set of those points x for which m X lim inf cos(nk x) − ξ = 0, for all ξ ∈ R, m→∞ k=1 equals 2π? (T. Murai)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Given an associative algebra A, with identity 1 and countable basis, then for a finite-dimensional subspace V spanned by the vectors {ej }kj=1 we have the differential operator Xk ∂ ej ∂xj j=1 acting on differentiable functions defined over domains in V and taking their values in A. We call a function f : U ⊆ V → A a left analytic function if k X ∂f ej (x) = 0 ∂xj j=1 for all x ∈ U . Ryan [692] has shown that there is a generalised Cauchy integral formula Z k X f (x0 ) = G(x, x0 ) (−1)j ej dx̂j f (x), ∂M j=1 with real-analytic kernel G(x, x0 ), where M is an arbitrary, compact real n-dimensional manifold lying in U ; and x0 ∈ M̊ if and only if there are elements {pj }kj=1 ⊆ A satisfying the relation pj el + pl ej = 2δjl . (a) Is the result still valid if we only assume G(x, x0 ) to be a C 1 function? (b) What analogous result holds if we assume the algebra to be non-associative? (J. Ryan)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Using arguments due to Ahlfors (see, for example [10]) any Möbius transformation in Rn can be written in the form (ax + b)(cx + d)−1 , where x ∈ Rn and a, b, c, d are elements of a Clifford algebra An that satisfies certain constraints. It can be shown that the linear differential equations whose solution spaces are conformally invariant are of the type D k fk ((ax + b)(cx + d)−1 ) = 0, k ∈ N, where D is the Euclidean Dirac operator, and the associated conformal weight is ( (cx + d) ∗ |cx + d|−n−1+k for k = 2p − 1, Jk (cx + d) = |cx + d|−n+k for k = 2p, where ∗ is the involution described in [10]. 1. What are the non-linear differential equations whose solution spaces are confor- mally invariant? 2. Can their conformal weights also be expressed in terms of cx + d, and what re- lationship do these solutions have to the linear conformally-invariant differential equations? (J. Ryan)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Given a domain of holomorphy Ω ⊆ Cn , n ≥ 2, what conditions are required on Ω to admit an analytic function p : Ω → C which cannot be analytically extended beyond the boundary of Ω, and satisfies the complex version n X ∂2 p(z) = 0 ∂zj2 k=1 of Laplace’s equation? (J. Ryan)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let D1 , D2 be domains in {|z| < R}, and let λ1 (z) |dz| and λ2 (z) |dz| be their hyperbolic metrics. What is the least number A = A(R) such that the hyperbolic metric λ(z) |dz| of D1 ∩ D2 satisfies the inequality λ(z) < A(λ1 (z) + λ2 (z))? (W. H. J. Fuchs)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: In their famous Acta paper [377], Hardy and Littlewood introduced the celebrated Hardy-Littlewood maximal function in connection with complex function theory. Since then it has proved an invaluable tool in real analysis. Here we ask some questions about the dependence of constants on dimension. Let B be a convex compact symmetric body in Rn , normalised to have Euclidean volume 1. Let the Hardy-Littlewood maximal functions be Z  M f (x) = sup n |f (x + y)| dy t>0 t tB and Z  M̃ f (x) = sup kn |f (x + y)| dy . k∈Z 2 2k B (a) If B is the Euclidean ball in Rn , does there exist a constant C such that meas{x : M̃ f (x) > λ} ≤ Cλ−1 kf k1 for all λ > 0, with C independent of n? (b) If so, what is the answer to the same question for M f ? (c) In the case that n = 1, a conjecture of F. Sonia and the proposer is that the best constant in the inequality meas{x : M f (x) > λ} ≤ Cλ−1 kf k1 is C = 23 . Prove this. (d) Let 1 < p ≤ 32 . Can the best constant in the inequality kM f kp ≤ Cp kf kp be taken to be independent of n and the body B? Even if B = [− 21 , 12 ]n , can the constant be chosen independent of n? The following relevant facts are known. For (a) and (b), the best known constants are found in [729]. For (c), Sonia and the proposer have shown that the answer is ‘yes’ if 2 < p ≤ ∞; for B with suitably-curved boundary, the answer is ‘yes’ for 1 < p ≤ ∞; for the sphere, see [728]. (A. Carbery)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Prove or disprove the following statements about analytic capacity γ. (a) If E ⊆ C is compact and φ is a C 1 -diffeomorphism of C onto C, then γ(E) = 0 if and only if γ(φ(E)) = 0. The statement is false if φ is a homeomorphism or a quasi-conformal mapping. (b) If E ⊆ C is compact and φ ∈ GL(2, R), then γ(E) = 0 if and only if γ(φ(E)) = 0. (c) If E, F are compact subsets of C, then there exists a constant K > 0 (independent of the choice of E and F ) such that γ(E ∪ F ) ≤ K(γ(E) + γ(F )). Perhaps one can take K = 1? See [183] for related results. (d) If K is a compact subset of C with γ(K) = 0, then γ(E \ K) = γ(E) for all compact subsets E of C. Here γ(E \ K) means the inner capacity sup{γ(L) : L ⊆ E \ K, L compact}. An interesting special case would be that when K is the ‘corner quarters square Cantor set’ (the so-called Garnett set). (A. G. O’Farrell)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Prove or disprove the following statement: If K is a compact subset of C with continuous analytic capacity α(K) = 0, then α(E \ K) = α(E) for all compact subsets E of C. An interesting special case is when K is a C 1 -arc. The case when K is a C 1+ε -arc has already been settled. (A. G. O’Farrell)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: We will say that g(x) is a rearrangement of f (x) if m{x : g(x) < y} = m{x : f (x) < y} for all y ∈ R, where m is Lebesgue measure and f and g are defined on some finite interval I. What are those functions f (x) for which f ′ (x) is a rearrangement f (x)? Obvious examples of such functions are f (x) = kex on any interval and f (x) = k sin x on [0, 12 π]. What others are there? How about other ‘differential rearrangements’ than f ′ (z) ∼ f (x)? (L. A. Rubel)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Does there exist a sequence {zn }∞ 1 of distinct complex numbers such that X 1 X 1 <∞ and 6= 0, |zn | z − zn for all z ∈ C? This has the following physical interpretation. If we imagine electrons (really unit-charged wires perpendicular to the complex P plane) placed at each point zn , then these generate P a logarithmic potential given by log |z − zj |. The gradient of this potential is 1/(z − zn ). Thus the question is whether such a field must always have an equilibrium point - that is, a point where a free electron (or wire), once placed there, would remain there. Of course, the corresponding problem could be asked for Rn , n ≥ 3 also. (L. A. Rubel)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let f be analytic on a domain G in C. We will say that a point z0 ∈ G is a MacLane point of f if there exists some neighbourhood N of z0 such that the restrictions to N of the successive derivatives of f , {f (n) |N : n ∈ N}, form a normal family of functions on N . Let M (f ) denote the set of MacLane points of f . What can be said about the set M (f ), besides the fact that it is open? Must M (f ) be connected? If G is simply-connected, must M (f ) be simply-connected? Or can M (f ) be an arbitrarily prescribed open subset of G? Similar questions can be asked about functions meromorphic in G. Perhaps it is more natural, also, to ask such questions about{f (n) (z)/n!} rather than simply {f (n) (z)}? Some relevant facts can be found in [546] and [221]. (L. A. Rubel)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let f be an inner function, with f (0) = 0; then f induces an ergodic (Lebesgue-) measure-preserving map of the circle onto itself. What is the entropy, h(f ), of f ? It is conjectured that h(f ) < ∞ if and only if f ′ belongs to the Nevanlinna class; and that, in that case, then Z 2π h(f ) = log f ′ (eiθ ) dθ. 2π 0 (See [266] and [657].) (J. L. Fernandez)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let I denote the class of all inner functions. Then I, as a subset of H ∞ , enjoys some of the properties that the collection of unimodular functions have as a subset of L∞ ∞ R (the real-valued functions in L (Π) [706]). Is it true that if {Λn } ⊂ (H ∞ )∗ and if for each function φ ∈ I one has |Λn (φ)| ≤ C(φ), then sup kΛn k(H ∞ )∗ < ∞? n This is known to hold if Λn ∈ L1 \H01 (⊂ (H ∞ )∗ ) ([267], [451], [706]); the corresponding real-variable result is also known [706]. (J. L. Fernandez)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let E ⊂ C, and the function F : E × D → C satisfy the following conditions: (a) F is injective on E, for all z ∈ D; (b) F is analytic in z ∈ D, for each w ∈ E; (c) F (z) = z, when w = 0. Does there exist a function G : C × D → C that satisfies conditions (a), (b) and (c), and for which G = F on E? (D. Sullivan, W. Thurston, H. Royden; communicated by D. Hamilton)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let G be a finitely-generated Fuchsian group of the first kind. (a) If F : Π → Π is a G-invariant quasi-symmetric function, is F totally singular? (b) Is the Teichmuller space TG dense in the space SG (Schwarzians of G-invariant univalent functions)? (O. Lehto; L. Bers; I. Kra; communicated by D. Hamilton)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let L = {L}∞ 0 be a non-negative increasing sequence such that ∞ X Lk r k < ∞ (0 < r < 1). k=0 If f (z) is analytic in |z| < 1, we will say that f ∈ PL if there exists a constant A such that, for each integer n ≥ 0 and each polynomial Pn of degree n, kPn ∗ f k∞ ≤ ALn kP k∞ , where ∗ denotes the Hadamard product. The infimum of such A for a given f ∈ PL defines a norm on PL which then becomes a Banach space. A variety of linear operators (such as subordination) have the property that they are norm-decreasing on PL . This enables one to obtain sharp coefficient inequalities for subordinate functions etc., once a function has been shown to lie in PL . The spaces PL are ‘large-growth’ spaces; for example, the case Lk = 1 (k ≥ 0) is the space of Cauchy-Stieltjes transforms. Convex sequences {Lk }∞ 0 (such as Lk = k) have the property that ∞ X Lk z k k=0 lies in the unit ball of PL . Can one relate known spaces to these spaces, for example H p , for 0 < p < 1? (T. Sheil-Small)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let G be a domain in C, and H(G) the ring of functions analytic on G. It is known that, for two domains G1 and G2 , H(G1 ) is isomorphic to H(G2 ) if and only if G1 and G2 are conformally (or anticonformally) equivalent. What can be said under only the hypothesis that H(G1 ) and H(G2 ) are elementarily equivalent in the sense of model theory? For a large class of domains the corresponding problem has been solved for HC (G), the algebra of functions analytic on G, by Henson and Rubel (see [434] and [435]). (L. A. Rubel)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Suppose that F is a relatively-closed subset of D, and let kf kF = sup{|f (z)|; z ∈ F } for functions f in the Bergman space A2 . Describe geometrically the set {z : |z| < 1, |f (z)| ≤ kf kF for all f ∈ A2 }. (A. Stray)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: If f and 1/f belong to the Bergman space A2 , does it follow that Pf is dense in A2 ? Here Pf denotes the set of all polynomial multiples of f , i.e. Pf = {pf : p a polynomial}. More generally, if f ∈ A2 and |f (z)| ≥ c(1 − |z|)a for some a, c > 0, then does it follow that Pf is dense in A2 ? (For partial results in this direction, see [4]). (A. L. Shields)

question_text: Let A denote the set of functions continuous on |z| = 1 which extend continuously to analytic functions on |z| < 1 (the disc algebra). Let Ã denote the set of functions of the form f ◦ φ where f ranges over A and φ ranges over the set of sense-preserving homeomorphisms of |z| = 1. Find a ‘good’ characterisation of Ã. Is there a function in Ã which coincides with ∞ X 2−n exp(−i2n θ) n=1 on some subset of |z| = 1 having positive measure? The proposer conjectures not. question_text: Let µ ≥ 1 be a singular measure on the boundary of the unit disc D; and let Sµ be the corresponding singular inner function n Z 2π z + eiθ o Sµ (z) = exp dµ(θ) , z ∈ D. 0 z − eiθ The function Sµ is said to be discrete if µ is discrete, and continuous if it has no discrete part. question_text: Do there exist inner functions in any strictly pseudo-convex domain of Cn , n ≥ 2? Alexandrov (no citation) and independently Løw (no citation) and Hakim and Sibony [361] have shown the existence of inner functions in the case of the ball. (R. Zeinstra)

question_text: In Pompeiu’s formula, f (z) and Γ f (ζ)/(ζ − z) dζ make sense for merely continuous functions, but Z Z ∂f 1 dζ dη Ω ∂ζ ζ − z needs at least some weak differentiability of f . question_text: Let ψ : S 1 → S 1 be a homeomorphism. When is it true that Re A = Re A ◦ ψ? That is, when is each function f in the real part of the disc algebra also of the form g ◦ ψ, for some function g in the disc algebra? O’Connell [609] has shown that it is necessary that ψ is absolutely continuous, and sufficient that ψ is C 1+ε . (A. G. O’Farrell)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: A sequence {zn }∞ 1 in |z| < 1 is interpolating for bounded analytic (harmonic) functions if, for each bounded sequence {αn }∞ 1 there exists a function u(z) bounded and analytic (harmonic) in |z| < 1 with u(zn ) = αn (n ≥ 1). It is known that a sequence is interpolating for bounded harmonic functions if and only if it is interpolating for bounded analytic functions ([140], [291], [767]); however all such proofs require knowledge of conditions implying that a sequence interpolates for bounded analytic functions. Find a simple proof of this equivalence which does not rely on knowledge of such conditions. (L. Zalcman)

question_text: Let K1 , K2 , K3 be disjoint closed sets in the extended complex plane, and C1 , C2 , C3 constants. Let ρn (f ) be the best rational approximation to the function f which equals Ci on Ki (i = 1, 2, 3); i.e. ρn (f ) = inf max |f (z) − g(z)|, g∈Rn z∈∪i Ki where Rn is the class of rational functions f order at most n. Find a geometric 1/n characterisation of limn→∞ ρn . For the case of two sets, see Gonchar [333]. (T. Ganelius)

question_text: Let D be an open subset of the extended complex plane with non-empty boundary ∂D, and let F be a relatively-closed subset of D. Let f be a function given on F , and {fn }∞ 1 a sequence of functions analytic on D such that fn → f uniformly on F . If E ⊂ (∂Fn ∩ ∂D) and if f extends continuously to F ∪ E, can each fn be extended continuously to F ∪ E? The answer is ‘yes’ if D is the unit disc, or if E is compact. (A. Stray)

question_text: Let us call a closed set E in C a weak Arakelian set if, corresponding to each function g(z) continuous on E and analytic in the interior of E, there exists an entire function g(z) such that, for any sequence {zn }∞ 1 in E, |f (zn )| → ∞ if and only if |g(zn )| → ∞. Korevaar)

Call F a set of harmonic approximation if every function continuous on F and harmonic in the interior of F can be uniformly approximated there by a harmonic function in Rn . Give necessary and sufficient conditions that F be a set of harmonic approximation. If F is nowhere dense, Šaginjan [771] has done this. If F is the closure of its interior, Gauthier, Ow and Goldstein [295] have given necessary conditions and sufficient conditions when n = 2, but not necessary and sufficient conditions. This has applications to Rubel’s

question_text: Let D be a planar domain. A sequence {zj } of points in D is said to be an interpolating sequence if whenever {αj } ∈ ℓ∞ there is a function F ∈ H ∞ (D) such that F (zj ) = αj , for all j. source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let Γ ⊂ C be a Jordan curve of logarithmic capacity 1, and let φ be a conformal map from the exterior of Γ to the exterior of the unit circle such that φ(∞) = ∞. We consider charge distributions on Γ consisting of n point charges 1/n at nth order Fekete points z1 , . . . , zn on Γ, n ∈ N. If Γ is smooth enough, the corresponding potentials n 1X log |z − zk | n k=1 give approximations to log |φ(z)| (outside Γ) and to 0 (inside Γ) which are O(1/n) away from Γ (see [482], [483], [486], [496]). Prove a similar result for the case where Γ is a square. It does hold in the degenerate case Γ = [−2, 2]. (J. Korevaar)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let K be a compact subset of Rn , n ≥ 3. For φ ∈ D, let D(φ) be a least-diameter disc containing spt φ; let d(φ) = diam (spt φ), and let kφk∗ = kφk∞ + d(φ) · k▽φk∞ . Are the following conditions equivalent for continuous functions f : Rn → R? (1) There exists a sequence {fn }∞ 1 of functions harmonic near K, such that fn → f uniformly on K. (2) There exists a function n such that n(δ) decreases to 0 as δ decreases to 0, for which Z f δφ dx ≤ η(d(φ))kφk∗ C(D(φ) − X). Rn Here C denotes the harmonic capacity of Rn obtained from the kernel r −n+2 . Note that (1) implies (2), and that (2) implies (1) if f is a C 2 -function. The condition (2) is formally analogous to one that occurs in rational approximation theory. (A. G. O’Farrell)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let f be continuous on a compact subset K of C. If there exists a sequence {fn }∞ 2 1 of functions analytic near K for which gn → f uniformly on K, ∞ does there necessarily exist a sequence {hn }1 of functions analytic near K for which hn → f uniformly on K? Paramanov has proved this under the stronger hypothesis that f ∈ Lip ( 12 ); it is also true under the hypothesis that f ∈ W 1,p (p > 2). (A. G. O’Farrell)

source_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
question_text: Let f1 and f2 ∈ H ∞ (unit disc) = H ∞ ; and let the function g ∈ H ∞ satisfy the inequality |g(z)| ≤ |f1 (z)| + |f2 (z)|. Do there necessarily exist functions g1 and g2 in H ∞ such that g2 = f1 g1 + f2 g2 ? In other words, is it true that g 2 ∈ I(f1 , f2 ) (the ideal generated by f1 and f2 )? Wolff has proved that g3 ∈ I(f1 , f2 ). Also Rao has given an example of a function g∈/ I(f1 , f2 ). For related results by Tolokonnikov, see [381, p. 399]. (J. Garnett)

question_text: Are there general principles that determine which renormalization-group domain wall or conformal boundary state is selected from the set of possible interfaces or boundary states connecting the ultraviolet and infrared endpoints of a renormalization-group flow in boundary or defect conformal field theory?

question_text: What is the correct quantum-field-theoretic description of the sine-Gordon model with a non-integrable boundary, and can techniques from quantum integrability still be adapted to study how integrability breaks down in that setting?

question_text: Can the relevant boundary conditions for the free fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3 be derived directly from first principles, or alternatively by adapting the methods of Novak and Runkel?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: How can one- and two-point functions in defect conformal field theory be exploited more fully as input to the boundary conformal bootstrap, and what additional structure of the three-dimensional theory living on the defect must be understood in order to make that program work for the present AdS/dCFT system?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: Can one find a closed tree-level formula for one-point functions of the closely related SO(5)-symmetric D3-D7 defect conformal field theory when the full scalar SO(6) sector is considered, beyond the already understood chiral-primary case?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: Can one perform a genuine string-theoretic computation of the one-point function of a non-protected operator in the defect AdS/CFT setup?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: How should one incorporate finite-string-tension corrections, i.e. 1/λ corrections, into the large-N, large-'t Hooft-coupling analysis of four-point correlators in AdS5 × S5 supergravity?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: How can the analytic-bootstrap approach used for loop corrections in AdS5 × S5 be combined either with direct one-loop Witten-diagram computations or with integrability-based methods, so that the different approaches constrain and check one another?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: Can the bootstrap analysis of conformal field theories on real projective space be extended to holographic or otherwise strongly coupled theories such as N = 4 super Yang-Mills theory or Liouville theory, and if so does it agree with the corresponding holographic predictions?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: What is the correct analogue of complex analysis on quasi Riemann surfaces, and how can one develop it in parallel with ordinary complex analysis on genuine Riemann surfaces?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: Is every quasi Riemann surface Q isomorphic to the space D_int_0(Σ) of integral 0-currents on some ordinary two-dimensional conformal space Σ with the same Jacobian, and if so how can that isomorphism be constructed concretely?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: Can one construct explicit families of local quasi-holomorphic curves from the complex disk into a quasi Riemann surface, for example when the ambient 2n-dimensional space is the sphere S^{2n}, so that local conformal-field-theoretic structure can be studied there?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: What is the spacetime interpretation of the local gauge symmetry that appears in the bundle of quasi Riemann surfaces, such as the local SU(2)×SU(2) symmetry associated with the self-dual point of the two-dimensional Gaussian model?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: Can standard two-dimensional conformal-field-theory constructions, such as orbifolding and perturbation theory, be reproduced or generalized on quasi Riemann surfaces so as to generate new theories of higher-dimensional defects?

source_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
question_text: When fields Φ(ξ) on quasi Riemann surfaces are restricted to very small defects ξ that look pointlike inside the ambient 2n-dimensional manifold, do the resulting ordinary local quantum fields define genuinely new local quantum field theories in 2n dimensions?

source_title: The Statistical Model of Nuclear Reactions: Open Problems
question_text: In the statistical model of nuclear reactions, partial gamma decay widths for isolated neutron resonances are usually assumed to follow a Porter-Thomas distribution (PTD), and total gamma decay widths are then obtained by summing a very large number of such partial widths over many gamma decay channels. The paper asks whether replacing the PTD assumption for the partial gamma widths with a different distribution could produce a predicted distribution of total gamma decay widths for neutron resonances in the compound nucleus 96Mo that agrees better with the experimentally observed distribution, which is much broader and centered at larger values than the standard statistical-model prediction.

source_title: The Statistical Model of Nuclear Reactions: Open Problems
question_text: The statistical model underpredicts the mean total gamma decay widths observed for neutron resonances and therefore appears to be missing gamma strength. The open question is whether the Brink-Axel hypothesis actually remains valid for all gamma transitions that contribute significantly to the gamma decay of those neutron resonances, since failure of that hypothesis could explain why the model does not reproduce the observed total gamma decay-width data.
context_brief: Brink-Axel validity for significant gamma transitions

source_title: The Statistical Model of Nuclear Reactions: Open Problems
question_text: A possible way to reconcile the statistical model with the experimental total gamma decay-width data is that a comparatively small number of gamma transitions to low-lying final states are much more strongly coupled than the rest. Such channels would need to be intense enough to shift the simulated total gamma decay widths toward the experimental values and few enough in number to evade the central-limit-theorem narrowing that normally makes the predicted distribution too narrow. The open question is whether a comparatively small number of such strongly coupled gamma decay channels could also change the Porter-Thomas distribution behavior of the reduced neutron widths.
context_brief: Strong low-lying gamma channels and neutron-width PTD

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: For a translationally invariant projected entangled pair state (PEPS) on an L × L torus defined by a local tensor A, let R be a square region and let H be the parent Hamiltonian obtained by translating the local projector associated to R. What are the weakest conditions on the tensor A, and how small can the region R be chosen, that guarantee the resulting PEPS is the unique ground state of H and that H has a nonzero spectral gap?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: Let T be a primitive quantum channel acting on D × D matrices, where the primitivity index p(T) is the smallest n such that T^n(ρ) has full rank for every positive semidefinite input ρ. What is the exact best possible upper bound on p(T) as a function of the dimension D?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: For a normal translationally invariant matrix product state (MPS) with bond dimension D, what is the exact best possible upper bound, in terms of D alone, for its injectivity index, meaning the smallest scale at which the associated tensor becomes injective?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: For a normal projected entangled pair state (PEPS) with bond dimension D, what is the exact best possible upper bound, in terms of D alone, for its injectivity index?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: Give an explicit and computable function f(D), preferably polynomial in the PEPS bond dimension D, that upper-bounds the injectivity index of every normal projected entangled pair state with bond dimension D.

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: Is the following bulk-boundary correspondence for PEPS exactly true: the parent Hamiltonian of a projected entangled pair state is gapped if and only if the corresponding boundary states can be written as Gibbs states of one-dimensional short-range Hamiltonians whose interaction terms decay exponentially with distance?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: In two dimensions, does every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian admit a global PEPS approximation under the spectral gap assumption alone, without any additional assumptions about the low-energy spectrum?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: For the two-dimensional global PEPS approximation problem, can the bond-dimension bound f(L) required to approximate an L × L system be chosen to grow polynomially in the linear system size L?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: In two dimensions, does there exist a local approximation theorem stating that every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian can be approximated on finite regions by a translationally invariant PEPS of finite bond dimension; can this be proved assuming only a spectral gap; and can the required bond-dimension bound g(ε) be chosen polynomial in 1/ε?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: Suppose two local tensors A and B define exactly the same projected entangled pair state on every L × L torus, meaning |Ψ_A⟩ = |Ψ_B⟩ for all system sizes. What local relation between A and B characterizes this equality of PEPS?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: Develop a Fundamental Theorem for PEPS in two and higher dimensions that applies to the largest possible class of projected entangled pair states, interpolating between the currently understood normal case and the fully general case where equality is undecidable.

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: Let A and B be PEPS tensors such that there exist ε > 0 and a size L0 with the property that for every L ≥ L0 the states they define on the L × L torus satisfy ‖|Ψ_A⟩ − |Ψ_B⟩‖² ≤ ε. Does this asymptotic closeness in the thermodynamic limit imply any local relation between the tensors A and B?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: For supervised machine-learning algorithms built from matrix product states or related tensor networks, can one express the Rademacher complexity or the Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension explicitly as a function of the bond dimension?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: What is the exact computational complexity class of the two-dimensional PEPS zero-testing problem?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: Given a finite group G and a normal subgroup H, does there exist a low-depth noisy quantum circuit that maps the quantum double phase associated to G to the quantum double phase associated to H?

source_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
question_text: What is the exact relationship between projected entangled pair states and quantum cellular automata in two and higher spatial dimensions?

source_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
question_text: In solar-wind turbulence at ion and electron kinetic scales, what is the physical nature of the fluctuations, and through which collisionless plasma mechanisms are those fluctuations dissipated? This question asks for a theory that can distinguish which competing collisionless processes are active at ion and electron scales and explain how they determine the observed kinetic-scale turbulent cascade and dissipation.

source_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
question_text: How does free energy cascade through phase space in kinetic plasma turbulence when multiple collisionless processes are active at ion and electron scales? A satisfactory answer must explain how turbulent energy is transferred across both spatial and velocity-space structure in weakly collisional magnetized plasmas.

source_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
question_text: Do common turbulence features exist across independently performed 3D3V kinetic simulations using different numerical models, in a way that would demonstrate a genuine universality of kinetic-scale plasma turbulence? This requires separating robust, model-independent properties from differences caused by the large-scale driving, box size, filtering choices, reduced mass ratios, or the distinction between hybrid-kinetic and fully kinetic physics.

source_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
question_text: Are sub-ion-scale field polarizations in kinetic plasma turbulence genuinely kinetic-Alfven-wave-like, or do the observed spectral ratios instead require a mixture of KAW-like fluctuations, other wave-like modes such as whistler, ion-cyclotron, or ion Bernstein fluctuations, and nonlinear effects that make the turbulence deviate from asymptotic linear KAW predictions? The question is specifically motivated by spectral ratios that are broadly consistent with KAW expectations but do not exactly match the linear-theory values.

source_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
question_text: What physical process causes the apparent contradiction between solar-wind observations, which show nearly scale-independent non-Gaussian turbulence statistics at sub-ion scales, and 3D kinetic simulations, which show excess kurtosis continuing to grow through the sub-ion range? More specifically, does collisionless reconnection limit the growth of sub-ion-scale kurtosis by disrupting sufficiently sheetlike intermittent structures, or are other mechanisms such as collisionless damping responsible for the observed saturation behavior?

source_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
question_text: Which dissipation mechanisms act on turbulent fluctuations under different plasma conditions in kinetic-range turbulence, and how do those mechanisms determine the resulting partition of energy among the different plasma species? A complete answer must connect the plasma conditions, the operative collisionless dissipation pathway, and the species-by-species outcome of turbulent heating.

source_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
question_text: How is turbulent energy distributed in space and time in kinetic plasma turbulence? The question concerns the spatio-temporal organization of turbulent energy, rather than only its scale-by-scale spectrum, and is posed as a fundamental target for future multi-spacecraft measurements.

source_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
question_text: What is the full three-dimensional anisotropic structure of energy transfer across scales in kinetic plasma turbulence? This asks for a direct characterization of how the cascade is organized in three dimensions relative to the magnetic field and local turbulent structure.

source_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
question_text: What are the high-order statistics of fluctuations in kinetic plasma turbulence? In context, this means determining the intermittency-sensitive, non-Gaussian statistical structure of the turbulent fields at kinetic scales, beyond low-order spectral descriptions.

source_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
question_text: Over what range of temporal and spatial scales is Taylor's hypothesis valid for kinetic plasma turbulence? The open issue is whether the usual conversion between temporal spacecraft measurements and spatial structure remains reliable across the broad range of scales relevant to kinetic turbulence.

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: For networking datasets in which each sample contains fixed metadata together with an associated multivariate time series, can generative adversarial networks be used to create synthetic datasets that remain high-fidelity and generalize across downstream networking tasks without requiring substantial human expertise about workload characteristics or target tasks?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: When releasing synthetic networked time-series data generated by GANs, what privacy definition should be used for a given data-sharing use case, given that different release scenarios may require different protection goals and threat models?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: In GAN-based sharing of networked time-series datasets, can the generator support flexible notions of privacy in practice, and if so, under what training or generation configurations can those privacy notions be achieved?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: Do privacy-preserving GAN training methods achieve a privacy-fidelity tradeoff that is practical for networking datasets, where the synthetic output must preserve realistic temporal structure and cross-feature relationships while still offering meaningful privacy guarantees?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: For networking and systems datasets that consist of time series and metadata rather than labeled images, how should GAN fidelity be evaluated when the standard, widely used GAN metrics were designed for image data and cannot be directly applied?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: When a synthetic data generator models both per-sample attributes and associated time-series records, how can practitioners realistically tune the attribute distributions of the released synthetic dataset while still preserving the conditional behavior between those attributes and the generated records?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: Can GAN training for synthetic systems and networking data be combined with simulators that encode the physical constraints of the underlying system, so that data generation benefits both from statistical learning and from domain-knowledge constraints?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: Can differentially private GAN mechanisms for time-series generation be improved enough to provide meaningful privacy guarantees without destroying the fidelity of the generated time-series data?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: For networked time-series datasets in which one released sample may summarize behavior of many users or entities rather than a single person, is differential privacy an appropriate privacy metric for the data-sharing problem at all?
context_brief: Is differential privacy the right metric?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: If differential privacy is not well aligned with GAN-generated networked time-series releases, what alternative privacy metrics should be explored for this form of synthetic data sharing?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: How can synthetic-data generation methods such as DoppelGANger be extended to handle networking datasets whose behavior depends on causal interactions between stateful agents rather than only on isolated per-agent traces?

source_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
question_text: How can practitioners perform what-if analysis by modeling changes in an underlying networking system and then generating synthetic data for the modified system, especially when larger interventions invalidate the conditional distributions learned from the original data and may therefore require explicit physical-system modeling or simulation?

source_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
question_text: Can quantum chromodynamics derive Bloom-Gilman duality from first principles, where Bloom-Gilman duality is the observation that at low Q^2 a structure function shows prominent nucleon resonances that average to the scaling function measured at some higher Q_0^2 and then slide down its slope as Q^2 increases, rather than only explaining a QCD-improved realization of that behavior?

source_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
question_text: How can alpha_s(Q^2) be determined with higher theoretical control when the higher beta-function coefficients b_i for i >= 2 are scheme-dependent and the perturbative series for delta_QCD(Q) converges slowly, perhaps because of renormalon divergences associated with non-perturbative contributions behaving as n! alpha_s^n?

source_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
question_text: How can the theoretical uncertainty in deep inelastic scattering be improved beyond the current practice of varying the renormalization and factorization scales within conventional brackets, given that the perturbative expression still contains higher-twist corrections and the source states that it is not clear how to do any better?

source_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
question_text: How should next-to-leading-twist effects be incorporated in Drell-Yan-like processes once perturbative NNLO calculations and data reach a precision where those effects can no longer be safely ignored, especially given that infrared divergences in higher-twist contributions do not cancel beyond the one-loop level for these processes?

source_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
question_text: Can lattice QCD devise a gauge-invariant way to characterize a confined constituent-quark propagator that peaks at a constituent mass roughly 300 MeV larger than a Lagrangian or chiral-model mass, and can it also determine whether one-gluon-exchange dominance explains mass differences between baryons with the same quark constituency but different spin or quark-spin alignments?

source_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
question_text: What is the correct internal structure of the observed tetraquark and pentaquark resonances: compact bag-like states containing all the quarks together, molecule-like bound states of two substructures, or the colored-molecule picture proposed for some states containing two heavy quarks?

source_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
question_text: Can QCD provide a quantitatively satisfactory first-principles account of hadronization and of the underlying event, rather than relying on phenomenological tuning, machine-learning-assisted tuning, string models, or cluster models, and can it justify factorization in this full realistic setting rather than treating factorization as an ansatz?

source_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
question_text: What is the correct solution of color confinement in QCD, beyond the existing lattice result for the large-distance potential between two static quarks, where the potential approaches sigma r + const/r as the separation r goes to infinity?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: How should the federated learning community define standard evaluation metrics and establish benchmark datasets that are appropriate for the major deployment settings, especially cross-device and cross-silo federated learning, so that proposed methods can be compared on realistic and broadly accepted criteria rather than ad hoc simulations?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: In fully decentralized federated learning without a central coordinator, how can stochastic-gradient-based training for deep models be made robust to temporary client unavailability, client dropout and joining, message loss, non-IID client data, heterogeneous update frequencies, and communication-topology choices, while still achieving good practical convergence time?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: For cross-silo federated learning, what formal privacy notion should be optimized in realistic deployments, especially when other participating silos may be a more important threat than the outside world and when each silo may represent many end users whose privacy may need to be protected at the user level?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: Can split learning be parallelized effectively on resource-constrained edge devices so that different parts of the split computation can run with lower centralized training time while remaining practical in federated deployments?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: What formal privacy guarantees can be proved for split learning, including guarantees that account for the information leaked by communicated activations or smashed data from clients to the server?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: How can researchers characterize the real cross-client distribution shifts that appear in real-world federated datasets, and use that understanding to build controlled but realistic non-IID benchmarks that stress-test algorithms under the kinds of heterogeneity seen in deployment?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: How should a federated optimization system choose the number of local client updates before aggregation, and potentially the aggregation rule itself, so that the resulting training process achieves the best wall-clock convergence rather than merely good iteration complexity?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: Can the multi-task or lifelong-learning perspective used for personalization and privacy in federated learning be extended to other phenomena such as concept drift, and can non-parameter-transfer lifelong-learning methods such as ProtoNets be made useful in federated learning?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: Under what data-distribution conditions does a single global federated model outperform independently trained per-client models, how much gain should be expected, and can personalization methods be given guarantees that match or exceed both the purely local baseline and the shared global baseline?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: What privacy-preserving debugging and interpretability methods can answer practical machine-learning workflow questions on decentralized user data, such as inspecting failure cases, outliers, or bias, and how can differentially private federated generative models be improved enough to support those uses faithfully?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: Can communication in federated learning be reduced substantially further, and what are the practical optimal trade-offs between communication cost and model accuracy once the optimization algorithm is taken into account rather than abstracted away?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: How can compression schemes for federated model updates be designed so that they remain effective while also being compatible with secure aggregation protocols and with differentially private noise-addition mechanisms?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: If homomorphic encryption is used inside federated learning, who should hold the decryption key, and what trust structure or threshold-encryption design can preserve client privacy without assuming an unrealistic permanently trusted external decryptor?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: Can interactive zero-knowledge proofs or non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs be made efficient enough for federated learning, both for proving properties of client inputs to the server and for client-side verification tasks that depend on information from multiple participants?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: What are the fundamental privacy-accuracy trade-offs for user-level differential privacy in federated learning when users contribute highly unequal amounts of data, and how should user contributions be clipped or bounded adaptively in that setting?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: Do privacy-amplification-by-iteration results known for convex optimization extend to the non-convex federated-learning setting, and can practical protocols provide formal privacy guarantees despite dynamic user eligibility, local participation decisions, and mid-protocol dropout?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: How can secure aggregation be made simultaneously efficient, robust, and privacy-preserving when the server may be stronger than semi-honest, when per-round aggregates may leak information, when sparse vectors must be aggregated efficiently, and when client inputs must be checked for well-formedness?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: Is it possible to perform communication-efficient federated training of sub-models while preserving the privacy of which sub-model each client is updating, and what sparsity regimes, private retrieval mechanisms, and secure aggregation variants would make that practical?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: Can federated learning adopt a realistic trust model in which the server is trusted but continuously verifiable, including explicit assumptions about what fraction of clients might be compromised and whether simultaneous compromise of server and many devices should be assumed?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: Can defenses such as data sanitization and network pruning be adapted to federated learning in a way that does not require direct access to private client data, and how should the gap between data poisoning and model-update poisoning attacks be quantified under realistic federated adversary capabilities?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: How can secure aggregation tolerate stragglers and dropouts more gracefully, for example through asynchronous variants or aggregation across multiple rounds, and what general-purpose debugging methods can diagnose federated data-pipeline failures without directly inspecting raw user data?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: To what extent can bias that originates in the data-generating process be detected or mitigated in federated learning, and what methods can apply post-hoc fairness corrections to models learned from potentially biased decentralized interaction data?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: How can unfairness be measured and corrected in federated settings where sensitive group membership is unavailable, including making approaches such as distributionally robust optimization and multicalibration scale to the large, high-dimensional regime typical of federated learning and developing new theory for fairness without explicit sensitive attributes?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: How do client-sampling constraints and decentralized data collection affect fairness in federated learning, and under what assumptions can fairness-improving methods from centralized learning be adapted to the federated setting?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: How should system-induced bias in federated learning be quantified and mitigated in realistic deployments, including through useful proxy metrics, root-cause analysis, stratification strategies, and scheduling or weighting policies?

source_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
question_text: What composite objective functions should be optimized when tuning federated learning systems that must trade off model quality, throughput, convergence speed, fairness, privacy, robustness, and resource use, and how can those settings be tuned automatically rather than manually?

source_title: The puzzle of global Double Field Theory: open problems and the case for a Higher Kaluza-Klein perspective
question_text: Can the pre-NQP-manifold approach to Double Field Theory be extended from the currently constructed global examples to general T-dualizable backgrounds, in a way that produces a globally defined pre-NQP manifold for non-trivially fibered spacetimes without having to assume the T-duality correspondence space in advance or duplicate topological data between a gerbe and its dual?

source_title: The puzzle of global Double Field Theory: open problems and the case for a Higher Kaluza-Klein perspective
question_text: Can Double Field Theory recover a general geometric string background, meaning a smooth spacetime manifold equipped with a non-trivial Kalb-Ramond field whose Dixmier-Douady class [H] is nonzero in H3(M, Z), rather than only the restricted cases in which the recovered gerbe is flat or torsion?
