source_title: The puzzle of global Double Field Theory: open problems and the case for a Higher Kaluza-Klein perspective
question_text: Can the Higher Kaluza-Klein framework developed here for global Double Field Theory be extended to the Heterotic DFT case?

source_title: The puzzle of global Double Field Theory: open problems and the case for a Higher Kaluza-Klein perspective
question_text: Can Exceptional Field Theory be formulated as a Higher Kaluza-Klein theory on the total space of the twisted M2/M5-brane bundle gerbe over 11-dimensional super-spacetime?

source_title: Notes on open questions within density functional theory (existence of a derivative of the Lieb functional in a restricted sense and non-interacting v-representability)
question_text: For the interacting Lieb functional FL[n] in density functional theory, can one prove that FL[n] admits a derivative in a restricted or weak sense for every interacting ensemble v-representable density n in the set B, even though FL[n] is nowhere Gateaux differentiable on the full Banach space X? Any such result must identify physically meaningful perturbation directions that preserve particle number and keep perturbed densities inside the admissible density set S, while still making the directional derivative finite and linear on that restricted class.
context_brief: Restricted differentiability of the interacting Lieb functional

source_title: Notes on open questions within density functional theory (existence of a derivative of the Lieb functional in a restricted sense and non-interacting v-representability)
question_text: Is the non-interacting v-representability conjecture true, meaning that every interacting ensemble v-representable ground-state density in the set B can be reproduced exactly by some non-interacting Kohn-Sham system, so that B equals the set Bs of non-interacting ensemble v-representable densities? Equivalently, when a sequence of non-interacting densities nε in Bs converges to an interacting density n in B, does the limit always correspond to an actually attainable non-interacting density rather than merely an arbitrarily good approximation?
context_brief: Exact non-interacting representability of interacting densities

source_title: Notes on open questions within density functional theory (existence of a derivative of the Lieb functional in a restricted sense and non-interacting v-representability)
question_text: Does the Kohn-Sham potential functional vs[ns], defined for non-interacting ensemble v-representable densities ns in Bs, admit a derivative in a restricted sense for every ns in Bs, and is that derivative bounded? The notes identify a positive answer as sufficient to prove the non-interacting v-representability conjecture, but they also note that establishing such a derivative rigorously is difficult, especially in degenerate cases, and that the inverse response kernel χs^-1[vs[ns]] is unbounded.
context_brief: Restricted bounded derivative of the Kohn-Sham potential

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: What phase of QCD matter is realized inside neutron stars, and what is the high-density QCD equation of state needed to determine that phase? More concretely, when baryonic matter is compressed to several times ordinary nuclear density so that neighboring nuclei overlap and it is no longer meaningful to assign quarks to individual nuclei, does the system remain a hadronic or nuclear medium, or does it enter a deconfined quark phase, and what first-principles finite-density QCD calculation can determine the corresponding equation of state?
context_brief: neutron-star phase and equation of state

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: Does the QCD critical point exist in the temperature-density phase diagram of QCD, and if it does, what are its critical temperature and density coordinates? Equivalently, can a first-principles finite-density QCD calculation establish either the existence or the non-existence of a critical endpoint separating crossover and first-order behavior in baryonic matter?
context_brief: QCD critical point existence and location

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: How do hadron masses, couplings, and related properties change inside nuclei or more generally at finite baryon density, and can partial restoration of chiral symmetry in nuclear matter be determined quantitatively from QCD itself rather than from phenomenological models? This includes determining how changes in the chiral condensate inside nuclear media modify hadronic observables and whether those modifications can be established reliably from first principles.

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: What breakthrough is required to obtain a successful, quantitatively reliable first-principles approach to finite-density baryonic matter from QCD? In particular, since existing phenomenological descriptions have substantial model dependence and there is currently no established successful method for finite-density baryonic matter, what new conceptual or computational development would allow QCD itself to describe such matter quantitatively?

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: Can one devise a genuinely practical method for performing QCD path integrals with complex actions at realistic computational cost, thereby solving the sign problem rather than merely circumventing it in limited regimes? This asks both for a method that remains reliable when the action is highly oscillatory and for a criterion of success based on feasible computational scaling rather than formal correctness alone.

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: How can one determine, in a robust and practically usable way, when a finite-density QCD method that is formally correct in principle is actually failing in practice and producing unphysical answers? This includes identifying diagnostics that distinguish trustworthy results from artifacts caused by pitfalls such as hidden overlap problems, uncontrolled phase fluctuations, or other failures of methods that are mathematically sound but numerically unreliable.

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: Can reweighting-based approaches control the overlap problem and complex phase fluctuations well enough to remain reliable at larger chemical potential, larger volume, and near phase-transition regions? More specifically, can one avoid the regime where the reweighting factor becomes dominated by a tiny subset of configurations or where phase cancellations drive the relevant averages effectively to zero?

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: Can Taylor expansion around zero chemical potential determine the QCD equation of state and, more importantly, identify phase transitions or the QCD critical point when only low-order coefficients are practically accessible and the convergence near the transition region is slow? This includes the open issue of whether sufficiently accurate higher-order coefficients can be computed to make the method reliable beyond very small chemical potential.

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: How reliable is analytic continuation from imaginary chemical potential once one moves beyond the small-µ/T regime where different fitting ansätze agree? In particular, can one control the strong fit-function dependence that appears when continuing pseudo-critical lines or other observables into the real-chemical-potential region?

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: What is the continuum-limit behavior of the Roberge-Weiss endpoint and related critical temperatures for Wilson-fermion lattice QCD, and can the continuum extrapolation be achieved there? This asks whether the qualitative picture known from staggered-fermion studies survives quantitatively when Wilson fermions are pushed to the continuum limit.

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: If the Roberge-Weiss endpoint is first order for some parameter regime, does the associated first-order line extend until it meets the crossover line and terminate at another critical endpoint, and can that additional endpoint be identified explicitly in lattice QCD? More broadly, can such an endpoint serve as a controlled testing ground for methods intended to detect critical points without facing the real-density sign problem?

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: Can the canonical method determine the QCD critical point and first-order transition structure on substantially larger lattices with controlled errors, rather than only on the small volumes used in existing successful studies? This includes whether canonical calculations can overcome the growing sign problem and computational cost enough to make their current critical-point claims robust in larger-volume regimes.

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: Why does the early-onset problem appear in finite-density lattice QCD, with severe phase fluctuations setting in when the quark chemical potential reaches mπ/2, and how can one reliably study the hadron phase beyond that threshold? In particular, what mechanism explains the onset of extreme difficulty at µ = mπ/2 and how can simulations be extended into the physically relevant dense hadronic regime associated with nuclei and neutron stars?

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: For the regime mπ/2 < µ < mN/3 at low temperature, how do complex phase cancellations operate so that physically the quark-number expectation value can remain zero even though individual gauge configurations can already give nonzero quark number? Equivalently, what is the detailed phase-distribution mechanism that enforces the Silver-Blaze behavior in this interval?

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: Can the complex Langevin method be made reliable in the low-temperature, finite-density hadron phase of QCD, where the singular drift problem caused by near-zero fermion determinants presently spoils the method? This includes whether deformations, generalized cooling, contour-based hybrids, or other ideas can remove or control the singularity-driven failures without changing the target theory.

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: Can the parts of the QCD phase diagram that are currently out of reach become accessible in the future, and are some of the results currently believed to be correct actually still vulnerable to revision? This is the paper’s broad meta-level open question about the long-term reliability and eventual completeness of present finite-density lattice QCD knowledge.
context_brief: future reach and reliability of current results

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: Is there a fundamental lower bound on the computational cost of evaluating physically relevant path integrals with sign problems, and if such a bound exists, how is it related to the P versus NP question in computational complexity? In other words, is an exponentially hard sign problem an unavoidable feature of some theories rather than merely a symptom of inadequate algorithms?

source_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
question_text: Can quantum entanglement or tensor-network-based descriptions provide a genuinely new route to solving or sharply characterizing the sign problem in finite-density QCD? More specifically, can entanglement serve as the right measure of the effective degrees of freedom and computational cost in a way that leads to new numerical strategies for dense QCD?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: In ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals heterostructures, what is the exact coupling mechanism between spins at the ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic interface that produces exchange bias?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: In ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals systems, does the observed exchange bias originate directly from ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic interfacial coupling, or does it require some other interfacial magnetic state?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: What roles do the ferromagnetic spins and the antiferromagnetic spins each play in producing the exchange-bias effect in ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals systems?
context_brief: Roles of FM and AFM spins

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: How does the type of antiferromagnetic ordering in the antiferromagnetic layer affect exchange-bias behavior in ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals systems?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: Is there a thickness limit of the antiferromagnetic layer below which or above which exchange bias can no longer be induced in ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals systems?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: Can an intermediate magnetically disordered interfacial phase form at a ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals interface, and if so, can that disordered phase itself induce exchange bias?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: Can ferromagnet/spin-glass or antiferromagnet/spin-glass interfaces form during fabrication of van der Waals magnetic systems, and can such interfaces induce exchange bias?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: What role does magnetic proximity from the ferromagnetic layer play in the exchange-bias effect observed in ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals and related heterostructures?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: Does charge transfer across the interface mediate the interfacial magnetism and the exchange-bias effect in ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals systems?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: What role does interlayer spin coupling play in setting the exchange-bias effect in ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals systems?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: Can exchange bias in van der Waals magnetic systems be tuned so that it occurs at room temperature rather than only at low temperature?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: Can exchange bias in van der Waals magnetic systems be tuned by external stimuli such as electric field or strain?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: For oxidized Fe3GeTe2, what are the chemical composition, thickness, and magnetic order of the oxide-related interfacial phase, and is the exchange bias produced by an Fe3GeTe2/oxide interface, an Fe3GeTe2/Fe3−xGeTe2 interface, or some combination involving disordered spins?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: In Fe3GeTe2/CrCl3 van der Waals heterostructures, is exchange bias caused purely by direct ferromagnet/antiferromagnet coupling, or is it altered by an interfacial oxide or spin-cluster layer, magnetic proximity between Fe3GeTe2 and CrCl3, and charge transfer across the interface?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: In Fe3GeTe2/FePS3, FePS3/Fe3GeTe2/FePS3, and Fe3GeTe2/MnPX3 (X = S, Se) heterostructures, how do oxidization of Fe3GeTe2, the type of antiferromagnetic ordering, interlayer coupling inside the antiferromagnet, reduced dimensionality, charge transfer, and possible interfacial spin reorientation control the enhanced magnetism and unusual exchange-bias behavior?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: Do the exchange-bias and quantum anomalous Hall effects predicted for CrI3/MnBi2Te4 ferromagnet/antiferromagnet heterostructures occur experimentally, and can analogous exchange-bias and quantum anomalous Hall phenomena be realized by interfacing MnBi2Te4 or related topological antiferromagnets with other van der Waals ferromagnets such as Fe3GeTe2 or Fe5GeTe2?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: In hybrid interfaces between a two-dimensional van der Waals ferromagnet such as Fe3GeTe2 and a three-dimensional non-van-der-Waals ferromagnet such as Ni, what are the interfacial spin textures and couplings, how does a possible oxidized Fe3GeTe2 interlayer affect them, and how would any resulting exchange bias influence the magnetic properties of the metal layer and spin transport across the interface?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: In Fe3GeTe2/MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 and related van der Waals spin-valve structures, what microscopic mechanism causes the magnetoresistance enhancement, is the magnetoresistance asymmetry caused by oxidized Fe3GeTe2 surface layers, and how do magnetic proximity, magnetic-domain reconstruction, spin-orbit coupling proximity, and charge transfer across the Fe3GeTe2/MoS2 interface contribute to the observed transport behavior?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: In Fe/MoS2 and other heterostructures that combine a non-van-der-Waals magnet with a defective or weakly magnetic van der Waals transition-metal dichalcogenide, how do charge transfer, magnetic proximity, orbital hybridization, defects, atomic diffusion, and dopant incorporation determine the interfacial magnetism, exchange-bias effect, and spin-transport response?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: Can ferromagnet/ferromagnet coupling at a defective van der Waals VSe2/MoS2 interface generate an exchange-bias effect even though the interface is not a conventional ferromagnet/antiferromagnet interface?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: In VSe2/MoS2 heterostructures, how are V-atom spins and defect-induced spins in VSe2 and MoS2 coupled at the interface, does work-function-driven charge redistribution and Schottky-barrier formation enhance the exchange-bias effect, and can the effect be tuned by changing MoS2 thickness, Se-vacancy concentration in VSe2, or by replacing VSe2 with other defect-magnetic transition-metal dichalcogenides such as WSe2 or TiSe2?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: How does exchange magnetic anisotropy, including anisotropy associated with surface oxidization and magnetic proximity, affect magnetoresistance, spin-orbit torque switching, spin Seebeck response, anomalous Nernst response, and optical control in van der Waals magnetic heterostructures that are being proposed for spintronics, opto-spintronics, spin-caloritronics, and related devices?

source_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
question_text: What new heterostructure designs and theoretical models are needed to explain exchange bias, magnetic proximity, and charge-transfer effects in van der Waals magnetic interfaces and to realize large exchange bias at or above room temperature?

source_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
question_text: How can offline reinforcement learning support a reliable end-to-end training workflow that selects hyperparameters, validates candidate policies during training, and decides when to stop training without any new interaction with the environment? In particular, the workflow must work from static logged data, avoid overfitting from repeatedly training on the same dataset, and replace the current practice of either depending on inaccurate off-policy evaluation or training for a fixed number of steps and evaluating the final policy online.

source_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
question_text: Which off-policy evaluation method can estimate or rank candidate offline reinforcement learning policies robustly enough to work across a wide variety of datasets, so that practitioners can trust it for policy evaluation or model selection instead of relying on environment rollouts?

source_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
question_text: How can an offline reinforcement learning algorithm dynamically modulate how conservative it is, so that it stays cautious in uncertain regions of the state-action space but relaxes its constraints when the data support confident generalization?

source_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
question_text: How should offline reinforcement learning handle nonstationary datasets and then fine-tune the resulting offline policy online, especially in settings where the data distribution or environment changes over time and the method must adapt without discarding what was learned from the static dataset?

source_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
question_text: How can offline reinforcement learning be made safe in safety-critical applications not only by avoiding out-of-distribution states and actions, but also by avoiding unsafe states that are already present inside the training distribution, for example through explicitly risk-averse objectives such as conditional value-at-risk?

source_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
question_text: How can offline reinforcement learning use unsupervised reinforcement learning or related techniques to exploit large amounts of unlabeled experience when reward labels are scarce or expensive, while still producing effective downstream policies from static data?

source_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
question_text: Which data-collection strategies and data-processing methods can produce more exploratory offline datasets and make better use of unlabeled data, so that offline reinforcement learning becomes effective in a broader range of real-world domains rather than only in settings with narrowly curated logged data?

source_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
question_text: How should the community build offline reinforcement learning benchmarks and datasets that better reflect real deployment conditions by including stochastic dynamics, nonstationarity, risky biases in the data, and multiagent settings, so that algorithms can be evaluated on the kinds of failures and shifts that matter in practice?

source_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
question_text: What security mechanisms can provide integrity and authentication, not only confidentiality, for underwater wireless optical communication systems, given that the surveyed literature mainly studies confidentiality and only a few theoretical works study quantum key distribution for direct light-based air-water communication?

source_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
question_text: What are the vulnerabilities, attack models, and effective countermeasures for magnetic-induction-based underwater wireless communication networks, including how confidentiality, authentication, integrity, and availability can be achieved in systems whose predictable channel response may expose them to eavesdropping and spoofing and whose nearby malicious coils may exploit mutual induction?

source_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
question_text: How can direct air-water wireless communication systems be secured against active attacks such as jamming and spoofing and passive attacks such as eavesdropping, while also modeling malicious nodes that can observe or attack both the air and underwater media and formalizing their behaviors, strategies, and computing and communication capabilities?

source_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
question_text: How do existing underwater communication technologies behave under smart malicious nodes that can switch between passive and active attack modes on the fly, and how should security be analyzed when those malicious nodes are equipped with state-of-the-art capabilities such as multiple-input multiple-output operation, full duplex, GPUs, and the ability to launch attacks in both air and water media?

source_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
question_text: What are the trade-offs between deploying security mechanisms and maintaining throughput, energy efficiency, spectral efficiency, and reliability in underwater and air-water wireless communication systems, and how can the cost of enforcing a chosen security level be quantified across those performance metrics?

source_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
question_text: How can machine-learning-based security methods that already appear promising in underwater communication, such as learning-based authentication or anti-eavesdropping approaches, be adapted and validated for air-water wireless communication systems?

source_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
question_text: Can cross-layer security approaches that protect information across multiple protocol-stack layers improve the security and privacy of air-water communication systems, where such approaches have not yet been studied according to the survey?

source_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
question_text: How can underwater nodes be localized securely in direct air-water communication systems by combining underwater reference or surface nodes with over-water localization mechanisms, especially when recently reported attacks such as Sybil and Wormhole show that localization protocols themselves must be hardened?

source_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
question_text: What authentication and integrity mechanisms are appropriate for direct air-water wireless communication systems, given that the surveyed literature does not yet contain studies addressing those two security properties for that setting?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: After a QCD axion is discovered, how can one determine its quantized photon coupling with enough precision to test ultraviolet predictions such as the Grand Unified Theory value E/N = 8/3, given that haloscope measurements determine a rate proportional to g_aγγ^2 ρ_DM and therefore are degenerate with the poorly known local dark-matter density? In particular, can one identify an axion dark-matter sub-component whose local density can be predicted more accurately than the total local dark-matter density?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: What experimental strategies, beyond combining existing photon and electric-dipole-moment measurements in the small overlap of their parameter space, can measure and test the quantized couplings of a discovered QCD axion after the initial discovery?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: For hyperlight axions with mass below the present Hubble scale, can one develop position-space cosmic-microwave-background polarization observables that detect the quantized jump in polarization across an axion string and quantitatively characterize the sensitivity of upcoming CMB experiments to that jump?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: In the axion potential generated by a real magnetic monopole, how do the neglected radial-mode degrees of freedom modify the axion-monopole dynamics, especially in the regime where the axion gradients near the monopole are large enough that the low-energy effective theory may break down?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: When the monopole is not point-like, for which monopole radii and field-gradient regimes is the usual approximation of replacing the monopole contribution by the electrostatic self-energy of a charged sphere reliable, and how should one compute the finite-size corrections more rigorously?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: In the presence of light charged fermions, can one derive from first principles how electric-field screening modifies or suppresses the monopole-generated axion potential, rather than relying on the approximation that replaces the potential by the electrostatic self-energy of a charged sphere with radius set by the inverse fermion mass?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: How is the axion potential generated by magnetic monopoles modified in a thermal bath of relativistic charged particles, where plasma screening changes the long-distance electric fields and therefore changes the monopole-induced axion potential relevant for cosmological applications?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: For the axion potential induced by virtual dyonic loops, is the dilute approximation in which a single dyon loop dominates and long-range Coulomb interactions between dyons are ignored actually valid, and if so in what regime?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: How does the axion potential induced by virtual dyonic loops change when charged fermions are present, especially in the limit where the fermions become massless and the dependence on the electromagnetic theta angle should disappear because a chiral symmetry is restored?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: What is the correct treatment of the interactions between magnetic monopoles or dyons and massless fermions, and how should those fermions be incorporated into the computation of virtual dyon loops so that the special massless-fermion limit is reproduced correctly?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: If one solves the problem of fermion effects in the axion-dyon system, does electromagnetism by itself imply a nonzero lower bound on the mass of an axion coupled to our photon, even in the absence of non-Abelian instantons?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: In axion models with electromagnetic duality invariance, equivalently SL(2, Z) invariance, what is the correct relation between the non-perturbative constraints imposed by the duality symmetry on the joint axion-saxion scalar potential and the perturbative loop calculations that seem to generate saxion and axion potentials?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: Can the existence of electromagnetic duality be tested experimentally through measured axion couplings?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: Within quantum gravity, can proposed solutions to the axion quality problem actually be implemented successfully, or alternatively is the quality problem itself not a genuine obstacle for the QCD axion once quantum-gravitational effects are treated correctly?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: Are large-field natural-inflation models built from one or more axions compatible with a ultraviolet-complete theory of quantum gravity, either because an explicit string-theory construction exists or because a strict no-go theorem proves that no such construction is possible?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: What is the correct physical motivation and precise formulation of the axion Weak Gravity Conjecture, including the correct order-one coefficient c in the bound f_a S < c M_Pl, given that present cosmological constraints from the conjecture depend crucially on that coefficient and on a better understanding of gravitational instantons and Euclidean wormholes?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: In axion monodromy and related relaxion constructions, can the backreaction associated with super-Planckian field excursions and towers of light states be kept under theoretical control inside a ultraviolet-complete quantum-gravity model?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: What is the precise order-one coefficient c′ in the axion-string version of the Weak Gravity Conjecture bound on string tension, T ≤ c′ f_a M_Pl, so that the resulting quantum-gravity constraints on low-energy effective field theory become quantitatively sharp?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: Can one prove the conjecture that every infinite-distance limit of scalar-field moduli space is the ultraviolet endpoint of a renormalization-group flow on an axionic string?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: For the post-inflationary Peccei-Quinn symmetry-breaking scenario, what analytic theory explains the observed scaling solution of the axion-string network, including the logarithmic growth of the network energy density and the converging length distribution seen in simulations?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: What is the correct energy spectrum of axions emitted by the scaling axion-string network, and therefore how large is the string contribution to the present QCD-axion dark-matter abundance?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: How does thermal friction from gluon scattering modify the dynamics of QCD axion strings, and can that friction leave observable signatures or substantially change the predicted axion number abundance produced by the string network?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: Around the QCD phase transition, what is the full temperature-dependent shape of the axion potential away from its minimum, especially near θ̄ = π where the low-temperature potential is cuspy, and how does that shape affect post-inflationary axion dynamics such as minicluster formation?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: Can one construct a viable cosmological model in which the QCD axion itself acts as the inflaton and QCD radiation generated through thermal friction sustains warm inflation, perhaps by finding an early-universe mechanism that makes the light quarks heavy enough to evade the chemical-potential obstruction from light fermions?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: How does the macroscopic thermal-friction coefficient Υ scale outside the well-understood strong warm-inflation regime, especially near the weak regime Υ ≲ H where the transport-coefficient approximation may fail and the predicted inflationary observables could change?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: What is the correct sphaleron-rate and thermal-friction behavior when the non-Abelian gauge coupling approaches the strong-coupling regime, such as α > 0.1, where perturbative calculations are unreliable and lattice results are still incomplete?

source_title: Some open questions in axion theory
question_text: How do tachyonic-instability-induced friction and thermal friction interact when both are available in an axion-gauge-field system, which mechanism turns on first, and how should one model the nonlinear evolution and initial conditions of the later stage?

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: Can the existing methods developed for the original Gan-Gross-Prasad conjectures in the Hermitian or untwisted setting be adapted to the twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad setting for skew-Hermitian spaces, in particular the integral formulas for branching multiplicities and the Jacquet-Rallis relative trace formula comparisons that underlie proofs of branching and period conjectures?

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: For a skew-Hermitian space V over a quadratic algebra E/F and the corresponding Weil representation ω_{V,ψ,μ}, prove the local twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad multiplicity-one and epsilon-factor prediction for irreducible representations Π of GL(V): first, that dim Hom_{U(V)}(Π, ω_{V,ψ,μ}) is always at most 1; second, that when Π is generic the sum of these multiplicities over all equivalence classes of skew-Hermitian structures on V equals 1; and third, that the unique skew-Hermitian space V giving nonzero multiplicity is characterized by the identity μ(det(V)) = ε(1/2, Π × σΠ∨ × μ^{-1}, ψ_E) · ω_Π(-1)^n · ω_{E/F}(-1)^{n(n-1)/2}.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: For a cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_E) and an n-dimensional skew-Hermitian space V over the global field E, prove the global twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad criterion that the global period integral P_V is nonzero exactly when every local Hom-space Hom_{U(V_v)}(Π_v, ω_{V_v,ψ_v,μ_v}) is nonzero and the central L-value L(1/2, Π × σΠ∨ × μ^{-1}) is nonzero, and prove that whenever this central L-value is nonzero there is a unique skew-Hermitian space V of dimension n for which P_V is nonzero.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: For the local normalized period integral I_v attached to Π_v and the Weil representation ω_{V_v,ψ_v,μ_v}, determine whether I_v is nonzero exactly when the local branching space Hom_{U(V)(F_v)}(Π_v, ω_{V_v,ψ_v,μ_v}) is nonzero, and compute this local integral at almost all places v of F where all data are unramified.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: In the unramified local setting where E_v/F_v is an unramified quadratic extension of residue characteristic not 2, ψ_v and μ_v are unramified, V_v admits a self-dual lattice with hyperspecial stabilizer, and Π_v together with the chosen vectors are spherical of norm 1, prove the explicit formula Conjecture 2.4 for the local period integral I_v, namely that I_v equals (L(1, M∨_{GL(V_v)}) / L(1, M∨_{U(V_v)})) · (L(1/2, Π_v × σΠ∨_v × μ_v^{-1}) / L(1, Π_v, Ad)).

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: For a tempered cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL(V), prove the refined global period formula Conjecture 2.7 stating that the square of the global period functional P is given by the central L-value L(1/2, Π × σΠ∨ × μ^{-1}), the motive factor L(1, M∨_{U(V)}), the ratio (L(s, M∨_{GL(V)}) / L(s, Π, Ad)) evaluated at s = 1, and the product of normalized local factors I_v^#.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: For the twisted restriction problem over finite fields, quantify precisely how and when the naive expected multiplicity behavior fails for cuspidal Deligne-Lusztig representations, and determine the extent to which the expected rule remains generically valid.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: For any irreducible generic representation Π of the finite symplectic group Sp_{2n}(F_{q^2}), determine the branching multiplicity dim Hom_{Sp_{2n}(F_q)}(Π, ω) for the Weil representation ω.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: Because the two-fold cover of Sp_{2n}(E) splits over Sp_{2n}(F), there is no direct non-archimedean analogue of the finite-field symplectic branching problem. The paper therefore asks whether one should instead pass to a four-fold cover of Sp_{2n}(E), assuming E contains the fourth roots of unity, in order to formulate and study an analogous branching problem over non-archimedean local fields.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: Establish the vanishing assumption for generalized Steinberg representations that the two branching spaces Hom_{U(V+V)}(Sp(π,2), ω_{V+V,ψ,μ}) and Hom_{U(V+W)}(Sp(π,2), ω_{V+W,ψ,μ}) are both zero for the two isomorphism classes V and W of m-dimensional skew-Hermitian spaces over E. The paper identifies this as a special case of the nontempered twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture and explicitly says it does not know how to prove it except when m = 1.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: Assume E/F = C/R. Let Π be an irreducible generic principal series representation of GL_n(C) induced from characters χ_j(z) = |z|^{r_j}(z/̅z)^{k_j/2} with k_j integers, and let μ(z) = (̅z/z)^α for a half-integer α that is not an integer. Prove that Hom_{U(V_{p,q})}(Π, ω_{V_{p,q},ψ,μ}) is nonzero exactly for the signature (p,q) satisfying #{j : k_j > α} = p and #{j : k_j < α} = q = n - p.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: Let V be an n-dimensional skew-Hermitian space over E/F and let π be an irreducible admissible representation of GL(V) with A-parameter M_A = ⊕_i M_i ⊠ Sym^{d_i}(C^2), where each M_i is tempered. Prove the nontempered twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture that if Hom_{U(V)}(π, ω_{V,ψ,μ}) is nonzero, then M_A must be a sum of a tempered A-parameter together with pieces of the form N_i ⊠ Sym^{d_i}(C^2) ⊕ μ·N_i^σ ⊠ Sym^{d_i-1}(C^2), equivalently that M_A and μ·M_A^σ are relevant in the sense of GGP3; and conversely, if those parameters are relevant, then Hom_{U(V)}(π, ω_{V,ψ,μ}) is one-dimensional for exactly one skew-Hermitian space V, namely the one predicted by Conjecture 2.1(iii).

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: For the case E ≠ K and a generic L-parameter M of U(V_K), prove the full local twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture 8.3: multiplicity one for each π in Irr(U(V_K)); the packet identity that the total multiplicity summed over both skew-Hermitian spaces V and all π in the L-packet Π_M equals 1; an epsilon-factor formula characterizing the unique skew-Hermitian space V_0 that contributes; and an explicit character formula identifying the unique packet member π with nonzero contribution via the local component group A_M.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: For the global case with E ≠ K, prove that the global period integral P is nonzero exactly when every local Hom-space Hom_{U(V_v)}(Π_v, ω_{V_v,ψ,μ_v}) is nonzero and the twisted Asai central value L(1/2, Π, As_{L/E} × μ^{-1}) is nonzero, and prove that a nonzero central value forces the existence of an n-dimensional skew-Hermitian space V over E for which the global period integral is nonzero.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: After fixing decompositions of Tamagawa measures and Petersson inner products in the global E ≠ K setting, prove the refined global conjectural identity expressing P ⊗ P in terms of the component-group factor 1/|S_Π|, the ratio L(1, M∨_{U(V_K)}) / L(1, M∨_{U(V)}), the twisted Asai central value L(1/2, Π, As_{L/E} × μ^{-1}), the adjoint L-value L(1, Π, Ad), and the product of normalized local integrals I_v^#.

source_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
question_text: Develop a relative trace formula, analogous to the one used in the original Gan-Gross-Prasad setting, that can address the global twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjectures formulated in this paper.

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: Which parameters, or combinations of parameters, in a biological model can actually be inferred with useful precision from the available prior knowledge and observed data, especially in large models such as whole-cell models where many individual parameters may be practically non-identifiable?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: How can model selection for biological systems be made statistically principled and computationally tractable when alternative models may have different effective parameter subspaces, many models can be nearly indistinguishable on available data, and the space of plausible models may not have any clear finite upper bound?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: Can flexible, universal, and automatable comparison methods be developed for biological models so that models written in different formalisms, with different structures, boundary conditions, and parameter regimes, can be compared rigorously enough to identify shared design principles behind behaviors such as oscillations, adaptation, switching, filtering, or pattern formation?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: How can biological model-development pipelines automatically generate, update, and compare large families of candidate models starting from a seed model while keeping the process reproducible and keeping parameter estimation and trans-dimensional model selection computationally feasible at each step?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: Can multiscale biological models be analyzed with systematic sensitivity methods that test how higher-level behavior depends on lower-level modeling choices, and can reliable statistical emulators replace prohibitively expensive simulations such as agent-based models without losing the scientifically important behavior being studied?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: How can submodels for gene regulation, metabolism, the cell cycle, mechanics, electrophysiology, and transport be linked into modular multiscale or whole-cell models that remain thermodynamically consistent across interfaces, especially when conservation laws and bond-graph structure must be respected?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: How can complex biological systems with nonlinear dynamics and stochastic effects be modeled and analyzed so that one can predict when deterministic qualitative features such as bistability, stationarity, or bifurcations survive the introduction of noise, and how can one build approximations that remain reliable in nonlinear stochastic regimes?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: What mathematically adequate genotype-to-phenotype maps are needed to explain how genes, gene expression, and their interactions produce phenotypes and complex diseases, especially when evolutionary dynamics combine deterministic selection, stochastic effects, and potentially omnigenic inheritance?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: How should hybrid biological models combine mechanistic equations with data-driven or machine-learning components so that the result improves explanation and prediction while also helping with outstanding problems such as model identifiability and parameter identifiability?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: What general theory of life can supply a mathematical definition of life together with general concepts and principles for living systems, rather than leaving biology with isolated descriptions that do not amount to a unified account of life as such?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: What rigorous mathematical definitions of emergence and emergent properties are needed for biology so that higher-level biological behavior can be characterized and explained in a mathematically usable way without requiring exhaustive reduction to lower-level constituents?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: How can mathematical biology reach the level of mathematical maturity needed for living systems by developing rigorous biological definitions, using theorem-proof style arguments where appropriate, and creating genuinely new mathematical theory rather than relying mainly on imported or ad hoc methods?

source_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
question_text: How can heterogeneous biological datasets and apparently different mathematical models be unified so that multiple hypotheses can be compared across broad evidence, related models can be recognized as conceptually similar, and a more integrated theory of biological systems can emerge instead of fragmented subfield-specific explanations?

source_title: Open questions in massive star research
question_text: What fraction of massive binaries merge before core hydrogen burning, during the pre-main-sequence phase, because residual accretion and tides from circum-binary material shrink their orbits? If such mergers are common, can massive stars on the long-lived core-hydrogen-burning main sequence be observationally separated into a population formed mainly by disk accretion and a population that gained much of their mass through binary merger, for example through distinctive stellar-spin signatures?

source_title: Open questions in massive star research
question_text: What physical mechanism produces the large-scale magnetic fields observed in about 5% to 10% of early-type main-sequence stars? In particular, do stellar mergers create the stable large-scale toroidal-poloidal magnetic topologies needed for long-term fields, or do only some mergers do so, and could the observed field incidence instead be limited by magnetic-field decay on a timescale comparable to the main-sequence lifetime?

source_title: Open questions in massive star research
question_text: Why do large spectroscopic surveys show a dearth of very young massive stars above about 20 solar masses in the Galaxy, the Large Magellanic Cloud, and the Small Magellanic Cloud? Are these stars still embedded in their birth clouds or still accreting for roughly half of their total lifetime, and if so why is the corresponding population of infrared-bright stars not observed?

source_title: Open questions in massive star research
question_text: Do the envelopes of massive stars inflate when the stellar envelope becomes locally super-Eddington, and how is that inflation altered by rotation? More specifically, can hydrostatic density inversions and envelope inflation inferred in one-dimensional and three-dimensional models be extended to a correct two-dimensional description of rotating stars near the Eddington limit, so that the effect of centrifugal force on the inflation is understood?

source_title: Open questions in massive star research
question_text: Are luminous blue variable stars physically close to their Eddington limit, with their observed large radius and brightness variations driven by inflated envelopes that cannot settle into thermal equilibrium under plausible mass-loss prescriptions? If so, does the same Eddington-limit physics also explain giant eruptions like η Carinae's, or are those eruptions instead products of stellar mergers in very massive multiple systems?

source_title: Open questions in massive star research
question_text: How efficient is mass transfer in close massive binaries, meaning what fraction of mass lost by the donor is retained by the accretor rather than immediately ejected or lost from the system? The open problem is to find a physical prescription for mass-transfer efficiency that explains why some systems evolve nearly conservatively while others evolve highly non-conservatively, and that captures the strong dependence on binary properties and stellar mass rather than assuming one constant efficiency for all systems.

source_title: Open questions in massive star research
question_text: When a core-hydrogen-burning star in a close binary accretes enough mass to grow substantially, to what extent is it rejuvenated, meaning how far does its convective core grow and how much fresh hydrogen is mixed into that core across the stabilizing mean-molecular-weight gradient? The unresolved issue is whether semiconvective mixing is efficient enough for nearly complete rejuvenation, and whether observed contact binaries and their period-change measurements support or rule out that scenario.

source_title: Open questions in massive star research
question_text: What fraction of observed Wolf-Rayet stars were stripped of their hydrogen-rich envelopes by a binary companion rather than produced by single-star mass loss and mixing? This includes the unresolved subproblem of how many Wolf-Rayet stars were stripped only after the initially more massive star had already become a compact object, a channel whose rate depends on uncertain compact-object natal kicks and common-envelope evolution.

source_title: Open questions in massive star research
question_text: Where are the pair-instability supernovae that theory robustly predicts from helium cores of roughly 60 to 135 solar masses, given that no observed supernova has yet been identified beyond doubt as a pair-instability supernova? Are such events being missed because low-mass pair-instability explosions from compact Wolf-Rayet or helium stars can be comparatively dim, because hydrogen-rich pair-instability explosions resemble bright Type II-plateau supernovae, or because their occurrence is strongly restricted by metallicity and cosmic epoch?

source_title: Open questions in massive star research
question_text: What physical mechanism powers superluminous supernovae, especially the common hydrogen-poor Type Ic events and the still poorly understood hydrogen-rich subclass? The unresolved task is to distinguish among power from several solar masses of radioactive nickel produced in pair-instability explosions, conversion of ejecta kinetic energy into light through collision with dense circumstellar matter, and energy injection from a newly born millisecond magnetar, while also determining whether chemically homogeneous low-metallicity massive stars are truly the progenitors of the magnetar-powered Type Ic events.

source_title: Progress in Nuclear Astrophysics: a multi-disciplinary field with still many open questions
question_text: What is the correct 22Ne+α reaction-rate input, especially for the 22Ne(α,n)25Mg channel, in rotating massive stars, and how does that rate change the efficiency of the s process and the resulting production of p nuclides during later supernova explosions? The paper states that s-process production in massive stars remains sensitive to this rate, that recently questioned measurements can reduce the 22Ne(α,n)25Mg rate by a factor of 5 relative to an earlier reference value, and that the same uncertainty propagates into p-process yields.

source_title: Progress in Nuclear Astrophysics: a multi-disciplinary field with still many open questions
question_text: How can nuclear mass models for exotic neutron-rich nuclei be improved so that r-process calculations use masses and derived neutron-capture rates that remain accurate far from experimentally known nuclei? In the paper, current models can disagree by up to about ±5 MeV near important shell closures, causing neutron-capture rates to differ by 3 to 5 orders of magnitude, and the authors explicitly call for improved relativistic and non-relativistic mean-field models, beyond-mean-field corrections, and better treatment of odd-A and odd-odd nuclei together with broader agreement with other observables such as charge radii, neutron skins, fission barriers, spectroscopic data, nuclear-matter properties, and neutron-star properties.

source_title: Progress in Nuclear Astrophysics: a multi-disciplinary field with still many open questions
question_text: How can machine-learning methods be used in nuclear astrophysics so that they improve nuclear-data prediction or emulator efficiency without destroying predictive power when extrapolating to nuclei outside the training and validation region, especially heavy nuclei with Z ≥ 82? The paper reports that a neural-network test on masses truncated below Pb achieves good interpolation metrics inside the known region but produces an uncontrolled rms deviation of 37.8 MeV on the excluded heavy nuclei, and it therefore treats reliable extrapolation as an unresolved requirement even while arguing that ML can still be useful for reducing computational cost and scanning large model spaces.
context_brief: Reliable ML extrapolation for unknown nuclei

source_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
question_text: In branch-cut cosmology, how should the apparent cosmic anisotropy associated with the smoothness problem of small temperature fluctuations be explained consistently, especially in the final stage of contraction where the authors say a negative value of the dimensionless thermodynamic parameter epsilon reverses the scaling behavior of the anisotropy-related ratio while the remaining ratios stay locked in?

source_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
question_text: If the branch-cut scale factor shrinks only to a finite critical size well above the Planck limit, what is the physical nature of the finite-size transition between the primordial contraction phase and the primordial expansion phase, which the authors describe as a classical leap?

source_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
question_text: How should branch-cut cosmology be reformulated quantum mechanically, rather than only through leading-order classical equations of motion, so that the intrinsically quantum evolutionary domain near the primordial transition is described more faithfully?

source_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
question_text: What is the correct and more internally consistent way to map the evolution of the cut-planes in branch-cut cosmology, so that the time development of the model across its Riemann-sheet structure is described coherently?

source_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
question_text: What are the cosmological consequences in branch-cut cosmology of abandoning a symmetric treatment of the dimensionless thermodynamics connection epsilon(t), and of choosing a different ordering for the values taken by epsilon(t) during the universe's evolution?

source_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
question_text: What role does dark matter play in the evolution of the branch-cut universe, including any role it may have in the contraction-era scaling behavior that the authors connect to the epsilon parameter?

source_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
question_text: What concrete predictions does branch-cut cosmology make for the primordial energy-density fluctuation spectrum that seeds later structure formation, and can Cosmic Microwave Background measurements from Planck constrain or test those predictions?

source_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
question_text: If primordial multi-universes were in thermal contact inside a thermal bath and were subjected to a contraction crunch before later decoupling, what thermal evolution would our universe inherit from that earlier multiverse interaction?

source_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
question_text: Within branch-cut cosmology and its multiverse picture, how are the homogeneity of primordial radiation and the average density of matter established strongly enough to support the later formation of the structures observed in the universe today?

source_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
question_text: How can physical-layer security techniques be designed for satellite communication systems to preserve availability against denial-of-service and jamming attacks, given that satellites and satellite links can be overwhelmed by malicious traffic and can be targeted by multiple forms of jamming that distort signals and prevent correct decoding and processing, and given that any proposed method must remain feasible under the unique physical characteristics of satellite communication?

source_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
question_text: How can physical-layer security schemes be developed to secure uplink satellite communication from terrestrial or aerial devices to satellites, when the uplink is vulnerable to spoofing, message alteration, and denial-of-service attacks, carries large volumes of user data in broadband satellite systems, and must operate under performance and power constraints across heterogeneous devices and scenarios?

source_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
question_text: How should physical-layer security for satellite systems be redesigned under stronger and more realistic threat models in which eavesdroppers are not merely passive, single-antenna, static listeners with limited resources, but may actively intercept to extract main-channel state information, possess improved antenna and signal-processing capabilities, and move dynamically with unknown locations, for example as UAV-based adversaries?

source_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
question_text: How can physical-layer security authentication and anti-spoofing strategies be designed for satellite services beyond global navigation satellite systems, including broadband and satellite-IoT services, so that unauthorized devices cannot impersonate legitimate users or inject high-power spoofed signals and unauthenticated messages that grant illicit service access or leak information intended for legitimate users?

source_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
question_text: How can physical-layer security techniques be used to provide message integrity for satellite communication systems, so that man-in-the-middle style attacks that intercept, modify, and retransmit satellite-to-user or user-to-satellite signals can be detected reliably before corrupted information is accepted or processed?

source_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
question_text: How can physical-layer security strategies be developed specifically for inter-satellite communication, including both radio-frequency and optical inter-satellite links, when such links are increasingly attackable in low-earth-orbit constellations, remain understudied in the literature, and exhibit distinctive physical-layer characteristics such as fading, Doppler shift, and weather-condition effects that may be exploitable for security, while optical inter-satellite links still lack proposed defenses against threats such as eavesdropping?

source_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
question_text: How can machine-learning-based physical-layer security methods be adapted and validated for satellite communication systems, given that existing ML-based PLS work has been studied in other wireless settings such as device-to-device communication, cognitive networks, and non-orthogonal multiple access, but has not yet been explored for satellite scenarios or analyzed for applicability under satellite-specific operating conditions and physical characteristics?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: How can a reconfigurable intelligent surface element be completely deactivated so that its reflection is nulled with respect to all angles, and what physically realizable RIS design or control model would make that all-angle nulling possible for channel-training methods that rely on turning elements off?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: For RIS-aided sparse channel estimation in mmWave or THz settings, what pilot signals and RIS training states are optimal for sparse recovery, and what training-based capacity results follow when the channel is estimated through sparse recovery rather than standard linear estimation?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: When RIS reflection coefficients are updated only infrequently and the practical implementation therefore requires coding across many coherence intervals of the slower channel, should RIS configuration and beamforming be optimized for outage capacity or throughput rather than ergodic capacity, and how should that optimization be formulated?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: For RIS-aided systems that use statistical channel state information and optimize long-term performance under infrequent RIS updates, what achievable-rate inner bounds can be derived for the ergodic-rate optimization problem, instead of relying only on outer bounds?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: Under exactly what physical, angular, and surface-design conditions are RIS-induced channels reciprocal or non-reciprocal, and what validated theory or experimental evidence is needed to support communication-system models that assume a non-reciprocal RIS?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: Can an RIS channel model be derived that keeps the end-to-end channel in a factored form GΦH, while still capturing mutual impedances and coupling by allowing the RIS matrix Φ to become a possibly non-diagonal function of circuit parameters, and can a practical channel-estimation method be built for that model?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: Is perfect deactivation of RIS elements physically feasible for communication systems that need to suppress all RIS reflections during channel estimation, and if so, what electromagnetic design conditions and implementation methods make that feasible in a conclusive and communication-relevant way?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: If RIS elements cannot be perfectly deactivated in practice, how does imperfect deactivation change the accuracy and robustness of channel-estimation methods that assume complete absorption, complete transmission, or complete removal of RIS reflections?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: Can hardware structures that provide near-independent control of reflection amplitude and phase be shown to work effectively for RIS-aided communication systems, rather than only in related reflectarray or metasurface settings?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: Do the wideband remedies proposed in the reflectarray literature, such as true time-delay lines or multiple resonance elements, actually transfer to RIS-aided communication systems, and under what operating assumptions would they preserve useful beamforming behavior across the communication band?

source_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
question_text: What channel models and channel-estimation techniques are appropriate for RIS-aided near-field communication, where a large RIS violates the far-field planar-wave assumption and different RIS elements experience different angles and polarization conditions?

source_title: An Overview of Compact Star Populations and Some of Its Open Problems
question_text: Do neutron-star magnetic fields genuinely decay over astrophysical timescales, and if so do they fade almost completely within about 10^6 years or instead decay only partially to a persistent 'bottom field' that remains substantial even in very old systems such as black widows?

source_title: An Overview of Compact Star Populations and Some of Its Open Problems
question_text: What evolutionary relationships connect the observed neutron-star subpopulations, including ordinary radio pulsars, central compact objects, X-ray Dim Isolated Neutron Stars (XDINSs), Rotating Radio Transients (RRATs), magnetars, and other hidden neutron stars, and which of these classes are genuinely distinct populations versus temporary evolutionary stages of the same underlying objects?

source_title: An Overview of Compact Star Populations and Some of Its Open Problems
question_text: Are the recently discovered ultra-slow magnetars and other very long-period neutron-star candidates simply older evolutionary stages of magnetars that have cooled and spun down to extremely long periods, or are they a distinct population, possibly closer in nature to RRATs than to standard magnetar evolution?

source_title: An Overview of Compact Star Populations and Some of Its Open Problems
question_text: Does the compact-object mass distribution contain a true lower black-hole mass gap between about 2 and 5 solar masses, or is that interval only partially depleted, with some objects and formation channels populating at least part of the 2.5–5 solar-mass range?

source_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
question_text: Let N(R) denote the number of integer lattice points inside the radius-R disc B(R) in the plane. Is it true that the Gauss circle problem has error term N(R) = Area(B(R)) + O(R^(1/2+o(1))) as R → ∞? Equivalently, can one prove Hardy's conjecture that the discrepancy between the lattice-point count and the disc area is bounded up to subpower factors by the square-root scale R^(1/2)?
context_brief: Hardy's conjecture for the Gauss circle problem

source_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
question_text: For each fixed integer k ≥ 1, let C_k be the limiting correlation C_k = lim_{R→∞} (1/K(R)) ∑_{j=1}^{K(R)} (A_R(λ_j)·A_R(λ_{j+k}) - 1/4), where the lattice points λ_j in the annulus of width √2 around the circle of radius R are ordered by polar angle and A_R(λ) is the area of the unit square centered at λ that lies inside B(R). Do these limiting correlations vanish as the angular-index separation grows, i.e. is lim_{k→∞} C_k = 0?

source_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
question_text: As R → ∞ and then k → ∞, do the pairs (A_R(λ_j), A_R(λ_{j+k})) converge in distribution to the random vector (Y_1, Y_2) = (A_∞(r, θ), A_∞(r', θ)), where (r, θ, r') is uniformly distributed on [-1/√2, 1/√2] × [0, 2π) × [-1/√2, 1/√2]? In other words, after first taking the large-radius limit and then sending the index separation k to infinity, does the joint law of the two boundary-square intersection areas approach the random-model limit proposed in Conjecture 2.3?

source_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
question_text: Fix an angle θ and a shift parameter r in the tilted-and-shifted semi-infinite rectangle model R_{r,θ}. If one orders the lattice points of Z^2 ∩ R_{r,θ} by projection onto the long side of the rectangle and then projects them onto the short side, can one prove equidistribution of those short-side projections in [-1/√2, 1/√2] without averaging over the index ℓ, while instead exploiting averaging over r? The paper identifies establishing exactly this stronger equidistribution statement as the major challenge toward proving the vanishing-correlation conjecture.

source_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
question_text: In Proposition 6.1, the authors prove an asymptotic formula for the number of lattice points in the annulus Γ_R whose shifted polar data satisfy θ_λ ∈ [c,d] mod 2π and r_λ ∈ I, uniformly when the sector length |d-c| is at least R^(-1/2). Can this asymptotic be proved for a wider range of shorter sector lengths than the one established in the paper?
context_brief: Improve the sector-length range in Proposition 6.1

source_title: Stellar model calibrations with the Ai Phe binary system. Open questions about the robustness of the fit
question_text: What is the relation, if any, between stellar mass and the convective core overshooting parameter β that measures the extent of extra mixing beyond the formal convective-core boundary in stellar evolution models? In particular, can a physically meaningful mass–β relation be established, or do different analyses of binary-star systems support incompatible values of β even when the stellar masses are well measured?

source_title: Stellar model calibrations with the Ai Phe binary system. Open questions about the robustness of the fit
question_text: For the detached eclipsing binary system Ai Phe, whose primary star has already undergone first dredge-up while the secondary has not, how robust are stellar-model calibrations—especially the inferred system age and the convective core overshooting parameter β—to assumptions about microscopic diffusion and surface metallicity evolution? More specifically, if microscopic diffusion is allowed to alter the observable surface [Fe/H] of the stars versus being effectively canceled at the surface by competing mixing processes, do the same precise masses, radii, temperatures, and metallicity measurements lead to materially different calibrations?

source_title: Stellar model calibrations with the Ai Phe binary system. Open questions about the robustness of the fit
question_text: When fitting stellar models to a precisely observed binary system such as Ai Phe, do different stellar codes, inference pipelines, or modelling assumptions about microscopic diffusion and other extra-mixing processes produce different estimates of the system age and convective core overshooting efficiency? If they do, to what extent are the inferred calibration parameters properties of the stars themselves rather than artifacts of the modeller's chosen input physics and estimation pipeline?

source_title: Stellar model calibrations with the Ai Phe binary system. Open questions about the robustness of the fit
question_text: Can binary systems in the approximately 1.2–1.5 M⊙ mass range be used to robustly constrain free parameters in stellar evolution calculations, or are the resulting calibrations too sensitive to uncertain surface-[Fe/H] evolution and related modelling choices? In the specific case of Ai Phe, which of the competing surface-metallicity scenarios is the more reliable description of the system, and can precise measurements of the individual stellar surface [Fe/H] values discriminate between those scenarios?

source_title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
question_text: How can one give concrete physical interpretations for the infinitely many symmetries and conservation laws that arise in integrable systems, beyond the small subset that already have familiar interpretations such as space-time translation invariance, Galilean or Lorentz invariance, scaling invariance, and the conservation of mass, momentum, and energy?

source_title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
question_text: For integrable nonlinear partial differential equation systems, whose solution spaces have infinitely many degrees of freedom, are the currently known infinitely many symmetries complete, or do additional undiscovered symmetries exist beyond the standard families already generated in the literature?

source_title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
question_text: Can generalized symmetries, especially generalized local symmetries rather than only Lie point symmetries or nonlocal symmetry constraints, be used to derive exact multi-wave solutions of integrable partial differential equation systems, in particular multi-soliton solutions and other exact solutions beyond single periodic cnoidal waves, solitary waves, and Painlevé-type solutions?
